full_text:
The Eagles, who traded up to draft Makai Lemon at No. 20 this year, expect the rookie receiver to play a key role in the offense. Bill Streicher / Imagn Images
PHILADELPHIA — Makai Lemon said he felt a familiar pain. Yes, in his hamstring. Yes, the same hamstring that sidelined him for half of the Philadelphia Eagles’ OTAs. It was a “little tweak,” the rookie wide receiver said, which flared when he attempted to burst, just four days into training camp . The injury caused him to miss two weeks of practices, two preseason games and the competitive parts of two joint practices with the New England Patriots.
The repeat injury carried all the frustrating elements of a “here we go again” situation.
“It was definitely tough,” Lemon said. “I’m real competitive. Ain’t never want to be away from this game. So, me knowing that it’s the hamstring again, I’m just making sure I take the right precautions. (I’m) learning from it so it doesn’t happen again.”
Lemon, who returned to full participation in Monday’s practice, further defined his lesson as “making sure I’m more professional off the field.” He works with the team’s trainers. He adheres to the recovery plan they created for him. He makes sure to warm up properly before taking the field.
Professional . He repeated the word Monday, almost as if he were emphasizing his new standards. The No. 20 pick avoided making excuses, even when a reporter asked how many practices he thought it’d take to fully apply the mental reps he’d been taking.
“You’re supposed to take the mental rep, come out here and bring it to life,” Lemon said. “That’s about being a professional.”
That perspective suits the Eagles. The sooner Lemon is up to speed, the better.
Lemon was the primary acquisition in the organization’s overhaul of its wide receivers group this offseason. He was never expected to be a substitute for A.J. Brown, whom the Eagles traded to the Patriots in June. Philadelphia general manager Howie Roseman traded up from No. 23 to snatch Lemon at No. 20 in the 2026 draft because the 2025 winner of the Biletnikoff Award, as the best receiver in college football, had been a dogged and versatile chain mover, whose penchant for yards after the catch at USC made him a fit in the system first-time offensive coordinator Sean Mannion planned to run in Philly.
The Eagles’ financial core was also shifting to the team’s defense . Further still, Brown remains on this year’s budget as a $21.8 million dead money hit. Lemon and his affordable rookie contract (a $3.7 million cap hit in 2026) fit Roseman’s cost-effective strategy to provide DeVonta Smith ($10.7 million) with a supporting cast. Roseman also made a moderate gamble by spending $12 million in cash payouts this year to bring down the cap hits of veteran acquisitions Dontayvion Wicks ($2.3 million) and Hollywood Brown ($2 million). When Smith and Lemon suffered hamstring injuries in the second week of training camp, Brown’s series of drops underlined the rhythm and firepower the Eagles lacked without Lemon.
That Lemon spent Monday’s entire practice with the first-team offense suggested how much the Eagles need him on the field — and how much catching up Lemon must do in a short amount of time. The Eagles have two more training camp practices, plus a walk-through, before they host the Cincinnati Bengals in their preseason finale Friday. Lemon, who said he is prepared to play Friday if called upon, will have two more weeks of practice before the Eagles’ regular-season opener against the Washington Commanders.
Can Lemon become comfortable in the scheme by then? Mannion has confidence in him. He said Lemon has been “constantly” meeting with wide receivers coach Aaron Moorehead and passing game coordinator Josh Grizzard. Mannion said Lemon has been “locked in” during walk-throughs. Lemon also shadowed his position on the field when watching from the sidelines.
“Mentally, he’s been super engaged,” Mannion said. “I don’t worry about that one bit with Makai. I know the work he’s been putting in. Injuries, unfortunately, they happen in football, but he’s been a total pro about his approach to rehab, his approach to the mental side of the game. Like I said, the unfortunate nature of football is sometimes you might miss some time, but he’s done everything in his power despite not having those physical reps to be ready for us to make an impact.”
Lemon totaled four reps in seven-on-seven drills and 16 plays during team drills Monday. He primarily lined up in the slot, but he often motioned out wide or across the field. The Eagles clearly envision him as a versatile piece. He was targeted twice in team drills. On the first, he motioned right to left before the snap and ran a slant against Cooper DeJean. Quarterback Jalen Hurts fired into the small throwing window, and the pass fell incomplete. On the second, Lemon lined up as the right slot, stepped inward as if to run block, then looped back into the short flats, where Hurts struck him on a play-action bootleg. Lemon turned upfield for what would have been extra yards in a game setting.
The bootleg play is notable for Philadelphia’s new style of play. The 5-foot-11, 192-pound Lemon will have to sell run blocks in an offensive system that requires some of its run and pass plays to look identical. On the previous play, Lemon engaged edge rusher Jalyx Hunt with full strength and no hesitation during a wide-zone run — and held his own. Hunt gave Lemon a low-five after the play.
“Whenever a receiver has to block one of us, you kind of get to test the type of person he is on the field,” Hunt said. “So, he didn’t shy away from it. He didn’t try to just get around me. He put hands on me and tried to really block me. I respect that. And that’s cool to see. ‘Cause his demeanor on the field is totally different than who he is. He’s a laid-back guy, but on the field, he’s like, just a different energy, a different monster type of thing. It was just cool seeing it.”
When told of Hunt’s words, Lemon said, “It’s a man’s game.”
He added, “You put the pads on for a reason. So, to get out there, get a little hit on him, that felt good. We both working on both sides of the ball.”
Lemon mostly worked in personnel groupings with Smith and Wicks. Lemon needs to draw defenses’ attention to fulfill his off-the-ball responsibilities in Mannion’s offense. He motioned left and opened up an RPO pass to tight end Dallas Goedert. He motioned outside Smith, ran a crosser and freed Smith’s pathway to the left pylon. (Hurts’ deep-ball attempt fell incomplete.) Only so much can be gleaned from one practice. But Lemon’s teammates felt like the rookie was already fitting in.
“He’s been fitting into the culture well,” cornerback Riq Woolen said. “He’s a young pro. He comes in, he works, he does everything he needs to do so he can come back out and be available on the field. All the receivers, they do a great job as well — making sure he’s doing the right thing. I’m excited to have him coming back to practice and stuff like that. It’s pretty cool to see him out there standing, because that’s something that everybody wants to see: him, healthy and having fun again.”

full_text:
Aaron Rodgers led the Pittsburgh Steelers to 10 wins and an AFC North title in 2025. Mark Alberti / Icon Sportswire via Getty Images
A quick glance at the AFC North oddsboard would suggest it’s either the Baltimore Ravens’ or Cincinnati Bengals’ to lose — but that’s also what the oddsboard indicated heading into last season, before the Pittsburgh Steelers emerged victorious.
Listed at +510 odds that give them around a 15 percent implied probability to win, major sportsbooks like DraftKings aren’t ruling the Steelers out, and neither is The Athletic’s predictive analyst Austin Mock. Let’s dive into how his model projects every AFC North team’s chances to win the division, make the playoffs and more.
It’s a long shot, but it’s entirely possible the Steelers could win the AFC North.
First, the roster is actually in pretty decent shape. It skews older, but there are still quality players on both sides of the ball. The offense has plenty of weapons with DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr. at wide receiver, Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington at tight end, and Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle at running back. The offensive line is in pretty good shape as well. And while the linebacker group is average, the secondary has a good foundation and the defensive line has enough depth and potential to be awesome.
Of course, I left out a pretty important position. Aaron Rodgers’ prime is well behind him, but his reunion with Mike McCarthy could spark something. I wouldn’t say McCarthy is an elite offensive mind, but he has the ability to raise the offensive floor in Pittsburgh. And when you give him this much talent, there is a chance the Steelers could be around average (or slightly above). Would that good enough to win the division? I’m not sure. But paired with what should be a top-10 defense, they’re certainly good enough to challenge the Ravens and Bengals.
Another angle to factor in is that Baltimore and Cincinnati have pretty low floors.
Lamar Jackson was banged up last season and never quite seemed right. What if that spills into this season? Then you look at the Ravens’ offensive line and all of its question marks. The 32-year-old Derrick Henry has to eventually slow down. And the defense couldn’t generate pressure without blitzing last year. I’m bullish on coach Jesse Minter, and the addition of Trey Hendrickson should help, but that doesn’t guarantee a top-10 defense.
The team I’m most worried about is the Bengals. We know the offense is going to be really good if it’s healthy. And the Bengals finally added to a poor defense by trading for defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence and adding pass rusher Boye Mafe in free agency. The Bengals were 14th in expected points added (EPA) per play on defense in the second half of last season, so I do believe they improve. But what if they don’t? And they’re still a well below average defense?
All of those possibilities are well within the range of outcomes, which gives me enough confidence to say the Steelers could defend their AFC North title. Is it likely? Probably not. But it’s possible.

title: 2026 NFL win total projections for all 32 teams: Experts react to our model The Seahawks are among the teams favored to win 10-plus games this season. Is that too high? Our writers share their analysis. The Athletic NFL Staff 1
summary:
Sam Darnold, Nick Sirianni, Patrick Mahomes and John Harbaugh are all facing high expectations in 2026. Will they match or exceed their team win projections? Illustration: Demetrius Robinson / The Athletic; photos: Scott Taetsch, Jamie Squire, Steph Chambers / Getty Images; Chris Carlson / Associated Press
Week 1 for the 2026 NFL season is looming. In just over two weeks, on Sept. 9, a Super Bowl rematch between the champion Seattle Seahawks and runner-up New England Patriots kicks things off.
D
full_text:
Sam Darnold, Nick Sirianni, Patrick Mahomes and John Harbaugh are all facing high expectations in 2026. Will they match or exceed their team win projections? Illustration: Demetrius Robinson / The Athletic; photos: Scott Taetsch, Jamie Squire, Steph Chambers / Getty Images; Chris Carlson / Associated Press
Week 1 for the 2026 NFL season is looming. In just over two weeks, on Sept. 9, a Super Bowl rematch between the champion Seattle Seahawks and runner-up New England Patriots kicks things off.
Does either team have what it takes to return to the big game at Los Angeles’ SoFi Stadium on Feb. 14?
Regular-season team win projections from The Athletic ’s Austin Mock say they both have a chance. Mock’s model, which calculates an expected win total for every team, predicts the Seahawks to earn 10.8 wins in 2026 and the Patriots 10.3. Do our NFL beat writers think the projections for those teams are too high, too low or just right?
Read below for analysis of all 32 NFL teams and check out Mock’s full NFC and AFC projections as well.
Projected wins: 4.4 Verdict: Just right
Here’s the thing: The Cardinals should be more competitive than people expect. This team — with Trey McBride, Jeremiyah Love, Michael Wilson and Marvin Harrison Jr. — has offensive potential. QB Jacoby Brissett has been solid. First-year coach Mike LaFleur has been impressive. It’s just … everything else. Will the line — which has already lost rookie guard Chase Bisontis with a knee injury — hold up? Can the defense stop anybody? If everything goes right, six wins, even with a difficult schedule, would not be shocking. But that’s probably wishful thinking. — Doug Haller
Projected wins: 7.1 Verdict: Too high
It’s been a tough summer for the Falcons. One quarterback, Michael Penix Jr., was only cleared for full practice availability this week. The other quarterback, Tua Tagovailoa, has not looked great. Last year’s No. 15 pick, edge Jalon Walker, was lost for the season due to an ACL tear. Last year’s No. 26 pick, edge rusher James Pearce Jr., was suspended for the first eight games after violating the personal conduct policy. There are new sheriffs in town — president of football Matt Ryan, general manager Ian Cunningham and head coach Kevin Stefanski — but it’s going to take them a while to clean up these streets. — Josh Kendall
Projected wins: 10.9 Verdict: Just right
There’s a lot of volatility with the Ravens this year because of the new coaching staff. However, this we do know: Jesse Minter has had a really good defense just about everywhere he’s been and Lamar Jackson has been the league MVP in the first year of his last two offensive coordinators. The Ravens, at least now, are pretty healthy and have a forgiving schedule to start the season. A number of factors point to a Baltimore bounce-back. — Jeff Zrebiec
Projected wins: 10.7 Verdict: Just right
There is one simple and undeniable fact in Buffalo: As long as quarterback Josh Allen is healthy enough to play for the entire season — which he has every year since 2019 — it’s hard to envision the wheels totally falling off. The difference this year is there are a lot more variables. By firing Sean McDermott and promoting Joe Brady to head coach, the Bills believe they have raised their ceiling. But with a rookie head coach figuring it out on the fly, the floor may be much lower. They have a brand-new defensive scheme and a first-time NFL defensive coordinator in Jim Leonhard, another variable. That’s why 10.7 wins feels on the nose, as you could easily make the argument for slightly higher or lower. — Joe Buscaglia
Projected wins: 6.7 Verdict: Too low
I picked the Panthers to go 9-8 when schedules were released in May. But since then they’ve lost outside linebacker Nic Scourton for the season and right tackle Taylor Moton for a chunk of it, meaning the Panthers will enter Week 1 with new starters at both tackle spots, including rookie Monroe Freeling. That said, the defense will be better with the additions of Jaelan Phillips and Devin Lloyd and the Panthers play in the NFC South. So while 6.7 might be a tad low, there’s a real chance an eight-win team claims the division again. — Joseph Person
Projected wins: 9.6 Verdict: Just right
Injuries in camp may have tempered fans from making Super Bowl plans, with safety Coby Bryant out four to six months and the Bears still lacking clarity on nickel corner Kyler Gordon. They are probably another playoff appearance away from being in the upper echelon of Super Bowl contenders. The Ben Johnson-Caleb Williams duo with this offensive line and skill players has raised the floor in Chicago. Winning fewer than eight games seems unlikely. The defensive questions — from health to pass rush — lower the ceiling, though. — Kevin Fishbain
Projected wins: 10.3 Verdict: Too low
The Bengals are currently favored in 15 of 17 games. In the last 16 games Joe Burrow started as a favorite, the Bengals are 13-3. Their defense looks dramatically more reliable with quality veterans now plastered across the roster. The hedge here is on Burrow’s health and that’s always a notable variable. They also paid $6 million to Joe Flacco to mitigate it. It’s hard to imagine a full season of Burrow complemented by a steady defense falling below 11 wins. — Paul Dehner Jr.
Projected wins: 5.3 Verdict: Too high
For the Browns, 2026 is all about continuing to develop and evaluate a talented young corps. The quarterback play will almost certainly be dreadful, and the brand-new offensive line will need time to catch up. There’s little proven depth at any spot and six of the first nine games are on the road. The defense is still strong, but the focus is rightly on the future and the real goal should be a top-three draft pick. — Zac Jackson
Projected wins: 9.2 Verdict: Just right
If Dallas stays healthy, this should be a 10-win team competing for an NFC East title with the Philadelphia Eagles. The offense is loaded and the defense is showing signs that it could be significantly better in Christian Parker’s first season as defensive coordinator. But the offense would take a notable step back if franchise QB Dak Prescott or leading rusher Javonte Williams suffered a significant injury. That group probably has to be elite for Dallas to top the nine-win mark. — Jon Machota
Projected wins: 9.1 Verdict: Too low
The Broncos aren’t going 11-2 in one-score games like they did last season. History says regression in close games is coming, making it hard to envision them winning 14 games again. But the Broncos may be even deeper defensively than the units that led the NFL in sacks in each of the past two seasons. Offensively, they added Jaylen Waddle to bring a new element to the passing game, and new play-caller Davis Webb should help Bo Nix take a step forward in Year 3. There is too much talent on this well-coached roster to see Denver losing eight times this season. — Nick Kosmider
Projected wins: 10.2 Verdict: Just right
The Lions should greatly benefit from a schedule that ranks as the fourth easiest in the league, per Mock’s model. While there are major questions in the secondary and the offense will be without starting center Cade Mays until October, the Lions believe they’re better equipped to handle unexpected challenges this year. They have a new offensive coordinator in Drew Petzing, a younger and more athletic offensive line, a deeper defensive line rotation and return one of the league’s most talented rosters. Detroit’s projected win total of 10.2 wins is tied for the fourth-most in the NFC and leads the NFC North. Some things need to come together, and this division is one of the most competitive in football, but it’s certainly on the table for this group. — Colton Pouncy
Projected wins: 9.7 Verdict: Just right
Until the Packers’ group of unproven edge rushers proves me wrong, I don’t think it’ll be able to adequately withstand the absence of Micah Parsons — however long that may be. Can Jordan Love will this team to a couple…

title: Key Cardinals Missing From Monday Practice
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals returned to Tempe for their first and only home practice of the week before packing their bags for a trip to Green Bay.
Missing were some notable names including James Conner, Jeremiyah Love, Isaiah Adams and Isaac Seumalo today.
It's plausible most, if not all, were simply veteran rest days — though the team has a scheduled travel day tomorrow before their joint practice with the Packers.
Arizona, with their starting two offensive guards out of the lineup, rolled out Hayden Conner and Jon Gaines with their offensive line.
I do not see Isaiah Adams or Isaac Seumalo here at Cardinals practice. Jon Gaines was at right guard while Hayden Conner was at left guard with the first team offense. No James Conner or Jeremiyah Love here. pic.twitter.com/SU7VnUbHDP
Conner has been a hit-and-miss participant in practice lately, as the veteran running back is either looking to preserve his health for the regular season or is still managing a foot/ankle injury suffered in Week 3 of last season.
Previously speaking with reporters, head coach Mike LaFleur says Conner has earned the right to decide if he'll play in preseason — which hasn't been the case thus far. Green Bay is Arizona's final exhibition matchup ahead of the regular season.
Trey Benson was also not present — he was actually waived today. You can read more about that here .
Love continues to rest from a reported high ankle sprain suffered two games ago in Las Vegas, one that hasn't seen him practice in just under two weeks.
"He's doing well, progressing well, and kind of in the next phase of it," LaFleur said of Love today. He also added Love wouldn't be practicing, which isn't a surprise.
Seumalo has sometimes gotten veteran rest days in camp, so his absence isn't completely surprising. The free agent signing has been a consistent presence in prior stops at Philadelphia and Pittsburgh, so Arizona likely wants to keep him fresh and ready for their season opener.
Adams' absence is likely the most eye-opening, as the third-year guard isn't quite there in terms of earning those days off — especially with this being his first year as a full-time starter with inconsistent play in the prior two seasons.
Star pass rusher Josh Sweat did indeed return today from the PUP list — you can check that out here .
The Cardinals are unlikely to play their starters in Friday's preseason battle in Green Bay, mostly thanks to Wednesday's joint practice against the Packers. With Arizona traveling on Tuesday, we likely won't find out if any of the absences are serious until later in the week.

title: 3 Big Reasons Why the Cardinals Finally Gave Up on Trey Benson
full_text:
ARIZONA — They finally did it.
It was a day many saw coming in the Arizona Cardinals' facility as running back Trey Benson was officially waived/injured by the team in a flurry of roster moves announced Monday that also included Josh Sweat's return.
Benson, entering his third season, has mostly been sidelined due to a meniscus injury suffered last season. He was thought to be recovered entering training camp, though that clearly wasn't the case.
Now, the Day 2 pick moves on elsewhere while the Cardinals officially wipe their hands clean of the Florida State product.
X brutally honest takeaways from the move:
The Cardinals saw Benson exit with his knee injury in Week 4 of last season and he hasn't quite been the same since. Initially Arizona opened his practice window after he made a recovery from knee surgery to return late in 2025 before ultimately placing him on season-ending injured reserve.
After months of rehab, Benson was expected to return to training camp fresh and ready to fight for a roster spot. Benson initially participated in individual drills, though when he was finally upgraded to team activities, Benson's knee couldn't cooperate after suffering a "flare-up" with preseason play practically eliminated.
Benson, towards the end of his tenure, wasn't spotted practicing with the Cardinals — and it's a shame he hasn't been healthy for nearly a full year now.
Benson needed to have a strong camp/preseason to make the roster, though Bam Knight's emergence might have just been the difference between Benson hitting PUP/IR and him flat-out being waived like he was today.
One question the Cardinals find themselves heavily debating is how many running backs they'll ultimately keep on the final roster — and if that number is indeed four, Knight clearly has that final spot taken.
That's partly due to simply his availability, though Knight also emerged as a special teams contributor and strong rotational running back when called upon.
Perhaps if the Cardinals didn't have an obvious alternative, more time/patience would have been bought for Benson. However, Knight's performance made the decision easy for Arizona.
The Cardinals would have desperately loved to get something in return for Benson before ultimately cutting him, though the trade market around him was practically non-existent for a few reasons.
It's tough to get something of value when teams are anticipating getting Benson available on the waiver wire. Why give up draft capital if you could possibly get him for free?
His injury also muddied those waters. Potential inquiring teams probably wanted to see Benson healthy and on the field before making a move, though his flare-up ultimately may have cost the Cardinals.
It's not as if Benson's prior body of work was enough to warrant a return, either. Besides a handful of big runs, he was largely inconsistent as an NFL running back.
Perhaps that can change elsewhere, though Benson's time in the desert was clearly done.

title: Josh Sweat Returns to Cardinals: 3 Things It Really Means
full_text:
ARIZONA — Arizona Cardinals practices are about to get a lot more sweaty.
The Cardinals activated outside linebacker Josh Sweat from the Physically Unable to Perform list today in a swarm of moves that also featured the release of running back Trey Benson.
Sweat, for the first time in all of 2026, hit the practice field shortly after the news was announced.
Josh Sweat. In the flesh. pic.twitter.com/4p0kshYcDc
Sweat didn't participate in any previous activities such as OTAs, minicamp or training camp at State Farm Stadium. As a result of his absence, the Cardinals' room of outside linebackers was lacking their clear and obvious leader.
Names such as Zaven Collins, Baron Browning, Jordan Burch and BJ Ojulari couldn't collectively impact the passer in camp or preseason play thus far. Sweat, who paced the Cardinals with 12 sacks last season, now arrives back to the desert to build off a strong first outing.
If the Cardinals' defense will be anything this season, Sweat's presence wasn't optional — it was mandatory. Now, he's back in the mix, and Arizona's defense can move forward.
Sweat was spotted wearing a brace on his left leg in the practice video, which is something he's known to do — so that wasn't surprising given his history. There's been reports he has a degenerative knee issue and the Cardinals have been taking their time and protecting Sweat by placing him on the PUP list at the beginning of camp.
Arizona has consistently insisted Sweat would be ready ahead of the regular season, and now that's turned out to be true ahead of their final preseason game. Sweat now has three weeks to ramp up ahead of their regular season opener.
So long as Sweat can produce, all of the mystery and headlines around the Cardinals this summer will have been worth it. However, the organization clearly has been managing his knee injury and preserving him until the time was right.
Sweat reportedly requested a trade earlier in the offseason after the Cardinals fired Jonathan Gannon, and teams reportedly were inquiring on Sweat's availability earlier in the summer. Arizona, who didn't add any outside talent to their pass rush room, were wise to say no.
While the Cardinals weren't looking to offload Sweat now, that line of thinking could very well change later in the regular season if Arizona is far behind in the standings and Sweat's had enough.
Truth be told, it didn't make sense for the Cardinals to trade their only edge rusher. However, the dynamic could shift if they're clearly not going to compete this season and Sweat wants a fresh start elsewhere.
Arizona, who would be looking towards 2027 by the trade deadline, could likely get Day 2 compensation from a needy team looking to polish their Super Bowl push.

title: Carson Beck, Jeremiyah Love Lead Key Cardinals Injury Updates Before Packers Trip
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals have just one day of practice in Tempe before packing their bags and traveling across the country to take on the Green Bay Packers later this week.
The game isn't until Friday, though Arizona is set for a joint practice on Wednesday with the Packers.
During his Monday press conference, LaFleur divluged some key injury information on a handful of Cardinals players:
Beck suffered a rib injury in the team's Hall of Fame Game to begin preseason activities and practiced all week before being a late scratch against the Las Vegas Raiders. Beck did not throw in the ramp-up last week to hosting the Dallas Cowboys, where he also didn't play in the game.
LaFleur said Beck would have a throwing session after their final practice of the week, and today we got an update on Beck:
"Good with the throwing session. Still TBD in terms of what this Friday will look like," said LaFleur.
When asked if this would stall Beck's progress, LaFleur offered:
"It's easy to magnify the quarterback position and the rookie and all that kind of stuff, but yeah, you get better at football by practicing and playing football. So when you're not out there, it's hard to get better, right? So he's missed some days, but that's no different than the nose guard," he said.
"That's no different than the receiver. That's no different than the left tackle, particularly for the younger guys. So it is what it is. Injuries are part of this thing, and you know he's a tough dude. Like I said, he battled through it for three or four practices before the discomfort became so real that it just wasn't worth it to [play] because it wasn't going to improve until we gave him a little bit of time."
It might be a stretch to see Beck play on Friday, though anything is possible.
Love suffered an ankle injury in Las Vegas which was later reported to be a high ankle sprain. He did not practice at all this past week while not playing vs. Dallas, and that seems to be a similar fate for the week in Green Bay.
"He's doing well, progressing well, and kind of in the next phase of it," LaFleur said on Love.
"He will not be on the field doing any sort of practice or anything like that right now."
Love, the team's third overall pick, is also unlikely to play against the Packers on Friday as the team looks to put a bow on preseason action.
Taylor-Demerson went down on Saturday night after colliding with a Cowboys player and exited with a ribs injury. The hit drew a personal foul penalty for his hit on Zack Kuntz.
"He's got a little bit of a rib issue too. I mean, he hit him pretty good right there. So just kind of talked about in our team meeting about what's legal, what's not legal, stuff like that, in the targets and all that kind of stuff. But he'll be I guess you could say more day-to-day, and we'll kind of evaluate it every single day," said LaFleur.
Benson hasn't practiced with the Cardinals recently, and during training camp he was mostly relegated to individual drills as his recovery from a meniscus injury wages on.
"We're just taking it one day at a time with Trey right now. Truly, that's all I got for you with that," said LaFleur.
When asked if Benson (who is on the roster bubble ) was a candidate to begin the year on injured reserve, LaFleur said:
"We'll probably have a better understanding of that, I would say, after we get out of this game."
Gillikin provided a rare pre-game injury update for Cardinals fans while warming up against Dallas, one that saw him ultimately ruled out with a groin injury.
"He's good. We're going to keep him out this week, but we're not worried about anything long-term. I mean, there's no point in [having him] punt in this week," LaFleur said.
Kicker Chad Ryland took over punting duties last week, and it appears that will again be the case in Green Bay.

title: 3 Recent Cardinals Draft Picks Trending Toward the Roster Bubble
full_text:
ARIZONA — We're less than a week away from the Arizona Cardinals trimming down their final active roster to 53 players, and there's a few names that might just be on the verge of being dropped.
Arizona, under the first-year watch of head coach Mike LaFleur, will be forced to make some awfully tough decisions in terms of who stays and who goes. The Cardinals are hoping their early start in training camp and fourth preseason game (compared to the typical three teams have) will give them enough information on players.
It's never easy, and during this time of year, talented players always fall through the cracks. The Cardinals could see a handful of veterans depart:
Benson, a third-year running back, very likely finds himself on the outside looking in. Benson suffered a meniscus injury last season and already had his back against the wall entering training camp.
Benson needed to perform well, though he wasn't even healthy enough to take part in majority of team activities. As a result, Bam Knight has taken over RB4 duties and if Arizona does indeed decide to keep four running backs, Knight's the guy.
At this point, Benson appears very likely to either be cut, traded or perhaps even placed on PUP — which would require him to miss at least the first four games.
Regardless, Benson's time very much appears to be winding down in the desert.
Ojulari finds himself slipping down the depth chart not due to injury like Benson, but rather inability to fully bounce back from a prior knee injury suffered ahead of the 2024 season.
Since, Ojulari's been fighting to not only get back on the field but also replicate the success he had towards the end of his rookie season. That hasn't happened, and Ojulari has gotten deep run into every preseason matchup with little production to pair against backups.
The rise of Eku Leota is notable in the outside linebacker's room, and Ojulari's window of opportunity to really make noise is closing. The Cardinals running Ojulari deep into games is telling of how they view him.
Clark's in a deep cornerback room that is fighting for roster spots, and somebody will likely be left out. Clark brings a mix of versatility and prior starting experience, though Garrett Williams' recent arrival back from PUP does give Arizona back perhaps their most versatile chess piece.
With Sean Murphy-Bunting recently making the switch to the slot, the Cardinals are plenty stacked at every position both inside and out, which doesn't bode well for Clark with all of Will Johnson, Denzel Burke, Max Melton and Starling Thomas also battling for playing time.
The cornerback room is so deep, this could practically be anybody. However, Clark loses out to the number's game here.

title: Cardinals Made Telling Decision on Bam Knight’s Roster Chances
full_text:
ARIZONA — One of the Arizona Cardinals' more intriguing roster battles may have been solved over the weekend by a ball-carrier who didn't even play.
As the Cardinals work their way into final roster cuts , the organization has a few difficult conversations approaching. Spots such as running back, receiver, defensive line and cornerback carry the most weight in those conversations.
There's still one preseason game to be played, though Bam Knight's absence against the Dallas Cowboys over the weekend was more than telling. In a game where the Cardinals essentially sat their starters, Arizona opted not to dress Knight — who is battling for RB4 duties.
"‘Bam’ (has) played in this league quite a long time. I mean I had him in New York. It's like I've told you guys with (running) backs—it's hard to evaluate in practice. Well ‘Bam’ – it's not hard to evaluate ‘Bam.’ I think you guys saw that in the first game when we were in Canton, and even last year knowing his running style," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said after the game .
"(We) just wanted to make sure that we were taking care of him at this point and kind of where we're at in the running back room.”
The Cardinals have established names in Jeremiyah Love, Tyler Allgeier and James Conner already in the mix. Some would believe that's enough for Arizona, though the probability of carrying a fourth running back lurks.
Knight was set to battle with Trey Benson this preseason, though Benson has largely been unavailable for 11 v 11 drills due to his knee injury. That's set the table for Knight to impress, and that's exactly what he's done thus far.
"The depth in that room is amazing," Cardinals offensive coordinator Nathaniel Hackett said of Arizona's running backs during camp.
"I mean, some veteran guys that I have so much respect for, a young guy that's still a rookie, and even my experience with Bam in the past, everybody's been doing such a good job."
What could really push Knight's chances of making the roster over the top would be his ability to contribute to special teams, especially after ace player Joey Blount was lost for the season due to injury.
Knight likely won't get many opportunities to prove himself offensively — not with a deep room – though wearing multiple hats is the best way to ensure you're capable of making the final roster.
Nothing is set in stone, but it's tough not to feel strong about Arizona's running back room.

title: Projecting the Cardinals' Week 1 Starting Lineup Right Now
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals have one preseason game standing in the way between them and the regular season.
By this time next week, Arizona's preseason will have settled and the roster will have been trimmed to 53 players. From there, head coach Mike LaFleur will have to decide on his starting lineup.
Right now, here's what that looks like:
QB: Jacoby Brissett RB: Jeremiyah Love/Tyler Allgeier WR: Marvin Harrison Jr. WR: Michael Wilson SLOT: Kendrick Bourne TE: Trey McBride LT: Paris Johnson Jr. LG: Isaac Seumalo C: Hjalte Froholdt RG: Isaiah Adams RT: Elijah Wilkinson
The offense, for the most part, feels fairly set in terms of starters.
There's no doubting Brissett will be the Week 1 starter. As of now, he's best suited to run the Cardinals' offense and his $15 million guaranteed insists he'll have to lose starting duties later in the season. The likes of Gardner Minshew and Carson Beck will have to wait.
The running back room has seperated itself into different tiers, the first includes Love and Allgeier as a 1A/1B tandem. Both backs will be used, and while Love will likely have more touches than his counterpart, there's still going to be instances where Allgeier will get the nod on the first snap. It will all depend on package and personnel, so we wouldn't suggested diving too deep into who carries the starting label.
Receiver depth has been firmly established for the Cardinals, with Harrison and Wilson operating as boundary receivers while Bourne will mold into more of the slot guy. These roles, while concrete in terms of depth chart, aren't quite settled in terms of actual placement on the field. LaFleur will utilize his wideouts across different spots depending on the goal of the play.
Trey McBride. That's the tight end analysis.
Starters along the offensive line are fairly set, as right guard was essentially the only spot where a job was potentially up for grabs. However, after Chase Bisontis' injury, the Cardinals' starting right guard spot appears to be solely for Adams. All other four spots have been set for months now.
DL: Darius Robinson DL: Walter Nolen III DL: Roy Lopez OLB: Josh Sweat OLB: Zaven Collins ILB: Mack Wilson Sr. ILB: Jack Gibbens/Cody Simon CB: Will Johnson SLOT: Garrett Williams CB: Denzel Burke S: Budda Baker S: Andrew Wingard
The Cardinals' defensive line rotates heavily, so similar to the running back spot, we wouldn't put too much stock into who is a "starter" though Nolen very obviously will be out there every week. Robinson's stock continues to fall while Lopez is at the top of a bullpen-style DL room.
The same, to certain extends, can be said about the outside linebacker's room. Josh Sweat – whenever healthy — is the obvious top edge rusher while Zaven Collins will most likely get starts due to his first-round status and ability to play the run, though Baron Browning is the team's top rotational guy for obvious pass-rushing scenarios.
Inside linebacker is manned by Mack Wilson Sr. and what will surely be a committee approach between Simon and Gibbens. Both have different skillsets that will be deployed by defensive coordinator Nick Rallis. Gibbens is more equipped to handle pass coverage duties.
Johnson is a solid starting cornerback, and the team's recent elevation of Williams from PUP gives them their starting slot defender back into the mix. The third spot is believed to be a close race with numerous guys, though Burke's prior experience starting last year gives him the edge at this point in time.
Baker is a cornerstone for the team, though perhaps one of the biggest storylines resides in the arrival of Wingard and his ability to claim the starting title from Dadrion Taylor-Demerson. Wingard has impressed everybody in the Cardinals' building since his arrival.

title: Cardinals Say Josh Sweat Could Practice This Week
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals' preseason is nearly over, though outside linebacker Josh Sweat's prep for the 2026 season could just be beginning.
Sweat hasn't practiced at all for the Cardinals in 2026. Not in voluntary team activities, mandatory minicamp or training camp. Sweat was placed on the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list at the beginning of camp and has not played in any of Arizona's three preseason games.
We're roughly three weeks away from Arizona's season opener in Los Angeles. There's hope Sweat will have plenty of practices under his belt — and when speaking with reporters after last night's preseason battle against Dallas, Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur was asked if Sweat could potentially return this week.
“This coming week? Yeah. Josh is doing good," LaFleur said.
“We want all these guys, whether they're injured, they got injured a week ago or obviously in Sweat's case just getting them out there for that first time. We want all those guys back.
"Like I always say with the guys that are edge rushers, they rush the quarterback. It's a little different than the rhythm and timing of a quarterback and (wide) receiver—I’m just being real about it. It's one thing with rhythm, timing and working in combination with an offensive line. It's another thing when you know you are in that stance on third down and you're finding your point.
"(There is) no doubt in my mind (that if) you want to get better at football, you have to be out there in football. There is a little difference in my opinion. Not everyone would agree with me on that.”
The Cardinals have one more preseason game this coming Friday against the Green Bay Packers, though Arizona will hold a joint practice beforehand with Green Bay and likely won't play their starters.
After this week, they'll have a week off before game week arrives for Week 1 against the Chargers.
Whether Sweat, who is protecting a knee injury, will be physically ready to handle a full workload during a game remains to be seen. The Cardinals insist he is working out on his own and in meetings, though it's plausible Sweat could be on a pitch count to begin the year. Arizona rotates their outside linebackers often anyways.
"Josh is making good progress. Josh is getting closer every day," Cardinals general manager Monti Ossenfort said back on Aug. 10. "I think Josh is going to be out there in due time to get ready for the season opener, and we're excited to get him out there and get him going."
The Cardinals have one day of practice on Monday before traveling to Green Bay on Tuesday.

title: Arizona Cardinals Injury Report Following Preseason Week 2 Loss vs Cowboys
full_text:

"(P) Blake Gillikin ended up having a groin (injury), he'll get an MRI tomorrow. ‘Rabbit’ (S Dadrion Taylor-Demerson) with ribs, (WR) Xavier Weaver with a ‘hammy’ (hamstring), (CB) Kei’Trel Clark ended up having a hip (injury), (S) Wydett Williams Jr. and (CB) Kalen King are both getting evaluated for concussions," he said to begin his post-game press conference.

"Obviously in the preseason, I didn't even ask him. If this were Week 1, ‘could you-’, you know, what does it matter?”
LaFleur is unsure if Taylor-Demerson's injury is serious after he went to the ground following a collision.
“I can't answer that right now. I don't think so, but I'll have a better understanding of that tomorrow and then when I'm with you guys in two days," he said. The Cardinals have an off day today before returning to work on Monday.
Weaver was in a yellow non-contact jersey earlier this week during practice while Clark, Williams and King all practiced fine before picking up their injuries.

title: 8 Winners and Losers From Cardinals' Ugly Loss to Cowboys
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals put another preseason game in the books, and it was one to forget.
The Dallas Cowboys marched into State Farm Stadium and easily handled the Cardinals in 34-13 fashion. The two sides mostly rested their starters as one more preseason game looms before final roster cuts arrive.
In spite of the loss, there were still some noticeable winners to pair with some forgettable performances from Saturday.
Eight winners/losers from the Cardinals' loss against Dallas:
Leota has climbed up the Cardinals' outside linebacker depth chart during training camp and very well could have earned himself a roster spot last night. Leota registered a sack with two tackles for a loss and five total tackles — second-highest on the team.
"I thought from my eyes—I have to go back and watch this tape obviously (but) I thought from my eyes (that) this was the most productive he was through the three preseason games," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said after the game .
Leota has been a consistent winner for the Cardinals in the last few weeks. Last night only drove that home further.
The Cardinals only played a select group of starters against Dallas with majority resting — so anybody who got some run last night, it wasn't exactly for good reason.
Robinson was in that mix, and it's a fairly glaring endorsement on how the Cardinals' coaching staff views him at this moment in time.
"You can get a lot done in practice, but sometimes the live bullets, not having a script and all that kind of stuff (helps players grow). There are a few guys on the defensive side that we want to get out there in that kind of heightened competitive environment and see what they can do. Not ruling out anything for next week either," LaFleur said on playing Robinson.
Robinson logged one tackle, and the former first-round pick has again yet to make an impact during live action football.
Perhaps one of last night's biggest winners was a player who didn't even suit up.
Knight did not play, as the Cardinals opted to rest their running back — a player who is on the bubble of making the team's final 53-man roster, and his nonparticipation is a great sign of him making the team.
"I think you guys saw that in the first game when we were in Canton, and even last year knowing his running style. (We) just wanted to make sure that we were taking care of him at this point and kind of where we're at in the running back room," LaFleur said when asked about Knight not playing.
Knight feels like a good bet to make the team.
The Cardinals have been begging for somebody in their outside linebacker room to step up, with hopes of Ojulari fully bouncing back from an injury suffered ahead of the 2024 season.
That's yet to happen, and Ojulari has been getting consistently heavy run during preseason games. The combination of extensive looks with minimal production against third-string players simply has not mixed well for Ojulari's chances of making the team – especially with Leota's rise.
Ojulari did have three tackles last night, though he's still unable to reach the quarterback.
The race for Arizona's final receiver spot has been highly competitive through camp and preseason with things mostly being a two-man sprint to the finish between Jalen Brooks and Ihmir Smith-Marsette.
Fehoko didn't leapfrog anybody, though his team-leading 42 receiving yards on two catches was indeed a bright spot for a Cardinals squad that didn't see much of that.
This catch by Simi Fehoko 🔥 DALvsAZ on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/mhgVNDjpUr
Fehoko's special teams prowess should also keep him heavily in the mix for a roster spot. On a night where somebody needed to step up, Fehoko certainly did.
It's only preseason, but Rallis is being picked apart by people online after another forgettable outing on the defensive side of the ball.
While a mix of starters played, mostly role players and backups took the field — and fans have simply not been happy with the overall defensive product, which has been copy-and-paste this entire preseason.
The Cardinals' defense was expected to be different after Jonathan Gannon was fired. Thus far, it's been anything but a polished product under Rallis' watch in either run or pass defense.
Sharar's chances of making the roster, thanks to his status as a late-round pick and depth in the inside linebacker's room, will mostly come on special teams and his ability to make an impact there.
Sharar, a specialist at Iowa with over 500 snaps in that phase, has proved to be a playmaker on special teams, and last night was no different after setting the tone on the opening kickoff.
karson sharar is a special teams DEMON 👀 pic.twitter.com/LbF4goVkOX
That's exactly how you make an NFL roster as a Day 3 pick.
The Cardinals, consistently, have had issues with pre-snap penalties this preseason. Officials told reporters they'd be calling games more tightly to prepare teams for the regular season, which is fine, though Arizona's mishaps are mostly happening before the ball is even snapped.
Last night, the Cardinals had eight penalties for 63 yards, and LaFleur clearly was not happy with the operation.
"It’s sometimes a lack of focus. Sometimes (it’s) just other guys being in there that haven't been put in these situations. There are no excuses for it," LaFleur said.
"You guys are going to talk about it more because I'm always going to talk about it. Obviously, you guys are going to be looking for it a little bit more too. I wasn't happy with how we did against Las Vegas. You look at the totality of it, most people would say we were pretty clean that game. Well, not to our standard. If we have one, that's one too many.”

title: Falcons Named Big Winners after Rebound vs. Colts, Penix Injury News
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons were fairly downtrodden after a poor showing to open the preseason against the Denver Broncos. However, after a productive pair of joint practices with the Indianapolis Colts, the mood changed dramatically after the Falcons reserves dominated their counterparts in Indianapolis.
Sure, there weren't a lot of starters playing for either side, but there were still reasons for Falcons fans to be excited watching their team on Saturday afternoon.
From special teams improvements to undrafted rookie Jack Strand putting on a show, the Falcons came home feeling good about themselves. NFL media took notice on Saturday, and CBS Sports' Garrett Podell and Zachary Pereles named the Falcons one of the big winners after preseason Week 2 .
"Preseason scores do not matter at all, but there might not have been a single team needing a good week more than the Falcons. Atlanta got walloped by Denver, 27-7 , last week, hours after the news came out that James Pearce Jr. was suspended eight games . Tua Tagovailoa looked awful, the defense looked awful, and the vibes were bad," wrote Podell and Pereles.
Winning cures all, and the Falcons didn't just win on Saturday; they showed off their newfound depth, dominating the Colts 34-6 in a game that wasn't really that close .
Podell and Pereles mentioned the game, but they also factored in the Michael Penix Jr. injury news when lauding the Falcons' positive vibes.
"The best news, however, came after the game: Kevin Stefanski said Penix has been cleared to return to 11-on-11 work after a lengthy rehabilitation from yet another torn ACL. Maybe Tagovailoa is already the de-facto starter since it's taken Penix a bit, but it's always nice to get positive injury updates," they wrote.
While Penix has been cleared for 11v11s in practice, he hasn't been cleared for contact. On Monday, head coach Kevin Stefanski wouldn't commit to Penix playing against the Dolphins on Friday in the team's final preseason game.
With an open week before the Falcons' season opener against the Pittsburgh Steelers on September 13th, it wouldn't be a surprise to see Penix held out from game action, giving him another two weeks to fully heal before the season. One or two series in Miami on Friday isn't going to make much of a difference for Penix in the grand scheme of things.
Penix not playing on Friday would not automatically make Tagovailoa the de facto starter.
The Dolphins are in full tank mode for the regular season, but they'll have plenty of guys fighting for jobs on Friday. Another convincing win in Miami would add positive momentum for a team in desperate need of some as they head into Stefanski's first season.

title: Michael Penix Jr. Still a Doubt as Stefanski Details Falcons' Plans vs. Dolphins
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons are entering one of the most important weeks of the preseason, and head coach Kevin Stefanski is making sure his team approaches it that way.
Stefanski announced Monday that the Falcons’ starters will play in Friday’s preseason game against the Miami Dolphins, giving Atlanta’s top players valuable game reps as the team continues preparing for the regular season.
But Friday’s game will be about much more than simply getting the starters on the field.
The Falcons have several important position battles still taking shape , and the final preseason game could provide the coaching staff with valuable information as roster decisions get closer.
Quarterback remains the biggest storyline.
For now, Tua Tagovailoa will likely get the start at quarterback as the Falcons determine whether Michael Penix Jr. will be ready to play. Penix was recently cleared to return to full 11-on-11 work, putting him back into the competition with Tagovailoa for the starting job.
Head coach Kevin Stefanski was non-committal at his press conference on Monday morning on whether or not Penix would see action against the Dolphins, but his return to full practice gives Atlanta another important evaluation opportunity this week.
Tagovailoa, meanwhile, can strengthen his case with another preseason performance.
The quarterback battle isn't the only competition worth watching.
Atlanta is also evaluating its running back room behind Bijan Robinson. With Trey Sermon placed on injured reserve, younger backs such as Nathan Carter and Cash Jones have increased opportunities to make the roster.
Tyler Goodson also made a strong impression with his performance against the Colts , giving the Falcons another player to consider in the crowded backfield.
There are also battles across the defense and special teams, with young players competing for roster spots and playing time. The Falcons will have to determine which players have done enough throughout training camp and the preseason to earn a spot on the initial 53-man roster due on Sunday afternoon .
That makes this week particularly important.
Stefanski said the Falcons will essentially treat the upcoming week as if they were preparing for a regular-season game.
"We'll treat this week like a regular-season schedule. We'll be into our regular-season work. Today (Monday) will be a Wednesday."
That mindset should give the Falcons a true dress rehearsal before the regular season begins.
The starters will get an opportunity to play together, while coaches will get another extended look at players fighting for roster spots.
Friday's game could ultimately be one of the final pieces of evidence the Falcons use when making some of their most difficult roster decisions.
For the players competing for jobs, that makes every snap important.
For the starters, it's an opportunity to build momentum heading into the regular season.
And for the coaching staff, it's one final chance to evaluate the roster before the decisions become much more permanent.

title: Updated Atlanta Falcons 53-Man Roster Prediction Before Final Preseason Game
full_text:
When new Atlanta Falcons general manager Ian Cunningham took over in January, he was faced with no first-round draft pick in the upcoming draft and limited salary cap space to improve the team.
With that in mind, Cunningham stated one of his main goals for the 2026 version of the Falcons was to raise the floor of the team. In essence, this means getting better depth and talent on the back end of the roster for a team that has been top-heavy the last several seasons.
After the Falcons' second-and-third-teamers went out and dominated the Indianapolis Colts on Saturday, it appears Cunningham's goal of improving the depth has been achieved.
In doing so, the Falcons have created much more competitive roster battles at nearly every position, making it harder to predict a 53-man roster. We've made some changes from our predictions at the start of camp , some forced due to injury, some based on merit.
After nearly a month of training camp and two preseason games, here's how we see it, including players on the bubble.
We had Strand on the roster before the start of camp, and he's done nothing but solidify his spot since. Penix was cleared for 11v11 this week, but he hasn't been cleared for full contact yet. It would be a surprise if he plays against the Dolphins on Friday.
Bubble In: Jack Strand Bubble Out: Cooper Rush
Tyler Goodson looks to have solidified his claim to the No. 3 running back spot over Nate Carter. We originally had Jones on the roster at wide receiver, but he's been getting more action at running back since camp started. That versatility of being able to play slot, running back, and special teams earns him a spot.
Bubble In: Cash Jones Bubble Out: Nate Carter
The first four names at wide receiver are written in Sharpie. Blair has been the best of the rest and should get the nod for the fifth wide receiver. The Falcons kept seven wide receivers last year, but they can probably get away with using several of the bubble players on the practice squad and elevating them as needed during the regular season.
Bubble In: Chris Blair Bubble Out: Dylan Drummond, Juice Wells, Vinny Anthony, Beaux Collins
The first three are pretty straightforward. Atlanta could decide to take a fourth tight end, but they could also treat the position like wide receiver and stack several on the practice squad. Joshua Simon, Jack Velling, and Nick Muse have all played well at times during the preseason, and there's little risk they'd be picked up on waivers if cut.
Bubble In: None Bubble Out: Joshua Simon
Kyle Hinton and Michael Jerrell look safe as primary backups at several positions. Wanya Morris was set to be the swing tackle, but Jerrell has occupied that spot, leaving Morris vulnerable to a cut. Levin appears to be ahead of undrafted free agent James Brockermeyer. There's little chance seventh-round pick Ethan Onianwa would be claimed if cut, so the Falcons can re-sign him to the practice squad.
Bubble In: Corey Levin, Wanya Morris Bubble Out: Ethan Onianwa, James Brockermeyer
The first five names on this list look safe. The Falcons only kept five defensive linemen last year, and it's doubtful they make that mistake again. Carlos Allen Jr. has been a menace the last few weeks at camp, and he deserves a spot. Chris Williams got $2 million in free agency, and it's hard not to see him on the roster, but it's a possibility.
Bubble In: Carlos Allen Jr. Bubble Out: Chris Williams
The edge room has a whole new look. None of the names above have played a down for the Falcons. It's a bigger group with the addition of Thomas, Smith, and Sample. Thomas has the ability to put his hand down on the defensive line, while Ebukam and Smith are the best pure pass rushers.
This unit lacks the burst of last year, with Jalon Walker and James Pearce Jr. missing half the season, but they'll be better against the run.
Keshawn Banks has looked better than Ojulari in preseason games, but it might be enough to get him on the 53. Trice has missed the last two seasons with injury, and he's missed the last two weeks with another undisclosed ailment. If he's not back on the field soon, he could be a PUP candidate to start the year.
Bubble In: Azeez Ojulari, Bralen Trice Bubble Out: Keshawn Banks
The choices on defense are considerably harder this year, but linebacker is the one position that's relatively easy. Harris is penciled in as a starter next to Deablo, but he's getting pushed hard by Daniels. Perkins will find his snaps in reserve and on special teams. The only wrench in the works would be if the Falcons decide to keep five linebackers.
Bubble In: None Bubble Out: Channing Tindall
Bates and Watts form arguably the best safety tandem in the NFL. Hellams has done enough to warrant a backup and special-teams role, and Brown has nickel/safety versatility that should make him safe.
Bubble In: DeMarcco Hellams, Sydney Brown Bubble Out: Natrone Brooks, Jammie Robinson
Cornerback might be the hardest position to project for the Falcons, and that's not necessarily a good thing. Atlanta spent a second-round pick on Avieon Terrell, but the room is still thin. Holmes is one of several players getting snaps with the first team at nickel, so he's likely safe.
After that, Phillips and Bryant could be displaced by C.J. Henderson and/or Malcolm DeWalt IV. A.J. Woods has also taken reps with the first team at nickel, but he could be on the outside looking in.
This one is easy. Folk and Bailey have looked like massive upgrades at kicker and punter, respectively. Folk banged through a pair of 50-yard field goals against the Colts, and Bailey hit a 58-yard punt inside the five. If Folk was the kicker on this team the last two seasons, the Falcons might have made the playoffs both years.

title: Falcons Stock Up, Stock Down Heading Into Final Week of Preseason
full_text:
FLOWERY BRANCH – The Atlanta Falcons got back on track Saturday with a dominant 34-6 win over the Indianapolis Colts . This effort will help build confidence heading into the final week of preseason action, but wins and losses don't matter most this time of year.
Dozens of players are fighting for roster spots, and the individual performances throughout the summer are constantly being evaluated. Days like Saturday serve as checkpoints, and Friday night is the final one before Sunday's roster cuts.
As we head into the final full week of training camp, Falcons OnSI took a look at some of the risers and fallers.
The unquestioned winner of Saturday’s game in Indianapolis is undrafted free agent quarterback Jack Strand . He came out at the end of the first half and immediately led the first of his three scoring drives of the day.
Strand ultimately finished 12-of-17 for 212 yards and two total touchdowns, leaving social media buzzing for the upstart rookie. He is battling with the 32-year-old Cooper Rush, who also had a strong performance on Friday (10-of-11 for 86 yards) after his first-week struggles, and that competition is still up in the air. The rookie has much more upside, with elite size (6-foot-5, 240 pounds) and arm strength, but NFL coaches value experience.
Strand still has a lot to learn, but he is forcing the issue in Flowery Branch with performances like this.
Catching his touchdown was running back/wide receiver Cash Jones. The former Georgia Bulldogs third-down back has shown his value as a dual-threat weapon this summer, leading the Falcons on Friday with four catches for 62 yards and the score, while adding 41 yards on seven carries (5.6 yards per carry).
Jones’ path to making the roster is a difficult one, with the three rock-solid running backs ahead of him on the depth chart. He has shown additional value on special teams, but will that be enough to lock down a spot for himself?
Finally, defensive lineman Carlos Allen Jr. has made a name for himself. He had a tackle for loss and created some pressure in the Colts' passing attack that helped the Falcons get off the field. The majority of his work came in the first half, a potentially good sign for his status on the depth chart.
But like Jones, Allen will need to navigate through several veterans in his position group. At this point, he feels like a good bet to make the practice squad, which is still a net positive for a rookie UDFA.
The veteran quarterback was the perceived front-runner for the Falcons’ quarterback job all summer, and for good reason. Tagovailoa had every advantage possible, with Michael Penix Jr. still rehabbing from a torn ACL, but his struggles have left the door wide open.
Furthermore, Penix was cleared to return to practice on Saturday , and now Tagovailoa feels like he is scrambling to maintain his place in this competition. The Falcons have less than three weeks before they travel to Pittsburgh in Week 1, and they need to name a starter before too much longer.
Stefanski does not appear to be in a hurry to make that decision, but it would be surprising if one is not named after this week. If Penix can come in strong, then the incumbent starter could hold onto his job.
Tyler Goodson returned to his former team and appeared to lock down the third running back role in the process. His 49-yard touchdown run in the first half was the highlight of the game, and several teammates celebrated with him in the end zone after he scored.
He finished his day with 59 yards (9.83 yards per carry) on six carries, while Nathan Carter had 42 yards (2.47 yards per carry) on 17 carries. Goodson’s speed and versatility will be useful assets for the Falcons’ special teams unit, and he appears to be stamped in as the reserve behind Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson Jr.
The Falcons’ free-agency acquisition is not considered a bubble player, but his place as the surefire starting linebacker alongside Divine Deablo has taken a hit as of late. The emergence of rookies Kendal Daniels and Harold Perkins Jr. has relegated him to the background a bit.
Daniels’ emergence, in particular, has been notable. He has worn the green dot during practices in Deablo's absence, indicating the staff’s growing comfort with him alongside the veteran.
Furthermore, Harris played well into the game on Friday, which isn't always the best sign for a player. He will still be expected to have a role on this defense, but his starting job could be in jeopardy.

title: Jack Strand Shines at QB for Atlanta Falcons Despite Limited Practice
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons ' biggest questions this season revolve around the quarterback position. Who will be the starter? Can Tua Tagovailoa or Michael Penix Jr. stay healthy for an entire season? Can either of them be the long-term answer for the Falcons after struggling in 2025?
While those questions remain unanswered, the Falcons find themselves near the bottom of any kind of power rankings, even future power rankings that try to look four seasons down the road.
While the focus has been on Tagovailoa and Penix, the Falcons got an unlikely boost from undrafted free agent Jack Strand in Saturday's convincing 34-6 win over the Indianapolis Colts.
The Falcons spent last week in Indianapolis and had a pair of joint practices with the Colts that included the bulk of the first-team reps. With Tagovailoa and Penix splitting the opportunities, there was little work for Strand as he watched.
When he got his chance on Saturday against the Colts' second and third team, he shined. At 6'5 and 240 pounds with a strong arm and quick release, Strand has stood out since being signed by the Falcons out of Minnesota State University Moorhead (MSUM).
On Saturday, he kicked it up a notch.
Strand was 12 of 17 for 212 yards and a touchdown. He added another 16-yard rushing touchdown. At one point, Strand was 8/8 for 155 yards, a touchdown, and a perfect 158.3 passer rating.
. @AtlantaFalcons QB Jack Strand throws for 212 yards and scores 2 touchdowns in Preseason Week 2 🔥 pic.twitter.com/FVGq6WtkyV
Head coach Kevin Stefanski was impressed with not just Strand's performance, but his maturity in being able to learn and then thrive, despite being a spectator most of the week in practice.
"I think any quarterback gets great mental work when they're not out there," Stefanski said after the game on Saturday. "Jack didn't have a ton of reps in those joint practices, but he's getting every rep, both when he's watching it the first time and then when he's paying attention to the meeting room.
"He's getting that mental rep. So, he's somebody that can get better that way, which I think is a great attribute for young players, period. Certainly, at the quarterback position, I think you can apply a lot of those lessons learned. I saw that tonight from Jack.”
Having success against the Colts' reserves is a far cry from facing the Broncos' first-team defense in the Falcons' first preseason game, but Strand and the rest of the offense could only play who was put in front of them.
Atlanta outgained the Colts 461 yards to 164. They were 9 of 17 on third down compared to 1 of 11 for Indianapolis.
While Strand was the star of the show, the Falcons also got good play in the first half from Cooper Rush who was an efficient 10 of 11 passing for 86 yards.
“I thought the quarterback position, in total, both those guys made good decisions," Stefanski said. "I thought there were some unique looks that we got in the game that we really haven't seen a ton of, if you will, in the last week or so, and I thought they both saw it clearly. The ball went where the ball was supposed to go the majority of the time.”
The ball went into the end zone four times, and kicker Nick Folk added a pair of 50+ yard field goals for good measure.
Coaches often talk about complementary football, and the Falcons showed what that looked like on Saturday. Offense, defense, and special teams came together for a dominating win . Sure, it's just preseason, but there haven't been enough of those games in Atlanta in any season lately.
The Falcons only kept two quarterbacks last year on their initial 53-man roster , but at this point, it will be a shock if Strand isn't on the team after roster cutdowns next Sunday.

title: 3 Winners and 3 Losers From Falcons' Dominant Win Over Colts
full_text:
The Atlanta Falco ns needed a response after a disappointing preseason opener and delivered one Saturday.
Atlanta dominated the Indianapolis Colts 34-6, showing considerably more energy and physicality after spending the week in Indianapolis for two joint practices. The victory also provided another important opportunity for players competing for roster spots to make their final impressions before cut day arrives.
With several position battles still unsettled, here are three winners and three losers from Atlanta's preseason victory.
Goodson continues to make his case for a roster spot.
The running back was one of Atlanta's most explosive offensive players Saturday, breaking loose for a 49-yard touchdown and providing the type of big-play ability the Falcons have seen from him throughout training camp.
His performance is particularly important because Atlanta's running back room has become more competitive following Trey Sermon's placement on injured reserve.
Goodson has consistently shown the ability to create explosive plays, and Saturday was another reminder that he shouldn't be overlooked when Atlanta makes its final roster decisions.
The Falcons already know what they have in Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson Jr. The question is who will earn the next spot.
Goodson is making a strong argument that it should be him.
Strand may have been the biggest winner of the afternoon.
The undrafted rookie quarterback put together another impressive performance, completing 12 of 17 passes for 212 yards and a touchdown while also rushing for a 16-yard score. He also delivered several impressive throws downfield, including a 36-yard completion.
Strand's performance continues to make the QB3 competition much more interesting.
Cooper Rush entered camp with the experience advantage, but Strand has repeatedly shown poise and playmaking ability. He now has legitimate momentum heading into the final preseason game.
Atlanta's quarterback room could look very different depending on what happens over the next two weeks.
And Strand is making sure the Falcons have a difficult decision to make.
Daniels continues to be one of the most intriguing young players on Atlanta's roster.
The rookie linebacker has been making plays throughout training camp and the joint practices, and Saturday gave him another opportunity to show that his development is translating to game action.
Daniels' emergence is especially important because Atlanta has been evaluating several players at linebacker while dealing with injuries elsewhere in the group.
He is giving the coaching staff a reason to consider getting him on the field sooner rather than later.
For a young player trying to earn a role, Daniels has done exactly what he needed to do during the preseason: make himself difficult to ignore.
Ojulari needed to stand out Saturday. Instead, he was relatively quiet.
That doesn't mean Ojulari played poorly, but in the current state of Atlanta's edge-rusher room, simply being solid isn't necessarily enough. The Falcons need someone to emerge after losing Jalon Walker for the season with a torn ACL and facing an eight-game suspension for James Pearce Jr.
Ojulari was expected to be one of the players capable of helping fill that void.
Saturday presented another opportunity to make that case, and he didn't consistently create the kind of impact that would separate him from the rest of the group.
That matters because players such as Keshawn Banks, Cameron Sample, Bralen Trice and others are trying to take advantage of the opportunities created by Atlanta's depleted edge room.
The Falcons recently added veteran Za'Darius Smith, further increasing the competition for snaps and roster spots.
Ojulari has the talent to be an important piece of this defense.
But with Walker out and Pearce unavailable for the first eight games, Atlanta needs its edge rushers to show they can create pressure.
The door is wide open. Someone needs to walk through it.
Tagovailoa didn't play Saturday, but that doesn't mean the questions surrounding him disappeared.
If anything, the quarterback situation became more interesting.
Tagovailoa struggled in Atlanta's preseason opener and then had an uneven start during the Falcons' first joint practice against Indianapolis. He improved during the second practice, but the overall evaluation remains incomplete.
Meanwhile, Michael Penix Jr. continues working his way back from his knee injury.
Penix has now been cleared to return to 11 on 11 work and that will now add to the competition.
That creates a potentially fascinating QB1 situation.
Tagovailoa currently has the advantage because he's healthy and has been able to participate. But if Penix returns and performs well, the Falcons could suddenly have a much more serious decision on their hands.
Tagovailoa needed to take control of the job.
His recent performances haven't completely accomplished that.
The next time he takes the field, the pressure will be even greater.
Harris wasn't necessarily a loser because of something he did Saturday.
He was a loser because of what happened around him.
The Falcons' projected starters weren't slated to play against Indianapolis, but Harris entered the game in the second quarter. That is notable because Harris has been working with the starting defense and is currently projected to be one of Atlanta's starting linebackers.
If Harris were firmly established as the unquestioned starter, there wouldn't be much reason to see him in a preseason game when most of the projected starters were being held out.
Instead, the Falcons gave him additional evaluation time.
And that's because the linebacker room is becoming much more competitive.
Daniels has continued to make plays throughout camp, while Harold Perkins Jr. has also shown flashes of the athleticism that made him such an intriguing addition to the Falcons' defense.
Harris still has the inside track to start.
But the gap may not be as wide as it appeared when training camp began.
The Falcons have young linebackers pushing for opportunities, and Harris now has to continue proving that he deserves to remain at the top of that competition.
The Falcons now have one more preseason game before the real roster decisions begin.
That game against Miami will be an important opportunity for the coaching staff to finish evaluating the roster and determine which players have done enough to earn a spot.
For players such as Goodson, Strand and Daniels, Saturday helped their cases.
For players such as Ojulari and the other edge rushers, there is still work to be done.
And then there are the bigger questions surrounding the quarterback room, where Penix's potential return could add another layer to the QB1 competition while Strand continues to push for QB3.
Next week represents one of the final opportunities for players to put something on tape before cut day is upon the Falcons.
At this point in the preseason, every snap matters.
