title: Four New Additions to Buffalo Bills' Injury List Include Terrel Bernard, Jude Bowry
full_text:
The good news for the Buffalo Bills is they still have more than two full weeks to get healthy for the September 13 season opener on the road against the Houston Texans.
The bad news is four new injuries have apparently emerged, according to media on the scene tracking practice participation ( h/t Jay Skurski ) at One Bills Drive on Monday. Furthermore, six players remain sidelined with their absences  dating back at least one full week.
Inside linebacker Terrel Bernard, outside linebacker Javon Solomon, center Sedrick Van Pran-Granger and fourth-round rookie tackle Jude Bowry account for the four new additions.
While Bernard sat out with the other first-team veterans, Solomon (23), Van Pran-Granger (35) and Bowry (17) all played a significant number of snaps in the August 22 preseason road win over the Cleveland Browns.
Wide receivers Khalil Shakir and Keon Coleman, who have been banged up since playing in the August 15 preseason opener, were not seen practicing on Monday.
Running back Ty Johnson, center Connor McGovern, defensive lineman Ed Oliver and safety Chauncey Gardner-Johnson also missed the first session of the short week with the Bills' exhibition finale scheduled for Thursday, August 27.
Oliver is the only one of the four to have played in the preseason, logging 10 reps as a starter against the Carolina Panthers in the opener. He is currently out due to an undisclosed injury, although it could be related to the issue that kept him out of OTAs. The defensive tackle was present and walking around during Monday's stretch period.
Bowry, who started at right tackle, left the game early against the Browns, and he didn't return after a visit to the medical tent. He was seen wearing a walking boot on Monday inside the Bills' field house.
As for Solomon and Van Pran-Granger, who were both in the starting line-up on Saturday, their injuries are unknown, and the Bills don't have to routinely disclose information until the regular season begins.
It could just be a maintenance day for Bernard, who is apparently over the ankle problem that bothered him throughout 2025.
McGovern and Johnson have been out since the Return of the Blue & Red practice on August 8. Both players left the field that day with what appeared to be hamstring injuries.
With a four-to-six week recovery likely needed for acute strains, McGovern and Johnson may both enter September as questionable for the season opener. Notably, McGovern's backup , Lloyd Cushenberry, was held out of the last preseason game.
Shakir and Coleman are both dealing with lower-body issues, but neither appear likely to last for the long term.
Coleman, who was seen with a boot following the August 15 preseason appearance, seemingly tweaked his foot during the game.

title: Bills' Snap Counts vs. Browns Create Speculation for Final Roster Composition
full_text:
The end is near for the NFL Preseason, and there are a bevy of roster decisions awaiting for Buffalo Bills' brass .
The Bills played the second leg of their three-game preseason schedule on the road against the Cleveland Browns, and the August 22 player participation log offers multiple hints about what to expect on roster cutdown day.
Despite sitting all of the big names , Buffalo rolled to a 31-7 exhibition victory.
Here's what we learned from reviewing the player snap counts with an August 30 cutdown deadline looming.
Bills' Preseason Game 2 snap counts vs. Browns [via @NFL345 ] pic.twitter.com/cEA28y8fXE
The Bills' offense was first out on the field, and four first-team linemen — LT Dion Dawkins, C Connor McGovern, RG O'Cyrus Torrence, RT Spencer Brown — were inactive.
Of the four, only McGovern was unavailable due to injury. Even backup center Lloyd Cushenberry was held out, suggesting the veteran is highly likely to survive roster cutdown day .
Franchise quarterback Josh Allen, running back James Cook, wide receiver DJ Moore, wide receiver Keon Coleman, wide receiver Josh Palmer, tight end Dawson Knox and tight end Dalton Kincaid all watched from the sideline.
On defense, the six August 15 starters all registered DNPs against the Browns. That list includes edge rusher Bradley Chubb, edge rusher Greg Rousseau, defensive lineman Ed Oliver, nose tackle Deone Walker, inside linebacker Terrel Bernard and cornerback Christian Benford.
First-team safeties Cole Bishop and Chauncey Gardner-Johnson both missed their second straight preseason game while fighting what are believe to be minor injuries.
Seventh-round rookie offensive guard Armaj Reed-Adams was the lone Bills' player to play 100 percent of snaps on either side of the ball in Cleveland. With a lot of experienced interior line depth, Buffalo may be showcasing the seventh-rounder for a potential cutdown day trade .
Meanwhile, undrafted rookie cornerback Kani Walker, who has been trending toward making the cut , received the most playing time in defense. Walker, who was listed as a second-teamer on the unofficial depth chart, logged 47 of a possible 56 reps.
Seventh-round rookie cornerback Toriano Pride was third behind Walker and Danna with 30 defensive reps.
Veteran safeties Damar Hamlin and Geno Stone both started and earned 27 snaps apiece. The two men are seemingly competing for one available roster spot.
In what may be interpreted as a troubling sign for his survival chances, defensive tackle DeWayne Carter, a 2024 third-round draft pick , was playing deep into the second half alongside fourth-stringers. He took 29 of 56 possible reps.
The Bills are debating whether or not to keep a fullback on the roster, and Ben VanSumeren is making the decision difficult.
Buffalo deployed their lone fullback for 32 percent of the offensive snaps against Cleveland.
VanSumeren saw more special teams snaps (16) than any other player on the 90-man roster, which is a good sign for his chances to stick around.
The Bills have a veteran and a rookie battling for the punting role .
After seeing no live action in the August 15 preseason opener , veteran incumbent Mitch Wishnowsky handled holder duties on all Tyler Bass kicks.
The 34-year-old Wishnowsky, who played six snaps, also punted once in the win over the Browns, netting 58 yards on the boot.
Seventh-round rookie Tommy Doman played three snaps in Cleveland, punting three times for a 43.0 average with two inside the opponent's 20-yard line.

title: Surprise Undrafted Rookie WR Ja'Mori Maclin Extends Bills' Kentucky Connection
full_text:
Ja'Mori Maclin just made a name for himself in the Buffalo Bills ' second preseason game. He looks to add to a recent lineage for the Bills, given where he played college ball.
The nephew of former Pro Bowl WR Jeremy Maclin, Ja'Mori put on a show against the Cleveland Browns. He posted 108 yards on the day, buoyed by a 71-yard touchdown reception in the third quarter. We wrote about his performance changed the dynamic of the Bills' wide receivers competition.
While it was a treat to see a rookie take advantage of his opportunity again, it's also intriguing to note that he is another player making plays in Buffalo after playing college ball at Kentucky.
#Bills Ja’Mori Maclin has flashed. One handed catch last week, and now over 100 receiving yards today. Could be a sneaky practice squad guy. No doubt a play he will never forget! #BillsMafia @BuffTrenchTalk pic.twitter.com/UeWcFvP4uA
Maclin joins a growing list of Bills players who went to college in the Bluegrass State. The biggest name (literally and figuratively) drawing attention at the moment is Deone Walker. After a promising rookie season, the sophomore DT is looking more monstrous by the week .
He dominated his nine snaps in Buffalo's preseason opener against the Panthers , so he did not see the field in Cleveland. But it just goes to show how the coaching staff views Walker as he enters Year 2.
Next up is Ray Davis, who scored a rushing TD and totaled 43 all-purpose yards (21 rushing, 10 receiving, 12 punt return) against the Browns. He's added punt returning to his repertoire this summer after earning an All-Pro nod in 2025 as a kickoff returner.
Davis has also shown he can be a dependable backup RB. He's posted two 100-yard rushing games across his first two seasons in extended action.
Ray Davis scores on the opening drive 🙌 BUFvsCLE on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/4TaW9cpIBQ
The highest drafted player of the bunch is Maxwell Hairston. The 2025 first-rounder has been nicked up most of his tenure thus far, but he returned to practice this week after dealing with a groin injury.
Even as he works his way back, Hairston had some positives in the Bills' joint practices in Cleveland. He notably matched up with rookie Denzel Boston, knocking down a pass to the former Washington WR and ending a Browns' two-minute drill.
Now Maclin looks like another positive addition from Kentucky. The Wildcats may not be a blue-blood program in college football, but Brandon Beane is showing they still have a dearth of NFL talent coming through their program.
Ja'Mori Maclin on his 71-yard touchdown catch from Shane Buechele in the #Bills preseason win over the #Browns : "I didn't even think I was going to score low key." #BillsMafia pic.twitter.com/H5GEOvvyIE

title: Top Three Buffalo Bills Trade Candidates Entering Preseason Week 3
full_text:
As is often the case when the preseason winds down, the Buffalo Bills will need to make some tough decisions as they trim their roster from 90 players down to 53.
Buffalo has the luxury of a deep roster, which is why they're considered a favorite in the AFC . That also means there won't be too many open spots for young players trying to break through.
That being the case, here's a look at three Bills players who might not be able to make the final cut, but deserve to be part of an NFL franchise. Perhaps Buffalo could try and bring in draft capital rather than outright releasing these players and getting nothing in return.
Keleki Latu didn't make much noise in Week 2 against the Browns, but he went into this game with his arrow pointing all the way up. Latu has been a solid performer in all aspects, but is part of a very crowded tight end corps.
With Dalton Kincaid, Dawson Knox, and Jackson Hawes all ahead of him, Latu is likely on the outside looking in. Recently, I wrote about how teams will be interested in claiming Latu if he is indeed waived. With the anticipated interest, the Bills might want to see if someone is willing to give up a draft pick to avoid crossing their fingers on waivers.
A fifth-round pick out of Troy in 2024, Javon Solomon has always showed promise as a pass rusher. This year, seems to be close to breaking through thanks to his fit in Jim Leonhard's scheme. Solomon has been used as a stand-up pass rusher and looks far more comfortable. He has generated plenty of pressures and had a sack this weekend. Solomon could still make the team over Mike Danna , but he could also be an interesting trade piece.
Undrafted rookie Ian Wheeler has been one of the standouts during the preseason. After recording 41 yards and a touchdown against the Panthers, Wheeler added 56 rushing yards and 21 receiving yards on Saturday against the Browns.
It won't be easy for him to make the roster with James Cook, Ray Davis, and Ty Johnson all ahead of him, but his physical running style could make him popular among running back-needy teams. Rather than waiving him and risking getting nothing in return, the Bills could decide to add more draft capital, assuming they don't make the surprising move of keeping Wheeler over Johnson or Davis.

title: AFC Team Emerges as Trade Candidate for Bills' 2024 Fifth-Rounder on Roster Bubble
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills have plenty of intruging young offensive linemen, and not enough roster spots for all of them.
One player on the roster bubble who's likely on the outside looking in is 2024 fifth round pick Sedrick van Pran-Granger.
An AFC team with playoff aspirations just lost their starting center for the 2026 season, opening the door for Brandon Beane to pull off a trade so the Georgia product isn't lost for nothing.
This wouldn't be the first time Beane would move an offensive lineman right before cutdown day.
Buffalo has previously traded Cody Ford, Russell Bodine, Wyatt Teller and Marshall Newhouse in the months of August or September in exchange for a draft pick, with the logical conclusion that none of these players would've otherwise made or stayed on the 53-man roster.
Is it a guarantee that Van Pran-Granger won't make the team? No. But he seems to be an odd-man out given the depth Buffalo acquired at the center position this offseason.
Most importantly, the team re-signed starter Connor McGovern , locking down the middle of the offensive line for another four years.
Buffalo also signed Lloyd Cushenberry in free agency, the starting center for LSU while Joe Brady was part of the staff. The former third round pick has started 80 games in his career, and has routinely gotten second-team reps throughout the summer ahead of Van Pran-Granger.
Additionally, while Austin Corbett has been battling with Alec Anderson for the starting left guard spot, the former Panther logged 334 snaps at center while in Carolina last season.
Van Pran-Granger lacks the experience or versatility to push Cushenberry or Corbett as a reserve lineman, meaning he'll likely be a cut casualty at the end of the month.
It takes two to tango, so what NFL team could be in the market for a center?
The Los Angeles Chargers announced on Sunday that projected starter Tyler Biadasz was placed on season-ending injured reserve . Rookie Jake Slaughter is projected to step into Biadasz's role, moving from the guard spot he was projected to play in for his rookie season in.
With the Chargers' offensive line undergoing a shuffle, while also lacking depth along the interior of the unit, LA is a perfect candidate for Beane to direct a SVPG trade.

title: Bills' WR Roster Battle Just Got Really Interesting With Two Breakouts vs. Browns
full_text:
It's starting to feel like the Buffalo Bills are heavily interested in keeping a sixth wide receiver on the roster when cutdown day rolls around.
With DJ Moore, Khalil Shakir, Keon Coleman, Joshua Palmer and fourth-round rookie Skyler Bell seemingly destined for roster spots , barring a last-minute trade or long-term injury, there's realistically room for only one more wide receiver, and that player will almost definitely be asked to contribute on special teams.
Identifying the right option to fill that role, however, only became more difficult in the aftermath of Buffalo's 31-7 win over the Cleveland Browns on August 22.
Essentially, the Bills have eight wide receivers competing for one spot , and that's not including Tyrell Shavers, who was on the 53-man roster last year until tearing his ACL in the playoffs.
Although former Kansas City Chiefs' second-round pick Mecole Hardman, who initially joined the Bills last November in a reserve role, appeared to have a legit path to the Bills' sixth WR spot, mainly due to his punt return ability, there are multiple challengers threatening to overtake the two-time Super Bowl champion.
While Hardman's two drops didn't help his case on Saturday, two other candidates — veteran Trent Sherfield and undrafted rookie Ja'mori Maclin — made strong statements against the Browns.
The 30-year-old Sherfield is back for a second stint with the Bills . He played all 17 games for Buffalo as the fifth wide receiver in 2023.
"I love Trent," said Brady. "The personality that he has, the way that he goes about it, he's a leader in that room. He wanted to be a part of Buffalo, and he's doing everything he can to try and continue to be a part of the Buffalo Bills."
Sherfield played 17 of a possible 59 offensive snaps against the Browns, making four catches on four targets for 54 yards.
"Trent's always been great. He was here when I was here in '23 and he was awesome," said quarterback Kyle Allen. "Everyone in this building has a lot of trust in Trent. He just gets opens, makes contested catches. I feel great throwing him the ball. I know he's going to protect it."
He made back-to-back receptions for 18 and 17 yards, respectively, on the Bills' opening touchdown drive.
"He's just he's been making plays I think he has a comfort level understanding his role in the league," said Bills' rookie head coach Joe Brady after the August 22 victory.
Despite only 89 career regular season catches, including 11 as a Bill, Sherfield has proven valuable enough to stick around the NFL for eight-plus years. He played 35 percent of special teams snaps in 2023.
"You see a guy go out make plays like that in the receiver game and then draw a penalty and making tackles on special teams. He's such a selfless football player," said Brady.
Undrafted out of Kentucky , Maclin lacks great size and speed, but that didn't stop him from making plays in Cleveland.
Showing explosiveness and sound technique off the line, Maclin made two long receptions for 108 yards and one touchdowns against the Browns. One week earlier, he made a nice one-handed grab.
"He's been balling. He's been doing a good job. He works hard and he's got some juice to him, so it's fun playing with him," said quarterback Shane Buechele.
Prior to Buechele entering the game, Maclin caught a 37-yard pass from Allen with the Bills running their two-minute offense late in the first half.
Then, with Buechele at the controls late in the third quarter, Maclin pulled in an intermediate-range pass and turn up the sideline for a 71-yard touchdown.
Shane Buechele ➡️ Ja'Mori Maclin for a 71-yd touchdown! Tune into CBS pic.twitter.com/n1QbelEma2
"He's a guy that battled injuries in OTAs. You're undrafted and you're battling injuries in OTAs you better hope that you show something early to be able to continue to stick around. You guys know how this league works," said Brady. "He showed us a lot. He took advantage of the time when he was off and stuck around in the offseason, making sure that when his time was gonna come he was gonna be ready."
At this point, Maclin appears to have locked up a practice squad opportunity, and he's seriously challenging two veterans for a spot on the 53-man roster.

title: Why Buffalo Bills Need to Keep Ian Wheeler over Veteran RB
full_text:
Since signing with the Buffalo Bills ahead of the 2023 season, Ty Johnson has proven to be a reliable backup, especially on third downs. In three seasons with the Bills, Johnson has 545 yards and four touchdowns as a runner, while averaging 4.5 yards per attempt.
As a receiver, he's hauled in 49 receptions for 609 yards and six touchdowns while averaging 12.4 yards per reception. Simply put, he's been an efficient back, but looking ahead to 2026, he shouldn't be a lock to make the 53-man roster.
Johnson, who will turn 29 in September, saw a decline in his numbers this past season. His rushing yards per attempt went down from 5.2 in 2024 to 4.0 in 2025. His yardage per reception dipped as well, with Johnson averaging 11.0 yards per catch, down from the 15.8 in 2025.
Those numbers aren't likely to increase this season for two reasons. One is his age, as most running backs begin to decline as they approach 30 years old. More importantly, offensive coordinator Pete Carmichael made it clear that Buffalo plans to use Cook as a receiver more often . Doing so will limit Johnson's snaps on third down, which is where he has done the majority of his damage.
If that truly is the plan, keeping Ian Wheeler over Johnson could make sense. Wheeler is a more traditional RB2 and has shown during the preseason that he has no issues making the most of every touch. We recently wrote about his jaw-dropping hit during Thursday's joint practce .
Against the Panthers, Wheeler ran for 41 yards and a touchdown on seven carries. This week, he added 56 yards on 14 attempts, plus another 21 yards on two receptions. That gives him 118 yards on 23 touches, for an average of 5.1 yards per touch. As a pure runner, Wheeler is averaging 4.6 yards per attempt.
Not only is Wheeler proving to be an effective player , but he also makes significantly less than Johnson. Wheeler, an undrafted free agent out of Howard, has a cap hit of $885,000 compared to $3.275 million for Johnson . Buffalo would save $2.455 million by moving on from Johnson, who has been dealing with a knee injury this offseason.
Another option could be placing Johnson on the short-term IR to begin the season, allowing him to get his knee fully healthy. That could also give Wheeler time to prove he belongs in the NFL, without the risk of losing Johnson.

title: How the Panthers' Vaunted Secondary Stacks Up in NFL
full_text:
The reigning NFC South champions will play their final preseason game of 2026 on Friday when they host the Houston Texans. It’s the lone home contest of the summer for Dave Canales’s club, who owns a 2-1 record in its first three summertime tilts.
Last week, the staff at Pro Football Focus ranked the league’s 32 secondaries for 2026. The defending AFC champion New England Patriots own the top spot, with the Miami Dolphins bringing up the rear. Canales’s Carolina Panthers can be found in the middle of the pack at No. 14.
Mike Jackson intercepts Matthew Stafford for a Pick-6! LARvsCAR on FOX/FOX One https://t.co/HkKw7uXVnt pic.twitter.com/J2yeGsyNZK
“Carolina’s starting cornerback duo of Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson is one of the best in football. We know all about Horn’s ability, but Jackson’s 85.8 PFF coverage grade was the second-best among cornerbacks last season, helped by his five interceptions. Carolina played the most zone coverage of any defense last season.”
Those five picks include a theft of Rams’ quarterback Matthew Stafford in Carolina’s home playoff loss to Sean McVay’s club. You may also recall that Jackson picked off the 2025 NFL MVP during a regular-season victory over the Rams in Week 13, returning the interception 48 yards for a score in the Panthers’ 31-28 victory. Meanwhile, Horn finished with a career-best five interceptions and was named to the Pro Bowl for the second consecutive year.
There was also positive news elsewhere in the defensive backfield. “At safety,” added the Pro Football Focus staff, “Tre’von Moehrig was tied for the most tackles for loss or no gain among defensive backs (12). His 17 pressures were also the second-most of any safety.”
In his first season in Charlotte, Moehrig finished third on the team with 103 tackles . He also totaled three sacks, seven quarterback hits, and one interception. The former Las Vegas Raiders also add three stops in the playoff loss to the Rams.
So what about Moehrig’s counterpart at the other safety spot? Oddly, there was no mention by PFF regarding a fourth member of the starting secondary. This past season, veteran Nick Scott started all 17 regular-season games and finished second on the club with a career-high 109 defensive stops. He also amassed nine tackles in the wild card loss to the Rams. However, he managed only two takeaways and totaled just three passes defensed in 18 total contests.
Zakee Wheatley— continuing to make impacts play in the open field. Unfortunate non-recovery there. pic.twitter.com/OH3wSNVd3p
On the other hand, 2026 fifth-round pick Zakee Wheatley has seen plenty of action in three preseason outings, totaling a combined 18 tackles, along with a forced fumble. He led the team in stops vs. the Panthers (8) and Bills (7), and added three more tackles in the recent victory over the Jaguars. While the rookie defender got the starting nod in the Hall of Fame Game, Scott was in the opening lineup vs. Buffalo and Jacksonville.
Regardless, the Panthers’ defensive backfield is ranked in the upper half of the league. Perhaps a big year from either Scott or Wheatley (or both) could push this group further up the charts.

title: The Good and Not So Good from Panthers' Monday Practice: Jimmy Horn Jr.'s Chances
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers wrapped up practice on Monday, the final week of preparation before the last preseason game this Friday. For many, it's now or never, and stringing together good practices to close out camp as Week 1 inches closer is paramount.
But as usual, there were some good things and some not so good things in the Panthers' practice.
Practice ends with a Corey Thornton pick of Pickett. Thornton had dropped a potential INT a few plays earlier.
Corey Thornton is not only trending towards losing his job, but some have predicted that he won't even make the roster. He's had a rough summer, but today he bounced back. It's now or never for Thornton, and he closed practice with what some have referred to as his best play yet. Putting in good practices and a good preseason finale can change his fate.
Canales says if the starters get enough work in Wednesday’s joint practice, they will likely not play in Friday’s game. #Panthers
Dave Canales has seen his team come out flat to open the season twice in a row, and he hasn't really learned. The head coach has given the Panthers' starters more run thus far, but he may not let them play at all in the finale, though not for health. He said it will depend on how they do in joint practice . Either they need to play for the reps (which is likely), or it's not worth the health risk. Choose one.
Jimmy Horn just scored in seven on seven … and celebrated by doing a front flip.
Jimmy Horn Jr. has found himself in a muddled competition for the final few wide receiver spots. Whether the Panthers take six or seven receivers, Horn isn't guaranteed a spot on the roster. He has put in the work, though he hasn't excelled as a receiver yet. Today, he made a great play and celebrated accordingly because he has likely given himself a boost towards making the final 53.
Chuba Hubbard is expected to be ready by Week One; hit 20mph on Return-to-Play last week. Haynes King will not return for the preseason finale on Friday. #Panthers
Let's all hope the Hall of Fame Game was enough, because Haynes King is unlikely to return to the field this weekend. Not playing will hurt his chances of making the roster, even though Dave Canales might've hinted that he expects him to make the roster. He can do nothing towards that, though, and is fully at the mercy of the staff after one preseason game against the backups of backups . It's not ideal.
“I wouldn’t want to put him in a game setting after practicing for a week,” Canales on Darren Waller. He said they have to lean on his recent history because it’s hard to get an evaluation on a week in practice. He likely won’t play Friday but will be sprinkled in against…
Like Haynes King, let's all hope that Darren Waller's history and his impression in practice is enough, because he is unlikely to play on Friday. The veteran tight end was brought in to revitalize the tight end position, yet he hasn't played. That makes it hard to roster him, though the Panthers would probably be foolish not to.

title: Panthers Give Chuba Hubbard Injury Update, Confirm RB Plan With Jonathon Brooks
full_text:
With just a few weeks to go before the start of the season, the Carolina Panthers have a few questions in their backfield.
One of them has to do with the status of Chuba Hubbard, who has been sidelined during training camp with a hamstring injury . The other pertains to how Carolina plans on deploying Hubbard and his backfield mate, Jonathon Brooks.
On Monday, Panthers head coach Dave Canales provided some clarity on both of those subjects.
Canales told reporters on Monday that Hubbard is expected to be ready to go for the start of the season.
"Absolutely," Canales said when asked if Hubbard would be ready to roll for the season-opener. "He's ahead of schedule. He's doing a great job."
Hubbard also spoke to reporters and revealed he is feeling good and would have returned to practice immediately but the coaches and training staff are just being cautious with his injury.
"Yeah, to be honest, I feel pretty good," Hubbard revealed . "I think the coaches are just — and obviously the training staff — are just trying to take care of me. Obviously, last year I kind of came back a little early and it kind of lingered on for a little bit, so I think it's just them kind of protecting me from myself a little bit. I would have been out the next day if I could've, but I feel good, I feel healthy. Looking forward to Week 1."
All offseason long, the expectation has been that Carolina will have Brooks and Hubbard in a timeshare , at least to start the season.
Canales confirmed that will indeed be the case, with one back starting a series and the other coming in on third downs.
"We'll definitely roll it out just the way we have been, where you have a lead back for the series, the other guy comes in on third down so they can be in there for the protection, and also we run the ball on third down," Canales explained.
"So those are good opportunities to just keep a guy into the game while the other person, whether it's Chuba or JB, we'll make that decision when we get closer. But whoever the lead guy for the base downs is, they'll get the bulk of that rhythm so that they can kind of feel what's happening with the fronts and how the defense is trying to play as well," Canales added.
One thing to keep an eye on with Brooks is his pass protection. He had some rough reps during his two preseason games and he may be limited on third downs if he can't be more consistent, which would lead to more work for Hubbard.
Hubbard hasn't been great in pass pro during his career, but he is certainly better and more proven than Brooks as we sit here today.
While we're set for a 50-50 split to start the season, we've already seen Canales lean more toward one back if someone is playing better, as we saw with Hubbard and Rico Dowdle last season.
So, don't be surprised if one or the other seizes more control of the backfield as the season progresses.

title: Should Bryce Young, Panthers Starters Play Preseason Finale vs. Texans?
full_text:
Three preseason games down, one to go . The Carolina Panthers conclude their preseason at home against the Houston Texans on Friday, August 28th. Carolina's fourth and final preseason game takes place 16 days before Week 1 and just two days before the NFL's cut deadline, when 53-man rosters have to be finalized.
Because the roster cutdown day is just 48 hours after the Panthers' last preseason game, the game is even more important for guys on the bubble between making the roster and not.
Since the game is more important for undrafted free agents or late-round draft picks, it raises the question of whether the starters need to play at all.
It's correct to act cautiously in the preseason; having the starters ready for Week 1 is most important. That being said, the more live-game reps, the more prepared Carolina will be for their season opener against the Chicago Bears.
The Panthers, under head coach Dave Canales, are notorious for slow starts to the season. Each of the last two seasons, Carolina has started 0-2.
Starting fast has to be a point of emphasis for the Panthers moving forward, and if the starters are sluggish and don't have their chemistry down right away, then another 0-2 start could be on the horizon.
As far as how much the starters play, it doesn't have to be much. In each game thus far, the starters who play have logged roughly two series before their night ends. That number doesn't need to bump up much, but three or four drives would feel appropriate, as the season will be just over two weeks away.
Bryce Young and the offense looked like a completely different unit against Jacksonville than they did at Buffalo.
The second drive of that game was the best Young has looked this preseason, finding Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker and leading the Panthers to the one-yard line before Jonathon Brooks walked in a touchdown.
It's super important for the offense to continue to build chemistry, and for Bryce Young to get more comfortable. That being said, the offense hasn't been the most concerning unit; it's been the secondary.
This especially goes for the Buffalo game. Bills QB Josh Allen and their offense made the Panthers' secondary look silly, constantly finding chunk plays and easy throws down the middle of the field.
D.J. Moore's first @BuffaloBills catch of the preseason goes for 33 yards! Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/sErDqbd3Yl
While Allen is the best QB in the NFL, that doesn't excuse an awful secondary showing. Allen completed 6/8 passes for 111 yards and 1 touchdown in just two drives. The effort against Jacksonville was an improvement by the Carolina secondary, but not against a Jacksonville offense playing all their starters.
Whether Houston plays their starters or not, three or four series from both sides of the ball would be beneficial heading towards the beginning of the regular season.

title: Haynes King and 4 Other UDFAs Giving Panthers Tough Decisions
full_text:
To put it kindly, a UDFA in the NFL is lucky if they simply make the roster. Carolina Panthers star Jalen Coker is one of the best possible outcomes for an undrafted player, because the vast majority of the time, they are barely rostered.
The Panthers, however, have made use of undrafted players recently, and they are poised to bring some onto the final 53-man roster this year. Haynes King has obviously made headlines , but there are four others who could join him for Week 1 .
It all comes down to this weekend, but if Haynes King plays and plays like he did in the Hall of Fame Game, then the Panthers have a tough decision. Do they risk putting a clearly very talented player on the practice squad or do they use one of the few roster spots they have available on a third quarterback? Do they possibly cut Kenny Pickett? All options are on the table.
With Taylor Moton and Ikem Ekwonu out for the foreseeable future, the Panthers are dreadfully thin at tackle. Fortunately, they have Rasheed Walker and Monroe Freeling, but the depth is not there. However, Albert Reese IV is making a push to snag a roster spot after posting a team-high offensive PFF grade against the Jacksonville Jaguars.
Aaron Hall has had an up-and-down preseason/training camp, but the perilous depth on the defensive line gives him some leeway. The former Duke lineman is very talented and extremely athletic, but he'll need to continue putting it together to make the roster over some other deserving players.
The Panthers don't have a ton of cornerback depth, and DeVonta Smith could be forcing the issue. While the secondary as a whole has looked out of sorts this preseason, some individual players have done well, and Smith played well against the Jaguars, making a wonderful play to force a fumble that Cam Gill recovered.
Ja'seem Reed is not technically a UDFA anymore, but he was a UDFA last year with the Cleveland Browns until he got hurt, so he's still an undrafted player seeking his first NFL roster spot. And he's making the Panthers' wide receiver choice very difficult. He didn't play last week against the Jags, but he has been pretty great in other preseason action, looking like a potential steal at the back end of the depth chart.

title: Panthers Thankfully Predicted to Repeat Darren Waller Signing at Key Position
full_text:
A year ago, the Carolina Panthers made significant strides on defense. The worst unit in the league in 2024 finished 16th in the NFL in fewest total yards allowed this past season. After allowing 59 offensive TDs in 17 regular-season games the previous year, that number was cut to 44 offensive touchdowns in 18 total contests.
This offseason, general manager Dan Morgan added a pair of quality defenders in edge rusher Jaelan Phillips (Eagles) and 2025 Pro Bowl linebacker Devin Lloyd (Jaguars). Both players should be difference makers for Dave Canales’s team and coordinator Ejiro Evero’s unit.
Off Carolina’s 34-17 preseason victory at Jacksonville last Friday night, Panthers’ writer Mike Kaye of ESPN posed a question regarding just who will be in the starting lineup alongside one of the team’s key offseason additions this offseason?
“Carolina didn't play Devin Lloyd,” stated Kaye, “so Trevin Wallace and Claudin Cherelus both started Friday. Neither defender has gained an advantage in their position battle this summer, and the depth behind Lloyd could be upgraded before Week 1.”
Talk about equal time? Cherelus has started all three preseason contests, while Wallace played but did not start against the Bills. Both totaled 19 defensive snaps vs. the Cardinals, and each player saw 24 defensive snaps vs. Buffalo. The latter had two dozen defensive snaps vs. the Jaguars, and Wallace a total of 23 on defense. In three games, Cherelus has totaled nine tackles, with Wallace recording seven stops.
“Similar to tight end, added Kaye, “it wouldn't be surprising to see the Panthers search for a veteran free agent linebacker before or after the cut-down deadline next week.”
Of course, that tight end is nine-year veteran Darren Waller. He inked a one-year, $1.3 million deal last week with Canales’s club. He did not play against the Jaguars, but he does bolster a tight end room that has been somewhat underutilized in recent seasons. He played in nine games with the Dolphins this past season and caught six TD passes. Panthers’ tight ends have combined for eight TD receptions since 2024.
Back to inside linebacker. The roster cutdown to 53 players for each of the 32 clubs is Sunday, August 30, by 6:00 pm ET. Obviously, Morgan could act before then by adding a proven veteran not currently with a team.
Of course, the list is headed by ageless Bobby Wagner, who spent the past two seasons with the Washington Commanders. The 36-year-old pro has totaled 100-plus tackles in each of his 14 NFL campaigns—11 of those with the Seattle Seahawks.
Other available candidates include Kenneth Murray, who led the Dallas Cowboys with 81 tackles this past season, and Bobby Okereke—who racked up a club-high 143 tackles in 2025 with the New York Giants.
Will Morgan take the free-agent plunge one more time? It could be an interesting few days in Charlotte, starting with Friday night’s preseason finale vs. the visiting Houston Texans.

title: The Biggest Concern for Panthers in 2026 Isn't Bryce Young
full_text:
This Friday evening, the reigning NFC South champions will wrap up their four-game preseason by hosting the Houston Texans. The club owns a 2-1 record this summer, somewhat notable considering the team owned a combined 1-8 preseason mark the previous three years.
Late last week and prior to Carolina Panthers’ 34-17 victory at Jacksonville last Friday, Gordon McGuinness of Pro Football Focus identified the biggest concern for each of the league’s 32 teams entering the start of the upcoming season. For Canales’s squad, it’s a pretty obvious choice that team has hopefully found the solution to.
“The Panthers are currently without both starting offensive tackles ” explained McGuinness. “Left tackle Ikem Ekwonu suffered a ruptured patellar tendon in the wild-card loss to the Rams, while right tackle Taylor Moton is sidelined with blood clots. It remains unclear when either will return in 2026, but both appear likely to miss at least the start of the season.
Each of these blockers could be considered mainstays since joining the organizations. Ekwonu was the sixth overall pick in the 2022 draft from North Carolina State. He has played and started 65 out of a possible 69 games, including the aforementioned playoff clash with Sean McVay’s team.
Meanwhile, Moton was a second-round selection back in 2017 from Western Michigan. He played in all 16 regular-season contests and a postseason games as a rookie without a start. Since 2018, he has been in the opening lineup in 129 of the club’s 130 total outings. While Ekwonu’s availability has obviously been a question mark since mid-January, Moton’s medical concerns were revealed in June.
In any case, Panthers’ general manager Dan Morgan was already looking ahead this offseason when it came to the left tackle issue. He added four-year pro Rasheed Walker (Packers) in free agency, and used the 19th overall selection in April’s draft on University of Georgia standout Monroe Freeling.
“Walker earned a 69.3 PFF pass-blocking grade in 2025,” added McGuinness, “while Freeling was one of college football’s top pass protectors, allowing just two pressures on 469 pass-blocking snaps. Still, losing both starting tackles is a significant concern, and for all of Freeling’s potential, he has yet to play an NFL snap.”
Yes, I understand this was against the Jags 2s. Still, love seeing that right side of Robert Hunt, Monroe Freeling, and Tommy Tremble parting the seas for Jonathon Brooks. #Panthers pic.twitter.com/YgeLNjH8AP
To be clear, the former Bulldog did not play vs. the Arizona Cardinals in the Hall of Fame Game, but did log 10 offensive snaps in the team’s preseason loss at Buffalo. Freeling was back in the starting lineup vs. Jacksonville, playing 13 offensive snaps, as well as one on special teams.
Hence, as it stands at the moment, Panthers’ quarterback Bryce Young will be playing behind a vastly-different offensive front early in the season —which includes a new face at center as well—than he lined up with over his first three years with the franchise.

title: Could Haynes King Push Bryce Young for Panthers' QB1 Spot?
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers are not entertaining a camp battle at quarterback . They're all in on Bryce Young for now . But if we're all being honest, there's been one quarterback who has looked the best this preseason, and it's UDFA Haynes King .
They've all played varying sample sizes and against varying levels of competition, but if we're strictly evaluating how they played in a vacuum, then King has outdone Young, Kenny Pickett, and Kyle Trask, none of whom have particularly struggled.
Could King ever push the Panthers, who don't yet have an answer at quarterback beyond 2027, Young's option year, to start?
It was against the backups (and backups of the backups, to be truthful) for a team projected to nab the number one overall pick in the next draft, but Haynes King was electric in the Hall of Fame Game. And good football is good football.
We all began to fantasize about King's career that night. What could he be? Could the Panthers have found a true diamond in the rough? Couple that with a partly inauspicious preseason for Bryce Young, and there are legitimately some people wondering if the Panthers might be better off with King under center.
But, to be blunt, there's almost no chance King ever becomes a starting quarterback in the NFL. There have been five UDFA QBs who have gone on to be multi-year starters: Tony Romo, Warren Moon, Jeff Garcia, Dave Krieg, and Kurt Warner.
That's a good group of quarterbacks, but the odds are not in King's favor of joining them. There are a handful of undrafted quarterbacks every single year, and only five have ever been notable enough to start more than one season.
What King could do is become a good backup quarterback, and we believe that's his trajectory. It's a shame he has not been on the field since that Hall of Fame Game, but he showed enough to suggest that he could overtake Kenny Pickett, who's also been solid this preseason, as the primary backup.
The Panthers aren't, nor should they be, considering starting anyone else besides Young this year. That's partly because he's earned it and partly because it's pretty much the final year for evaluating the fourth-year QB.
But the Panthers do have an opportunity with King, even if he never starts. He could be a gadget player or a QB sneak option, as well as a good backup.
The Panthers have to roster him, though. They can't afford to lose King to another team if he lands on the practice squad, so they have to roster him. Then they can use him as the primary backup if he outplays Pickett or in 2027, when Pickett hits free agency.
No, King isn't better than nor should he start over Young, but he absolutely deserves a spot on the roster.

title: Panthers Have Not Given Bryce Young What He Needs in Make-or-Break Year 4
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers have tried to support Bryce Young , especially once it became clear that he could not overcome an abysmal roster in 2023. They began adding pieces at various spots on offense to try to help. Unfortunately, in 2026, it's clear that it didn't work very well.
The first thing a team can do for its quarterback is give him weapons to throw to. The Panthers have done a passable job of that, but we can't pretend this pass-catching unit is elite. Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker are doing all the heavy lifting.
PFF ranked them 22nd in the NFL , and it's hard to disagree with the ranking. There aren't 22 better duos in the NFL than McMillan and Coker, but there are so many other players to consider, and for the Panthers, most of them are simply not very good.
"Beyond those two, there is very little proven talent to speak of in this receiving room. Tight ends Ja’Tavion Sanders and Tommy Tremble have combined for four straight PFF receiving grades in the 50.0s over the last two seasons," the blurb for the Panthers read.
The second thing a team can do for its quarterback is provide him with a good running game. The Panthers have tried to do that and probably believe that they have, but the numbers disagree. Even with Rico Dowdle last year, the running game was not good.
This year, PFF ranked them 27th , and it's once again hard to disagree. None of Chuba Hubbard, Trevor Etienne, or AJ Dillon has the explosiveness needed to really succeed in the NFL. Jonathon Brooks might, but he's a wild card.
"Question marks remain over the health of Jonathon Brooks, who has taken just nine handoffs since he was drafted 46th overall two years ago," the blurb read.
The final thing a team can do for its quarterback is protect him. The Panthers have done a better job of protecting Bryce Young than providing him weapons or a running game, but it's still not a good situation thanks to injuries.
In fact, PFF rightly noted that the Panthers' offensive line is a top-five unit most primed for regression. The line was very good in 2025, but it could be rough in 2026. There are a lot of talented players, but how well do they fit?
Some key losses, both injury-related and other, have tanked this line. Ikem Ekwonu, Taylor Moton, Austin Corbett, and Cade Mays, all of whom posted 66.0 or better PFF grades, are gone for right now.
"Ekwonu is expected to miss the majority of the season after suffering a ruptured patellar tendon in the playoffs, while Moton will be sidelined into the starting slate due to blood clots in his lung. Also, former starting center Cade Mays headed to Detroit, while Corbett is now in Buffalo," PFF analyst Bradley Locker wrote.
Locker noted that the Panthers added nice replacements in Monroe Freeling, Rasheed Walker, Sam Hecht, and Luke Fortner, but that's a lot of new additions to the line, and there's no telling how rookies Freeling and Hecht will fare in their first NFL seasons.
Simply put, the Panthers have tried and failed to surround Bryce Young with help. This is probably the best overall offense he's had in the NFL, but the bar is on the floor, and even with the talent they do have, there are major question marks.

title: Jonathon Brooks' Biggest Issue in Preseason Week 2 Could Limit Snaps With Panthers
full_text:
Running back Jonathon Brooks had a few standout moments in the Carolina Panthers' preseason Week 2 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars, but it wasn't all good for him.
Brooks ripped off an 11-yard run during the contest, and he was able to find pay dirt for the first time in his career on a one-yard carry in the first quarter.
However, Brooks' pass-blocking left a lot to be desired. Brooks saw three pass-blocking reps, according to Pro Football Focus , and gave up two pressures and scored a putrid 6.6 grade.
Here's one of those snaps in which he gave up a pressure.
Jonathon Brooks has to be better in pass pro here. Bad whiff. This is likely a first down for Brycen Tremayne if Brooks does his job. Have to be better in this area if you're going to be reliable on third downs. #Panthers pic.twitter.com/wN2i57dpWn
Now, to be fair, Brooks did redeem himself in another pass pro rep later on, but his showing overall was not good.
It goes without saying that Bryce Young's life is going to be a lot harder if his running backs can't adequately block for him.
We saw that first hand in the clip above, as Young's throw was clearly impacted on a play that otherwise would have gained yardage if Young had a cleaner look.
More specifically for Brooks, he can't hope to see many snaps on third downs if his pass pro isn't up to snuff. If he doesn't improve, Brooks is going to cede even more work to Chuba Hubbard, who remains the favorite to lead the backfield at the start of the year, and quite possibly even Trevor Etienne or AJ Dillon.
PFF has charted four pass-blocking snaps in total for Brooks in the preseason. The third-year back had a successful rep in the previous preseason game, and had another in the second.
That said, the bad has been really bad thus far.
The good news for Brooks is that Etienne hasn't been much better with his pass pro snaps. Etienne has registered a 29.1 grade in two pass protection snaps this preseason, and he posted a 22.9 grade through three pass-blocking snaps last season.
Hubbard is the best and most proven blocker of the trio, but he isn't great in that area by any stretch after posting a lackluster grade of 46.8 in 2025.
All of this points to a pass protection problem in the backfield for the Panthers, and it's one they need to fix.
Outside of the clear struggles in pass protection, Brooks took a step forward in his second preseason game of the season.
He barely averaged three yards per carry and only finished with five carries for 18 yards, but those were still better numbers than last week. He also ripped off an 11-yard run when the right side of Carolina's offensive line opened up a nice hole for him.
That run, along with his score, will only help Brooks build confidence as the regular season approaches.

title: Braxton Jones' Stuggles Leave Bears with Few Options and Time Nearly Up
full_text:
Bears coaches and personnel need to make good use of their Monday off-day meetings described by Ben Johnson after Saturday's loss for one very good reason.
It has nothing to do with a sense of urgency after a meaningless preseason drubbing. Rather, the process has changed this year and the Bears need to be certain where they are headed with cuts approaching quickly.
Last year when Johnson went through his first roster cutdown, the Bears finished preseason and then had four days until the final roster cuts had to be completed. They started trimming the roster the next day and eventually, gradually got to the mandated 53 men.
Because they finish on Saturday, the last possible day for preseason games, they will have less than 24 hours after the game ends in Nashville until the cutdown deadline at 5 p.m. on Sunday.
Left Tackle and EDGE will cost Chicago Bears 10 games this year
So, they'd better have their ducks in a row well before they start making those phone calls and telling players to come see coach and bring their playbook.
The good thing for the Bears is they'll have two full weeks after cutdown day until their game. The roster is hardly a set feature then on cutdown day. In the few days, after forming a practice squad, they can shop for players who have been waived and waive more players from their own roster.
It's a fluid sort of roster formation, but in football you're not signing a player and bringing him in to play in a couple of days unless it's the kicker, punter, long snapper or possibly a running back.
Braxton Jones my goodness man pic.twitter.com/HW2agfAFlT
This is all part of the reason why the left tackle situation in the wake of Saturday's preseason game has to be so disheartening for coaches and personnel. They've fully invested in Braxton Jones handling the left tackle spot until Ozzy Trapilo could return, and they've got other options in Jedrick Wills Jr., Kiran Amegadjie and even Theo Benedet. Yet, not a single one of these players stepped up with what anyone could interpret to be a good game against Cincinnati.
It's even more disappointing for Jones to struggle as much as he did with a holding penalty on a run inside the 10-yard line for a first down by Roschon Johnson, and a horrendous Pro Football Focus pass blocking grade of 29.6 for the
For this reason, and because of the mediocre performance of their passing attack in the first team's only full and complete series, Johnson needs to announce early in the week the starters will be playing on Saturday.
The Bears’ Left Tackle Situation Is a HUGE Problem #ChicagoBears #DaBears #NFL #BearDown pic.twitter.com/mgp859Bew4
They need the work. They need to see real evidence Jones can hold his own without holding at left tackle for at least four games, because if they deem Trapilo in need of more work -- and they should -- then he'll need to stay on IR for four weeks before being activated.
They've already come too far into this and invested to much time and effort into Jones to abandon the ship now just because of 15 plays against the Bengals backups.
In the meantime, the other tackles didn't exactly excel enough to push into a starting role. Kiran Amegadjie was facing mostly practice squad types and players who will be out of football and did get a 70.4 run-blocking grade but only a mediocre 57.0 at pass blocking from PFF as he allowed three pressures.
Left tackle isn't much of a concern for @clayharbs82 because the Bears proved last year they can win with Braxton Jones and Theo Benedet starting. "Ben Johnson is going to be able to scheme for that," says Harbor. pic.twitter.com/0zbCQjqLTY
Jedrick Wills Jr. got it half right with the best pass blocking of anyone on the roster at 80.0 for 20 pass blocks. He gave up one pressure and  nothing more. Then again, he had an poor 47.5 run-blocking grade for 15 running plays blocked.
Then again, both Wills and Amegadjie were playing right tackle and not left after both saw action on the left side against Cleveland.
My biggest concern of the night for #DaBears is Braxton Jones getting bull rushed into oblivion by what im assuming was 2nd or 3rd string edge rusher. I didnt see it live, so I dont know it was. I could be mistaken. 🤷‍♂️ pic.twitter.com/CZEPuJtewg
Benedet came closest to an acceptable performance as Jones' replacement at left tackle. Against backups, he came in at 66.6 for 13 run-blocking plays but only 50.4 as a pass blocker on 13 plays.
Bears offensive line coach Dan Roushar better get Jones' buddy and  blocking mentor, former Saint Terron Armstead, back to Halas Hall and try to figure out what happened to the Jones who started training camp with so much hope.
We really gotta figure out the LT position. Far too often Braxton Jones is missing a block or committing a penalty. My hope is Jedrick Willis steps up to his 1st round caliber skillset and takes over the job. We’ll see.
The Bears have come too far with him as their answer to this position to back off of it now, and any answer they can come up with who is not on the team already would probably not be an opening day answer at this point
Simply, the Bears have run out of time and Jones must step up because Trapilo hasn't even begun practicing with the team in scrimmage yet. He's only doing stretching and running and a few individual drills at practice.
Trapilo isn't there yet and won't be for a while. Jones has to be the answer or the team is facing huge problems straight out of the gate and can do nothing but struggle until Trapilo finally is back.

title: Where Toughest Chicago Bears Cuts Should Come Based on PFF's Grades
full_text:
A Monday off entirely for players was strategically placed by Bears coach Ben Johnson before preparations to face Tennessee.
This allows them to take stock of what they have seen to date in two preseason games as well as training camp and offseason practices. It's a pause so they can assess who should be in the bubble or not for the final game against the Titans, as roster cuts loom .
"That’s where there is this discussion — players’ day off on Monday — with the personnel staff," Johnson said following Saturday's disappointing performance in Cincinnati . "That’s a pretty big day for us, to make sure we are all aligned, we all see it the same way.
"It will be a big week for them (players) as well. I said it a week ago that I don’t think there was much clarity, and actually it’s a good thing as we have a really good competition across the roster for a number of spots. Between the game tonight, we’ll watch that tape in depth and get a good evaluation of guys and then next week I’m certain we’re goingto be able to pick our 53 (roster) and I also think for our practice squad as well, as we get the best 69 guys because the practice squad in a 17-game season, they’re going to come up and help us.”
Being a fly on the wall in that room would be fun, except, of course, then you'd be a fly. Since no one could know what they're sayg about how they rate some of these players fighting to make the roster, there is one source that can help. Pro Football Focus grades are not necessarily the most reliable but are at least professionally compiled and sometimes dead on accurate.
For two preseason games, PFF says the Bears should have a tough time deciding whether to cut players at these three areas:
If they choose to keep six cornerbacks, it's still going to be difficult determining who goes or at least goes to the practice squad. There are a lot of players vying for only one spot, and versatility will rule the day.
PFF actually has cornerback Deantre Prince graded first in coverage (81.2) among all defensive players after two games, just ahead of Jaylon Johnson, but Prince was a player not in camp when practices started and has been judged for only 12 preseason game reps in coverage, 22 plays overall.
One spot behind Prince among cornerbacks is another player who wasn't with the team when practices began, but has 61 preseason reps. That's Beanie Bishop Jr. Against Cincinnati, Bishop didn't have the same kind of game as his two-interception effort against Cleveland and his run defense and tackling remain issues. He is graded worst tackler among all defensive backs at 27.5.
All-American CB Beanie Bishop Jr. with the fastest 40 at Big 12 Pro Day: 4.39u! @WVUFootball @FastTwitchDrink pic.twitter.com/GtVbAa60di
The fight for the last cornerback spot could simply come down to this last preseason game and/or who is healthiest at final cuts among Jaylon Jones, Josh Blackwell, Terell Smith, Prince and Bishop. Blackwell's value as one of the top special teams players looms large in any decision.
One thing to remember about Bishop is if they decide to keep him, he is out three weeks because of a suspension BUT his spot on the roster does not count. So they get an exemption while he serves the penalty for a past drug policy violation.
Not that anyone should have expected Roschon Johnson to be a cut victim this year, but, well, if you look at social media he was all but ticketed on his plane ride out of town. Instead, Johnson has done exactly what Ben Johnson wanted to see from backs in a few ways.
Roschon Johnson missed a huge hole on the left side. #DaBears pic.twitter.com/DG48Qf03hb
First, the veteran backup is No. 1 among all offensive players in pass blocking for a very limited number of reps. Ben Johnson made the remark about this being critical for backs in his offense. Roschon Johnson also showed up big earlier in his career as a pass blocker, before being beset with injuries. His running was the most obvious aspect of his grade, as a power back in short yardage production, and he is only 3.2 points behind breakaway running back Salvon Ahmed. Like Johnson, Ahmed's pass blocking has not been bad, and his touchdown on a screen pass indicates his potential value as a receiving back.
What makes this battle difficult is Brittain Brown trails both of the other two in grades for most categories, but hasn't performed poorly, either.
It could be a case where Brown winds up on the practice squad but Ahmed makes the roster because he might have niche value in the passing game to some other team just like he does in the passing game for the Bears.
I'm starting to lean toward keeping Roschon Johnson as RB3 (Kyle Monangai replacement until he comes back) and stashing Salvon Ahmed on the PS as the potential call up to replace D'Andre Swift's speed if anything were to happen to Swift.
This is going to be difficult  because of Skyler Thomas' performance to date but mainly because of all the health concerns throughout camp for players like Cam Lewis,  Xavier Woods and Elijah Hicks. Although Thomas, an undrafted rookie from Oregon, gave up a touchdown pass in Saturday's loss, PFF says he has had exemplary play in two games. This much is certain: Thomas has withstood the rigors of anyone else in the hunt for a job in this secondary. The guy is constantly on the field at practice, whether it's on defense or special teams. He has answered the call, and this is a lot more than several other defensive backs have done.
PFF has Thomas as their fifth-highest graded defensive player and third overall among DBs. What Thomas has done that can really endear him to coaches on both defense and special teams is tackle. He is the highest-graded tackler overall (85.7), one spot better than Cam Lewis despite having three times as many total reps (75). He also made an interception Saturday, and takeaways never hurt. With another good game Saturday, it would be a very tough cut to make based on these grades.
The decision here seems to be whether they keep Thomas or count on Elijah Hicks coming off PUP. At this point, go with the high PFF grade because he's healthy and producing.
Skyler Thomas stole it away for the INT 😳 Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/qVunxHicG9
Regardless of Austin Booker's health — and no one can be certain of that right now after he was held out of Saturday's game without explanation — this looks like a difficult cut to make entirely because of Jamree Kromah and the recent signing of Marcus Davenport. If Davenport figures as the fourth edge behind Montez Sweat, Austin and Dayo Odeyingbo, Kromah would find it difficult to squeeze onto the roster because veteran backup Daniel Hardy can provide them with both edge rush ability and past special teams excellence.
For Kromah, consistency of PFF grading has been there in two preseason games and 78 reps. That's  many more reps than most players coaches must assess.
Kromah is said to have taken well to the different and more extensive fundamental approach coaches were able to use becausse they weren't burdened by introducing an offense and defense to everyone this year. Kromah did get plenty of offseason work with the first team in place of Sweat.
. @ChicagoBears @Browns @jamreekromah was the best defensive player in this preseason game. Got real size; real power; can really bend and plays with a style that can only be described as Full Metal Jacket #dabears #BaldysBreakdowns pic.twitter.com/quz7ZVSNn8
For two preseason games, PFF grades him the second-best defensive player overall behind only starting strongside linebacker D'Marco Jackson (90.8). With 44 more reps than Jackson, that easily means he would have the highest defensive grade. Grades tend to decline with more reps. Kromah has a 77.1 pass-rushing grade for the two preseason games, which is No. 1 for all their edges, and trails only rookie Jordan van den Berg (87.5) and Gervon Dexter (87.0).
Kromah should give the Bears something to consider while Davenport is still "ramping up." If…

title: Biggest Risers and Fallers in Bears Training Camp So Far
full_text:
It's been a long training camp for the Chicago Bears this year, and thankfully it's been far less messy than what we saw in 2025. Caleb Williams has been sharp, the offense has been more consistent, and the defense had a good showing against the Cincinnati Bengals' starting offense in a joint practice last week, which means general manager Ryan Poles' big gamble on defense could soon be vindicated.
The Bears have one more joint practice this week against the Tennessee Titans, who will be their preseason Week 3 opponent. After that, however, comes roster cutdown day. On August 30th, the Bears will have to trim their roster from 90 players to just 53, and few of those decisions will be easy. Some players were relative unknowns at the start of camp yet now seem indispensable to the operation of the team. Others who looked like roster locks, however, may find themselves without a chair when the music stops.
With that in mind, let's consider some of the biggest risers and fallers from the Bears ahead of their final week of training camp.
Whether the Bears carry five or six wide receivers on the depth chart this year, it's hard to imagine Walker not earning a spot. His rise truly began a year ago as an undrafted rookie when he caught a go-ahead touchdown pass in Chicago's preseason Week 3 thriller against the Kansas City Chiefs, then hit a crescendo when he became the unlikely hero in the Bears' wild Week 15 comeback win over the Packers .
Throughout training camp and preseason this year, Walker has continued to impress with his acrobatic catches and nifty route running, including this 36-yard reception against the Bengals on Saturday. He may not ever be a starting receiver for the Bears, but he looks like one of the better depth options in the league.
When the Bears signed Kyler Gordon to a market-setting contract extension in April of 2025, they thought they were locking in the services of the NFL's best nickel cornerback for the next four years. Since then, Gordon has played just five games including the playoffs and has not practiced at all in training camp as he rehabs a soft tissue injury.
This has been a frustrating issue for everyone involved: Gordon himself, Ben Johnson, the media, and the fans. And as if to add insult to injury, Ozzy Trapilo defied history with his improbable return from a ruptured patellar tendon. I'm sure Gordon will play again at some point this season, but his stock has cratered, especially with the coaches, and I imagine the Bears will be looking to move off of his contract as soon as feasible.
Should the Bears carry just five receivers on their depth chart this year rather than the customary six, I don't think Davis would make the cut, but he may have done enough already to force the Bears to make room for him. The undrafted rookie receiver from NW Missouri State has repeatedly ended training camp practice sessions with walk-off touchdown receptions. In the Bears' preseason Week 1 win over the Browns, Davis led the team with four receptions for 88 yards.
Despite a poor showing on Saturday night against the Bengals, I'm still counting Davis among the risers of training camp. He may have been entirely unknown among the fans a month ago, but he's quickly become a fan-favorite and a proven contributor in a depth role.
The sooner Trapilo can return to full action for the Bears, the better. The left tackle position has become a big problem for the Bears that can't be addressed adequately so long as Trapilo is sidelined. In the Bears' preseason Week 2 loss to the Bengals , everyone who suited up at left tackle for the Bears looked outmatched by Cincinnati's backups and rookie pass rushers. Even Braxton Jones, who had distinguished himself earlier in training camp, has fallen far over the past week.
That's an untenable situation for a team hoping to take another step towards Super Bowl contention. Hopefully, Trapilo returns sometime in September and looks as good as he did back in January before he got hurt. If not, the Bears could be in trouble.
One of the most popular players among Bears fans since the 2026 NFL draft has been defensive tackle Jordan van den Berg. His perfect Relative Athletic Score (RAS) wowed the Bears and convinced them to select him in the sixth round, and he has lived up to every expectation and then some since then.
After a slow start to training camp, van den Berg saw a training camp surge as he got some work in with the starters a couple of weeks ago. He's further impressed in both preseason games so far, especially after Saturday. Van den Berg was a menace against the Bengals , solidifying what was already a strong case for a roster spot.
There wasn't much room left for Hyppolite to fall after spending most of his rookie season as a healthy scratch, but this seems like rock bottom for him. The second-year player was nearly a complete ghost throughout training camp, only shining on one day in particular. Meanwhile, between returning linebackers, the signing of Devin Bush, and the drafting of Keyshaun Elliott, it's hard to see the Bears making room for Hyppolite on this year's roster.
Is it too soon to move off of a 2025 draft pick? Maybe. But in this business, it's often better to be too soon than too late.

title: Predicting Chicago Bears Final Roster: 5 Bubble Locks and 3 Surprise Cuts
full_text:
Roster cutdown day is almost upon us and the Chicago Bears will soon whittle their roster down to 53.
Cutdown day will fall on Sunday, Aug. 30 , and once Chicago's cuts go through, the Bears will be scouring the waiver wire to find other players who can help them, so the initial 53 could change rather quickly.
With cutdown day rapidly approaching, here's a look at five players who were previously viewed as being on the bubble that we now view as locks.
We also have three players who will fall short of making the 53-man roster and amount to at least mildly surprising cuts.
The rookie entered training camp as a cut candidate because of his status as a late-round pick and because he didn't show much during OTAs and minicamp .
However, van den Berg has flipped the script completely with great showings in training camp and in the preseason, with his preseason Week 2 performance being especially impressive.
It's no longer a question of if van den Berg makes the roster, but rather how big of a role he's going to have out of the gate.
While Ahmed has worked behind Roschon Johnson in both of the preseason games, he has outperformed Johnson in both , also.
The same can be said throughout camp, where Ahmed has clearly been the better back and one of the bigger standouts for Chicago overall.
What does Ahmed making the roster mean for Johnson? We'll touch on that shortly.
While Davis was blanked in the second preseason game, he was also out there with the ones on the opening series, which is a good sign for his roster chances .
Before that, Davis had been one of Chicago's bigger standouts in practice, and he had an outstanding showing in preseason Week 1, when he led all Bears pass-catchers in receptions and yards.
Davis' ability to play on special teams, including as a returner, will put him over the top.
While Ruben Hyppolite has come on strong of late, Sanborn has been the more consistent player during training camp and the preseason, and he's an experienced and solid special teams contributor, which is important for a backup linebacker.
This doesn't mean Hyppolite is cooked, however, and he could still make the roster, but he's going to need something specific to happen for him to do so. More on that shortly.
When the Bears signed Woods , we still did not know exactly what was up with Coby Bryant, which made Woods a question mark in terms of making the 53-man roster.
But now that Bryant is out for most or all of the season , Woods is going to make the roster for sure, even if Elijah Hicks returns from the PUP list before cutdown day.
We wouldn't exactly be shocked if Johnson is cut, as he has been pegged as a cut candidate all offseason long. But the fact that he has been the clear RB3 in the preseason suggests he might be safe.
That said, Johnson has done nothing to impress us with his preseason touches, and he has routinely been outperformed by Ahmed, both in practice and in exhibition play.
His special teams prowess and the injury to Kyle Monangai might save him, but for now, we think Johnson simply hasn't done enough to earn a roster spot.
It isn't normal to see a team part ways with a fourth-round pick in Year 2, which is why Hyppolite getting cut would be at least some semblance of a surprise.
While he has shown flashes, including in preseason Week 1, he also need a strong showing in the second preseason game, something Hyppolite failed to do.
He has not been as good as Sanborn, who is going to earn the LB4 spot in our projection, and at this point, Hyppolite's only chance to make the roster is if rookie linebacker Keyshaun Elliott remains on the shelf and starts the season on the PUP list.
However, NFL Network's Stacey Dales reported last week that the rookie is close to returning to practice, and if he does before cuts are made, that will be the death blow to Hyppolite's time in Chicago.
Coming off a signficant injury, Smith played a good amount of snaps for the Bears in 2023 and 2024, and with the injuries at cornerback, his chances of making the roster increased.
However, with Jaylon Johnson, Tyrique Stevenson, Kyler Gordon, Malik Muhammad, Jaylon Jones and Josh Blackwell all locks to make the roster, Smith is in a precarious spot. He also has not been able to stay healthy this offseason, which is another problem.
Even if Gordon stays on the PUP list through final cuts and opens up a spot for another cornerback, we still believe Smith will get cut, as Dontae Manning has been available and better this offseason, even with his struggles in preseason Week 2.

title: Two Rookies Land Among Bears' Highest Graded Players in Loss to Bengals
full_text:
Despite a humiliating preseason Week 2 loss to the Bengals , Saturday night's game wasn't all bad for the Chicago Bears. Defensive end Dayo Odeyingbo looked plenty motivated for a bounce-back season in the limited action he saw, nearly landing a crushing sack on Bengals quarterback Josh Johnson . And even though the starting offense was held out of the endzone on their lone drive of the night, Caleb Williams appeared in complete command.
Additionally, a few Bears players earned elite Pro Football Focus (PFF) grades for their efforts, including two rookies who could have outsized impacts in 2026, if they make the Bears' final 53-man roster . With that in mind, let's take a look at the three highest graded Bears from Saturday night's game.
The Bears did not register many splash plays in what was ultimately a 27-9 loss to the Bengals, but undrafted free agent (UDFA) rookie Skyler Thomas provided a big one. Early in the fourth quarter, he dove in front of a pass intended for Bengals tight end Jack Endries , ripping the ball away and surviving some rough contact with the ground to complete the takeaway.
Even before training camp started, Thomas was considered one of six UDFA's with the best odds to make the roster , and his performance on Saturday certainly helped his case. Aside from the nifty interception, he provided sticky coverage against Cincinnati's receivers, and his 88.2 PFF grade was the second highest from either team, behind only Bengals linebacker Liam Anderson.
There was plenty of blame to go around for the Bears' loss to the Bengals on Saturday, but not for Maurice Alexander. The former USFL receiver hauled in all five targets that came his way, racking up 60 yards in the process and securing an 87.3 PFF grade, the highest offensive grade for either team.
Alexander is currently fighting with fellow receivers Jahdae Walker and Kaden Davis for a roster spot in what could be a crowded wide receiver room. Walker impressed yet again with a leaping 36-yard catch against the Bengals while Davis has been steadily improving all throughout camp. If Alexander can repeat this performance in the Bears' final preseason game against the Tennessee Titans, Ben Johnson and receivers coach Antwaan Randle El could have a tough decision on their hands.
Van den Berg's late training camp surge has carried over into the preseason, making the sixth-round rookie a near lock to make the roster. In two preseason games against the Browns and Bengals, van den Berg has played like a man possessed, racing left and right, up and down the field, providing quality play against both the run and the pass.
Though he still hasn't registered a sack this preseason, van den Berg has been credited for multiple pressures in each game, and against the Bengals he showcased impressive effort in chasing down the ball carrier on an outside run and stopping him for no gain. He also channeled a little of the spirit of Chicago Bulls legend Dennis Rodman when he dove at Bengals quarterback Sean Clifford as he raced out of bounds.
Van den Berg earned an elite 84.4 grade from PFF for that performance, and even that felt a tad low. Still, it's a testament to how far van den Berg has come since OTAs in the spring. If he continues developing at this pace, it won't be long before he gets some serious playing time in regular season games.
