title: Bears 53-Man Roster Projections 4.0: Who Will Stick Around After Two Preseason Games?
full_text:
The Chicago Bears suffered a disappointing 27-9 loss against the Bengals. Despite many of their starters seeing at least some action on both sides of the ball, they struggled to keep up with Cincinnati (especially on defense) as soon as the first whistle blew.
Nevertheless, a few players still helped themselves with strong performances against the Bengals. At the same time, others might've hurt their roster chances when the Bears are tasked with cutting down to 53 players next week.
We predicted a few significant changes to the Bears roster in our previous 53-man roster prediction after the preseason opener against Cleveland. We followed a similar script after Saturday night's blowout loss against Cincinnati.
QB (3): Caleb Williams, Tyson Bagent, Case Keenum
RB (4): D'Andre Swift, Kyle Monangai, Salvon Ahmed, Roschon Johnson
WR (5): Luther Burden III, Rome Odunze, Kalif Raymond, Zavion Thomas, Jahdae Walker
TE (3): Colston Loveland, Cole Kmet, Sam Roush
OL (9): Braxton Jones, Joe Thuney, Garrett Bradbury, Jonah Jackson, Darnell Wright, Logan Jones, Theo Benedet, Jordan McFadden, Ozzy Trapilo
DL (10): Montez Sweat, Austin Booker, Grady Jarrett, Gervon Dexter Sr., Dayo Odeyingbo, Neville Gallimore, Daniel Hardy, Jordan van den Berg, Kentavius Street, Marcus Davenport, (Shemar Turner (IR)
LB (6): Devin Bush, T.J. Edwards, D'Marco Jackson, Keyshaun Elliott, Jack Sanborn, Ruben Hyppolite II, (Noah Sewell - IR)
CB (6): Jaylon Johnson, Kyler Gordon, Tyrique Stevenson, Malik Muhammad II, Josh Blackwell, CB6
S (4): Dillon Thieneman, Cam Lewis, Xavier Woods, Elijah Hicks, ( Coby Bryant - IR)
Specialist (3): K Cairo Santos, P Tory Taylor, LS Beau Gardner
Kiran Amegadjie gets cut: Amegadjie needed to stack solid performances to stick around. Unfortunately, he stacked disappointing ones. Unless another team loved him as a draft prospect and thinks he would benefit from a change of scenery, the Bears will probably be able to get him back on the practice squad. That is, if they're not ready to entirely give up on him.
Roschon Johnson makes the roster: ....by default? The Bears have been giving running back Roschon Johnson a ton of work in the two preseason contests. He responded with a solid performance against Cleveland and a relatively disappointing one (at least compared to what it could've been) against Cincinnati. With Kyle Monangai recovering from an ankle injury, I think they'll opt to keep four backs. That'll either be good news for RoJo or whoever they snag off waivers to fill that role.
Marcus Davenport makes the roster: Defensive end Marcus Davenport, whom the team picked up off the scrap heap last week , is a lock to make the roster. The team desperately needs to improve their pass rush, and they think the veteran can move the needle in that regard. I'm not sure if he'll be anything more than depth, but edge rusher depth is something that every team covets.
Jaylon Jones gets cut for... CB6: The Bears need to add another player to the cornerback room. Whether it be a pickup on the waiver wire or a trade for Joey Porter Jr. (a guy can dream, right?), their current depth just isn't going to cut it. Josh Blackwell's status as a core special teamer will probably make him a lock to make the roster. Jaylon Jones is probably a bit more sound in coverage, but he could fall victim to a numbers game.
Kaden Davis: The dragon was slain. The mighty Kaden Davis, who received incredible reviews coming out of training camp , finally looked mortal. He muffed a kickoff and failed to register a catch in the stat sheet. Despite the hype he's received, I still think they'll like their odds of getting the 27-year-old back on the practice squad. They'd also ideally prefer to keep five receivers and use the roster spot on someone with a better chance of contributing on game day.
Jamree Kromah: Defensive end Jamree Kromah quietly had another solid performance against Cincinnati. Aside from Jordan van den Berg looking like a monster among men, he's arguably been their best defensive player over their first two preseason contests. Still, he falls victim to a numbers game here. He's a lock to bring back on the practice squad if he can make it there, though. If injuries strike at DE, he'd surely get the first call over another player on the street.
James Lynch: Defensive tackle James Lynch also falls victim to a numbers game. They might not have a game-wrecker at the position (besides sixth-round selection and future Hall of Famer Jordan van den Berg, of course), but they do have a lot of depth there . They'd love to get him back on the practice squad, as well. However, with him carving out a role as a rotational contributor over the past few years, he's far from a lock to get past the waiver wire.
Terell Smith: Cornerback Terell Smith was a dark-horse candidate to start opposite Jaylon Johnson this season . However, he needed to stack strong training camp and preseason performances to do that. Unfortunately, he's once again been plagued by injuries and hasn't had an opportunity to do so. He's shown promise whenever he's been healthy over his first few seasons, and that might be enough to land with another roster. However, he's also a strong practice squad candidate if they can get him back into the fold there.
Beanie Bishop Jr.: Unlike Smith, Beanie Bishop did make a positive impression last week against Cleveland, snagging two easy interceptions. However, he failed to build on that performance against Cincinnati. It feels like the Bears will add to the cornerback room instead of sticking with their current depth. Bishop's lack of impact on special teams would probably make him a casualty in that regard.

title: Bears Should Keep Tabs on These Chiefs, Cardinals Players Who Could Get Cut
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals and Kansas City Chiefs each have a cut candidate the Chicago Bears should be keeping an eye on.
In an article listing six cut candidates ahead of cutdown day on Aug. 30, Bleacher Report's Gary Davenport mentions Arizona Cardinals running back Trey Benson and Kansas City Chiefs cornerback Kristian Fulton.
Davenport cites Arizona's crowded backfield that also includes Jeremiyah Love, Tyler Allgeier and James Conner as the reason why Benson could get axed in the desert. Bam Knight is another player who appears more likely to stick over Benson.
Meanwhile, Davenport thinks Fulton could get booted from the roster because he's buried on the depth chart behind guys like Mansoor Delane, Nohl Williams, L'Jarius Sneed and Kader Kohou.
Here's why the Bears should be keeping tabs on both.
The Bears' running back situation is a bit of an issue right now.
Not only is Kyle Monangai dealing with a hyperextended knee that leaves his status up in the air for Week 1, but the team's favorite for the RB3 role, Roschon Johnson, has posted a pedestrian performance during the preseason.
Unless you're a believer in Salvon Ahmed, it's safe to say the Bears could use a move at running back.
A former third-round pick, Benson saw his 2025 campaign cut short due to injury, but he did rip off 5.5 yards per carry in four games, which shows some promise.
Benson hasn't been more than a limited participant in training camp, though, as he works his way back from last year's knee injury, so that is obviously something to monitor.
But if Benson gets healthy and the Cardinals end up cutting him or are willing to deal him for a late-round pick swap, the Bears should have interest.
The Bears have seen a littany of injuries in the secondary during the offseason. At cornerback, Kyler Gordon and Jaylon Jones are both injured, and that could leave Chicago depending on a rookie in Malik Muhammad to start in the slot come Week 1.
As if that wasn't concerning enough, Tyrique Stevenson is slated to be the starter opposite Jaylon Johnson and we saw how badly that went in 2025, when Stevenson got himself benched .
Fulton's career has been a disappointment overall, and there have been injury issues for him, but he is still a fine insurance policy to have around, as evidenced by his 55.6% completion percentage and 81.7 passer rating allowed when targeted last season.
Chicago could do a lot worse than Fulton when it comes to adding a backup. He should be on their radar for a cheap trade or waiver claim.

title: Top 7 Chicago Bears Trade Candidates Entering Preseason Week 3
full_text:
We are through two weeks of the preseason and that means we are inching closer to the Chicago Bears putting together their initial 53-man roster.
This is the time of year when we start looking for teams to trade their spare parts, and by spare parts we mean players who aren't going to make the roster but could have under different circumstances at a given position.
We saw this in the Sunday night trade between the San Francisco 49ers and New Orleans Saints. The Niners had an extra running back but needed a linebacker, and the opposite was true for the Saints, so the two teams swapped Deion Jones and Zamir White.
The Bears have at least seven players who can be viewed as possible trade candidates. Here's who they are.
Ozzy Trapilo's faster-than-expected recovery from a torn patellar tendon has completely flipped the tackle position on its head in Chicago.
Even if he isn't ready for Week 1, Trapilo is likely to avoid beginning the season on an injured list, leaving one less tackle spot open on the initial 53.
That is bad news for Kiran Amegadjie and Jedrick Wills, both of whom are now more firmly on the roster bubble after starting the offseason as left tackle competitors. If one is heading for the cut pile, the Bears would be amenable to trading whoever loses out.
We would not put Braxton Jones or Theo Benedet anywhere near the roster bubble, but Chicago could be open to trading one of them given the situation and if the right offer comes along.
That said, Amegadjie and Wills are far more likely to be moved than Jones and Benedet.
With Jordan van den Berg ascending and locked-in to make the 53-man roster, and with the recent addition of Marcus Davenport , Chicago now has a more crowded situation upfront.
The Bears carried five defensive tackles on their initial 53-man roster last year and have Gervon Dexter, Grady Jarrett, Neville Gallimore and van den Berg as roster locks and that probably leaves just one spot up for grabs.
At defensive end, Chicago is likely to keep no more than five, also, and they have Montez Sweat, Dayo Odeyingbo, Austin Booker and Daniel Hardy all locked-in, and Davenport is likely to make Chicago's roster, also, after being signed recently.
Kentavius Street and James Lynch appear to be the best bets to make the 53-man roster out of the remaining defensive linemen, but one of them will likely have to go. Knowing that, don't be surprised to see either one traded before cuts.
The Bears have been ravaged by injuries in the secondary during the offseason, but Smith could still miss the cut, making him a trade candidate.
As things stand now, Jaylon Johnson, Tyrique Stevenson, Malik Muhammad and Josh Blackwell are locked in, and if Kyler Gordon and Jaylon Jones can get healthy, that gives the Bears six cornerbacks, which is how many they kept last year.
Smith isn't proven, but he has shown promise over two seasons after posting a 76.5 Pro Football Focus coverage grade in 2024. It's possible teams will be interested in a trade in order to avoid running the risk of missing out on him on the waiver wire.

title: Should the Chicago Bears Consider Trading For Joey Porter Jr.?
full_text:
The Chicago Bears fell flat on both sides of the ball in their 27-9 preseason loss against the Cincinnati Bengals. However, their defensive performance was especially alarming (or at least as alarming as a mid-August performance can be).
Yes, they didn't have all of their defensive starters on the field. A lot of them were early on, though. Conversely, NONE of the Bengals' offensive starters suited up. In fact, a few of their key backups didn't suit up, either. That didn't stop their second- and third-string offense from marching down the field on a 14-play, seven-minute drive to start the game.
Sure, it was a small sample size. It was also a preseason game, and they held them out of the end zone. The sky is not yet falling. It's still fair to point out that the Bengals' practice squad moved the ball at will on Saturday night regardless of who was on the field. It shouldn't have been competitive early on.
The performance has led some to question whether the Bears could add to the cornerback room ahead of Week 1. CHGO's Adam Hoge predicted that they'll surely do so .
"I'm telling you right now, with what they have, they're going to add somebody," Hoge said. "I don't know if it's a trade, I don't know if it's a waiver wire claim, rosters change at the end of the 53 when they need to be set."
Hear me out... rumors are swirling that Joey Porter Jr. is reportedly unhappy in Pittsburgh. He's in the final year of his rookie contract, and NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported last week that teams around the league think he could be available. NFL legend James Harrison (who played with Porter's dad and could conceivably be a soundboard for the cover man) also said he should hold out if the Steelers don't put pen to paper before the season.
It's a messy situation that could become A LOT messier once the season kicks off. That could cause the Steelers to lower the asking price for Porter, who has already established himself as one of the league's premier cornerbacks. The fact that only a select number of teams (ones that are both in win-now mode and have a boatload of future cap space) would also limit the potential suitors.
With the Bears coming off their best season in over a decade, they clearly check off the first box mentioned above. Conversely, they don't check off the second box yet, but they easily could after making a few cuts they're already probably considering at this stage.
The Bears currently rank 19th in 2027 with just over $16 million in available cap space. According to Spotrac, they would save $15 million by getting Dayo Odeyingbo's contract off the books next season, and another $12.75 million by cutting Grady Jarrett . The site also indicates that they'd save nearly $8.5 million by cutting Kyler Gordon .
It's safe to assume they would offload those deals to land Porter, whose ability to thrive in both press coverage and man-to-man situations makes him a perfect fit for Dennis Allen's defense, in a heartbeat.
The most significant aspect to consider when weighing the cost of trading for Porter is what comes next. First off, Ben Johnson doesn't seem to be too fond of Kyler Gordon. His future will be up in the air if he doesn't return to the lineup and play at a high level upon doing so. That opens up a potential void at nickelback.
Meanwhile, Tyrique Stevenson is playing out the final year of his rookie contract, and he hasn't shown nearly enough to make them feel comfortable committing to him long-term . Jaylon Johnson will also be entering the final year of his contract in 2027. Before last season began, he hinted about getting back to the negotiation table after outplaying his deal in the 2024 campaign. Assuming he returns to his high level of play this season, he probably won't want to play out the final year of his contract. He'd be an obvious holdout candidate without a new deal.
Also, this might be my Madden franchise GM brain doing overtime... but Johnson is still a great player. I don't love the idea of giving up a second-round pick and some change for Porter, but it becomes pretty palatable if the Bears can recoup similar capital for their star cornerback (albeit a bit less, based on the fact that Johnson will be 28 and Porter just turned 26) if there is fear of a holdout next offseason.
On the other hand, the Bears could be in a situation where they have to cave to Johnson's demands. Can you imagine their defense without him in the fold right now? Safe to assume his agent will pull that one out at negotiations.
We still haven't gotten any clarity on the Kyler Gordon front . If they think he can be back before October, then they should stand pat with their current CB room. Reap the benefits of a relatively soft early schedule and see if either Stevenson or Muhammad can provide stability on the outside after Gordon brings some juice to the nickelback position.
Alternatively, if they don't expect to see him until midseason (or after that point, considering they haven't given a timeline), then they should do whatever they can to improve the cornerback room.
That's the only way they can survive without expecting the offense to win shootouts every week. If they could land Porter without giving up a first-round pick, then he would be well worth the price of admission for a team on the rise.

title: The Key Questions for Chicago Bears Coming Out of Loss to Bengals
full_text:
Every game in the NFL produces answers, and those answers lead to more questions.
Even preseason games, like Saturday's 27-9 Bears loss to Cincinnati, follow this pattern. The questions might even be more numerous because it is only preseason.
It might be what happened in the game or even before it, but there were more questions arising from the Bengals-Bears game and practice, carrying over to this week's Titans practice and game.
Here are seven big question to come out of a Bears loss at Cincinnati.
Bears will never be a superbowl contending team until Poles gets the DL, primarily the pass rush right.
Although they used starters against the Bengals, one of their starting edge players didn't play at all. Dayo Odeyingbo was in for 16 snaps coming back from Achilles surgery, six more than Montez Sweat. Yet, Booker didn't suit up and hadn't been listed with any injured players.
The Bears need Booker healthy badly for the start of the season. They can't stand to have  the same thing happen that happened last year, when he was injured on special teams in a preseason game and missed half the schedule. Then again, if Booker isn't hurt, then why rest him when they're playing Montez Sweat?
I don’t care that Grady Jarrett is a tenured vet. Put him in the game and let him hurt someone on the other team
Apparently he ranks behind Cam Lewis in the safety pecking order because they started Lewis and then brought in Woods.
Eventually, Woods finished with 14 reps on defense. Woods, who is 31, has played over 6,800 snaps at safety in his career. Lewis has been a slot cornerback as much as he has been a safety, and has been a sub as often as he has been a starter.
Are the Bears unhappy with what they've had from Woods?
Not seeing much on film w/ the Xavier Woods injury. 3 plays before he left the game, he chased down Dylan Sampson on a screen. He appeared to briefly motion down the #Bears sideline after the play, but he stayed in on the next 2 plays and appeared to be moving fine. #DaBears pic.twitter.com/JzjLrD6scS
He signed on Aug. 17. Ben Johnson said he would need to be ramped up a bit to start practicing. It's almost a week and he hasn't been involved in practice and certainly didn't play. Did he injure himself signing the contract? Ogunjobi signed and failed a physical, then never played for the Bears.
Maybe Davenport just requires a bigger ramp based on all of his past injuries?
Grady Jarrett and Marcus Davenport on my DLine pic.twitter.com/mglnpWoCXN
When the Bears reported for camp, GM Ryan Poles was re-assuring everyone about some injuries.
Poles said Elijah Hicks, their backup safety to Coby Bryant and Dillon Thieneman, had an injury.
"Elijah Hicks has some discomfort in his shin; we got that taken care of," Poles said. "So that’s going to take a little bit of time, but he’s on the mend, he’s walking around; we don’t see that as anything major."
Hicks hasn't been taken off of the PUP list.
Poles also said something else, this about rookie linebacker Keyshaun Elliott.
"Keyshaun Elliott has some discomfort in his back; we took care of that," Poles said of their fifth-round pick. "He’s in really good shape, if you saw him walking around you would have no idea — he’s running. Obviously, there’s return-to-play protocol where you’re getting back to being a football player in terms of your strength, your conditioning, so he’ll be in that.
The two players they "took care of" still haven't practiced almost a month later.
Who else did they "take care of" and who's doing the taking care?
Like Hicks, Kevin White had a shin issue and then the first Bears pick of the 2015 draft never really did anything in his career. A back injury is never a good thing for a linebacker.
Has anyone heard anything on Elijah Hicks injury & possible return timeline? Reason I ask is he was a key contributor & big asset on Special Teams last season.
With people covering the team all but giving the practice squad journeyman a roster spot after one preseason effort, Davis came out of Week 2 in preseason with only one target and no catches. For Davis to make the roster as a fifth or sixth receiver, he'd need to be entirely useful as a return/coverage man. He had two kick returns of 29 and 19 yards and had punt returns of 12 and minus-1 yard. None of this speaks to kicking down the door and making a roster. Davis has to be so good that he causes the Bears to decide against keeping a player at another needed position. Game 2 was not that good.
I don't think anyone on the #Bears is a winner today,  but there are some losers. Kaden Davis- he just is a bad returner. Has good speed and shimmy with the ball in his hands,  but can't be relied to catch the ball. Logan Jones- two bad snaps just doesn't cut it for an older
His only preseason effort to date was 2-of-5 with a missed receiver near the goal line. His practice at Cincinnati turned up a nice completion to Dexter Lawrence, the Bengals defensive lineman. Including that one, he threw three interceptions in practice to go with some good red zone work. Johnson suggested the pass Williams overthrew against Cincinnati to Colston Loveland should have gone elsewhere, but if a receiver is open for a TD and is spotted who cares if it's where the coach intends for the ball to be thrown? There was nothing but talk of the more accurate Williams when camp started and as it's progressed there has been less and less evidence of it.
Caleb Williams on his focus and mistakes from Today: “I felt like I was pretty on Today. We had one or two batted balls, and then I had the wrong incompletion on purpose just because the linebacker got up under it. It's a thing you can control. There are so many details within… pic.twitter.com/7GwGPz7hlH
Johnson keeps getting asked about this and the answer is always the same. Status quo hasn't changed with the injured calf muscle. No one is sure.
At this point, it appears they're hoping Malik Muhammad can play there instead, but Muhammad struggled again in that position in Saturday's game. He's more of a boundary corner.
Kyler Gordon is soft. Ben thinks it, he just can’t say it about one of his players. https://t.co/k5AJ1WoQa0

title: Bengals Could Fix Big Weakness With Recently Released Free Agent
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals already have a lot of bodies in their running back room, but an unexpected name on waivers could be too intriguing to ignore.
The Arizona Cardinals waived Trey Benson with an injury designation on Monday. If Benson clears waivers, he will revert to Arizona's injured reserve. The Bengals should at least consider placing a claim on the former third-round pick.
Benson's current knee injury obviously has to factor into the equation. If the Bengals are comfortable with his medical outlook, though, there is enough talent and long-term potential to justify adding him to an already crowded position group.
For starters, the Cardinals selected Benson with the No. 66 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft, following an impressive career at Florida State.
Injuries have clearly kept him from establishing himself as a major part of the team's offense, but Benson has been productive when given opportunities. He has rushed for 451 yards on 92 carries over two seasons, averaging 4.9 yards per attempt.
Last season, Benson was even more efficient in limited action, averaging 5.5 yards per carry on 29 attempts. Durability has been his issue. He only appeared in four games.
Landing with the Bengals could be an ideal scenario for a player like Benson, who is trying to re-establish himself after a rough start to his NFL career. Chase Brown is firmly established atop the depth chart, with veteran Samaje Perine providing experience behind him.
The Bengals also have Tahj Brooks, Gary Brightwell, Kendall Milton, Kentrel Bullock, and Jamal Haynes competing for reserve roles.
Brooks is the favorite for the third running back job behind Brown and Perine. Benson could come in and compete for that job.
Brooks — and a surplus of training camp bodies — shouldn't keep the Bengals from pursuing a player with Benson's profile.
Benson, still just 24 years old, was considered one of the more talented backs in the 2024 draft class and has shown flashes of legitimate impact at the NFL level. Players with that combination of age and talent don't typically become available during roster cutdown season.
The biggest question is Benson's health.
The Cardinals' decision to waive him with an injury designation means the Bengals would have to determine whether the knee issue is worth inheriting. If the Bengals believe Benson can return to full strength, however, his long-term upside could outweigh the value of keeping another depth option already on the roster.
Simply put, Benson could be one of the more interesting players available on the waiver wire this week. The Bengals' front office should, at the very least, consider what he could bring to their team.

title: 3 Free Agents the Bengals NEED to Sign Before Week 1
full_text:
The Bengals released veteran lineman Cody Ford following a string of poor performances. Ford had been with the team for three seasons, serving as the primary swing tackle throughout that span.
Zac Taylor preached faith in the young players currently on the roster as possible replacements at swing tackle. However, Taylor also emphasized that all options are on the table at the position, including a potential free-agent addition.
"We're always open to everything." Taylor said when addressing the depth at offensive tackle.
While the tackle options on the free agent market are few and far between, there are plenty of options to come in and serve as a quality backup. Here are three veterans that the Bengals should consider signing to bolster their offensive tackle depth:
This is by far the most obvious option. Williams was the first pick made in the Zac Taylor era and went on to be an average-level starter at left tackle before Orlando Brown Jr. replaced him in 2023.
Williams swapped to right tackle at that point and remained there during his time with the Cardinals. He received his fair share of criticism during his time with the Bengals as a starter, but would be a well-above-average option as a swing tackle right now.
Williams could be open to returning to the team that drafted him, with the goal of finishing what he and the Bengals started when they reached the Super Bowl in 2021. As the first tackle off the bench, it would give him a great opportunity to re-establish his value across the league should an injury hit Brown or Amarius Mims.
Beachum is still playing well at 37 years old. While he finished with an overall grade of 51.6 on Pro Football Focus last season, he still stood tall with a pass-blocking grade of 78.3, doing so as a swing tackle.
Beachum is entering his 14th season in the NFL and has played at an average-to-above-average level throughout his career. Having never appeared in a Super Bowl, joining an offense with playmakers at every corner could sway Beachum to join Cincinnati and compete for his first Super Bowl.
He would bring more urgency to win a Super Bowl now to an offense already feeling pressure to win.
Another veteran who is likely to sign with a competitor this season.
Lucas had the worst season of his twelve-year career last season with the Browns, though it came in a limited role. The Browns' offense was also a mess last year, and the team turned over its entire offensive line this offseason.
Outside of last season, Lucas has shown quality play during his career as a backup tackle. He earned a 75.4 overall PFF grade in 2024 during his time with the Commanders, including a 79.1 grade as a pass blocker that season across 464 total snaps.
With Jalen Rivers inconsistent performance at left tackle this preseason, the best option at swing tackle for the Bengals could very well not be on the roster currently. Javon Foster has looked like the most capable swing tackle on the roster for the Bengals, and even he has not proven to be someone you can feel great about.
Considering the lack of any young player standing out, the team should absolutely be looking at free agent options on the tackle market. This could easily become a situation similar to Dalton Risner last year, when the Bengals signed him right after the preseason. Risner went on to become a key cog in the offensive line's improvement last season, and the team may look to test those waters once more a year later.

title: C.J. Uzomah Signs 1-Day Deal To Retire with Cincinnati Bengals, Lines Up Post-NFL Work With Team's TV, Radio Shows
full_text:
C.J. Uzomah was back at Paycor Stadium today to ceremoniously retire as a member of the Cincinnati Bengals , but there are many more trips planned as the former tight end will be working with Dan Hoard on some television and radio shows.
After taking in practice with his wife and young daughter, Uzomah, wearing a sharp Bengals button-down shirt he purchased during the Super Bowl season, spoke with reporters about some of his fondest memories as well as why it was important for him to retire as a Bengal.
“Even when I left, I was like, 'I want to end my career in Cincinnati,'" Uzomah said. "I actually did this math because in my head, I was like, 'I spent so much time here. I want to figure out how much time.' The answer is 21.21 percent repeating is the amount of life that I spent here. And I don't remember the first 21.21 percent of my life to begin with.
"If you think about it from that perspective, I spent most of my maturing days – I'm probably still maturing – here. And all of my fondest memories are here. I live in Nashville, but this is always going to be my second home.”
Among the fond memories Uzomah listed were the touchdown catch in the 2021 playoff victory against the Raiders – “but the celebration was so terrible” – playing in Super Bowl LVI on a torn MCL and his second touchdown against the Jaguars when he ran the wrong route and Joe Burrow still found him for the score.
That was a Week 4 Thursday night game when Burrow famously screamed “You can’t zero me” and Uzomah had 95 receiving yards, which remained his career high.
So it only makes sense that the Bengals will be bringing him back to be Ruler of the Jungle this season in Week 4 against the Jaguars.
A fifth-round pick in 2015, Uzomah played seven seasons for the Bengals, logging 79 games with 61 starts.
He signed a three-year, $18.3 million extension in 2019 after Zac Taylor was hired as head coach.
Following the Super Bowl season, he signed a three-year, $24 million contract with the New York Jets, where he played for two seasons. In 2024, he played for the Philadelphia Eagles and won a Super Bowl, although he was injured for the entire postseason run.
Uzomah nearly missed playing in Super Bowl LVI for the Bengals.
He tore his MCL in the AFC Championship Game win against the Kansas City Chiefs and showed up to the sendoff party at the stadium on crutches.
“After he got hurt in the AFC Championship game, I think he maybe practiced one time,” tight end Drew Sample said. “I mean, he could barely move. And to his f--king credit, he went out there and played in the Super Bowl and played like 35-40 snaps. It was just really impressive.
“The whole time we're like 'Dude, are you sure you want to do this?' He kept saying he was going to be ready. And whether he did enough to get ready or he felt like crap and just played through it, I remember being like, 'Damn. That's a real professional.'”
Uzomah said as soon as he found out it wasn’t an ACL, he knew he was playing.
“Unless something was severely broken, I was playing in that game,” Uzomah said. “When the early reports said it wasn’t the ACL, I was like ‘I’ll be fine. I can deal with the pain.’”
At the Super Bowl sendoff party, Uzomah played to the crowd by chucking his knee brace.
ICYMI: CJ Uzomah is officially active for today’s Super Bowl! #SuperBowl #RuleItAll pic.twitter.com/URXzxOQqXZ
"That was classic," Sample said. "But we were like, 'Uh, you might need that.'"
The season before the Super Bowl run, Uzomah ruptured his Achilles in Week 2 and fought back to be ready in time for the start of 2021.
In 2018, he played through a painful shoulder injury after taking over as the starter when Tyler Eifert and Tyler Kroft suffered season-ending injuries.
And he’s not slowing down in retirement. In addition to working with Bengals TV and radio shows, he has written a Broadway musical – although he said he needs someone else to write the music and lyrics – about a football player.
He also has landed a part in a TV series about golf that has yet to be released. Uzomah, who made $38,034,514 in career earnings,  also invested in the project and said they have already shot the pilot.
After staying in the shadows his rookie year, Uzomah let his personality shine and became one of the more popular Bengals among the fan base. And he’ll have to chance to continue connecting with him in his new endeavor with the team-produced shows.
“Rookie year I was very just chill and didn't wanna step on anybody's toes,” he said. “I didn't wanna be myself too much. Then after that, being with Tyler Eifert, definitely helped. Seeing him just be like, ‘Do whatever you want to, man. It's fine.
“And that helped a lot. I was just myself – goofy, quirky,” he continued. “And I think if I was that way and wasn't good on the field, then that would have been something different. But I gave it my all and tried my best and thankfully that was enough for the most part. And I think they respected that in a way, that I was having fun and also performing well.”
Uzomah is tied for eighth in Bengals history for games played by a tight end with 79.

title: Bengals Get Positive Injury News on Veteran B.J. Hill Ahead of Season Opener
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals got another encouraging sign from veteran defensive tackle B.J. Hill on Monday as he continues to work his way back to full strength.
Hill participated in 11-on-11 work for the first time this training camp. The 31-year-old worked with T.J. Slaton and the second-team defense during that period, as Cincinnati continues to increase Hill's workload gradually.
"To be honest, I am truly blessed to be back out there," Hill said after practice. "What I've been through the last couple of months, it wasn't an easy road. A lot of frustration, a lot of ups and downs, but I don't take it for granted. It was really awesome just being back out there."
It's another significant step for Hill, who opened training camp on the Physically Unable to Perform list while recovering from a lower-body injury. The Bengals cleared him to practice on Aug. 15, and Monday's reps mark the latest progression toward having one of the team's most experienced defensive linemen ready for the regular season.
Hill's return to 11-on-11 work comes more than a week after he participated in his first practice of camp. Cincinnati has, understandably, taken a cautious approach with the veteran defensive tackle.
"The hardest part was watching my guys out there grinding when I'm not out there," Hill said earlier this month . "That's really the hard part. So I've been doing everything possible to try to get back. It just takes time."
Working with the second-team defense doesn't necessarily mean Hill has fallen down the depth chart. The Bengals are still ramping him up after he missed most of training camp — and getting through full-team periods is another box he must check off before returning to his normal workload.
Hill remains one of the team's most reliable defensive linemen, alongside star Dexter Lawrence. He started in all 17 games last season, finishing with 66 tackles, five tackles for loss, and four sacks. He was also named a team captain.
The veteran has been a staple of Cincinnati's defense since arriving in a trade with the New York Giants, like Lawrence, ahead of the 2021 season. He's been a full-time starter since the Bengals' Super Bowl run and signed a three-year, $33 million contract to remain with the Bengals in the 2025 offseason.
For Hill, returning to team drills is another positive development as Week 1 approaches. He admits that the past few months have been challenging, but he's in a good place with the season opener 20 days away.
"Just not being where I wanted to be health-wise," Hill said of the frustrations. "I feel like some days I felt really good. Some days, the next day, I might not feel as good. It's kind of frustrating, and also not being out there with my guys. When you're a leader on this team, you want to be out there fighting with your guys, putting in the hard work and the time with those guys."

title: Bengals Announce Retired Fan-Favorite Player as a 2026 Ruler of the Jungle
full_text:
The Bengals are welcoming back a key member of the 2021 Super Bowl team as Ruler of the Jungle for Week 4 of the 2026 season. C.J. Uzomah just retired as a Bengal today and will lead the big cheer against the Jaguars.
The 10-year veteran got drafted by the Bengals in 2015 with the 157th overall pick in the fifth round out of Auburn.
Uzomah, 33, is at practice today and sent a heartfelt goodbye message to fans.
"History has a way of repeating itself, and there’s no place I’d want to formally announce my retirement than the place that started it all for me and gave me my chance," Uzomah posted on X today. "The place I will always think of as my second home and will always hold a special place in me and my family’s heart. The place where we won a playoff game for the first time since before I was born, and went on an odds-defying run to the Super Bowl. A place where I’ve met people who have become like brothers to me. Cincinnati, thank you for everything. Who Dey Forever."
It mirrored his goodbye message back in 2022.
"I've had a difficult time putting into words what this city has meant to my family and me over the years," Uzomah penned . "As I look back on my time in this organization, I couldn't be more proud of what we have accomplished together. I came into this city 7 years ago as a boy, and I am leaving now as a man. You have allowed this goofy kid to be himself. I couldn't be more grateful for that. I want to start by thanking the Brown Family for taking a chance on me and allowing me to grow as a player and a person.
"To my guys in the locker room - every one of you that I've ever stepped on the field and fought with - I will forever cherish the battles we had together. To the coaches I've learned from who have become my mentors and the trainers I've worked with who have become my family, I say thank you. I am blessed to have you and so many others, whose relationships will last a lifetime. I truly wouldn't be the man I am today without your constant love, support, and encouragement."
Meanwhile, Cincinnati is back at work on Monday afternoon with a looming final preseason game on Friday against Philadelphia.
Zac Taylor detailed what the next few days will look like for Cincinnati before getting close to a game-week schedule starting next week.
"These next two days I still look at like a training camp format," Taylor said. "I know the day has changed for you all and us, but I'm still really focused on getting some stuff installed and ironing out some stuff that we've been working on in the last 25 days."

title: Three Cincinnati Bengals Who Solidified Their Spot on  the 53-Man Roster in Preseason Game vs. Bears
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals have to trim their roster from 89 – following the release of offensive lineman Cody Ford – to 53 by 6 p.m. Sunday.
Monday afternoon before practice, head coach Zac Taylor said anybody who plays in the preseason finale Friday night at Philadelphia should not feel as though they are a lock to make the 53-man roster.
“I don't feel like anybody should feel comfortable going in this last week that they've made the team,” he said. “That's a big part of it, is we want guys that we can depend on. So they’ve got to continue to be consistent and accountable over this last week through the Philly game. And we'll make our decisions this weekend.”
In reality, there are multiple players who will play Friday night who are locks to make the team.
Some of them were before Saturday night’s 27-9 win against Chicago.
A few feel as though they cemented their spots with their performance against the Bears.
It’s been building for a while with all of the plays he’s made in practice and his strong performance against the Detroit Lions in the preseason opener, buy Meyers cemented his spot with another impressive all-around performance against the Bears.
Meyers led the team with five receptions, and his six targets were second to Colbie Young (eight). He also had 41 receiving yards and got a chance to return two kickoffs and two punts.
His kickoff returns were for 29 and 25 yards, while his punt returns went for 25 and 9 yards.
And if the eye test wasn’t telling enough, Josh Johnson said the quarterbacks have been talking about Meyers since the spring and went on to offer an even stronger endorsement.
“Dohnte pops off the film,” he said. “I think now you're just seeing him put his mind with his ability, and that's a great sign for a young player to be able to do that as quickly as he's doing it.
“All of the quarterbacks have confidence in him,” Johnson added. “You don’t need to say a lot when you’ve got Joe speaking out about him, Flacco always throwing the ball to him, and when I get out there, we throw the ball to him. There’s a reason. He’s been showing me there are no limitations to his game.”
The 2024 second-round pick actually might have sealed his spot in the win against the Lions, when played 48 percent of the snap and recorded five tackles, one shy of the team lead, and a sack.
Jenkins has not played up to his second-round draft slot the last two seasons, and with the additions of T.J. Slaton last year and Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen this spring, he was on notice coming into training camp.
What was so telling about Jenkins’ standing in the eyes of the coaches Saturday night was how little he played, logging just nine snaps.
Guys given the final three quarters off should feel pretty good.
Then again, Jenkins could be a trade piece, and limiting his snaps could be a way of preserving his value. Regardless, he’s going to be a 53-man roster somewhere this time next week.
The seventh-round rookie could be a big variable in whether the Bengals shop Jenkins.
He has two sacks in his first two preseason games, logging 1.5 against the Bears and a half sack against the Lions.
“I’ve seen cleaner tackles in my life, but he did a good job coming clean, looping around, and kind of not wasting any space there, and closing down on the quarterback before you could really see him coming,” Taylor said. “Just like I say with any guys competing for some of these backup jobs — just the consistency. It doesn’t always happen. His flash play — it’s great to see his flash play. That was a big, big play, but we really want to see the consistency that if people in the game have to play five to 20 snaps, that you’re going to do your job and allow those around you to do their jobs as well.”
Robinson also has six pressures, which are tied for 12th in the league and are second on the team behind Isaiah Foskey’s eight.
It will be interesting to see how many snaps Jenkins gets Friday night, but you can expect Robinson and Meyers to play a lot.
Same goes for linebacker Swayze Bozeman, who hasn’t quite locked up a roster spot yet but is moving strongly in that direction.

title: Zac Taylor Starts Final 2026 Preseason Week With Injury Updates on Dax Hill, Bryan Cook, Swing Tackle Search
full_text:
The Bengals are back on the practice field this afternoon to continue 2026 training camp. Plenty of attention is on the injury list as multiple key secondary members continue building their strength back.
Zac Taylor gave the latest update on injuries to starting safety Bryan Cook and second boundary cornerback Dax Hill. Both have missed over two weeks of practice and both preseason games with the ailments.
Taylor did not commit to the two talents appearing in a practice this week, as less than three weeks remain until Week 1. "Continuing to make progress. I won't make any promises about whether they will practice this week or not, but still encouraged with what we're seeing from those guys," Taylor said.
The Bengals backups are barrelling toward the final (and first away) preseason game of the season on Friday night in Philadelphia.
Taylor and the Bengals got some great work in last week to carry over into the final preseason game week. It won't continue with Cody Ford on the roster, as the team just cut the versatile veteran lineman during an ongoing swing tackle battle. "I always think back to Cody. I mean, he served a lot of roles for us. A lot of times, not a lot of prep work," Taylor noted about Ford. "There were times we practiced him as a guard, and then the next week started him at tackle in games, having to block some big-time rushers in this league, and just always appreciative of the role Cody played for us, the attitude he had. "There was never, 'Man, he practiced me at guard all week, and now I'm playing tackle. He practiced me at tackle. I'm playing guard.' There was none of that. It was just whatever I got to do to help the team. And so he's made a really strong impression on me ever since the draft process. We liked him in the draft process, and then we acquired him years later, and he gave us three good years of football. And now I wish him the best on the next part of his journey."
He did not commit to the eventual swing tackle being on the current roster.
"I think we're always open to everything," Taylor said. "These guys are really competing. I feel like I'd like to see someone grab it and us be able to say that. But certainly, with time still in the practice, we got some stuff to sort out."
The franchise practices a few days in the afternoon this week before traveling to the City of Brotherly Love on Thursday.

title: Bengals Releasing Veteran Offensive Lineman Entering Final Week of 2026 Preseason
full_text:
The Bengals are moving on from veteran offensive lineman Cody Ford.
"The Bengals are releasing OL Cody Ford, who has played in 50 of 51 regular-season games with the team over three years in Cincinnati," Mike Garafolo posted on X .
Cincinnati has been searching for a semi-reliable swing tackle option to back up Amarius Mims and Orlando Brown Jr. this season, and it's clear Ford won't be that guy now. He played all over the line for Cincinnati since joining the team in 2023, but rarely at a palatable level.
He made 10 starts — five at left tackle, two at left guard, one at right tackle, and two as a tackle-eligible third tight end. His best Bengals highlight came in the Bengals' win over Arizona in Week 16 of the 2025 season, when he caught a pass from QB Joe Burrow for a 21-yard completion.
The veteran was a second-round draft choice of Buffalo in 2019 and spent his first three seasons  with the Bills, then played for Arizona in the 2022 season. He has made 42 career NFL starts.
Zac Taylor discussed the backup tackle battle after a rough night for that group in Saturday's preseason win over Chicago.
“Consistency," Taylor said about what he wants to see from that spot. "Just trust that the backup tackle is going to go in and win the game, and we want to keep playing the way that we play. You’ve just got to be able to trust through the game. And so, I think there’s probably a competition there.”
Taylor is ready for more work this week.
“We just need to continue to practice, and I think just as many situations as we can put ourselves in, get our players comfortable with that," Taylor said. "But we’ve gotten good work at this point. Now, we’re going to do some three-day stretches. We’re getting some good work this week, leading into Philly, and then three days leading into a bye, so we’re really looking at nine practices there. Ten practices, really, to get to Tampa Bay. So, that’s the way I think of it. We’ve got 10 real practices to get ourselves ready to go, and that’s really where our focus department turns to."
Cincinnati has not announced an ensuing signing.

title: Cincinnati Bengals Offensive Lineman Named Top 2026 Breakout Candidate
full_text:
The Bengals have a few young players who could pop this coming season, including a key factor along the offensive line. Pro Football Focus's Gordon McGuiness rolled with Dylan Fairchild as his Bengals breakout projection.
The former Georgia player posted a pretty solid rookie season after earning a starting job from Week 1 and beyond. Now, Fairchild is entering Year 2 with more confidence and the same running mates beside him.
"The Bengals drafted guard Dylan Fairchild with the 81st overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft, and the former Georgia Bulldog started 15 games as a rookie," McGuinness wrote. "Over the final eight games of the season, his 74.3 PFF pass-blocking grade ranked first among rookie guards and fourth among all rookie offensive linemen. He is capable of developing into the Bengals’ best offensive lineman by the end of the 2026 season."
Fairchild posted a 59.1 overall Pro Football Focus grade on a hefty 961 snaps last season.
His tutelage at Georgia helped him go from SEC guard to NFL stalwart in short order.
"I think they just demand a lot from their players. They demand a lot physically," Bengals offensive coordinator Dan Pitcher said about the Georgia program last year. "They demand a lot mentally. It's obvious when you see the success they've had under that head coach and under that program, and when you go down there, you feel the energy in that building. You see what's demanded of those guys and you feel the energy they have for one another, their teammates and the program. I think it's always good to have guys from an environment like that."
Ted Karras sees a big jump coming. He discussed Fairchild with offensive line expert Brandon Thorn this offseason.
"Like just the amount of force he can generate. That's such a thing you can't even teach," Karras said. "You just have to find those guys."
Check out the full breakout list from McGuinness here .
Ted Karras on what made Dylan Fairchild's rookie season so encouraging. "Some guys just generate a different amount of force." A good discussion on a trait that's difficult to measure but easy for offensive linemen to recognize. pic.twitter.com/J05Dof88eu

title: Browns Name Starting Quarterback For Bengals to Prepare For Late in 2026 Season
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have landed on a quarterback in their lowly battle at the position this summer. Cincinnati plays its division rival twice in the back half of the season and is slated to face Deshaun Watson over Shedeur Sanders as of this writing. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported the ne
Watson missed all of 2025 with a torn Achilles and has been one of the worst passers in the league since signing his mega deal with the Browns in 2022.
That poor play and huge salary, mixed with multiple sexual harassment lawsuit settlements , have turned Watson into arguably the most despised player in the NFL.
Plenty of Browns fans are on that side, as evidenced by the preseason crowd booing him during his appearance this past weekend. He was horrendous in the team's 31-7 preseason loss to Buffalo, going 5-of-12 passing for 36 yards and one interception. Alas, the Browns had few better options; Sanders didn't separate himself this summer and was arguably the worst QB to touch an NFL field last season (18.9 ESPN QBR in 2025, nearly 20 points worse than Cam Ward last season, who ranked last among qualified passers).
"The whole world knows it has nothing to do with the performance," Watson said about the boos after the game. "It's a little bit [more] personal than that. So I think it's a disrespectful thing. So yeah, I mean, I'm going to keep whatever I feel with my family and me internally on how I feel about that. And yeah, just move on.
"Last time I played on this field, I tore my Achilles. And that same fanbase, they cheered when I got hurt," Watson later said. "So what does that have to do with anything about performance? When a person gets hurt, especially for your own city, and they cheer?"
This should be music to Bengals fans' ears; he has two touchdowns and two interceptions against Cincinnati in three Browns outings and has been sacked seven times. Cleveland is 1-2 in those games.
All in all, Watson has a 33.1 Total QBR in Cleveland that would rank last if he had enough starts to qualify.
Cincinnati plays them on Dec. 6 and in the season finale.

title: Todd Monken Wastes No Time Justifying Browns’ Deshaun Watson Decision
full_text:
Deshaun Watson has been officially named the Cleveland Browns starting quarterback going into the 2026 NFL regular season and with that decision being made, head coach Todd Monken knows he’ll face great scrutiny all season long.
After all, it won’t be easy for his offense to operate over the course of the next four months while playing “17 away games”, as Watson characterized his relationship with Browns fans after being booed during the team’s second preseason game last Saturday.
Nonetheless, what might be Monken’s biggest and most critical resolution as an NFL head coach came extremely early in his Browns’ tenure, as was evidenced by how quickly he had to stand up and defend it from outside observers.
“What they’re not seeing is the film. They’re not in the building. So they’re not gonna know what we know. Now, you can see with your own eyes. You can forecast what you expect it to be. A number of those people weren’t even in practice. So I don’t really concern myself with what they really think. I know what we think, and what we see every day in our building, and our players and the momentum we have, and we’re 100 percent behind Deshaun.”
Todd Monken: “I know what we think and what we see everyday in our building and our players and the momentum we have. And we’re 100% behind Deshaun.” pic.twitter.com/waHIEOMV4S
One thing that does stand out in Monken’s comments is him saying “we’re 100 percent behind Deshaun,” because we truly don’t know who that “we” is. Is it the trio of top decision-makers for the team -- owner Jimmy Haslam, general manager Andrew Berry and Monken? Is it Monken and his staff? Is it the locker room? The franchise as a whole? Because at this point it’s pretty obvious that Shedeur Sanders does have some support in his corner.
And while Monken stated his decision to start Watson wasn’t a week to week thing , he did seem to backtrack a little later on.
“That’s what we do. That question is not a quarterback question, it is everybody’s position, right? Every single week we have to prove it. That’s what we do. As pros, we have to prove it every week.”
Monken waited long enough to get his first shot at an NFL head coaching job. As a matter of fact, only five first-time NFL head coaches with no interim head coaching experience in the league debuted in a regular season game older than Monken’s age when Week 1 comes around, at 60 years and 220 days old.
Monken knows chances like this don’t come around often, and fumbling his shot in Cleveland might mean never getting another one . Not one of the five older debuting coaches that Monken head coached another NFL team, and two of them, Rod Rust and David Culley, were one and done on the job.
On the flipside, the Browns have had two head coaches last for just one season under Haslam, Rob Chudzinski -- his first ever head coach hire as an owner -- in 2013 and Freddie Kitchens in 2019. In both instances, poor quarterback play was a major factor.
Backups Dillon Gabriel and Tayler Green are expected to split quarterbacking duties for the final preseason game on Thursday, with Watson and Sanders watching from the sidelines.
Then, the first real test comes along, when the Browns visit the Jaguars for Week 1 of the regular season, on September 13.
We’ll know soon enough if Monken hitched his incipient head coaching career to the right quarterback soon enough.

title: Deshaun Watson Starting Again Is the Browns Fans’ Worst-Case Scenario
full_text:
For Browns fans hoping to finally turn the page from Deshaun Watson, Monday was yet another reminder that it’s not going to happen anytime soon. Watson was named Cleveland’s starting quarterback to begin the 2026 season , Todd Monken announced Monday.
Is this rock bottom? No, it’s the Browns’ quarterback situation.
The Browns went 0-16 in 2017. They’ve had 42 different starting quarterbacks since 1999. And somehow, someway, Cleveland’s quarterback situation might be in its worst spot yet.
This isn’t simply about a bad quarterback situation anymore. It’s about a fanbase that desperately wants to move on from Watson and all of his baggage, a quarterback who has failed to live up to the historic price Cleveland paid for him, and a team that has now decided to put him back in the starting lineup anyway.
For Browns fans, it’s hard to imagine a worse outcome.
For a franchise that has made a lot of questionable decisions since 1999 (and before that), this one might be the cherry on top.
Leading up to his first game back in Cleveland on Saturday against the Buffalo Bills, Watson had a simple three-word response last Wednesday on the potential reaction from Browns fans during the game.
Saturday was supposed to be a chance for Watson to secure the starting job against a Buffalo Bills team that sat many of its starters.
Instead, Watson’s postgame press conference became the biggest headline of the Browns’ dismal 31-7 loss.
With Watson only playing the second half, he went against all backups, including plenty of players who won’t make Buffalo’s 53-man roster ahead of the regular season. Even with that, Watson completed just 5-of-12 passes for 36 yards and an interception.
Watson was booed by the home fans in Cleveland five times – the same number of passes he completed.
Even before he took a snap, Browns fans booed Watson as he ran onto the field for his first drive of the game – his first appearance in front of the home crowd since he tore his Achilles on Oct. 20, 2024. Many fans cheered when he suffered that injury.
This takes us back to Watson’s postgame comments on Saturday, proving that he did, in fact, care about how the fans have reacted to him in his last two games in front of the Dawg Pound.
Four questions and less than a minute into the presser, Watson was asked about his reaction “in the moment” after hearing the boos.
That was the point of no return.
“Man, I didn’t have any reaction. I think the biggest thing is, I think you guys know, and I think the whole world knows, that it has nothing to do with the performance. It’s a little more personal than that,” Watson said. “So, I think that’s a disrespectful thing. I’m going to keep whatever I feel with me and my family internally on how I feel about that, and just move on.”
He was then asked if playing better and winning would help eliminate that.
“Last time I played on this field, I tore my Achilles, and that same fan base cheered when I got hurt,” he said. “So, what does that have to do with anything about performance? When a person gets hurt, especially in their own city, and they cheer.
“The only time I feel that energy is when I’m in the stadium or it’s on social media,” Watson continued. “Like I mentioned before, when I’m in public, no one’s mentioning anything. So, I think that’s the only time those people who are holding it in are trying to disrupt the energy. Because on social media, players can’t respond back, and in the stadium, players can’t respond back. So, I get it, I understand it. It is what it is.”
Watson then said that he would rather play on the road than in front of Cleveland fans.
“I don’t know. It’s a mental battle every day. I feel like I get more love on road games than I do at home games,” Watson said. “So, if it is my spot and he does make me the starter, maybe it’s 17 away games, then. I don’t know.
“Again, I’m not sure. I don’t know,” he continued. “I thought being away for two years and working myself back from two Achilles injuries and putting the time in, being around the facility, being around the city, doing charity work in the city, supporting the Cleveland Browns, hanging out with fans whenever I do see them, being honest, being the type of person I know I am, and the character would help, and I guess it hasn’t. So, that’s why I say it’s more personal. It is what it is. People have their own opinions, and there’s only so much you can do to change that. So, at the end of the day, I just have to continue to work on it and strive to be better mentally moving forward.”
By the time the second half started, the crowd at Huntington Bank Field was very sparse, especially after a lengthy lightning delay at the beginning of the game.
Watson was this bothered on Saturday by a few thousand fans booing? Granted, the boos were still loud enough to be heard on the broadcast, but just wait until it’s a sellout crowd for the home opener in Week 3 against the Carolina Panthers.
Watson seemed to frame the Browns fans as antagonists while acting like a victim. He doesn’t get to do that.
Cleveland traded three first-round picks for him and gave him a five-year, $230 million fully guaranteed contract before he even set foot in the Browns’ facility.
Since arriving in Cleveland, Watson has completed 341-of-557 passes (61.7%) for 3,365 yards, 19 touchdowns, and 12 interceptions in 19 games. He hasn’t thrown for more than 1,150 yards in a season since 2020, when he led the NFL with 4,823 yards. He then missed all of 2021 and the first 11 games of 2022.
Watson has been one of the worst quarterbacks in the league over the last three seasons, yet he's portraying himself as the victim?
Whether we like it or not, winning cures a lot of things, at least on game days. If Watson had been among the league’s top quarterbacks – as his contract makes it look like he is – and leading the Browns to plenty of victories, Browns fans would have plenty to cheer – not boo – about.
Monken addressed that perfectly on Sunday.
“I’m not concerned about that,” he said. “What I’m concerned about is us playing well as a team and on offense, because when you play well, none of the other stuff matters. Just play well, coach well, score points, win games, and none of that will even matter.
“The business we’re in is a performance-based business. It is what it is,” Monken continued. “When we expect a service, we’re going to be disappointed when we don’t get that service. If you go to a restaurant and your soup comes out cold, you’re going to be upset. If you order from the grocery store and six of your eggs are broken, you’re going to be pissed. So, I get it; that’s what we’re in. That’s why we’re paid what we are, to perform at a high level, and when we don’t, there are repercussions. We’ve run into this smoke. This is the job we’ve chosen, so this is part of it.”
The overwhelming majority of Browns fans seem to be against Watson playing – let alone starting – again for the Browns. Cleveland is over it, especially because Watson hasn’t been good since he arrived.
It’s not often that a fanbase is this united on one opinion, yet here we are.
Booing a player on your favorite team isn’t ideal, but Browns fans are showing their frustration the only way they can inside the stadium.
It’s too late now, given that Monken announced Watson as the Browns’ starting quarterback to begin the 2026 season, but that’s a decision many Cleveland fans wish the head coach hadn’t made.
I don’t care if Sanders was the second-best quarterback throughout camp.
I don’t care if Sanders must work on certain things a quarterback has to be able to do pre-snap.
I don’t care if Sanders isn’t the future of the Browns. Watson isn’t either – clearly.
I’d rather watch opposing teams do Sanders’ signature watch celebration after the quarterback throws an interception than have to watch Watson try to be a competent quarterback again.
The majority of Browns fans would rather watch Sanders play this season than Watson, even if it leads to more losses. Sanders…

title: Browns Gaining Back Defensive Line Starter To Help With Thin Depth
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are set to embark on their third and final preseason game before the start of the regular season, and they’ll be getting back one of their best veterans on defense.
After the news of Alex Wright’s season ending Achilles injury this past weekend, the Browns were in a position to be extremely thin on their defensive line, even more than before.
Now, a returning Maliek Collins should help their defense look and play more sound.
#Browns DT Maliek Collins (quad) passed his physical and can begin practicing.
Collins is an established veteran in the NFL and was a serviceable starter on Cleveland’s defense last season before his quad injury shut him down for the remainder of the 2025 campaign. His return to the lineup will be felt due to his presence as a quick and reactive defensive tackle.
With the injuries and inexperience on the defensive line before this news was announced, the Browns needed Collins back in the lineup desperately. He’ll slot right into their starting position opposite of second year standout Mason Graham.
Having Collins back in their lineup is positive news that Browns fans needed to hear. Here’s how his return should help their defense return to form and how it helps their thin depth overall.
Collins brings his ten-year NFL experience to a young Browns defense that can always use any amount of leadership. That’s not something teams can find easily, especially for a 31-year-old defensive tackle that is still producing at a high level.
Even though Collins was limited to 12 games in 2025, he was already on pace to have one of his best seasons of his career. Collins had the second most sacks on Cleveland’s defense last season at 6.5, and had 25 total tackles, 15 solo tackles, and one fumble recovery.
Having Collins still playing at a high level is exactly what the Browns need, especially with fellow defensive tackle Graham expected to take a step forward in his second season. Knowing how disruptive both Collins and Graham can be should also take pressure and eyes off their pass rushers.
Adding Jared Verse to the equation will also help out their defensive tackles in terms of their disruption for opposing offenses. After Wright’s season ending injury, the Browns went out and added another veteran defensive lineman by signing Derek Barnett over the weekend .
Cleveland’s front office knew how thin their defensive line was before the injuries but were quick to act on that with the regular season right around the corner. With a much-improved defensive line on paper ready to go with Collins returning and Barnett’s arrival, this should also help their linebackers and secondary make plays and hopefully force turnovers.
Collins should be returning to the practice field as early as this week, although the Browns could play it safe and not force him back right away to preserve him for the start of the season.

title: Deshaun Watson Won’t Start for Browns All Season: Here’s Why
full_text:
Cleveland Browns fans are rightfully outraged after reports circulated that Deshaun Watson will be the team’s starting quarterback this season.
Watson melted down against third and fourth stringers during the third quarter of Saturday’s preseason game against the Buffalo Bills. He completed just 5-of-12 passes and had a QBR of 14.6. After that performance, he blasted Cleveland’s loyal fanbase for booing him, stating it was personal and disrespectful. After that performance and those remarks, some doubted Watson would ever be able to show his face in Berea ever again.
But he somehow beat out Shedeur Sanders in Cleveland’s weighted quarterback competition and will start Week 1 against the Jacksonville Jaguars.
If we’re being honest, Watson gets this nod for a number of reasons, none of which are new. He’s a veteran, and 60-year-old head coach Todd Monken probably likes that. He’s owed $46 million, and the team stands to make sure there’s no juice to be squeezed out of their “swing and a miss” trade in 2022.
There’s nothing to gain from playing Watson, but Shedeur Sanders is still developing and the Browns are likely planning to draft a quarterback in April’s 2027 draft.
The player that sank the franchise has only played in 19 games since that disastrous trade in 2022. He’s broken his shoulder and ruptured his Achilles tendon twice, on top of the 11-game suspension for violating the league’s personal conduct policy stemming from over two dozen accusations of sexual misconduct.
Browns fans and Watson have never clicked. And that’s part of the reason why this experiment could be over by Week 3, Cleveland’s home opener against the Carolina Panthers.
The Browns are hoping Watson plays well in Florida and the Browns start 2-0 against the Jaguars and Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Then, nobody would boo their undefeated team ahead of their home opener, right?
Well, if the Browns go 0-2 – or even 1-1 – and Watson looks as shaky as he has during training camp, we’re in for quite the scene at Huntington Bank Field in Week 3. That’s unless the Browns hook Watson in favor of Sanders, which is a real possibility if the season starts poorly.
This also feels like one of those years where the Browns could need everybody. Dillon Gabriel and Taylen Green are both on this roster, and maybe the Browns embrace carrying four quarterbacks this season.
Gabriel has been dreadful in limited opportunities, struggling to move the ball downfield. But Green impressed during Cleveland’s joint practices against the Bills on Thursday, and will make his preseason debut in Cleveland’s finale against the New England Patriots.
Just because Watson started the season doesn’t mean he’ll end the season. And the end of the season will likely result in the Browns preparing to make a very important decision in the 2027 NFL Draft.

title: Browns Make Deshaun Watson Decision That Could Define Todd Monken’s First Season
full_text:
Todd Monken has reportedly made his first big decision as the head coach of the Cleveland Browns.
According to NFL insider Jordan Schultz, the Browns informed the team on Monday morning that Deshaun Watson will start at quarterback for the Browns in 2026. While there hasn’t been an official announcement from the team, Watson will be starting at quarterback for the Browns in 2026. Schultz’s report indicates that Monken felt more comfortable with Watson’s veteran experience, but this was a close competition that came down to the end.
“But it’s my understanding that he will have to continue earning it once the season starts and the games are for real,” Schultz reported.
Luckily for the Browns, this journey will begin on the road against the Jacksonville Jaguars and Tampa Bay Buccaneers. If it were up to Watson, who just won Cleveland’s weighted quarterback competition, the Browns would rather play all of their games on the road to get away from the most passionate fanbase in the NFL. That’s what Watson said when he blasted Cleveland’s passionate and loyal fans, as the 30-year-old felt disrespected for getting showered with boo birds during an outing where he completed 5-of-12 passing and a 14.6 quarterback rating.
"It's a little bit more personal than that, so I think it's a disrespectful thing,” Watson said.
The newly-appointed face of the franchise (who shouldn’t be) has only played 19 games since the controversial trade that landed him in Cleveland back in 2022. There’s reason to believe the Browns will need to continue developing their backup quarterback Shedeur Sanders , who impressed in his preseason start against the Bills, which didn’t factor as much into this decision.
After Watson’s viral remarks , many wondered if the Browns would release the starting quarterback, who used his postseason media availability to challenge the fans.
But Watson’s devastating cap number prevents the Browns from doing so. Instead of stashing Watson on the roster, the Browns will give him the starting quarterback job, even though almost everything points to Sanders being the better option.
This offseason, the Browns hired Monken and had another really impressive draft class. Then, they traded Myles Garrett and started Watson at quarterback, which is an indication that this franchise is still rebuilding, regardless of what they say publicly.
Cleveland’s quarterback situation will undoubtedly take them to April’s 2027 NFL Draft, which is expected to have a loaded quarterback class featuring Texas’ Arch Manning.

title: Who the Cleveland Browns Plan to Play in Their Final Preseason Game
full_text:
Suddenly, the Cleveland Browns just have one preseason game to go until the 2026 season begins on September 13th vs the Jaguars. Cleveland has not fared well in the preseason so far, as they are 0-2 with losses to the Bears and Bills.
We know these games do not count, but they do matter for many players trying to make the roster, secure starting spots, or make the practice squad. The quarterback drama will finally end tomorrow when Todd Monken officially names the team's QB1; for now, we know who will be playing in their preseason finale vs. New England.
Monken says the starters will get a rest, and the backups will get the bulk of the work on Thursday.
Todd Monken does not anticipate playing starters in the Browns’ preseason finale against the Patriots on Thursday night.
Expect to see second-year guy Dillon Gabriel under center first for the Browns, then rookie Taylen Green to get some game time. Raheim “Rocket” Sanders will mostly be in the backfield again, as he was for the Buffalo game yesterday. As far as Gabriel’s weapons, he’ll be throwing to guys like Malachi Corley, Luke Floriea, and Gage Larvadain.
The offensive line will be an interesting group to watch the whole day, as we saw some young guys battling on Saturday. Against Buffalo, the lineup started as KT Leveston at left tackle, Zak Zinter at left guard, Luke Wypler at Center, Austin Barber at right guard, and Dawand Jones at right tackle. Kingsley Eguakun rotated in to play center a bit, Jeremiah Byers got run at left guard, Tyre Phillips at right tackle, and Izavion Miller came to play right guard.
The line looked solid vs Buffalo, giving Shedeur comfortable time to throw; we can hope that play stands for Gabriel.
The spot that will get a lot of looks on defense will be the starting defensive end opposite of Jared Verse because of the heartbreaking season-ending injury to Alex Wright .
Cleveland signed veteran Derek Barnett for depth, but the starter could also come from one of the guys still battling it out. That would be players like Isaiah McGuire, Julian Okwara, Benton Whitley, or even Mike Hall Jr., who was playing on the edge yesterday and collected a huge sack.
Winston Reid and Nathaniel Watson will lead the group of linebackers, both still looking to earn that third starting job among Carson Schwesinger and Quincy Williams. The rookie from Alabama, Justin Jefferson, will be another player to watch.
In the secondary, the corners will consist of Tre Avery, Michael Coats Jr, Jeremiah McClendon, and Tyler Hall, while the safeties are rookie Emmanuell McNeil-Warren, and second-year guys Donovan McMillion and Christopher Edmonds.

title: Browns Waive Tight End Aiming to Return to College Football
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are dealing with several bizarre situations at the moment. One in particular represents a new reality for college football and the NFL.
The Browns signed rookie tight end Dae'Quan Wright earlier this month to add some depth to the position. He was waived today for quite the unique reason.
It was revealed a few days ago that Wright successfully sued to allow him and others to return to college football. This comes after the NCAA changed the rules to give all players five years of eligibility. Wright, and others, left college before the rule change.
This news came out , but Wright was still a member of the Browns.
That made it incredibly odd to see him warming up on the field before Saturday's game, as he was already in the transfer portal.
This is interesting. Dae’Quan Wright is in uniform and warming up with the Browns right now. He has not been in any of the practices since being claimed  and just entered the NCAA transfer portal.
Then came Sunday's news in which he was waived, clearing the way for his return to college football. Adam Schefter shared the news on social media.
History: the Browns are waiving tight end Dae’Quan Wright and, if he clears waivers, he has an agreement in place for the 2026 season to play for LSU, per agents Drew Rosenhaus and Kyle Lincoln. Wright is believed to be the first player who could play for an NFL team, and then… pic.twitter.com/3MLKNFYInY
Wright is reportedly all set to join the LSU Tigers, given he clears NFL waivers. He should in fact do so as teams won't want to deal with the headache of him angling to return to college.
This is, for lack of a better word, weird. Wright spent the summer in NFL camps and is now taking that experience with him to LSU. Such a move had only come up facetiously in the past. Now, it's the new reality.
This becoming the norm will impact recruiting, as coaches will much rather take veteran players with NFL experience over incoming freshmen out of high school.
So what does this mean for the Browns? Wright was undrafted and just joined the team a few weeks ago, so this is not a big loss. Yet it's a loss in terms of the team being incredibly thin at tight end behind Harold Fannin Jr. That is even more true with the lack of clarity on rookie Joe Royer's status.
Blake Whiteheart is up behind Fannin, which is not ideal. Whiteheart appeared in all 17 games last season and recorded a total of two receptions. The blocking tight end cannot be relied upon as a key player in the passing game.
The Browns are full of drama and losing a player to the college football transfer portal is certainly up there in terms of ridiculous stories out of Berea.
