title: Broncos 53-Man Roster Projection 4.0: Game 2 Shakes Up the Roster Bubble
full_text:
Only one preseason game remains before the Denver Broncos have to cut their current 90-man roster down to the final 53 players. That deadline is on August 30.
By returning most of their 2025 roster, the Broncos have a good idea of who will make the cut this year. Honestly, analyzing this roster, there are maybe five spots open.
In the wake of the Broncos' 33-13 loss to the Green Bay Packers , it's time to project the 53-man roster and 16-man practice squad once again. Let's see how things may have been shaken up compared to our version 3.0 projection coming out of the Atlanta Falcons game last week.
There are no changes here, and fans shouldn’t expect any in the quarterback room. Stidham and Ehlinger aren’t in a true battle , and the Broncos seem unlikely to carry three quarterbacks on the roster.
Even with some injury concerns over Dobbins, the Broncos still only roll with three running backs. They could look for more on the practice squad, but it seems like Tyler Badie and Jaleel McLaughlin would land elsewhere, leaving Schrader as the practice squad back, and there are no qualms there, as he has outplayed Badie and McLaughlin in the preseason games.
There will be a fullback on the roster; Sean Payton has said as much, and new offensive coordinator Davis Webb clearly has something in mind for how to use him.
Due to roster math, Humphrey misses out on the 53-man roster, but he has a chance to make it, as Nix, Payton, and Webb seem to have a lot of trust in him as a weapon. The question is how the practice squad shakes up, and Ross has looked good on offense, with Katsis standing out as a returner.
Denver needs help in the tight end room, and until then, this will be the outlook for the room. Each day Lohner misses increases his chances of being one of the players put on injured reserve at the cutdown as someone who could potentially return.
With how bad Crum has been in the preseason, there is a chance the undrafted rookie could take his spot, as Miller has done quite well. However, Crum has been running with the second unit, while Miller has been with the fourth-unit offensive line, signaling a pecking order.
Throckmorton has been doing well in games and in practice, which should be making Forsyth feel some heat, as he wasn’t doing the best in practice before he got hurt. There's also positional versatility with Throckmorton, which you don’t have in Forsyth.
Outside of those two players, the interior offensive line is pretty much set.
Barring a trade, the Broncos' defensive line seems set, even for the practice squad. They like to keep seven on the roster, and those seven are clear.
With Miller, he saw the field in the second half against Green Bay, and the last defensive linemen didn’t take the field until the fourth quarter. Miller has done well and seems like a shoo-in for the practice squad.
The practice squad is up for a battle, and Denver could look outside the team to find another rush linebacker. Drew Sanders is hurt again, and Johnny Walker and McCullough haven’t been great. The Broncos' five outside linebackers are locks, barring a surprise cut or trade.
The top three seem pretty much settled, but the fourth spot is still up for grabs with Turner and Murdock competing for it. Both have had some bad moments, but also some bright spots.
Turner got the edge over Murdock here for special teams play, but it could honestly go either way. York is out of the running for the roster because of his lack of special teams ability, as he made multiple mistakes on special teams against the Packers.
There has been a debate about whether Denver would keep five or six corners, and Fresch is pushing for a roster spot with his play on defense and special teams, but the team could probably sneak him onto the practice squad.
The Broncos' top five corners are set, though, and that's great because it speaks to their depth.
Yes, Rapp makes it even as a new addition because he is a high-football-IQ veteran who should pick up the defense quickly, upgrading the third safety spot, which is much needed. This pushes Key back down into a key special teams player and the fourth safety.
Skinner sticks around for his third-phase play. Scott and Robertson have shown plenty of flashes to keep around and continue to develop.
No competition for Lutz or Crawshaw, and Fraboni is clearly ahead of Luke Basso. There doesn’t seem to be much of a long snapper competition after all.

title: Lions Veteran WR, RB Placed on IR, New Defensive Back Signed
full_text:
The Detroit Lions ' roster depth took a big hit Saturday with the injury to veteran wide receiver Cedrick Wilson Jr.
Wilson exited Saturday's 17-13 preseason win over the Washington Commanders with an apparent leg injury.
He caught back-to-back passes on the team's third drive, but left the game one play after his second catch where he appeared to land hard on his leg.
According to reports, Wilson has been placed on the injured reserve list, along with running back Raheem Blackshear.
Head coach Dan Campbell admitted he was concerned about the injury in his postgame press conference.
"I don't know for sure. I'm worried, I'm worried on that one. I love Wilson, man," Campbell said. "He's just a smart, crafty football player. Gets it, can play all the spots at receiver, special teams. We don't know. We're getting that knee looked at. We don't know, but I'll leave it at that."
Wilson finishes the preseason with three catches for 44 yards. Furthermore, he had been having a strong training camp thanks to his veteran presence in the receiver room. Before the injury, Wilson was considered to be one of the top contenders for the fifth wide receiver spot behind the team's established group of Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, Isaac TeSlaa and Greg Dortch.
A 2018 sixth-round pick of the Dallas Cowboys, Wilson has notched over 100 receptions and over 1,200 receiving yards in his seven NFL seasons. The Lions are the fourth organization he's suited up for, joining the Cowboys, Miami Dolphins and New Orleans Saints.
Wilson played collegiately for Boise State, where he notched back-to-back seasons with over 1,000 receiving yards including 1,511 yards in his final campaign. He spent two years at Boise State after beginning his college career at Coffeyville Community College.
Other competitors in the race for that spot include Tay Martin, Tom Kennedy, Lucky Jackson, Tarik Black and Lucky Jackson. The Lions have already lost one other receiver for the season, as fifth-round draft pick Kendrick Law suffered a torn ACL during offseason workouts.
In corresponding moves, the team made the signing of running back Roydell Williams official.
Also, the team inked defensive back Jason Taylor to a contract.
Taylor, 26, appeared in three games during his freshman season at Oklahoma State.
He secured 99 tackles with six interceptions as a redshirt senior and was named a first team All-Big 12 player. After being selected in the seventh-round by the Los Angeles Rams in the 2023 NFL Draft, he has also had stints with the Cardinals, Chiefs and Orlando Storm.
He has appeared in eight career games (2023) and recorded five solo tackles.

title: Detroit Lions Are Signing Former Alabama, Florida State Running Back
full_text:
The Detroit Lions were required to add a running back to the roster, after Jabari Small suffered a head  injury in the second preseason game of 2026.
According to multiple reports, the front office has made the decision to sign former Alabama Crimson Tide and Florida State Seminoles running back Roydell Williams.
In his first year playing in the SEC, Williams secured 19 rushing attempts for 71 yards and a touchdown.
The following year, he secured 250 yards rushing and four touchdowns on 56 carries. Following the 2023 season, Williams entered the NCAA transfer portal.
Williams only appeared in 10 games in the past two years at Florida State, recording 41 carries for 99 yards and two touchdowns. Unfortunately, multiple injuries derailed the end of his collegiate career. He suffered an undisclosed lower-leg injury against his former team in September of 2025.
He went undrafted and signed with the Indianapolis Colts. He was cut when veteran wideout Keenan Allen joined the team.
The Lions faced a pair of familiar faces over the weekend, when the Washington Commanders visited Ford Field.
Cornerback Amik Robertson and running back Craig Reynold spoke to reporters after losing to the Lions, 17-13.
“It was great seeing a lot of people," said Robertson. "Like I say, man, this organization, this city welcomed me with all love. I don’t have nothing bad to say about Detroit, man. I appreciate them, and I wish them the best in the future.”
The veteran defensive back also shared, when asked about bringing the pressure early in the game, “Just a great play call by (Commanders defensive coordinator) Daronte Jones. My number was called, and I harp on, whenever my number’s called, I gotta make my plays. I had a call by our DC, and I was able to be aggressive, disguise the blitz and make a play.”
Reynolds remains close with Detroit's running backs, who regularly message each other in group chats.
“It was fun to go out there and compete, talk trash. Talk a lot of trash," said Reynolds. "And get a chance to really hit them now, because you practice against them, but it’s not really like that. It was a lot of fun.”

title: The Biggest Decision Lions Coach Dan Campbell Must Make This Week
full_text:
With the new roster cut date, the Detroit Lions will have to make several key decisions in a timely manner.
Detroit plays its preseason finale against the Indianapolis Colts at Noon Saturday, and must make their initial 53-man roster final by 6 p.m. Sunday. As a result, the final evaluations provided by players in the preseason finale will carry some weight, but the performance in the week of practice leading up to it will be just as important.
The Lions have had nearly a month to evaluate many of the position battles on their roster, but one that has been held in a relatively short amount of time is the backup quarterback competition.
Detroit entered the preseason with two players competing for the job behind starter Jared Goff in veteran Teddy Bridgewater and undrafted free agent Luke Altmyer . Bridgewater was expected to be a lock for the spot due to his leadership ability and experience in the offense.
However, a wrench was thrown in those plans when Bridgewater announced his retirement, and as a result the Lions signed veteran Joshua Dobbs to compete with Altmyer. However, Dobbs has been with the team for two weeks, and some of his evaluation will have to be based on his previous playing experience as a result.
Now, head coach Dan Campbell will have to make a decision this week about which of the two quarterbacks to carry into the regular season. Both have their respective cases, with Dobbs being an experienced option with familiarity in coordinator Drew Petzing's scheme and Altmyer being a rookie with promise and the ability to develop behind Goff.
Goff has proven to be one of the NFL's most durable quarterbacks, however trends across the league indicate just how important it is to have a quality backup. Last season alone, 63 different players started a game in the regular season.
While the Lions have been fortunate to have Goff for all but three games of his five seasons with the team, they need a reliable backup given their championship aspirations should he go down.
Between the two, Dobbs has the inside track to the job given the fact that he has proven he can be successful. He's made 15 starts in his career, and while he has a 3-12 record in those games he has proven he can get hot for stretches and fuel an offense.
However, there is a case for the team to keep Altmyer. He's shown some ability, and while he doesn't have nearly the level of experience that Dobbs has, he has demonstrated an ability to operate within the scheme.
There is another path Detroit could follow, as they could seek out a quarterback who didn't make their team's respective roster after final cuts. They faced a similar dilemma in 2022, when neither David Blough or Tim Boyle showed enough in the preseason to warrant being the backup.
In that instance, the Lions signed Nate Sudfeld who was cut by the San Francisco 49ers to serve as Goff's understudy.
Now, the Lions are in a similar predicament. With Goff expected to sit out in the preseason finale, the good news is Detroit will get a long look at both quarterbacks. Dobbs is the favorite amongst the group, but a strong showing from Altmyer could certainly change the organization's thinking.
Regardless, the competition for the backup spot is carrying plenty of intrigue into the final week of training camp, and it's set up for an exciting preseason finale.

title: Detroit Lions Updated Bubble Watch After Commanders Game: Offense
full_text:
The Detroit Lions will play in their final preseason game of the year on Saturday against the Colts, yet still have multiple players vying for roster spots.
On offense, a few players stood out this past weekend against the Commanders.
Notably, tight end Jackson Meeks and running back Trayveon Williams delivered impressive performances.
Meeks emerged as one of Luke Altmyer's go-to targets Saturday, finishing the exhibition contest with four catches for 33 yards. And one of his four catches came on a critical fourth-down conversion late in the fourth quarter. It helped set up a Jake Bates field goal which sealed the deal vs. the Commanders.
Meanwhile, Williams, who was signed by the Lions on August 16, didn't miss a beat in his preseason debut with Dan Campbell's squad.
The veteran back, who split time with the Chargers and the Browns in 2025, amassed a team-high 60 yards from scrimmage and accounted for the Lions’ final touchdown of the game Saturday. He also helped set up the score by hauling in a 24-yard pass from Josh Dobbs on the initial play of the drive.
Williams proved he's more than capable as both a runner and pass-catcher in his first game donning the Honolulu Blue. And even more importantly, he proved he's going to give fellow bubble backs Jacob Saylors, Raheem Blackshear and Jabari Small a run for their money the rest of camp.
As a whole, the Lions’ backfield produced a solid effort vs. Dan Quinn's team, notching 169 total yards and two touchdowns on 35 carries.
Just like Williams, Saylors compiled 30-plus yards on the ground in the preseason tilt, averaging 5.3 yards per carry. Small also recorded 5.3 yards per rush attempt Saturday, albeit on just three carries.
Detroit's backs managed to accomplish this despite the team's offensive line producing an overall lackluster effort.
Rookie right tackle Blake Miller delivered the only real respectable showing, holding his own for the majority of the afternoon. Meanwhile, Larry Borom, his main competition at the position, struggled all game. He seemingly allowed pressure after pressure (including on Detroit's first two drives), and hardly looked the part of a savvy vet.
Offensive linemen Seth McLaughlin, Colby Sorsdal and Miles Frazier also all struggled mightily. They each succumbed to the Commanders’ stifling pass-rush, and Sorsdal was so bad that he was eventually benched.
Fellow bubble lineman Melvin Priestly didn't fare much better, and was called for a false start penalty late in the third quarter.
Priestly, McLaughlin, Sorsdal and Frazier each need to have much better outings in the Lions’ preseason finale in Indianapolis.
Along with the aforementioned names, here is the list of Detroit players firmly on the bubble heading into the final week of the exhibition season:
Luke Altmyer, Tarik Black, Malik Cunningham, Lucky Jackson, Tom Kennedy, Lawrence Keys, Dominic Lovett, Tay Martin, Michael Niese, Cedrick Wilson, Thomas Gordon, Zach Horton, Giovanni Manu and Devin Cochran.

title: Lomas Brown: 'I Expected a Lot Better Execution' Against Commanders
full_text:
In any NFL preseason game, question marks start to arise regarding the actual talent level a team has.
For the Detroit Lions , there are now significant concerns regarding the depth along the offensive line. With Seth McLaughlin, Miles Frazier, Larry Borom, Melvin Priestly and Colby Sorsdal all struggling with consistency, there are many wondering who will step up and be reliable, if something should happen to one of the starting guards.
On the broadcast team, color analyst Lomas Brown also walked away with question marks and concerns, after the team did not execute the way he would have expected.
Detroit's second preseason game was a dress rehearsal for the regular season and featured many starters playing in front of the home crowd.
Additional Lions Insider Analysis: 5 Risers, 4 Fallers Following Week 2 Preseason Win
"I hate to say this, but I think it's more questions coming out of this game than answers that we have for us. I really do," said Brown. "I thought the Cincinnati game, I thought that was a pretty good game for us, especially being the first game of the season. But I expected a lot more, a lot better execution in this game."
Detroit gave up a fumble and touchdown return on the second snap of the game, finding themselves down 7-0 after receiving the opening kickoff.
Detroit's reserves on the offensive line did not play well and gave up far too any pressures and sacks.
On the Lions postgame radio show, host Marc Ryan also had concerns, but found positives in the play of the defense.
Detroit's defensive line had a positive performance, with many defensive ends stepping up.
"Quite honestly, it's not to say it was all bad news, but the offense was, it was a pretty, pretty putrid. offensive performance. Their backup quarterbacks, offensive line was offensive. The defense, bravo. Bravo to the defense. Round of applause even for the defense, right," said Ryan. "The defense stepped up, held the Commanders out of the end zone. That's exactly what you're looking for. That's exactly what you want.
"Six points for the Commanders offense. As a matter of fact, the Lions gave the Commanders, the Lions offense gave the Commanders more points, seven, than the the Lions defense allowed them, which was six."

title: The Good, Bad and Ugly of Lions Preseason Victory Over Commanders
full_text:
On Saturday, Detroit had their only home game of the preseason and took down the Washington Commanders 17-13. With the game came plenty of tape that will help shape the roster as Detroit finishes their last of the preseason next Saturday.
It also gives fans a preview as to what worked with the backups at the wheel, along with what worked for the Lions. Here are the good, the bad, and the ugly of a preseason win over the Commanders.
Yet again, the Drew Petzing offense is clicking on all cylinders when it comes to running to football. The Lions had a dominant game on the ground despite their top two backs, Jahmyr Gibbs and Isiah Pacheco, not playing a snap on Saturday.
The backs by committee even lost a player midgame with Jabari Small heading to concussion protocol. It did not matter, as the Lions saw Jacob Saylors, Trayveon Williams, and Raheem Blackshear all show flashes.
Additional credit goes to the offensive line and pass catchers for their efforts in the run blocks. Blake Miller had a play where he slipped on the turf and recovered to push a defender out of the hole on an eight-yard gain. Tyler Conklin and Tay Martin combined for two massive blocks on a 50-yard touchdown run by Joshua Dobbs.
Even on fourth-and-two, the Lions handed the ball off to Blackshear to seal the victory. All around, it was a great day for runners and run blockers.
Quarterback Pressure and Dominant Defense
In a repeat of last week, the Lions were able to harass the Commanders quarterbacks . D.J. Wonnum and Derrick Moore each made their preseason debuts and had a sack in their limited reps. Skyler Gill-Howard could have been charged rent in the Washington backfield by the end of the game. Undrafted EDGE Eric O’Neill impressed again with solid flashes and dismantling a go-ahead drive attempt by the Commanders.
Levi Onwuzurike provided a solid push. Devin White nearly sacked Jayden Daniels on the opening pass attempt of the game. Keith Abney II nearly got home twice in one drive on nickel blitzes. Malcolm Rodriguez recorded a quarterback hit. Kelvin Sheppard’s defense only allowed nine first downs all game.
In a friendly environment, procedural penalties such as false starts are inexcusable. The Lions saw their fair share of mental mistakes, including back-to-back false starts by Seth McLaughlin and Miles Frazier. Melvin Priestly added his own false start with the Lions on the verge of the red zone in a go-ahead situation in the second half. Larry Borom lined up improperly on a strip sack that was recovered in the end zone.
Mistakes like these will come back to haunt players trying to earn a spot on the 53-man roster or practice squad in the next few weeks. Additionally, rookie defensive back Keith Abney II had a holding penalty on what would have been a sack, alongside getting a whistle for pass interference later in the game.
For the second time, the starting quarterback for the Lions opened the game by giving the ball away on the first possession. Joshua Dobbs got the start and fumbled the ball on his first pass attempt. He followed that up with a poorly advised throw across his body into double coverage while under pressure in his second drive, giving him a multi-turnover game.
Luke Altmyer had flashes, but did not have the same sharpness he seemed to possess against the Bengals in week one of preseason. It was not a day where either player vying for the backup job “won” it. Joshua Dobbs’s best play came with his legs, while Altmyer avoided turnovers, but also had a series where he took three sacks.
Last week saw the Lions escape Cincinnati without any major losses, but that is likely not the case this week. Wide receiver Cedrick Wilson Jr. suffered an injury where the prognosis was worrying, per Dan Campbell. Offensive lineman Michael Niese was carted off the field and seen exiting the locker room in crutches.
Those two losses could be on the long term end of the scale. Additionally, running back Jabari Small exited the game and is in concussion protocol. Miles Frazier left the game for injury at one point, but later returned. Jacob Saylors, Christian Mahogany, and Chuck Clark all suffered minor bumps and bruises.
When combined with Sam LaPorta’s Week One status in doubt, there is some concern for the season already.
While the offensive line deserved flowers and a ton of credit for an organized run game, the pass game was not the same story. When there were not procedural penalties that should be avoided, the pass blocking suffered.
The opening play of the game saw Borom get beat badly, preventing Dobbs from stepping into a throw and susceptible to a blitz by former Lion Amik Robertson. Seth McLaughlin allowed a sack by assuming a defensive tackle would give up on a play. Borom allowed a pressure on the Dobbs interception.
Tyler Conklin got blown by on a block that resulted in a sack. Colby Sorsdal got benched in the second quarter, and that might be it for his chances of making the roster.
At the end of the day, the Lions won, but the top priority appears to be keeping the starting offensive line healthy after Washington’s defense and backups dominated the reserves whenever a pass was attempted.

title: Roundtable: Biggest Questions Lions Must Answer in Final Week of Camp
full_text:
The Detroit Lions OnSI staff takes a look at the biggest questions the Lions must answer entering the final week of training camp.
Christian Booher: I think it was a fun win for the Lions. In particular, the defensive performance was phenomenal as they allowed just six points. The performance of the pass-rush was very promising, while the secondary showed some growth with their communication.
Additionally, I was intrigued by the way both quarterbacks responded to adversity. Josh Dobbs really dialed it in after about as rough a start as one can imagine, while Luke Altmyer kept the offense afloat despite taking four sacks.
Vito Chirco: It was a nice win, but I don't place a ton of stock in it because the Lions’ best players (i.e. Jared Goff, Penei Sewell, Jahmyr Gibbs, etc.) sat out the contest. At this juncture, I believe the defense is a bit ahead of the offense, although I'm not overly concerned with that being the case.
Emmett Matasovsky: While preseason wins do not really mean much (as evidenced by a 4-0 preseason in 2008), it is heartening to see the Lions send the fans home happy in the only preseason contest of the year at Ford Field. The Lions showed promise and made enough plays defensively to earn their win. That defensive depth and effort, with only nine first downs allowed, are a phenomenal sign.
Booher : At this point, the offensive line's performance is a little concerning. They have a pivotal injury in Cade Mays that they'll have to overcome, and Ben Bartch's absence has prevented Christian Mahogany from really being challenged. I expect that this group will struggle a bit early in the year, but with Penei Sewell as the anchor, I still think this is a unit that enters the season in the top-half of the league.
Chirco : It sure does. I'm still not convinced the Lions have found a viable replacement at center for Cade Mays. As much as Seth McLaughlin and Juice Scruggs could end up being solid depth pieces, I just don't envision either of them being very proficient at center. With that said, I believe there will be a void at the position until Mays’ return.
Matasovsky : It concerns me, as the reserve linemen did not have a good game. Defensive blitzes caught the line off guard, and swing tackle Larry Borom had an outing to forget.
However, in the sense of being concerned about the overall football product with a healthy offensive line, I am not concerned. The starting linemen, save Borom, earned their keep Saturday. If Blake Miller has not bypassed Borom, Saturday should have secured Miller a spot in the lineup in Week 1.
Booher : I was really impressed with Skyler Gill-Howard. I wrote about Gill-Howard earlier in the week, and he delivered another solid performance in Saturday's game. I'm really intrigued with how well he's able to win off the line and rush the passer, and I think that can be a real asset in the Lions' defensive scheme.
Chirco : I'll give two names: EDGE Derrick Moore and defensive tackle Skyler Gill-Howard. I believe that both rookies clearly improved their stock with their performances Saturday. Each defender got after the quarterback often, and looked the part of reliable pass-rushers. I think that both could play meaningful roles in Kelvin Sheppard's defense in 2026.
Matasovsky : In terms of solely week two, I would say the highest riser this week was tight end Jackson Meeks. Meeks proved a solid weapon in the receiving game, hauling in four passes, while also stripping the ball out on kickoff coverage.
When it comes to the overall preseason, defensive lineman Skyler Gill-Howard and EDGE Eric O’Neill are the highest risers. Both put together their second consecutive week of terrorizing offenses, and O’Neill is making it harder to ignore his talent. Gill-Howard is decimating defenses, and at this pace, could be challenging for meaningful minutes sooner than later.
Booher : I think Dobbs has the upper hand for a couple of reasons. Dobbs is more mobile, and has familiarity with the scheme having worked with Drew Petzing previously. Altmyer is certainly intriguing, but at this point I believe the Lions would be able to get him through to the practice squad if they were to cut him. I still think that Brad Holmes will be looking for options after final cuts, but Dobbs appears to be a serviceable option as the backup despite his rough start to Saturday's game.
Chirco : As much as maybe it should be undrafted rookie Luke Altmyer based on his performance in camp thus far, I believe it's Josh Dobbs. I believe his previous NFL playing experience is too valuable to disregard in this competition, and I believe it gives him a slight upper hand in the battle for the backup QB job.
Matasovsky : Both quarterbacks have had rocky starts in their turn to be the starter. They both have rebounded nicely, however. Personally, I think Altmyer has the higher ceiling. That said, Dobbs is leading the quarterback race. He adds a dynamic element with his legs, and his longevity in the league makes him invaluable if Goff cannot be on the field for a series.
Altmyer is facing typical rookie issues of holding onto the ball too long and the occasional play he wants back. At this moment, in preseason week two, Dobbs is the answer if I need to pick Goff’s replacement for a game.
Booher : I think the biggest question the Lions have to answer quickly is who the starting center will be. That is arguably the most important position on the field, and the Lions don't have a clear answer to this question right now. I think Scruggs will be the guy ultimately until Mays returns, but he hasn't done enough to set that in stone at this point in training camp.
Chirco : I believe it's who is going to start at outside cornerback opposite D.J. Reed. And to a lesser degree, it's who is going to claim the slot corner job out of camp. Right now, I don't believe the Lions have a clear-cut answer for either. Although at this present juncture, I would say Rock Ya-Sin becomes the starter opposite Reed, while Roger McCreary captures the starting gig in the slot.
Matasovsky : The top question in the short term is how to tackle the nickel corner situation. Abney had good plays in each of the two preseason games, but also had two penalties against Washington. Meanwhile, Roger McCreary is not making a massive flash at nickel. Christian Izien is an option for later in the season, but might be tasked with a starting safety role in Week 1 as Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph rehab their injuries.
In the long term, the question is how the backup line will shake out. The Lions have seen attrition catch up with their line in most seasons of the Dan Campbell era, so the question becomes which four-to-five linemen make the cut as backups. Against Washington, it was hard to point out high quality backups, which is a concern.

title: Lions Updated Bubble Watch after Commanders Game: Defense
full_text:
The Detroit Lions just have one preseason game remaining, but still have multiple players on the bubble for roster spots.
On the defensive side of the ball, a few players stood out in the Lions’ preseason victory over the Commanders Saturday.
Notably, EDGE Derrick Moore delivered a solid performance in his preseason debut. For starters, he amassed one of Detroit's two sacks in the exhibition tilt, with the other being produced by veteran D.J. Wonnum.
Moore also generated two total pressures and a pair of defensive stops in the outing. And for his efforts, he earned a 70.9 overall grade from Pro Football Focus.
Moore and Wonnum are very much in contention for the starting EDGE job opposite Pro Bowler Aidan Hutchinson. And while Wonnum is likely currently in the lead, Moore can't be counted out quite yet. And at the very least, the University of Michigan product has a legitimate shot to produce meaningful snaps in his first year as a pro.
Additionally, defensive lineman Skyler Gill-Howard continued to impress Saturday.
The 2026 sixth-round pick further solidified his spot on the Lions’ 53-man roster to open the season, showcasing yet again the relentless motor that has become a signature element of his overall game. On 23 snaps against Washington, he recorded a 76.7 PFF overall grade.
Lions head coach Dan Campbell continues to sing Gill-Howard's praises , too.
"... He knows he’s not a huge guy, but he knows who he is and he knows how he has to play,” Campbell said about Gill-Howard in the postgame. “And he plays with high effort and he’s crafty, man. He’s explosive and he’s violent.”
Recent free-agent signing Ben Stille also logged some quality reps at both nose tackle and the “Big End” position. Still, the 28-year-old, who most recently suited up for the Buccaneers and the Cardinals, is likely on the outside looking in when it comes to a roster spot.
While Moore, Gill-Howard and Stille clearly improved their stock, fellow defensive linemen Myles Adams, Tyre West and Eric O'Neill failed to do so. It wasn't all because of their own doing, either.
Adams and O'Neill each didn't see the field until the fourth quarter, and West didn't log a single snap. It's pretty telling of what the coaching staff thinks of the three of them headed into the Lions’ preseason finale with the Colts next Saturday. I would say it's safe to assume each of them will be left off Detroit's season-opening roster.
Meanwhile, in the secondary, cornerback Nick Whiteside perhaps hurt his stock the most.
For as well as he was performing prior to Saturday, it needs to be mentioned he had a rough day in coverage against the Commanders, permitting the most receiving yards of all the team's defensive backs. He allowed 69 yards on three receptions, with 55 of those yards coming on the boundary against Washington WR Nick Nash.
Overall, it was a forgettable showing from Whiteside, who now faces increased pressure to come through with a much stronger effort against Indianapolis.
Along with the aforementioned names, here is the list of Lions players on the bubble entering the final week of the exhibition season:
Thomas Harper, Ahmed Hassanein, Ennis Rakestraw Jr., Mekhi Wingo, Tyler Lacy, Chris Smith, Aidan Keanaaina, Anthony Lucas, Joe Bachie, Erick Hunter, Troy Reeder, Aamaris Brown, De'Shawn Rucker, Loren Strickland and Dan Jackson.

title: Updated Lions Depth Chart After Preseason Week 2
full_text:
The Detroit Lions roster hopefuls will have one more opportunity to impress the coaching staff.
Saturday marked the second of three preseason games for the Lions this year, with the finale coming Saturday against the Indianapolis Colts. Roster cuts will have to be made shortly thereafter, so time is running out for players to impress the coaches and front office.
However, some have used their opportunities nicely through the first two preseason games. As a result, some changes have been made to the depth chart.
Here is an updated depth chart prediction for the Lions after their second preseason game.
Starter: Jared Goff. Backup: Josh Dobbs. Reserve: Luke Altmyer.
The Lions' backup competition will carry into the preseason finale . Dobbs has the upper hand with his mobility and his knowledge of the system dating back to his time in Drew Petzing's offense in Arizona, but Altmyer has caught the eye of the coaching staff and won't go down without a fight.
Starter: Jahmyr Gibbs. Backup: Isiah Pacheco. Reserves: Sione Vaki, Jacob Saylors, Trayveon Williams, Raheem Blackshear, Jabari Small.
Pacheco has been injured, and with Gibbs being limited to prepare him for the regular season the Lions have made training camp a showcase of their depth.
Saylors has been the most consistent, but Williams and Blackshear are intriguing experienced veterans. Vaki will also factor into the equation, but he hasn't participated in a preseason game yet.
Starters: Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, Isaac TeSlaa. Backups: Greg Dortch, Tom Kennedy, Tay Martin. Reserves: Cedrick Wilson Jr., Dominic Lovett, Lucky Jackson, Tarik Black, Malik Cunningham. Injured: Kendrick Law (IR).
TeSlaa has been up and down throughout camp, and as a result him being the bona fide third wideout isn't as much of a sure thing as it was coming into camp. Dortch figures to be the next player in the mix.
Martin has been brought up plenty by the special teams coordinator for his work in that phase, and as a result he'll be in the mix to make the roster. Wilson is also in that conversation, though his chances may have taken a hit with his injury in Saturday's game.
Starter: Sam LaPorta. Backup: Brock Wright. Reserves: Tyler Conklin, Jackson Meeks, Zach Horton, Thomas Gordon.
The Lions have some solid depth at this position, as Meeks has proven over the first two preseason games. Wright has a role due to his ability to block, and Conklin is a solid veteran presence. The Lions could keep four at this position if Meeks can contribute on special teams.
Starters: Penei Sewell (left), Blake Miller (right). Backups: Larry Borom, Devin Cochran. Reserve: Colby Sorsdal. Injured: Gio Manu (NFI).
Borom has struggled as of late, and his showing in Saturday's game didn't inspire much optimism. The Lions will still likely count on him as the swing tackle in jumbo packages, but Miller appears to be pulling away with the right tackle job.
Starters: Christian Mahogany (left), Tate Ratledge (right). Backups: Miles Frazier, Ben Bartch. Reserves: Mason Miller, Melvin Priestly,
Bartch's injuries throughout camp have hurt his chances of competing for the left tackle job, and possibly even making the roster. Frazier has struggled, but his versatility likely puts him next in line in the event that the Lions deal with another injury. They could also look to add depth here.
Starter: Juice Scruggs. Backup: Seth McLaughlin. Reserve: Michael Niese. Injured: Cade Mays.
With Mays injured, the Lions have started an impromptu competition for the starting spot. Scruggs is the favorite and will get every opportunity to earn the job until Mays returns, but McLaughlin has had some bright moments. If he has interior versatility and could provide depth at guard, he would boost his chances to make the roster.
Starters: Tyleik Williams, Alim McNeill. Backups: Skyler Gill-Howard, Levi Onwuzurike. Reserves: Tyler Lacy, Chris Smith, Ben Stille, Mekhi Wingo, Tyre West, Myles Adams.
One of the top performers this preseason has been Gill-Howard, who has dominated rushing the passer from the interior. He looks the part of a potential contributor, and has rose up the depth chart as a result. He'll certainly be a player to watch as the regular season begins.
Detroit has some depth questions to short out come final cuts, as all of their reserve options could theoretically contribute in the rotation during the regular season.
Starters: Aidan Hutchinson, D.J. Wonnum. Backups: Derrick Moore, Ahmed Hassanein. Reserves: Eric O'Neill, Anthony Lucas, Payton Turner.
Turner's stock has dropped dramatically throughout camp, as he hasn't practiced since the first day of camp. Meanwhile, Moore, Hassanein and both undrafted free agents have all made their case at making the roster.
This competition for the final spots will go down to the wire, and whoever doesn't earn a spot could find a new landing spot on an active roster through the waiver process.
Starters: Jack Campbell (MIKE), Derrick Barnes (SAM). Backups: Devin White, Malcolm Rodriguez. Reserves: Jimmy Rolder, Trevor Nowaske, Damone Clark, Joe Bachie, Erick Hunter, Troy Reeder, Amen Ogbongbemiga.
It appears as though the Lions may be shifting their base defense to nickel, which would put two linebackers on the field. Still, the competition between White and Rodriguez for the third spot has carried throughout camp even though Rodriguez missed some time with injury.
The Lions have plenty of depth here, and each of the reserves has a case for making the team. Like the EDGE position, those who don't make the cut could find new homes quickly.
Starters: D.J. Reed, Rock Ya-Sin, Christian Izien (Nickel). Backups: Ennis Rakestraw, Roger McCreary, Reserves: Keith Abney II, Nick Whiteside, Khalil Dorsey, Aamaris Brown, Bump Cooper Jr., Ekow Boye-Doe.
Izien appears to be stepping into first team nickel duties, but Abney and McCreary are both still in the mix. Whiteside's stock has cooled off some, but he still could find his way onto the roster with his work on special teams.
Starters: Chuck Clark, Avonte Maddox. Backups: Thomas Harper, Dan Jackson. Injured: Kerby Joseph (PUP), Brian Branch (PUP).
Joseph and Branch are both expected to miss the start of the regular season at this point. The team could possibly benefit from another addition at this spot, as they have become thin on depth after Loren Strickland was waived with an injury designation.
Kicker: Jake Bates. Punter: Jack Fox. Long-snapper: Hogan Hatten.
The Lions still haven't added any competition to this group, and all three appear set in their roles with the regular season approaching quickly.

title: Grades: Strong Defensive Effort Helps Lions Prevail Over Commanders
full_text:
The Detroit Lions finished up their second of three preseason games Saturday against the Washington Commanders.
Head coach Dan Campbell got some of his starters a portion of the action, holding out some of the stars but playing many of the players atop their depth chart. It resulted in a (RESULT)
Here are grades for each position group based on performance in Saturday's preseason game.
It was a tough start to the day for Josh Dobbs, who got the start with Jared Goff sidelined. On his first dropback, he was blindsided by a corner blitz from former Lion Amik Robertson resulting in a sack fumble that was recovered for a Commanders touchdown.
On the ensuing drive, Dobbs airmailed a receiver and was picked off by Quan Martin. However, he then settled in and had two nice completions to Cedrick Wilson Jr. on his third drive before taking a zone-read 50 yards for a touchdown.
Altmyer took the field for the remainder of the first half and led two series. The first was a 13-play drive that started backed up but stalled out when he was sacked on third-down. His second series saw him move the offense once again, but emerged without points after Jake Bates missed a 55-yard field goal.
Dobbs would re-enter in the third quarter and lead two drives, the second of which ending in a touchdown. He finished 7-of-12 for 74 yards and an interception.
Altmyer finished the game with the final two drives. He led a field goal drive to start the fourth quarter, then led the game-icing drive that featured two fourth-down conversions. One of those came when he extended the play by scrambling before hitting Jackson Meeks to move the chains.
For Altmyer, the final line featured nine completions on 13 attempts for 86 yards, but he did take four sacks.
The Lions' run game continued to be solid for most of Saturday's game. Sione Vaki did not play, with Jahmyr Gibbs and Isiah Pacheco both also being out. As a result, the work was divided up between Jacob Saylors, Jabari Small, Trayveon Williams and Raheem Blackshear.
Saylors didn't have the same impact that he did in the preseason opener, as he got leveled in pass-protection on one play-action rep. Williams stood out amongst the crowd, with his most notable stretch being a third-quarter drive during which he had a 24-yard reception on a screen and capped it off with a 1-yard touchdown run.
Williams led the group with 36 yards on 10 carries, while Saylors had 32 yards on six carries. It was Blackshear who converted the game-winning fourth-down, as he plunged forward for the 3-yard conversion to ice the game.
Cedrick Wilson Jr. helped steady the offense with two catches on the team's third drive, but he unfortunately left with an injury shortly after the second catch. It was a mostly quiet day otherwise out wide, with a majority of the targets going to the tight ends.
Tay Martin had a big block on Dobbs' touchdown run, and also notched an 11-yard catch. However, he missed a major opportunity at a big play when he dropped a crossing route that would've gone for a big gain.
Elsewhere, Lucky Jackson contributed two catches for 15 yards while Malik Cunningham, Tom Kennedy and Dominic Lovett each had one grab apiece.
The Lions got production from both Jackson Meeks and Tyler Conklin throughout Saturday's game. Meeks was a favorite target of Altmyer's catching four passes for 33 yards including the critical fourth-down conversion in the fourth quarter.
Meanwhile, Conklin hauled in two passes for 21 yards and also contributed to the Dobbs touchdown run with a nice block.
Brock Wright had one catch for three yards, but his day got off to a rough start when his chip on Amik Robertson couldn't derail the blitz, leading to the strip sack touchdown for the Commanders.
The Lions started four of the five they anticipate rolling out in the regular season, with Penei Sewell being the only one out of action. In addition to Wright's failed chip attempt, Larry Borom was beat inside on the disastrous second snap for the offense.
Unfortunately, the second-string offensive line struggled to protect Altmyer throughout Saturday's game. Altmyer was sacked a total of four times, with Colby Sorsdal and Seth McLaughlin being among the linemen who were beaten for sacks.
There were also multiple procedural penalties on the Lions' offensive line throughout the game. Miles Frazier and McLaughlin were both whistled for false starts.
For as poor as the game started offensively, the defense was much better. D.J. Wonnum set the tone with a sack on the first drive on Jayden Daniels, and notched another one in tandem with rookie Skyler Gill-Howard that was negated by penalty.
Rookie Derrick Moore had a big showing in his debut after missing the preseason opener. He notched a strip-sack to end the half, showcasing the explosiveness that the Lions liked about him coming out of college.
Eric O'Neill also continued his strong week, as he had a solid final defensive series. He pushed the pocket on multiple dropbacks, and had the hurry that forced Sam Hartman's incompletion on fourth-down.
Gill-Howard and Levi Onwuzurike both had good showings on the interior. Onwuzurike had three tackles, while Gill-Howard had multiple clean wins leading to hurries to go along with a tackle for loss. Mekhi Wingo also showcased good hustle chasing down a screen pass at the line of scrimmage.
Devin White made an immediate impact with a pressure of Jayden Daniels on the first defensive snap of the game. Malcolm Rodriguez also had a nice pass-rush on a well-timed blitz, as he smothered Athan Kaliakmanis to force a hurried throw.
White and Trevor Nowaske paced the group with three tackles each, while Rodriguez and Erick Hunter each had two. Hunter was in coverage on the final fourth-down incompletion by the Commanders.
D.J. Reed, who is expected to be the team's top cornerback, looked the part in Saturday's game. He had multiple stops and showcased great technique, which helped him tally two tackles for loss in his half of action.
Avonte Maddox blew up a screen pass for a tackle for loss. There were some struggles in coverage, as rookie Keith Abney II was whistled for two penalties including a defensive pass interference where Commanders wideout Jaden Bradley made an outstanding catch.
However, Abney bounced back to help with Rodriguez on the pressure that hurried Kaliakmanis. He also had good coverage on a third-down to force a punt later in the game.
It was a solid day for the Lions' special teams units, with the exception of a missed 55-yard field goal that Jake Bates pushed wide right. The biggest play came late after the Lions connected on a field goal to push their lead to four, when Jackson Meeks punched out a ball that Erick Hunter recovered on the ensuing kickoff.
The Lions balanced the workload between Dobbs and Altmyer, splitting each half to ensure that they got similar workloads. It was a solid gameplan defensively, however, that helped the team rebound after a tough start offensively.
Ultimately, Detroit gained some clarity in key spots that will help with roster decisions moving forward. Coordinator Kelvin Sheppard's efforts were key to the victory, as he dialed up a number of interesting stunts and blitzes to keep the Commanders off balance offensively.
Detroit is facing some tough roster choices heading into their final week of preseason play. However, it's clear that there are strengths along the defensive line and potential issues along the offensive line. As a result, it should be an intriguing final round of training camp practices leading up to the preseason finale and ensuing final cuts.

title: Total Domination: Everything I Saw From Practice 15 of Packers Training Camp
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Late in Monday’s practice at Green Bay Packers training camp, with the defense beating up on the offense play after play, Matthew Golden caught a pass and was tackled by Barryn Sorrell.
A fight – that word used a bit loosely – ensued. Lukas Van Ness and Aaron Banks got involved, and Zaire Franklin added a little fuel to the fire.
“We’re just being competitive, man, going out there and playing football,” Sorrell said. “Things happen. Emotions get high. Got into it a little bit. That’s my boy. I’m his boy. We’re still cool. It’s football.”
The former Texas teammates – the Packers drafted both players last year – had made up by the end of practice.
“You know how it is when you’ve got a brother-type thing,” Sorrell said. “Me and Matt are always getting into it. It’s just how our relationship is. Today it got out on the football a little bit and everybody thought we were so serious. The whole time we were joking around a little bit. Like I said, it’s football. It’s how it gets. It’s fun.”
Throughout Monday’s practice, the defense took the fight to the offense. And that’s where we’ll dive into our daily training camp report.
The defense has been the top unit throughout most of training camp. Monday’s practice, the 15th of training camp, was no different – other than the level of domination.
Jonathan Gannon’s unit made life a living hell for the offense. From the first play to the last, from the starters to the backups, from runs to passes, the defense kept swinging and the offense kept getting clobbered.
Late in practice, with the pocket collapsing, Jordan Love threw a no-look pass in the general vicinity of his checkdown player in the flat. Maybe Love was trying to make a play. Or, maybe it was the frustration of the moment.
The defense produced three takeaways. First, during a 2-minute drill, Love had nowhere to go on fourth-and-10 and was intercepted by Keisean Nixon. Next, a handoff to MarShawn Lloyd turned into a fumble, which was recovered by Barryn Sorrell. Finally, Kyle McCord was intercepted by Kitan Oladapo.
“Every time we go out there, we (play) aggressive defense,” Sorrell said. “We’re trying to compete. It starts with our play style. We try to have a really good motor out there and we try to play violently. Obviously, whoever’s across from us might not like that and whatever happens, happens after that. At the end of the day, we’re going to go out there and we’re going to play our brand of football.”
New injuries: CB Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring), Arron Mosby (illness).
PUP: Edge Micah Parsons (knee), LS Matt Orzech (calf), TE Luke Musgrave (neck), DT Jordon Riley (Achilles).
Old injuries: S Javon Bullard (foot), edge Collin Oliver (calf), WR Savion Williams (ankle), TE Thomas Yassmin (knee), DT Warren Brinson (calf).
Returned to practice: CB Brandon Cisse (knee), WR Jayden Reed (personal), T/G Darian Kinnard (ankle), WR J. Michael Sturdivant (concussion protocol).
Brinson was injured during pregame warmups at Denver and didn’t play.
“He felt a little tweak in his calf, so he’ll miss a little bit of time,” coach Matt LaFleur said amid several updates before practice .
Sturdivant, an undrafted free agent who is challenging for a roster spot, suffered a head injury on his one catch at Denver but was back doing individual drills on Monday.

title: Play and Players of Day at Practice 15 of Training Camp (Bad News, Haters)
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The first play of Green Bay Packers training camp on Monday was a handoff to Josh Jacobs. Cornerback Brandon Cisse beat his man and was waiting for a tackle for loss.
The last sequence was a goal-line stand.
And so it went for about 2 hours. The 15th practice of Packers training camp was total domination by Jonathan Gannon’s defense. Starters, backups. It didn’t matter. So, naturally, our daily feature is defense-centric.
On third-and-8, impressive first-year quarterback Kyle McCord fired the ball downfield. Safety Kitan Oladapo, who has been playing mostly in the slot the last couple weeks, made a leaping interception.
“Just dropped to the curl-flat and Kyle was looking right at me. I don’t know why he actually threw it,” Oladapo said, unable to stifle a laugh.
The Packers drafted Oladapo in the fifth round in 2024. At the Scouting Combine, he posted a 36-inch vertical jump. That was while wearing shorts and gym shoes. There’s no way of knowing, obviously, but it seemed like a full-pads Oladapo jumped higher than that.
“Yeah, I’m a gamer. I’m not a good test-taker,” he said with a laugh.
The team held a closed practice on Sunday, Oladapo intercepted Tyrod Taylor in that one.
“I dropped down as a hook player and Tyrod play-actioned and tried to throw a dig and I just jumped up and I caught the dig,” Oladapo said.
“I probably got higher yesterday, I’m not going to lie,” he added. “I’m just glad to make the most of my opportunities.”
The starting cornerback tandem for Week 1 at Minnesota might be set. Brandon Cisse almost certainly will be one. Keisean Nixon probably will be the other.
With Benjamin St-Juste out with a hamstring injury, Nixon took all the No. 1 reps and had an excellent day.
First, Jordan Love went deep up the right sideline to Jayden Reed. Nixon had textbook coverage and swatted the pass aside with his left hand. Next, on fourth-and-10 in a 2-minute drill, the play broke down and Love extended the play to his right. With no good options, he threw one up but Nixon made a leaping interception.
Fine, but how about against the speed of Matthew Golden? Love went 0-for-2 on deep passes. On the first, Nixon walled off Golden so he couldn’t get to the ball; from afar, it seemed like Nixon might have been able to make a play on the ball rather than simply forcing an incompletion. A few plays later, Love tried it again but Nixon had excellent coverage and the ball fell harmlessly incomplete.
While Jonathan Gannon might be able to scheme up some pressures, it’s indisputable that the key to the opening stretch of games will be the ability of Lukas Van Ness to help replace some of Micah Parsons’ pass rush.
Van Ness has had some good days and some quiet days. This was a really good day.
It started with Van Ness stuffing a handoff to Josh Jacobs during the opening series of plays. In the passing game, Van Ness provided pressures against both of Green Bay’s tackles.
Against left tackle Jordan Morgan, he ducked underneath Morgan and got to Jordan Love. Love hit Matthew Golden for a big gain near the sideline, but Van Ness might have had a sack.
Later, during a 2-minute drill, Van Ness beat Morgan again to force a throwaway. A couple plays later, on third-and-10, Van Ness tossed premier right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele at the feet of Love, which resulted in an errant checkdown to MarShawn Lloyd.
“It’s been awesome,” he said last week. “I’ve really enjoyed the defense. It’s putting us in a position to win and just a lot of different looks and fronts and schemes. We’re having fun. I’ve been happy with the way they’re utilizing me and I’m excited to see how I can grow.”
The tone-setters of the defense will be the elite linebacker tandem of Edgerrin Cooper and Zaire Franklin. They’ve seemingly traded dominant days all summer, with Monday being Cooper’s turn.
During the starters’ second set of plays, Cooper broke up a pass over the middle to tight end Tucker Kraft. Shortly thereafter, he ruined back-to-back plays for MarShawn Lloyd. First, Cooper didn’t buy any of the misdirection stuff in the backfield and tackled Lloyd for a loss. Next, on third-and-4, Jordan Love checked it down to Lloyd but Cooper stopped the play well short of the marker.
Later, Cooper set the edge on a perimeter run by Jacobs and teamed with Barryn Sorrell to make the play near the line of scrimmage.
Finally, during the starters’ last set of plays, Cooper almost intercepted a pass intended for Kraft on third-and-2. A couple plays later, Lloyd tried to bounce a run to the outside but Cooper was there in a blur.
“I just feel like with me and Coop, it’s really just being honest with each other, first and foremost, on what we both can be better at,” Franklin said last week. “And we hold each other accountable, which I think is a great thing.
“I think we both have a great energy. We both love football and we both just really enjoy playing. That always comes out. At the end of the day, whether I’m not really in a mood or he’s not in a mood, at the end of the day, we both love playing. And I think we always connect over our love of ball.”

title: Packers-Cardinals Fight? Matt LaFleur Has Fun Solution
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The final week of Green Bay Packers training camp begins with the second-to-last public practice of training camp on Monday. The main event of the summer will come on Wednesday with a joint practice against the Arizona Cardinals.
It will be a brother battle between longtime Packers coach Matt LaFleur and the Cardinals’ new coach, Mike LaFleur.
“It’s going to be a pretty cool experience,” LaFleur said at Lambeau Field before Monday’s practice. “It’s not the first time but it’s certainly the first time as head coaches. I talked to him last night, just trying to finalize the details and the plan for practice and look forward to seeing him.”
LaFleur tried to downplay coaching against his brother before finally admitting that it will be cool to work with his brother at Wednesday’s practice and against him during Friday’s final preseason game.
“I think it’s going to be pretty special but, at the end of the day, we’re just looking to try to get good work on both sides,” he said. “Certainly, always going to prioritize the Green Bay Packers but if there is another team in the National Football League that I’ll be rooting for, it will be the Arizona Cardinals.”
His parents will be there, of course.
“They’ll probably look like a Christmas tree, green and red,” LaFleur joked.
Mike LaFleur isn’t Matt LaFleur’s brother. He’s Mike LaFleur. Staying true to that has been an important part of his career, Matt LaFleur said.
“I think it’s a byproduct of a lot of things,” Matt said of his brother’s career path. “I’d say certainly, he’s never shied away from the work. He’s earned the opportunity, and then it’s also, we’ve both been fortunate to be around a lot of great people. This doesn’t happen unless you get those experiences and learn from some of the best in football. But it is cool to see him get his shot.”
Before practice, LaFleur discussed a handful of injuries.
Rookie cornerback Brandon Cisse, who has emerged as a likely starter, played only one series against Denver because of a knee injury, “should be good to go” this week, LaFleur said.
Second-year defensive tackle Warren Brinson was a surprise inactive against Denver.
“Yeah, it happened in warmups, he felt a little tweak in his calf. So, he’ll miss a little bit of time,” LaFleur said.
Long snapper Matt Orzech remains on PUP because of a calf injury. In his absence, rookie kicker Trey Smack has found a groove with Cal Adomitis doing the snapping.
“I think he’s getting closer,” LaFleur said. “To say he’ll be back this week, I think it might be too soon to say. But I know he’s getting close.”
Running back Josh Jacobs, who returned to individual drills last week following a calf injury, will take a step this week.
“He’ll be limited in all team periods, but he’ll be out there practicing,” LaFleur said.
Rookie receiver J. Michael Sturdivant remains in the concussion protocol, which will obviously hurt his chances of making a last-minute dash to a roster spot.
“He’s done a lot of good things,” LaFleur said. “What I really like about him is just doing all the little things, because I think it’s true with most young players, especially guys that are trying to carve out a role on this football team, it’s like, the more you can do. I think we’ve seen it in the run game, just how he goes out there and blocks. I think we’ve seen it on special teams, his ability to go out there and contribute.
“There’s going to be a lot of tough decisions though down the stretch.”
LaFleur has done a bunch of joint practices during his tenure. It’s a collaborative effort between the coaches to get the work done in a way that work for everybody.
“He’s quick to criticize everything that I put on the schedule,” LaFleur joked. “So, he’s like, ‘Why are we doing this? Why are we doing that? We never do this.’ And I was like, ‘All right, Mike, you’ve got all the answers.’ Nah, it’s been healthy, it’s been good. There’s been give and take on both sides, for sure.”
Joint practices can get chippy, especially with fewer ramifications in terms of NFL fines and suspensions. After all, it’s a practice and not a game.
LaFleur isn’t sure if the brother-vs.-brother nature of the practice will impact the teams’ behavior. However, in a carrot-and-stick approach, playing time will serve as LaFleur’s stick.
He punctuated his answer with a joke.
“It goes back to what we’ve been saying for years,” LaFleur said. “First of all, if there is an issue in practice – we’re not going to play everybody in the game, but if you don’t get your work in, you’re going to play in the game. And conversely, if you’re somebody that needs that work, to get those snaps so the whole world can see it, you’re going to be limited or not at all playing in the game.
“The second part of that is if there’s an issue, I’m going to tell the guys, ‘Hey, you come tag me in. They can tag in my brother. And we’ll throw down on the 50.’”

title: Ultimate Packers Longshot Anthony Campbell’s Journey Started in Jamaica
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – It took about 2.5 seconds for Anthony Campbell to beat his blocker and sack Broncos quarterback Sam Ehlinger on Saturday.
Campbell’s path toward beating some incredible odds and potentially earning a spot on the Green Bay Packers’ 53-man roster has taken about half a lifetime.
Campbell was born in Kingston, Jamaica. Football was definitely not on his radar.
“I played a lot of different sports like soccer, rugby, track and cricket – a lot of sports,” he told Packers On SI recently. “I played more soccer. In middle school, when I moved over here in 2013 (or) ‘14, around there, I started playing soccer. I was a goalie back in Bartow, (Fla.), so that’s where it started off.
“And then in high school, a school resource officer, RIP Officer (Michael) Quinn – he died from cancer – but he seen me in the hallway walking around, he was like, ‘You should come play football for us.’”
Because of his background in soccer, Campbell started out as a kicker. As a sophomore, he started playing as a 215-pound defensive end.
“And my junior year, I started getting looks and offers and all that crazy stuff,” he said. “So, it’s been a big transition to football.”
There were a couple big detours along the way, though. Offers from Florida Athletic, Indiana and other schools dried up when he missed his senior season at Bartow High School because of a leg injury.
So, he spent the 2019 and 2020 seasons at Independence Community College in Kansas, which got him back on recruiters’ radars, and the 2021 and 2022 seasons at Louisiana Monroe, where he had 3.5 tackles for losses during his final season.
That got him his big opportunity at Miami.
“I wanted to go against better competition, get experience, better coaching and stuff, and we was losing and had ups and downs there, so I transferred to Miami and stuff happened.”
Campbell played in one game for the Hurricanes in 2023 and eight games in 2024. In two seasons, he played 56 snaps on defense. He wasn’t hurt. He just didn’t get on the field.
“Not wanting to bash nobody, but it’s just opportunity,” he said. “You know, stuff happens and then opportunity. You just got to be in the right place at the right time.”
Campbell’s confidence could have been crushed. If he wasn’t good enough to play in college, how on earth would he be good enough to play in the NFL?
Campbell, however, wouldn’t take no for an answer. He listened to those close to him and kept chasing what might have seemed like an impossible dream.
“You got people in your background telling you that you can do whatever you want,” he explained. “Because I’m very dedicated. Once I put my mind on something, I’m going to accomplish it. And I’m going to try to push myself to overcome anything, any obstacle that’s coming my way. I like to challenge myself and prove people wrong.”
Not surprisingly, Campbell went undrafted in 2025. He signed with the Seahawks about a month after the draft and competed for a roster spot during training camp but was released. He spent a couple days on their practice squad, and that was that.
Campbell was out of the league until the Packers signed him to their practice squad for the final week of the season and then retained him with a futures contract.
That humble start kicked off one of the more amazing Packers training camp stories in years. Campbell started camp by batting down a pass or two every day. As camp has progressed, he’s made more plays in the backfield, whether tackles for losses on running plays or pressures of the quarterback.
Against Denver, he clobbered Ehlinger. He finished the game with three tackles, according to the official stats, and a team-high four pressures, according to Pro Football Focus.
Anthony Campbell had a big night at Denver. Here’s his sack. pic.twitter.com/yarFNSW6L4
“A.C., man, he’s a guy that’s going to maximize every opportunity you give him,” position coach Vince Oghobaase said last week. “In the spring, every technique, every alignment, every drill, he wants to do it to perfection. When you get out there and tell him to do something to an offensive lineman aligned at this position, do this technique, he’s going to do it.
“He’s maximizing his opportunity. I think he’s batted over 10, 12 balls over the course of training camp, dating back to the spring. He’s been playing lights out, playing fearless, playing confident, playing with a chip on his shoulder. He’s come a long way. He’s done an incredible job. That confidence piece is huge for defensive linemen. When you’re confident, and you play fast, you play free, things can happen for him. He’s going like that (hand angled up).”
How? How did a player with exactly one tackle in two seasons at Miami put himself in position to make the Packers’ roster?
“It’s just something in me,” Campbell said. “My mom, the same way. It’s something in me.”
He shared a tackle for loss with Chris McClellan against Denver and with Warren Brinson against Pittsburgh.
“Just doing my job. Coach J.G. calls the right call, I’m going to do my best to execute it. Just doing my job. Coach V.O. teaches a lot of stuff to do. We got techniques we work on every day. You do it. I’m just going to go out there and do my best. Not think a lot, just go. Do my job. Whatever they tell me to do, I’m going to do it.”
From Kingston to kicking, from out of the league to challenging for a roster spot, it’s been an incredible journey.
“It’s not over yet,” he interjected. “I’m still working but, at the end of the day, I want to look back and I’m saying, damn, I’m strong. I’m going to keep pushing. Whatever happens here or somewhere else, I’m going to keep pushing.”
A huge final week of training camp will kick off on Monday. It will culminate with a joint practice against the Cardinals on Wednesday and a preseason game on Friday. Gutekunst will select his 53-man roster on Sunday.
“I love this transition for me,” Campbell said. “I like the experience I’m getting right now. Everything here is beautiful here. I love everything here. Players, everybody.”
