title: Andre Cisco's Outlook Could Skyrocket After Performance in Jets' Preseason Win vs. Steelers
full_text:
There was a lot to be pleased with from the Jets' preseason Week 2 shutout win over the Pittsburgh Steelers on both sides of the ball, but one particular player stood to benefit the most with his back already against the wall.
Safety Andre Cisco signed a one-year extension to remain in the Big Apple following a 2025 season that was cut short due to a pectoral tear, though he has been one of the biggest losers from training camp with his dissipating ball skills and the standout play from offseason acquisition Dane Belton.
While Belton logged four total tackles and had a great first half in Friday night's 17-0 win, Cisco came away with the team's first interception since the 2025 preseason on a jumped crossing route deep in the red zone, showcasing the type of skill set he can bring to this secondary when he is healthy.
Andre Cisco in the right place at the right time 😌 NYJvsPIT on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/eLGuXJYqMB
The goal coming into the offseason was to have a stiff competition for the starting safety position opposite of veteran Minkah Fitzpatrick. Belton has had the upper hand and it was clear that Cisco needed a big game against the Steelers to save his roster spot , but his outlook greatly improved as one of the team's best performers on Friday.
Although Cisco, the 2021 third-rounder of the Jacksonville Jaguars, registered as many as 73 total tackles in 2022 and had four interceptions in 2023, injuries derailed his 2025 debut season in Gang Green and left him fighting for something to prove going into Year 2 in Gotham.
On top of that, Pro Football Focus gave Cisco the 67th-ranked coverage grade (54.5) and the 28th-ranked run-defense grade (75.6) out of 98 qualified safeties last season. He has not been bad against the run, but the lack of impressions throughout the offseason had done nothing to ease the pressure until his preseason Week 2 breakout flipped the script.
That said, he lost a lot of ground to Belton in the safety battle prior to the win over the Steelers and faced an uncertain outlook for the 2026 season. After all, Belton recorded the second-most tackles (120) on the New York Giants last season and forced the same number of turnovers (four) as the entire Jets defense.
Belton has thrived in training camp with multiple pass breakups, interceptions and by consistently making plays at the line of scrimmage. He also recorded the lowest missed tackle percentage (4.1%) among all safeties who played at least 400 snaps last season, per PFF .
Even though Belton has never been a full-time starter, his stock has been soaring as he continues to emerge as a legitimate candidate to get the nod at safety. His work ethic and overall production at training camp have impressed head coach Aaron Glenn and made this an intriguing battle for reasons that many did not expect when the offseason began.
Prior to Friday night, Belton had put himself in front of Cisco as the front-runner to land the starting spot alongside Fitzpatrick. Throw in the fact that fellow safety Malachi Moore has underwhelmed and failed to make any significant plays and it should come down to Belton and Cisco for the starting duties.
After Friday's interception and highlight-worthy performance, Cisco has reminded everyone that this is not Belton's position for the taking just yet.
He certainly gave him an opening with his unimpressive offseason showing up to this point, but his ability to force one of two Steelers interceptions one week after Pittsburgh committed zero turnovers at all against the Green Bay Packers was the type of performance he needed at just the right time.
Sure, it was still a preseason game that had little meaning in the grand scheme, yet it was also a major step in the right direction if he wants to retain his roster spot.

title: 5 Winners, 3 Losers From Day 15 of Eagles Training Camp: Makai Lemon Has Big Role
full_text:
The final week of training camp is officially underway at the Jefferson Health Training Complex.
The Philadelphia Eagles had a light day of practice on Monday, going in just helmets and shorts before showing off in front of the fans at Lincoln Financial Field -- their only open practice of the summer. They'll have one final practice of training camp open to the media Wednesday afternoon before wrapping things up with the preseason finale on Friday .
Then it's roster cutdown day on Sunday night. The countdown to Week 1 is coming.
While this was a light practice on Monday, the observations explained everything you needed to know about this practice. So will the winners and losers on Day 15 of training camp.
Makai Lemon: Not only was Lemon a full participant at practice for the first time since August 3, but the Eagles had him with the first team offense at full go. Lemon is going to start come Week 1, as the Eagles are going to use him in motion and in the slot. He just needs to stack up days.
Tanner McKee: He didn't wow anyone in practice on Monday, yet it's noticeable McKee is the QB2 and started firts with the second team. Guess the preseason performance had an effect on the backup quarterback decision after all -- at least for the first practice of the week.
Jalyx Hunt: A dominant performance for Hunt in this light practice, as he finished with multiple sacks and pressures during team drills. Hunt has showcased his quickness on the right side all summer, and is keeping up his status a sthe best player in camp. He'll be fun to watch this year.
Moro Ojomo: The entire first team defensive line was dominant, but Ojomo gets a shout out for a sack and creating consistent pressure up the middle. He's another player that will be fun to watch, and it's easy to see why Vic Fangio wants to keep him around past this year.
Elijah Moore: Another good day for Moore, who is being used in various roles in the offense. Hollywood Brown had a good day as well, catching a few deep balls, but Moore is making it harder for the Eagles to cut him. If he keeps getting open, he'll be forcing the Eagles' hand.
Eli Stowers: A hamstring injury following a less-than-ideal training camp? Not good for Stowers, who was trending towards a healthy scratch in Week 1. Now he could be out of a few practices, further hurting his development. The Eagles need him to get as many reps as he can over the next fe weeks.
Cole Wisniewski: In a battle for the No. 4 safety spot, Wisniewski has a concussion and did not practice. I think the Eagles will try to get him on the practice squad, but this was a setback for the roster chances. The Eagles were giving Wisniewski a long look at safety once he returned from a hamstring injury last week.
Andy Dalton: No matter how Dalton practiced on Monday, it was noticeable he didn't get the first reps with the second team offense. Tanner McKee did, and we'll see if that continues as the week goes on. McKee should be the front runner for QB2, but this still appears to be a competition.

title: Eagles Sign Two Players For Preseason Finale, Add Depth at RB and DB
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles did fill their 90-man roster in the wake of the release of J.T. Gray and putting Ja'Quinden Jackson on the waived/injured list. Since the Eagles had two roster spots available, the added more depth at running back and defensive back to get through the preseason finale .
Philadelphia announced the signings of running back Jordan Mims and Jaylen Mahoney on Monday, getting to the max of 91 players (Eagles have an international player exception).
These moves are strictly to get the Eagles through Thursday, as they are thin at running back and defensive back.
Mims has been in the NFL since 2023, when he was an undrafted free agent signing by the Buffalo Bills. He never played for the Bills, but ended up with the New Orleans Saints practice squad.
In two seasons with the Saints, Mims played 13 games. He had 20 carries for 70 yards and 12 catches for 71 yards, all in the 2024 season. He wound up with the Tennessee Titans in 2025, playing one game (nine special teams snaps).
Mims was with the Minnesota Vikings in training camp before being waived earlier this month. He also was with the San Francisco 49ers in minicamp.
The Eagles don't have many available running backs to get them through the preseason finale. Assuming Will Shipley does not play on Friday (as he's essentially a roster lock), teh Eagles would have Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele as their running backs.
Pierce was upgraded to limited Monday as he's battled a hamstring injury the past few weeks. Steele is batting for a spot on the team at fullback. Mims would likely get some touches lat some point in the game if Pierce and Steele both play.
Mahoney is listed as a defensive back, but played one NFL game as a safety for the San Francisco 49ers in 2024. He's never played a defensive snap in the league and was signed as an undrfated free agent by the 49ers before ending up with the New York Jets last December.
He spent this spring in the UFL, playing in six games for the Orlando Storm, recording 26 tackles, one tackle for loss, and two pass breakups. The Eagles were the first team to sign Mahoney since his UFL stint.
Philadelhis is thin in the secondary, yet could use more bodies at safety. With the release of Gray, the Eagles have Andre Sam, Maximus Pulley, and Kapena Gushiken competing for the final safety job. Cole Wisniewski is also in the competition, but missed Monday's practice with a concussion. Unknown if Wisniewski would be ready for Friday at this stage.
Regardless, the Eagles needed another body at safety after the release of Gray. Mahoney could play cornerback based on his position listing, and may see time there with Jakorian Bennett and Ambry Thomas on the mend.
The Eagles have Isaiah Bolden, Shaun Wade, and Gushiken healthy. Mac McWilliams (shoulder) and Ambry Thomas (groin) are also banged up at cornerback, so the Eagles are just trying to get through this game.

title: Eagles' Release of J.T. Gray Likely Clears Up One of Biggest Remaining Position Battles
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles are starting to trim down their roster with days remaining until final cuts.
Two roster moves were made on Monday, one involved the release of J.T. Gray with six days remaining until the initial 53-man roster deadline. Gray was one of the Eagles' signings in March, so there were plans for him to make the roster early in the offseason .
Players on one-year deals aren't guaranteed much, especially when the deal was for $1.3 million with $200,000 guaranteed salary. Gray was always on the roster bubble , regardless of when he signed with the team.
The thought still remained the Eagles signed a special teams standout, a three-time All-Pro in that phase of the game. Gray was given an opportunity to make the team at safety, and beat out Kelee Ringo on special team.
Neither materialized, as Gray fell down the safety depth chart early in camp and Ringo did enough at cornerback to stick around. While Ringo is still a bubble player, it's unlikely he gets cut given the Eagles' depth at cornerback.
This doesn't concern the entire position, just the back end ay cornerback. The Eagles have their starters in Quinyon Mitchell, Cooper DeJean, and Tariq Woolen. Behind them is Jonathan Jones, who has been out with a shoulder injury (and may be out a while longer).
The Eagles will need to find players to fill out the No. 4 and No. 5 cornerback spots if Jones remains out, at least one spot. Ringo is the best of the bunch between himself, Mac McWilliams, and Kapena Gushiken.
Ambry Thomas isn't making this roster and the Eagles placed Tariq Castro-Fields on injured reserve. Shaun Wade has played well this preseason, but he likely isn't making the team. Isaiah Bolden was just signed last week.
Ringo has held his own this preseason and is one of the best gunners in the NFL. There's a spot on this roster for him.
What about the other position battles in the secondary -- and on the remainder of the roster? There are what to watch for over the final week of camp.
The contenders: Tanner McKee, Andy Dalton
The Eagles insist this is still a competition, but McKee should have taken the lead in the battle given how he has performed in the preseason compared to Dalton. While Dalton has been abysmal, the Eagles have a pulse when McKee has been under center.
The contenders: Hollywood Brown, Darius Cooper, Elijah Moore
These three wideouts are battling for two spots, and Brown is close to sealing his spot on the roster. Hard to envision the Eagles moving on from Brown given he's owed $5 million guaranteed.
Cooper has been one of the best wideouts in training camp and does the dirty work as a blocker. He also may have a roster spot in hand. Moore is making it difficult for the Eagles to cut him, so they could keep six.
The contenders: Jake Majors, Micah Morris, John Ojwkwu, Cameron Williams
The Eagles have their first nine offensive linemen settled. The question that remains -- who's the 10th?
Majors has played well at guard, but the Eagles have Drew Kendall and Willie Lampkin as the backup guard and center. Markel Bell and Fred Johnson are the backup tackles, which makes nine.
Morris has been fine this summer, but injures have set the sixth-round pick back. Ojukwu was coming around and can be a hybrid guard/tackle before a pectoral injury set him back. The Eagles like Williams, but it's difficult to have five tackles (and Williams doesn't play guard).
This position is still wide open. The question is whether the Eagles go tackle or guard.
The contenders: Uar Bernard, Joshua Weru
The Eagles are going to reserve one spot on the 53 for the International Pathway Program players. The spot was for Bernard, who they drafted in the seventh round. Could the Eagles actually protect two IPP players on the 53?
Thanks to how Weru has played this preseason, it is a possibility. Hard to justify the Eagles leaving Weru exposed to waivers after how he's performed this preseason, as he'll likely get claimed by another team. The Eagles may have no choice to protect Weru, but does that come at the expense of Bernard?
Are the Eagles really going to protect two IPP players? They may only protect one based on their needs at the bottom of the roster at other positions.
The contenders: Kelee Ringo, Kapena Gushiken, Mac McWilliams
If the Eagles only keep five cornerbacks, Ringo gets the spot (assuming Jonathan Jones is back).
The Eagles could go with six, and Gushiken and McWilliams could make it. McWilliams can play the outside and the slot, and the 2025 fifth-round pick has gotten a long look this summer. Gushiken can play safety and the slot -- while having special teams versatility.
Based on the Jones injury, the Eagles may keep both.
The contenders: Cole Wisniewski, Kapena Gushiken, Maximus Pulley, Andre Sam
This battle is coming down to the final preseason game, and there isn't a favorite. The Eagles like Gushiken because of his position versatility, and he can play cornerback and safety.
Pulley has been impressive this summer as an undrafted free agent and the Eagles have been giving a long look at Wisniewski since he's been back (only to be sidelined again with a concussion). Sam isn't out of the race yet either.
How the preseason finale goes may determine the roster spot.

title: Play and Players of Day on Practice 15 of Eagles Training Camp: DeVonta Smith and Makai Lemon Are Back
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA -- The Eagles' offense felt whole for the first time since early August on Monday with receivers DeVonta Smith and Makai Lemon returning to team drills as full participants after fighting through hamstring issues for most of the month.
During a short 70-minute practice session in shells, Smith and Lemon took the field with the first team in an 11-personnel look with Dontayvion Wicks as the other receiver.
Smith, Philadelphia’s top wideout, had an immediate impact during 7-on-7 drills by hauling in a crossing pattern for about 15 yards. He also had one of the highlights in a team period when snaring a low and outside pass near the right sideline before getting both feet in.
Jalen Hurts tried to get Lemon involved early with a tight-window throw with Cooper DeJean in coverage that went incomplete.
Near the end of practice, Hurts did get Lemon involved on another misdirection off play-action that connected for a minimal gain.
PLAY OF THE DAY: The highlight was a deep shot to Hollywood Brown for about 30 yards. However, the play could have been whistled dead and ruled a Jordan Davis “sack.”
Hurts had another opportunity to hit Brown on a post route with Drew Mukuba in coverage but the ball was overthrown under a heavy rush., which was a problem for the offense throughout the session.
-- The Eagles made some roster moves before practice , waiving/injured running back Ja'Quinden Jackson and releasing special teams ace J.T. Gray. Jackson was involved with the scary injury on the opening kickoff against the Patriots on Saturday might. He will revert to IR when he passes through waivers. To replace Jackson and Gray on the roster the Eagles signed defensive back Jaylen Mahoney (Vanderbilt), and running back Jordan Mims (Fresno State).
-- The injury report grew after Saturday’s preseason game at New England with rookies Markel Bell (thumb/leg), Eli Stowers (hamstring), and Cole Wisniewski (concussion) new to the list. Wisniewski had just returned from a hamstring injury.
Also added after the loss to the Pats were interior offensive lineman Willie Lampkin (stinger), cornerback Mac McWilliams (shoulder), CB Ambry Thomas (groin), and WR Quez Watkins (foot).
Others missing practice were CB Jakorian Bennett (knee), TE Grant Calcaterra (back), and CB Jonathan Jones (shoulder).
WR Danny Gray (groin), OL John Ojukwu (pec), RB Dameon Pierce (hamstring), and DT Byron Young (shoulder) were limited participants.
-- Lemon did confirm after practice his hamstring injury in the spring was the same one he had been dealing with in August.
-- After an impressive performance against the Pats on Saturday night, Tanner McKee began the day as the Eagles’ QB2. Andy Dalton mixed in later, but it was another session in which the Eagles didn’t give many reps to the twos.
Dalton did have consecutive out routes that were impressive during his limited opportunity to both sides of the field, the first to Elijah Moore and the second to Darius Cooper.
-- At WR, the Eagles also mixed in Moore and Cooper with the first team at times That's a smart move because the team has to hedge its bets that Lemon will be ready to handle the workload by Sept. 13.
-- With several new injuries on the OL had to shuffle the second-team unit. From left to right it was: Fred Johnson, Drew Kendall, Zeke Correll, Micah Morris, and Myles Hinton. Correll had at least two poor shotgun snaps.
-- The pass rush was relentless today, particularly from Jalyx Hunt and Moro Ojomo.
-- The Eagles unveiled a look where Dallas Goedert was essentially a fullback blocking for Saquon Barkley. Goedert was also involved as a receiver in an RPO look, which will be infrequent in this offense.

title: Eagles Waive Ja'Quinden Jackson With Injury Settlement, Release Three Time All-Pro On Special Teams
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles are starting to trim their roster heading into the fianl week of training camp.
In a series of roster moves prior to the start of the final week of training camp, the Eagles waived running back Ja'Quinden Jackson with an injury settlement and released safety J.T. Gray.
Jackson suffered a major injury scare on the opening kickoff of the Eagles' preseason game against the Patriots on Saturday night. He left the field in an ambulance and had feeling and movement in all extremities -- per the Eagles. Jackson was taken to the hospital for further evaluation and traveled home with the team.
Since the Eagles waived Jackson with an injury settlement, Jackson will be off the roster and another team will have 24 hours to claim him. If no team claims Jackson, the Eagles will have a short period to reach an injury settlement with him -- usually compensates for the expected amount of weeks he'll miss.
Once the injury settlement is finalized,  Jackson immediately becomes a free agent once he's medically cleared. Jackson can sign with any other NFL team then, but can not re-sign with the Eagles until the injury settlement weeks expire plus an additional three weeks as a "penalty."
Gray signed with the Eagles in March and was a contender to make the roster as a special teams standout . He's a three-time All-Pro on special teams, the most recent coming in 2024 with the Saints. Gray is still regarded as one of the top gunners in the game.
The Eagles gave Gray an opportunity to win a job at safety this summer, but he fell behind on the depth chart and out of the mix in recent weeks. Gray has played 103 games in eight seasons.
So what does the Gray move mean in terms of roster construction? There are some ramifications.
Ringo plays another position than Gray, even though both are defensive backs. How does releasing a safety ensure Ringo is essentially a roster lock?
Both Ringo and Gray are special teams standouts, and it was difficult for the Eagles to keep two of them in the same secondary. Ringo is one of the best gunners in the league, and so is Gray.
The difference? Ringo is a contender in his battle for the final cornerback spot and Gray faded in the battle for the final safety spot.
The injuries at cornerback in recnet weeks for the Eagles helped Ringo state his case for the final cornerback spot. Ringo made a few highlight plays this preseason, getting an opportunity after Jonathan Jones was sidelined with a shoulder injury.
The Eagles need proven depth at cornerback and Ringo knows the system. Also helps he was a standout special teams player.
Gray faded out of the safety picture in recent weeks. Playing late in preseason games was the sign, as Cole Wisniewski, Andre Sam, Maximus Pulley, and Kapena Gushiken were ahead of him in the competition.
For the Eagles, it made sense to release Gray with a week remaining in camp. This gives Gray an opportunity to latch on with another team prior to cutdown day -- or immediately after the roster deadline. Gray doesn't have to go through waivers like the younger players that are cut, so he could latch on with another team sooner rather than later.
The Eagles didn't sign any players for Jackson or Gray yet, which makes sense pending on who they want to see in the preseason finale. Even though the Eagles need bodies to get them through the final preseason game, the roster is still at 89 players.
Philadelphia could always add players for Friday's game, but let's look at who's available at running back and safety this week.
Will Shipley could play in the preseason finale, even if it's just for a few snaps. He did make the 53, so perhaps the Eagles don't want to risk that. Dameon Pierce (hamstring) upgraded to a limited participant Monday, so perhaps he may be ready for Friday. The Eagles may want to give a long look at Carson Steele as he's battling for a roster spot.
There are plenty of candidates that could win the No. 4 safety spot -- and they are highly likely to play Friday. Andre Sam, Maximus Pulley, Cole Wisniewski, and Kapena Gushiken are all are expected to see time in the secondary -- as all four are battling for the final safety spot.
In Gushiken's case, an extra defensive back who can play the slot, safety, and special teams. Perhaps Gushiken was why the Eagles moved on from Gray.
These are the first of many roster moves the Eagles will make over the next week. Let's see if the Eagles add any players for Friday, but they may have enough at running back and safety to get them through the preseason finale.

title: 8 Biggest Winners, 6 Largest Losers From Eagles Preseason: Willie Lampkin Takes Over
full_text:
Two weeks into the Philadelphia Eagles preseason. One week of training camp remains.
Then the Eagles will have the initial 53-man roster set before the preparation of the regular season begins. This is going to be a wild week for the franchise as they look to finalize the 53.
Who were the biggest winners and losers of the preseason so far? We're looking at this strictly form a roster perspective. Who played their way onto the 53 and who are playing their way off?
Willie Lampkin : The uncertainty on the interior of the Eagles offensive line was eased with the development of Lampkin, who shined in the two preseason games. Lampkin has created holes in the run game as a guard, and has gotten the ball off quickly at center. His A-gap blocking shows when rewatching games. Lampkin has earned a roster spot.
Drew Kendall: While Kendall may be undersized as a guard, he moves at the position fluidly. Kendall has seized the No. 3 guard spot. emerging as the top option at left guard and right guard. He's also the backup center to Cam Jurgens as well. Kendall has looked impressive blocking the A-gap and B-gap in both preseason games.
Will Shipley: Benefitting from the Eagles offensive line and injuries to his competition, Shipley took the bull by the horns with the RB3 job. He's ran the ball with authority and has created some big plays after hitting the hole. The RB3 job belongs to Shipley, and he may have an opportunity to help out this offense at some point in a 17-game season.
Ty Robinson: Vic Fangio challenged Robinson and he answered the call, shining with 3.0 sacks in six preseason quarters. The Eagles were hoping Robinson could justify having a roster spot at a loaded position like defensive tackle, and he locked up that opportunity. Perhaps Robinson helps this defense in 2026 if he can get on the field.
Joshua Weru: An afterthought towards making the 53 once training camp started, Weru has played his way into roster consideration. That's a massive win for a player who never put on pads until a month ago. The Eagles seriously have to consider Weru on the 53 instead of exposing him to waivers. Weru may get claimed.
Elijah Moore: Whether Moore makes the 53 or not is up for debate, but he played his way into consideration to make this team. The preseason games haven't shown it, but Moore has outplayed Hollywood Brown in training camp. He outplayed Darius Cooper -- who has been a camp standout -- in recent weeks. The Eagles will find it hard to keep Moore off the roster.
Markel Bell: Bell showcased early in training camp he earned the No. 3 tackle job, but this preseason essentially sealed the deal.The run blocking and play recognization has been noticeable on first and second watch, but also how much Bell has improved as a pass protector. He's the top option should Jordan Mailata or Lane Johnson go down.
Jeremiah Trotter Jr.: He was already on the 53, but Trotter Jr. has been the Eagles best player this preseason. Trotter has been around the football all summer, showing he's a starting linebacker in the league. The Eagles are set at inside linebacker, and Trotter Jr. will earn that opportunity to start in Philadelphia or somewhere else.
Andy Dalton: The Eagles have basically handed Dalton the QB2 job, and he couldn't seize it. Philadelphia can't even justify Dalton having the job based on how he's performed this preseason. Tanner McKee has been better than Dalton, even if that doesn't show up all the time in practice. The Eagles just can't trust Dalton to play a football game against a first-team defense. They should look to move on.
Eli Stowers: While Stowers is making this team, his performance this preseason has reminisced his play in training camp. Stowers is not ready to play in an NFL game, and he may have to based on the state of the tight end position. Stowers may be a healthy scratch come Week 1 and the Eagles may be in the market to improve at TE2 -- unless Stowers drastically improves over the next three weeks.
Rocco Underwood: The Eagles didn't sign a veteran long snapper this offseason to compete with Underwood, allowing him to win the roster spot that's currently his. Underwood has been inconsistent -- and the Eagles don't have to keep him on the initial 53. They can look for one of the available long snappers next week, and then make the call on Underwood, which may be what they do.
Micah Morris: Tough to make a declaration Morris is in jeopardy to make the 53, but this is the result when Willie Lampkin and Jake Majors are ahead on the depth chart. If John Ojekwu gets healthy, he may be ahead of Morris too. Morris hasn't been terrible and injuries held him back -- yet has been outplayed. He still needs more development.
Fred Johnson: Another player who has been okay this summer, but Johnson appears to be ceding the No. 3 tackle job to Markel Bell. Johnson should still have a spot on this roster, since the Eagles need veteran depth at tackle. Have to wonder if Johnson could be a trade candidate.
Andre Sam: Hard to tell who is going to make the final roster spot at safety (should the Eagles keep four), but Sam appeared to blow his opportunity. The Eagles want to give a longer look at Cole Wisniewski and Maximus Pulley, while Kapena Gushiken has come on strong. This is the biggest wild card on the 53, and Sam is still in the race.

title: Eagles 53-Man Roster Projection 4.0: Are Carson Steele, Joshua Weru Locks?
full_text:
A lot can change in a week, especially when it comes to the Philadelphia Eagles and roster construction.
Joint practices and a week of preseason football will accomplish that, as the Eagles had plenty of winners and losers throughout their week in Foxborough. There were players that appeared to seal their roster spot and other bubble players who are set to be cut .
The 53-man roster changes consistently, and the Eagles were a week away from finalizing their initial roster. Heading into the final week of camp, this is my latest projection of the 53 following the second preseason game against the Patriots.
We'll update this every week leading up to cutdown day next Sunday and highlight the changes from the previous edition .
Previous: Jalen Hurts, Andy Dalton, Tanner McKee
Whether performances in the second preseason game will matter will tell where the Eagles stand at QB2. McKee should be the front runner for QB2, as Dalton has been dreadful this preseason.
Dalton has been getting more snaps than McKee in practice, but McKee has significnatly outperformed him in the preseason games. Mckee has been with the third team for the majority of those games, yet that should be in the plus column based on how well he's played.
Payton hasn't done anything to make this roster. He'll stick around, however, as the Eagles will attempt to deal the loser of the QB2 competition. That should be Dalton, who played his way off the 53.
Previous: Saquon Barkley, Tank Bigsby, Will Shipley
Notice how there are four running backs instead of three? Steele did enough in the second preseason game to earn a roster spot at this stage of training camp.
The Eagles are looking for a fullback in Sean Mannion's offense. Steele showed he can be a weapon in the flat and generate yards after the catch. He also runs the ball with authority too and played that fullback role with the Chiefs.
Steele gets the edge over Cameron Latu at this juncture, thanks to several running backs going through injuries that led to more touches.
Previous: DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, Makai Lemon, Hollywood Brown, Darius Cooper
There are the five I'm going with, even though Elijah Moore is making this decision very difficult. Moore had a good week of practice in Foxborough, but a neck injury hurt his chances to outplay Cooper in the second preseason game.
Brown has shown enough to justify sticking around on the 53, as he also had a good week up north. The Eagles have $5 million reasons not to cut Brown, even if Moore has outplayed him this summer.
Cooper isn't a roster lock yet, but he's close. The Eagles need a blocking receiver and Cooper is the best option they have at the moment. There could be a trade in the works too.
Previous: Dallas Goedert, Eli Stowers, Johnny Mundt, Cameron Latu
I'm skeptical having three tight ends right now. Stowers just isn't ready to play in an NFL game and Mundt is more of a blocking tight end than a contributor in the pass game.
The depth at tight end is a concern, and the Eagles aren't keeping four if Latu can't play fullback. No reason for Grant Calcaterra nor E.J. Jenkins to be on this team either. The Eagles may be looking to add depth here too.
Steele gets the fullback spot over Latu for now. The Eagles have three tight ends and four running backs.
Previous: Jordan Mailata, Landon Dickerson, Cam Jurgens, Tyler Steen, Lane Johnson, Fred Johnson, Markel Bell, Drew Kendall, Micah Morris, Willie Lampkin, John Ojukwu
The first nine players listed here are locks to make this roster. The Eagles have an excellent second team offensive line, which displayed their dominance in the first two preseason games. They developed their interior offensive linemen well, as that concern from early in the summer is an afterthought.
Where does the decision get tricky? Finding the 10th offensive lineman.
Majors had a strong preseason showing against the Patriots, taking advantage of John Ojekwu missing the game. Ojekwu was in a prime position for this spot prior a pectoral injury suffered last week, allowing majors to get more work with the second team.
Micah Morris was a sixth-round pick, but he's been stuck on the third team. Cameron Williams is a tackle the Eagles like, but he hasn't done enough to make the roster. The Eagles could make things interesting by trading Fred Johnson, yet having a veteran at tackle behind the starters is paramount.
The 10th offensive lineman will be the battle to watch this week. Perhaps the Eagles go 11 offensive lineman too, but that seems like a lot for a roster that has some holes to fill.
Previous: Jonathan Greenard, Jalyx Hunt, Nolan Smith, Arnold Ebiketie, A.J. Epenesa
Two factors are in play here. Will the Eagles place Greenard on PUP and create a roster spot for Weru or will Greenard be healthy enough not to miss the first four weeks of the season and the Eagles still protect Weru.
What happens with Greenard impacts Weru, as defensive coordinator Vic Fangio admitted he's concerned Greenard won't be ready by Week 1 with his pectoral injury.
Will the Eagles actually expose Weru to waivers after the preseason he's had? Weru is also getting better by the day and looks like he can help the team this year -- crazy to think a month ago.
I don't think Howie Roseman is going to allow that to happen. Weru makes this team for that reason.
Previous: Jalen Carter, Jordan Davis, Moro Ojomo, Ty Robinson, Byron Young, Uar Bernard
Bernard has been on every single one of my roster projections. This was the first time I didn't have him as a stone cold lock.
Would the Eagles really go expose Bernard to waivers? Thanks to the emerge of Weru, it sure could trend that way. The Eagles can take the risk Bernard won't get claimed has he still has a lot of development before he can contribute to any team. I'll keep him on for now by putting on my general manager cap (you'll see by scrolling down).
Having Bernard on the 53-man roster would be a huge investment for any team this year.
Robinson is off the roster bubble by the way. He made the 53 and should not have to play in the preseason finale this week.
Previous: Zach Baun, Jihaad Campbell, Jeremiah Trotter Jr. Smael Mondon, Chance Campbell
Vic Fangio believes this is the deepest position on the Eagles, as position which Philadelphia has three starters. Smael Mondon is pretty good too and Fangio likes Campbell, so these are the five.
Deontae Lawson has had a good summer, and he's been productive in the preseason games. He should have a spot on the practice squad.
Brandon George has made a lot of plays on special teams despite only being here a week. Perhaps he can play his way onto the practice squad.
Previous: Quinton Mitchell, Cooper DeJean, Tariq Woolen, Kelee Ringo, Jonathan Jones
The Eagles are thin at cornerback thanks to injuries, leaving the door open for Mac McWilliams to compete for a roster spot. These are the five the Eagles go with, but who knows when Jones will be back.
Jones has 20 days to be ready for Week 1, and he's essentially a lock for the 53 as the top backup on the outside and in the slot behind the starters. Ringo is an excellent special teams player and has done enough at cornerback to stick around.
Wouldn't be surprising if the Eagles looked to upgrade the depth at cornerback, pending on how significant the Jones injury is.
Previous: Andrew Mukuba, Marcus Epps, Michael Carter II, Andre Sam
Assuming the Eagles go with four safeties, the final roster spot for safety is what to watch for in practice this week. The Eagles want to give Wisniewski a shot now that he's healthy, and appear to letting the seventh-round pick play as much as he can.
This is why I have Wisniewski over Sam and Maximus Pulley. A good week for Wisniewski could seal the final safety spot, especially if Wisniewski can play special teams. That's his ticket towards the 53.
A big preseason finale for Pulley could chance the Eagles mid. Pulley has had a good summer and should be on the practice squad.

title: 10 Eagles Players On The Bubble Who Could Be Cut Following Latest Preseason Game
full_text:
The second game of the preseason is a bit of a tell all .
Reading between the lines and the snap counts, it's easy to figure out who's playing the game early and who's playing late. The ones playing late in the game are a long shot to make the roster -- especially in a week where joint practices take center stage.
Player performance also plays a role in this too. Do preseason performances have that much value in today's NFL? There are ways to play your way out of a job in the preseason.
These players on the roster bubble are in danger of not making the 53 next week.
Who knows what the Eagles are going to do with Dalton at this point. Is Dalton the QB2 or is he going to be off the roster?
Dalton shouldn't be the QB2, even if the Eagles are giving the signs that they may be the case. McKee outplayed him in the preseason game on Saturday, and Dalton hasn't done anything to seize the job from McKee.
There's a better chance Dalton gets traded than making the roster at this stage. He's definitely on the roster bubble.
Moore didn't play Saturday and didn't practice on Thursday (neck), but he's played his way onto the roster bubble with a strong few weeks. Getting reps with the first team in the joint practice this week helped, even though Moore is battling Hollywood Brown for a roster spot.
The Eagles need to find wide receiver depth , so Moore may not make the 53 through no fault of his own. Howie Roseman may be busy this week, which could come at the expense of Moore.
All Moore has to do is continue to stack up good practices.
The performance of Carson Steele on Saturday may force the Eagles to keep four running backs . So how does that come at the expense of Latu?
Sean Mannion may incorporate the use of a fullback in certain packages, and Latu was the front runner for that role until Steele's performance on Saturday night. Steele has experience as a blocking back with the Chiefs, and can adjust to the fullback role.
Based on how Steele caught passes in the flat, not a great sign for Latu to make this team.
Notice how Morris was on the third team at guard and didn't enter the game until late in the second quarter? That's the first sign Drew Kendall, Willie Lampkin, and Jake Majors are ahead of Morris on the depth chart.
The rookie sixth-round pick may not make the 53. If Morris does, that's the 10th spot on the offensive line.
Williams played 38 snaps on Saturday, but didn't enter the game until Fred Johnson and Markel Bell departed. The Eagles like Williams -- a sixth-round pick from last year -- but he's also battling John Ojekwu for a roster spot. Ojekwu can also play inside at guard as well.
With little position versatility, Willams would have to dominate the last preseason game. It may be too late.
Ojekwu gained some momentum prior to the joint practices by moving inside to guard -- and playing well there. A pectoral injury has sidlined Ojekwu. enough where he didn't practic ethe past few days and sat out the preseason game.
Pending on how serious the injury is, that affects Ojekwu's roster chances. He had a strong chance to make the 53 prior to this injury. Let's see how long he's out for.
Bernard appeared to have a spot on the 53 thanks to his developent as a player on the International Pathway Program. The Eagles couldn't afford to risk a player like Bernard to waivers.
Bernard may not be the IPP player that the Eagles need to protect. That may be Joshua Weru, who's had a strong preseason and is making the decision to cut him hard for the Eagles. Doesn't hurt the Eagles could use more depth at pass rusher with Jonathan Greenard on PUP.
Weru looks like he can help an NFL team this season. Bernard isn't close to where Weru is in development. There's the answer.
Hall has performed well his preseason, even having an early pressure to force an incomplete pass by Tommy DeVito on third down to get the Patriots off the field on the first series.
The issue? Ty Robinson has locked up his roster spot. There just isn't room for Hall to make the 53 at a position as loaded as defensive tackle. Hall deserves to be on an NFL roster, but his chances of making the Eagles are slim.
McWilliams is battling for one of the open cornerback spots, as the position has opened up with the Jonathan Jones injury (shoulder). Who knows how long Jones will be out, but if he still has to miss a few more weeks -- McWilliams has a shot.
While McWilliams started the game and made a few plays, he left with an apparent injury. Pending on the severity of the injury, that affects his roster chances.
Sam was the leader in the clubhouse for the No. 4 safety spot (should the Eagles keep four), but Cole Wisniewski and Maximus Pulley are coming on strong in the final week.
Wisniewski playing only the second quarter should give a sign where Sam stands towards making the team. He also made a nice special teams play that will help his roster chances.
The final safety spot (again if Eagles keep four) is up for grabs. Wisniewski seems to have the lead over Sam and Pulley.

title: Six Eagles Who Solidified Their Spot on the 53-Man Roster in Preseason vs. Patriots
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles have to send in their initial 53-man roster in a week from Sunday.
Jobs still are on the line, yet there are some roster spots that were solidified on Saturday night in the second preseason game. This is why the Week 2 of the preseason was massive for the second team players, as it was an opportunity for them to showcase why they deserved to be on the roster.
Who basically locked up their roster spots? These players are expected to be on the 53-man roster when the Eagles announce it next week.
Shipley was essentially a roster lock heading into this game, but he slammed the door on any possibility he doesn't make it. He hit the hole hard and with authority in the second preseason game, taking advantage of the massive holes created by his offensive line.
Shipley had 51 yards in the first quarter and a touchdown run in the second. He looked poised when carrying the football and has more confidence reading the hole than at this time last year.
Bottom line -- Shipley is a roster lock. He'll be the RB3, even though the opportunities are scarce with Saquon Barkley and Tank Bigsby ahead of him.
McKee should have the QB2 job after the atrocious performance from Andy Dalton on Saturday night. He was the better quarterback and clearly had more command of the offense than Dalton -- and was playing with third team most of the game.
McKee went 16-of-22 for 173 yards and two touchdowns (125.8 rating) in the game, and went 5-of-6 for 64 yards on third down with a touchdown (150.7 rating). This was the most poised McKee has looked all summer, as he backed up his claim to be the QB2.
Theer shouldn't be a QB2 battle this week. McKee earned the job.
Watching Lampkin block opponents Saturday night and continuing to wear out defensive tackles, how do the Eagles leave him off the roster? The Eagles started Lampkin at center in game two of the preseason and he was able to get off the snap quick and create massive holes in the A-gap.
This cames a week after Lampkin excelled at guard in the preseaosn opener, showcasing he can play both spots in an NFL game. The Eagles interior of the offensive line isn't a concern anymore,a nd Lampkin is a huge part of that.
He should be on this team next week.
Robinson has "come alive" over the past few weeks after being on "life support," per Vic Fangio. He didn't need much convincing on Saturday with a dominant first half -- totaling four pressures, two sacks, and three quarterback hits.
The Eagles were waiting for Robinson to break out after a poor rookie campaign, and he's done taht with three sacks in six quarters of preseason action. Robinson should take a seat for game No. 3, as he's on the roster.
Vic Fangio has said inside linebacker is the deepest position on the Eagles, and looking at his top three linebackers he can back up that claim.
The fourth linebacker is pretty good too. Mondon had a good pressure on a blitz on Tommy Devito early in the first quarter, a play DeVito got away from him (Mondon just didn't finish the play) and ran for the first down. This was still an impressive read to the quarterback by Mondon, one that will play on NFL Sundays.
Mondon was essentially a lock to make teh team because of his play on special teams, but he solidified his spot on Saturday.
I still think Weru making this team is an overreaction , but how can the Eagles just let this player go through the waiver wire? Some team in the NFL is going to claim Weru based on watching the film from Saturday night.
The move Weru made to get past Dametrious Crownover took notice across the league, and teams are hoping Roseman leaves Weru available to claim. Roseman is too smart of a general manager to leave that up to chance, knowing teams are thinking about getting their hands on someone who can help the Eagles this year.
Putting on my GM cap here, Weru makes this team for that reason.

title: Why Lack Of Size On Perimeter Could Hurt Eagles Run Game In The Long Run
full_text:
The Eagles waived king-sized wide receiver Johnny Wilson with an injury designation Friday, a move that is both pragmatic and perhaps quietly disruptive.
There is no use pining over what the 6-foot-6, 228-pound former sixth-round pick could have done as a blocker in Sean Mannion's wide-zone philosophy because Wilson is dealing with a lingering knee issue that had limited him in recent practices.
If the Florida State product clears waivers, he will revert to injured reserve. Either way, the Eagles have lost their biggest skill-position body just as Mannion is installing a rushing scheme that places heavy demands on receivers and tight ends as blockers.
Wilson’s path to this point began last summer. Late in training camp last August, when he was on track for a 53-man roster spot, he suffered significant knee and ankle injuries on a run play during practice that required season-ending surgery.
He returned this offseason determined to earn a roster spot and showed flashes of the physical presence the coaching staff had valued since drafting him in 2024, before the problematic knee issues resurfaced.
As a rookie, Wilson played 16 games with four starts, catching five passes for 38 yards and a touchdown while earning quiet respect for his willingness to do the dirty work on the perimeter for a Super Bowl-winning team.
That combination of length and blocking ability made him a natural fit, if healthy, for what Mannion and his chief lieutenants in the run game—run-game coordinator Ryan Mahaffey and offensive line coach Chris Kuper—are building.
The shift is toward a wider, more horizontal zone-run attack. Outside zone, when done properly, often features condensed formations, cutback lanes, and stretch principles that require eligible receivers and tight ends to reach, climb, and sustain blocks with the same urgency as the offensive line. There are no spectators in this philosophy.
Wilson’s frame and physicality was uniquely suited to walling off edge defenders and creating the soft corners Saquon Barkley could thrive with.
Without Wilson, the Eagles’ wide-receiver room suddenly looks undersized, with quickness and route-running as its primary strengths.
DeVonta Smith remains a polished centerpiece and a good blocker for his size, but there are limitations at 170 pounds. The top supplemental players are Dontayvion Wicks (6-foot-1, 206 pounds), the biggest of the remaining wideouts, and rookie first-round pick Makai Lemon, who has dealt with a hamstring issue for much of August.
Enjoy our content? Make Eagles On SI a Preferred Source to see more stories from us on Google: https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=si.com
Of the others making a run at a roster spot—Hollywood Brown, Darius Cooper, Elijah Moore, and Britain Covey—none reach 6 feet, and only Cooper has a frame that hints at competent blocking ability.
Mannion has praised the group’s complementary skill sets and flexibility. Yet the potential for pure size and the ability to physically impose on the perimeter is now absent.
That will likely shift more of the burden to the tight ends, particularly Dallas Goedert and Johnny Mundt.
In the end, Wilson is simply not healthy enough to play, so it is not as if general manager Howie Roseman made a poor decision. Still, the move underscores a broader truth about scheme transitions: personnel and philosophy have to align.
The Eagles spent years building a physical, vertical identity under previous coordinators. Moving toward wide zone asks for different traits—angle awareness, sustained leverage and, ideally, some length on the outside. Losing the one receiver who most clearly possessed the last two qualities leaves a gap that might force the Eagles to look outside the organization to fill.

title: Steelers 53-Man Roster Projection: QB Roller Coaster Continues
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers have one final preseason game separating them from a major roster deadline.
The Steelers, and the rest of the NFL, have roughly one week left to decide who will be on their initial 53-man roster to begin the 2026 regular season. The team must split their group of 91 players basically in half, providing head coach Mike McCarthy and his staff with quite the task before the regular season begins.
After their battle with the New York Jets however, the roster is rounding into form. There are a few key questions to answer, but with one preseason game left, this is what the 53-man roster in Pittsburgh will look like to begin the regular season.
After he performed like any young quarterback would in a challenging preseason situation, Will Howard finds himself without a spot on the 53-man roster. If McCarthy hadn't seen all he needed to see from the veterans, this might be a different story, but unfortunately that's not the case for Howard.
A small but powerful room of running backs enter the season in Pittsburgh. Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle will be the top tandem, with Homer spelling that duo and providing special teams contributions.
Versatile, strong, and willing to do whatever on the field, Riley Nowakowski has more than earned a spot on this roster. He brings a thunderous blocking skill to the run game and will also be a key special teams player.
Everyone on this list is a lock besides rookie Kaden Wetjen . After he's been the subject of criticism from the head coach and he coughed up a silly fumble on a punt return, maybe he lost his spot. Or maybe, McCarthy and company are pushing the youngster because they see a ton of upside in him.
The other X-factor in all of this is Roman Wilson. He's been an improved version of himself in training camp, but is that going to carry over into the regular season?
Another small position group with big expectations on offense. Pat Freiermuth is hoping a new offensive approach benefits him, while Darnell Washington tries to improve upon a breakout 2025 campaign. Adding to the mix is veteran Robert Tonyan, who once caught 11 touchdowns from Rodgers as a member of the Green Bay Packers.
Offensive line is a huge area of concern all of a sudden, but the group of nine linemen they should enter the season with is obvious. Unless injuries change things, this group is who Mike McCarthy will have to trust to keep Rodgers upright.
The strongest position on the team is undoubtedly along the defensive line. The question is will they keep six or more for their front line? Rookie Gabe Rubio has impressed enough to earn a situational role as a run-stopper. Veteran Dean Lowry has also been excellent this preseason, and he might have earned his way onto the roster too.
All the money in the world is tied up in the outside linebacker position, and the hope is that it is the bedrock of a resurgent defense. Nick Herbig is the wild card, as he is in line for a huge increase in snaps taken. But Alex Highsmith looks in peak form, and T.J. Watt is on a revenge tour. Things will get interesting.
E-Rob is a last-minute addition, rounding out a four-man group. He might even end the season as the guy wearing the green dot and being first on the depth chart. He should also take the pressure off of both Patrick Queen and Payton Wilson, as they try to bounce back from tough 2025 seasons.
Jalen Ramsey’s activation off the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) List is a huge boost as they wrap up the preseason, giving this team yet another experienced and productive defensive back. Recent third-round pick Daylen Everette is the lone rookie in this group, and he's going to be an impact player from the jump.
One question is when does Joey Porter Jr. return and how much richer is he when he does?
After an impressive preseason, seventh-round pick Robert Spears-Jennings earns a spot as the team’s 10th defensive back.
Nothing to even debate or think about when it comes to the special teams. This is the trio that will anchor this unit.

title: Former Steelers WR Announces Retirement, Shares Appreciation in Video
full_text:
A former Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver has officially called it a career ahead of the 2026 NFL season.
On Instagram, Allen Robinson II announced that he is retiring after an 11-year stint in the league spent between the Jacksonville Jaguars (2014 - 2017), Chicago Bears (2018 - 2021), Los Angeles Rams (2022), Steelers (2023) and Detroit Lions (2024).
"As I reflect on another year of life, I find myself especially grateful; not just for where I am, but for the journey that brought me here," Robinson wrote . "This birthday feels a little different. It marks not only another year, but the beginning of a new chapter.
"To every love story, there comes a final chapter. Football gave me more than I ever could’ve imagined. It challenged me, shaped me, humbled me, and rewarded me in ways I’ll carry for the rest of my life."
Former Pro Bowl WR Allen Robinson is officially retiring from the NFL after 11 seasons, as he announced on IG. Robinson finishes his outstanding career with 565 catches, 7,058 yards, and 43 TDs. (🎥 @AllenRobinson ) pic.twitter.com/zbDfUHyicn
Robinson had plenty of positive things to say about his lone year with the Steelers , shouting out Mike Tomlin in particular.
"Shoutout to Coach Tomlin and the Pittsburgh Steelers. I had one of the strongest connections coach-wise with Coach Tomlin. When he coached, the things that he said day in and day out was an experience like no other, to the point where I called my agent and I told him that I didn't know that I could play for any other coach other than Coach Tomlin," Robinson said.
He also went on to show some love to some of his fellow receivers in Pittsburgh in George Pickens, Diontae Johnson and Calvin Austin III.
"I feel like I enjoyed playing the game again," Robinson said. "Playing with George Pickens, playing with Diontae Johnson, playing with Calvin Austin, those guys kept me young."
Entering the second year of a three-year, $46.5 million deal with the Rams, Robinson was traded to the Steelers in March 2023 as the two teams exchanged seventh-round picks in the 2023 NFL Draft.
Robinson II was coming off a season-ending foot injury in Los Angeles, though he played in all 17 games that year for Pittsburgh and finished with 280 yards on 34 catches.
In the Steelers' Wild Card round loss to the Buffalo Bills, he logged two receptions for 12 yards.
The organization later cut Robinson II in March 2024. He proceeded to sign with the New York Giants, who released him that August.
He then signed with the Lions and played in 12 contests for them, posting 30 yards in what would end up being his final season.

title: Three Steelers Whose Roster Odds Improved After Jets Game
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers' latest preseason game was rather ugly, but a few players saw their positioning when it comes to making the initial 53-man roster strengthen.
With final roster cuts under a week away, the Steelers are going to have a handful of meticulous decisions on their hands over the coming days.
When it comes to these three veterans, however, there's little doubt that they belong and should be kept around heading into the regular season.
Ironically enough, one of the biggest winners from Pittsburgh's victory over the Jets didn't even play in the contest.
Rudolph, who started against the Green Bay Packers in the preseason opener and completed 10 of his 11 passing attempts for 93 yards, was sidelined vs. New York after head coach Mike McCarthy stated that he, "saw what he needed to," from him.
For a good chunk of the offseason, Rudolph was viewed as expendable and likely to find himself as the odd man out in Pittsburgh's quarterback room.
Once training camp began, however, it became increasingly apparent that Rudolph was the favorite to win the backup job over Will Howard while Drew Allar would slot in at the bottom of the depth chart with his roster spot guaranteed as a third-round rookie.
Because Howard showed some flashes against the Packers by going 7-of-9 for 86 yards, however, there was some quiet speculation that Rudolph's name could start popping up in trade conversations ahead of the regular season.
Howard essentially wrecked his chances of usurping Rudolph and taking the No. 2 role with a two-interception showing against the Jets, though, further cementing the latter's status as the second-in-command to Aaron Rodgers and keeping him off the trade block.
The math at the safety position may become a little tougher now that Jalen Ramsey is off the PUP list , though Jenkins has to feel rather secure about where he stands ahead of final roster cuts.
It didn't always feel like a guarantee that Pittsburgh would hold onto four safeties if Ramsey were healthy, and Robert Spears-Jennings' involvement on the first-team defense in training camp coupled with his solid preseason debut against the Packers put Jenkins on thin ice when it came to cracking the 53-man roster.
Jenkins knew what was on the line vs. New York, however, as he flew around the field and made a couple of plays as a blitzer, including forcing Cade Klubnik into an intentional grounding penalty.
The 32-year-old's physicality flew off the screen in the run game as well, and overall Jenkins looked like a man on a mission.
It's not necessarily a 100 percent lock that the Steelers will keep four safeties on their initial 53-man roster, but that feels like the way things are headed with the way Jenkins performed against the Jets.
Tonyan continues to fill the role of a quarterback's best friend, and it has led to him being all but assured a 53-man roster spot at this point.
The 32-year-old signed with Pittsburgh in June largely as a byproduct of his preexisting relationship with Aaron Rodgers from their five years playing together as members of the Green Bay Packers from 2018 to 2022, a span during which Tonyan logged 1,437 yards and 17 touchdowns on 137 catches.
He posted just one receiving yard between the 2024 and 2025 campaigns while filling more of a special teams role. If training camp and the preseason are any indication, however, Tonyan might be in line for a bit of an offensive resurgence this year.
After finishing with 61 yards on four receptions vs. the Packers, Tonyan caught both of his targets against the Jets for 17 yards, one of which went for 12 yards on a crossing route with a defender right on him.
Tonyan is the clear No. 3 tight end, and he should have some real opportunities to make an impact once the regular season arrives.

title: Steelers OT Competition Wide Open After Max Iheanachor News
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers got some much-needed positive news when it comes to the health of their first-round pick Max Iheanachor .
Ahead of practice on August 24, head coach Mike McCarthy told reporters that Iheanachor (upper-body) is set to practice for the first time since August 6 and may play in the Steelers ' preseason finale against the Buffalo Bills on August 27, though his snap count will largely be dependent on how he looks over the next few days at UPMC Rooney Sports Complex.
"I really wanna see him go today," McCarthy said about Iheanachor. "I know he's anxious to go. I'll be watching him a lot through the individuals. We've got two padded practices, so it'll be a really good indication of how much he'll be able to play Thursday. We'll see how it goes."
Dylan Cook was pencilled in as the starter at right tackle for a vast majority of the offseason after an impressive five-game sample size to close out the 2025 campaign over at left tackle following Broderick Jones' season-ending neck injury.
Before Iheanachor went down with his injury, however, he appeared to be making up some serious ground on Cook in Latrobe, especially when the pads came on and he was tasked with stopping the likes of T.J. Watt, Nick Herbig and Jack Sawyer.
Iheanachor's injury initially seemed to dash any hopes of winning the starting right tackle job , but Cook has been mediocre at best across the first two games of the preseason.
Jones' struggles are incredibly evident too, as he's given up three sacks and four pressures over 66 pass blocking reps between left and right tackle (per Pro Football Focus ).
With neither Cook or Jones looking like a true solution, the door may still be open for Iheanachor to make headway in the race and prove why he should be handed the reins at right tackle with a strong outing against the Bills.
Iheanachor has all the traits to eventually become a stalwart and high-level player at right tackle. His good start to training camp was an important step, as his standout athleticism and raw strength immediately stood out.
Not being able to play in Pittsburgh's first two preseason games undeniably put him behind the eight-ball, however, especially when the team's initial plans likely didn't involve starting the Arizona State product right off the jump considering how much growth was needed from a technical standpoint when he entered the league.
Some of those concerns were answered at Saint Vincent College, but playing in a game setting is a big test for Iheanachor and will be telling when it comes to his prospects of making an impact early in his rookie year.
Should he see the field a decent amount against Buffalo and excel, that could open up the possibility of some real conversations taking place amongst the Steelers' brass when it comes to deciding who to roll with at right tackle in Week 1.
In all likelihood, Pittsburgh will look to build Iheanachor back up and initially give the starting job to Cook before potentially revisiting that decision later in the season.
With how uninspiring Cook and even Jones have been at right tackle this summer, though, Iheanachor making a late surge for that role can't be ruled out.

title: Steelers' Mike McCarthy Pushes Back at QB Rumor
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — With one final preseason game left, the Pittsburgh Steelers still do not have clarity at the quarterback position. Yes, the starting job was secured the moment Aaron Rodgers signed his contract to return to the franchise.
Behind Rodgers, however, things remain up in the air for the Steelers. Mason Rudolph is presumably on the roster after head coach Mike McCarthy opted not to play him or Rodgers in the second preseason game. It left a huge opportunity for second-year player Will Howard, who put together an unimpressive first start in the NFL.
But a recent report from veteran insider Gerry Dulac claimed that McCarthy had already decided to keep all four quarterbacks on the team’s initial 53-man roster. The head coach pushed back on that assumption, however, making it clear that nothing has been officially decided yet.
“Yeah, I haven’t been part of any conversations where the 53 has been selected already,” he clarified for reporters. “Anything, Any position, any realm, we definitely have ideas. But I think it’s evident we’re trying to play the players in as many combinations.”
The thought of keeping four talented quarterbacks is certainly an enticing one for the Steelers, but the reality is it makes very little sense to do so.
Firstly, four quarterbacks is a roster construction nightmare when it comes to versatility and efficiency, two things the coaching staff has stressed all offseason. How do you justify keeping four on the roster, rendering two inactive on a weekly basis? If all things go well, the Steelers will only have one QB on the field for all 17 games in the 2026 season, so what good is having four in that scenario? Even in case of injuries, you don’t need three backups to fill the void. That’s at least one spot that could be used for another, more useful and productive player.
Secondly, the four quarterbacks available are not players that they cannot afford to part with. Rudolph is a dime-a-dozen backup quarterback in the NFL. He’s talented and provides value, but he’s not indispensable. Howard showed that he’s still a long-term project, and it doesn’t guarantee he will be anything further than a Rudolph-level backup in the NFL.
Meanwhile, the Steelers already have their long-term project. Drew Allar has shown flashes in his limited preseason reps, and it’s clear that McCarthy views him favorably.
Furthermore, it’s clear that Allar is progressing under the new head coach. His footwork has looked drastically improved, and that is an encouraging development for the former third-round pick.
That leaves very little space for a fourth quarterback, and that unfortunately leaves Howard as the odd-man out. At the least, nothing has been determined, according to McCarthy.

title: Steelers Sign Navy FB, Texas CB
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers made a series of roster moves before they take on the Buffalo Bills later this week for their preseason finale at Highmark Stadium.
In addition to activating cornerback Jalen Ramsey from the PUP list , the Steelers announced that they signed cornerback Jaylon Guilbeau and running back Alex Tecza. They had an additional open roster spot after releasing kicker Laith Marjan on August 23.
Furthermore, Pittsburgh also cut defensive back Israel Mukuamu. He signed with the team on August 5 and appeared in their preseason opener against the Green Bay Packers, a game in which the former sixth-round pick posted a sack.
Ramsey's return is huge news for the Steelers, as he's set to serve as their primary slot corner while also likely seeing time at safety in new defensive coordinator Patrick Graham's system.
Mukuamu had spent the first four years of his NFL career playing under Mike McCarthy with the Dallas Cowboys from 2021 to 2024 before joining the Carolina Panthers for the 2025 campaign.
He reunited with McCarthy in Pittsburgh a few weeks ago, though he suffered an apparent injury during one of the team's final practices at Saint Vincent College in Latrobe on August 15 and hadn't participated since.
Guilbeau has stepped in and taken Mukuamu's spot on the roster for the time being after being one of three cornerbacks to try out for the Steelers on August 23 alongside Dee Williams and Eli Ricks.
In 43 games at Texas from 2022 to 2025, Guilbeau logged 125 total tackles and an interception. He signed with the Panthers as an undrafted free agent in May before being let go on July 22.
Tecza was teammates with fellow Steelers rookie Eli Heidenreich both in high school at Mt. Lebanon and in college at Navy.
The pair also participated in Pittsburgh's rookie minicamp together back in May, though Tecza was there on a tryout basis.
While Tecza didn't sign with the Steelers immediately following rookie minicamp, he's now back with Heidenreich and his hometown team ahead of their upcoming bout with the Bills to close out the preseason.
Over 38 contests for Navy, Tecza recorded 2,236 and 23 touchdowns on 409 rushing attempts to go with 451 yards and three touchdowns on 41 receptions.

title: Steelers Activate Star CB From PUP List
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are getting a huge boost as they prepare for their final preseason game. The Steelers will take on the Buffalo Bills to close out their preseason schedule, but the defense can already look forward to the regular season.
The Steelers will get one of their star defenders back soon. Head coach Mike McCarthy addressed the media ahead of a recent practice, and shared the update that Jalen Ramsey is being activated off of the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) List. Ramsey previously suffered a knee injury earlier in the offseason, and missed the entirety of training camp and the preseason up until this point.
With Ramsey coming off of the PUP List, that also means that the veteran defensive back will return to practice. The timing of his return is perfect as well, as McCarthy clarified that there will be multiple. padded practices ahead of their contest against the Bills. His exact timeline to return to game action is not yet known, and it's unlikely that he suits up for the final preseason game. Regardless, this is a huge step for Ramsey and the Steelers.
Ramsey's return is the boost the defense needed to finish their preseason. Without him, the team had been utilizing Brandin Echols as the primary slot corner, but an injury  giving second-year undrafted free agent Doneiko Slaughter significant snaps with the first-team. The experience was huge for Slaughter, but there's no denying how much more impactful Ramsey is in the slot and the open field.
Ramsey also provides a significant level of leadership, both on the field and in the locker room. He's a Super Bowl winner and multiple-time All-Pro cornerback. His experience and wisdom is paramount for a Steelers defense desperate to reach the next level.
While the Pro Bowl is no longer the undisputed indicator of success it once was, people are quick to dismiss that Jalen Ramsey once again made the all-star fesitivities in his first campaign with the Steelers. He managed to perform well despite a flawed defensive structure, a coaching staff on the way out and switching positions midway through the year.
This season, defensive coordinator Patrick Graham is the man with a plan. He's detailed, structured, meticulous and determined. Using Ramsey primarily as a nickel corner should get the most out of the veteran and capitalize on the skills he is still elite at.
For the Steelers, that hopefully helps them reach the top-15 or higher in both passing and team defense this season.

title: Steelers Going to Surprise Us With QB Decision
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers didn't have the quarterback showing they had hoped for against the New York Jets. In fact, it was so bad that many admitted it may be time to trim the fat of the room and head into the season with just three options.
That group of "many" doesn't include the Steelers.
Even after Will Howard threw two interceptions against the Jets, the Steelers feel pretty content with keeping all four QBs this season. According to Pittsburgh Post-Gazette's Gerry Dulac , head coach Mike McCarthy has already decided that he's keeping all four quarterbacks this season , and that Howard's play didn't change anything.
That has remained the belief over the last week or so. At some point, something about keeping all four passers became realistic and felt like McCarthy's plan from the start.
Not anymore. Howard's poor play against the Jets should remove him from most teams' list of candidates they'd add during the waiver claim window. After that, adding him back to the practice squad should be easy, and it'd be even more surprising than keeping four QBs if he chose to sign elsewhere instead of Pittsburgh.
The Steelers don't need a 53rd roster spot to win a Super Bowl. Their last linebacker or final offensive line position isn't going to be the deciding factor between being a contender or not. But it does help to have more even depth on the roster than making two quarterbacks inactive on game day.
The Steelers should instead be comfortable putting Howard on the practice squad and going from there. Maybe in a year, Howard improves enough to challenge for a starting job. Maybe he doesn't.
In the meantime, Pittsburgh should have faith in Drew Allar, who's shown flashes during his two preseason games and has developed a lot since he showed up for rookie minicamp in the spring.
Things really are different in Pittsburgh this season. In years past, Mike Tomlin would never think of keeping four quarterbacks on the roster, no matter how good or bad some of them looked. It just wasn't a thing that made sense.
Well, McCarthy is an offensive coach and a quarterback developer. He wants options. And it seems like he has two that he likes and wants to continue working with.
Three games aren't going to be enough, so he's ready to keep four around throughout the season and figure out how that changes his team.

title: Steelers, Joey Porter Jr. Need to Stop Fighting a Deal
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers have one contract to sign before the start of the regular season. Right now, it doesn't feel like that's going to happen, but it should. And it shouldn't take much battling with numbers to figure it out.
The Steelers have yet to sign Joey Porter Jr., and according to reports , it's not going to happen this offseason.
That makes little sense. Unless Porter Jr. is looking to become the highest-paid cornerback in the NFL, the Steelers should have little problem signing him to a massive deal. One that makes him feel like a top-5 cornerback in terms of value, and one where Pittsburgh takes a chance on a player they've been hoping will work out.
It's been a long time since the Steelers have developed a cornerback on their own. Really, the last #24, Ike Taylor, is the best example of a cornerback Pittsburgh developed into a star.
Porter has been a long time in the making, and now that the Steelers have done it, there's no sense it ruining it.
The Steelers want Porter around long-term. They have little intention of letting him go; they aren't going to trade him , and when this is all said and done, it feels like a contract is going to be signed at some point over the next two years unless he completely falls off.
Pittsburgh should very easily hand Porter top-5 money in terms of average salary per year, and then give him top-3 to top-5 guaranteed money. He's worth it, and you're not overpaying for a player who will likely become a top-5 player at the position this season anyway.
On Porter's side of things, he should want to be signed this offseason and not next. The franchise tag for the position won't exceed what he'd likely sign for, and at 26 years old, he'd be risking that his first big NFL contract would come at 28.
That's not going to get you two long-term deals. So, he should want to sign now, make his money for the next three seasons and then hope to sign again at 29 years old.
If he believes he'll make up for lost time by waiting, then fine, but it's a risk he'd be taking. One that doesn't make much sense, but also one that the Steelers should minimize by signing him now.
It makes too much sense for both sides to get this over with before Week 1.

title: Joey Porter Jr. Shares Cryptic Post in Midst of Steelers Negotiations
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- Joey Porter Jr. may be hinting at something, or could just be reminding everyone how good he is. Either way, there appears to be an intentional message being sent from the Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback.
Porter Jr. shared a video on his I nstagram story of him being introduced at Acrisure Stadium before a Steelers game with the hourglass emoji. He also allowed two other comments to be shared: one with the eyeballs emoji and the other that reads "BEST IN THE [expletive] LEAGUE."
Joey Porter Jr.’s Instagram story pic.twitter.com/JrwaUZN7NL
In recent days, Chris Halicke of DK Pittsburgh Sports reported that the Steelers and Porter Jr. were not close to a new deal and were not expected to sign one before Week 1 of the regular season. Jordan Schultz reported that because no deal has been done, other NFL teams are curious about a potential trade.
Well, Porter Jr.'s owns words and actions may be hinting to something different.
At a bare minimum, it feels like Porter is making it known that he'll be on the field come Week 1 of the regular season. Right now, he's on the Physically Unable to Perform list with a back injury, according to the team. Many believe it was a way for Porter to miss training camp and not make it look like he was holding in.
Maybe, whether or not a deal gets done, Porter will be back in the Steelers' lineup by the time the regular season starts.
It may also be him sending a message to the Steelers that he deserves to get paid as a top cornerback in the NFL.
Porter and the Steelers haven't made much progress throughout the summer on a new contract. It appears Porter is looking for more than the Steelers believe he is worth and while they want to keep him, they aren't going to overpay.
The third outcome could be that Porter and the Steelers are on the verge of signing a deal and things have drastically changed in the last few days. It's not impossible, and contract negotiations change quickly in the NFL all the time.
No matter what Porter means by the post, the story continues. An offseason that has felt very quiet on the Porter signing front has ramped up in recent days and may continue to do so as the season approaches.
