title: 3 Safeties Seahawks Can Sign After Bud Clark Injury
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are going to need some reinforcements at the safety position after losing Bud Clark to an ankle injury during the team's 19-16 loss against the Tennessee Titans in the second week of the preseason.
The Seahawks could find Clark's replacement from within on the back half of the depth chart , but they could also look at the open market to see if any veterans are willing to come on board. Here's a look at three players the Seahawks could look into signing to boost their safety depth.
Smith has played his entire 14-year career with the Minnesota Vikings after being chosen in the first round of the 2012 NFL Draft. He has six Pro Bowls on his resume, which brings a ton of experience to any team in the league.
Smith was released by the Vikings earlier this offseason, but he has yet to announce his retirement. He is still trying to figure out exactly what he will do for the upcoming season, but the Seahawks might be the ideal fit for him. At 37 years old, Smith is not necessarily looking to join just any team. He will want to play for a squad that has Super Bowl potential, and the Seahawks are among those squads that do.
Smith would sign a veteran's minimum contract, which wouldn't hurt the Seahawks salary cap much, if at all. Adding Smith to an already elite defense will give the Seahawks some boosts both on and off the field, which could be what the team needs to achieve its lofty goals.
The Seahawks brought Wilson in for a workout earlier in the offseason, but ultimately decided not to sign him at the time. Things might be different now that Clark is injured, as Wilson could be his replacement.
Wilson spent the first seven seasons of his career with the Dallas Cowboys, where he played under Aden Durde, who is now the defensive coordinator for the Seahawks. Wilson's experience with Durde and other players like Trevon Diggs, Dante Fowler Jr., and Demarcus Lawrence could be a plus for the Seahawks in what they are looking for.
Diggs may have played his final down in the NFL after not signing with a team during the offseason, but he could be looking to suit up for the Seahawks one more time.
Diggs made three Pro Bowls with the Seahawks from 2020 to 2022, but ultimately left the team ahead of the 2024 campaign. He played with the Titans for 17 games across two seasons but re-signed with the Seahawks in November of last year. Diggs did not suit up for the playoffs, but he was awarded a Super Bowl ring for being part of the roster.
Diggs has gone unsigned for the entirety of training camp, but a return to the place where he had his best NFL success could be an option. His knowledge of the system would allow him to jump right back in and provide depth on an as-need basis.

title: 3 Observations from Seahawks Loss vs. Titans
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are going into their final week of training camp as they put the finishing touches on their 53-man roster.
Their 19-16 loss against the Tennessee Titans revealed a lot about where the team is and how much further they have to go ahead of their Sept. 9 season opener against the New England Patriots inside Lumen Field.
Here is a look at three observations from the Seahawks' loss against the Titans:
The Seahawks opted to sit most of their key players for the game, but some of those who are anticipated to play a decent amount during the preseason got some run during the game.
The main players that helped the Seahawks win this bowl last season and are back for another run are ready to go. Seattle looked strong in the first quarter, going up 16-3 against Tennessee. While not every starter played, the Seahawks should feel confident in the group of players that were on the field during the first quarter.
"The things we said we wanted to improve on from last week, I think we did those things. So operation-wise just how we get in and out of the huddle, how we take the line, all those kind of before-the-play type of things that we wanted to improve on, I think we did, which is great," Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said postgame.
"I thought we played physically. I thought we rushed the passer really well. It was good to see the run game get off a little bit in the first half. Be great to run it better in the second half. A lot of good things; a lot of good things."
Injuries are going to happen in a physical game like football. The Seahawks shouldn't feel regretful that rookie second-round pick Bud Clark played and hurt his ankle in the first quarter against the Titans.
Clark is a rookie, and he needs reps in order to get more comfortable with the speed of the NFL game. He won't get that entire league in the preseason, but after coming into the league with no professional experience, this is what the preseason is all about.
Clark is expected to miss multiple months with his broken ankle. He will still have the chance to learn alongside his teammates and hope to become a strong piece of the puzzle when the team needs him in the second half of the year.
While Jalen Milroe started off training camp on the right foot, the two preseason games he's participated in have proven that he is not on the level where he should be. The 2025 third-round pick is firmly third on the quarterback depth chart, and his performance against the Titans solidified that place.
Drew Locke performed very well, completing 12 of 14 passes for 103 yards and a touchdown. Meanwhile, Milroe completed just six of 11 passes for 52 yards and a pair of interceptions.
"Me and Jalen have a lot of good talks. I think for him, the thing that I have experienced in my career is just continuing to find ways to get to the next play. Just clear your head no matter if it was your fault, somebody else's fault," Lock said postgame. "He does a great job of that. I think that's just the constant reminder that we play a special position where we always have the ball in our hands, so everybody is looking at us.
"It's also ten guys around us, and we all need to be on the same page and executing at the same level. Sometimes that doesn't happen. You learn lessons as a young quarterback, even as an old quarterback. I'm sure Sam (Darnold) learned lessons last year. It's about continuing to get better and moving on to the next play and perfecting your process."
The Seahawks are expected to carry Milroe on the 53-man roster during the season. With injuries to players like Clark and an offensive lineman, Mason Richmond, it might benefit Seattle to utilize that roster spot for someone who could contribute on special teams rather than a third quarterback who is likely going to be inactive during most games.

title: Seahawks React to Bud Clark Injury vs. Titans
full_text:
Bud Clark is on the road to recovery after suffering an ankle injury in the Seattle Seahawks' 19-16 loss against the Tennessee Titans in the second week of the preseason.
Clark has only been with the Seahawks since April, when he became the No. 64 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft out of TCU, but he has already made quite an impression in Seattle's locker room.
"I just think, like, to see how our team reacted, I think we had the whole team go out there to give him some love. I think that tells you what everybody thinks about him," Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said postgame.
Macdonald hugged Clark at halftime, knowing how significant the injury could become.
Clark was emerging as one of the top contributors for the secondary, in hopes that he would replace Coby Bryant, who signed with the Chicago Bears earlier in the offseason. However, he likely won't be able to return to the field until the middle of the season at the earliest.
It begs the question as to when the Seahawks should rest their key players for the preseason or not. Clark, however, is a rookie, and him benefitting from the reps from the preseason was a priority for the Seahawks. Unfortunately, it didn't work out in their favor.
"Yeah, that's one thing you obviously try to avoid as much as you can in the preseason games. It is the life of football, though," Seahawks quarterback Drew Lock said postgame. "... Bud (Clark) coming in, working as hard as he has, figuring the system out, finally getting comfortable, to have something like that, I don't know what happened. But it was serious enough to get carted off."
"It almost takes like the life out of the game. With an injury like that, just to know what he's going to go through, and the pain that he's in, it's bigger than football at that point. Your heart just breaks for your brother. So, it takes a minute to kind of regroup as a team. We'll just lift him up and he'll be in our prayers," Seahawks linebacker Connor O'Toole added.
Clark was figuring out the system pretty quickly, which would have given him a good chance to earn playing time right out of the gate. Now, he will learn from the sidelines as he attempts to come back from his injury . Macdonald and the Seahawks will now figure out who will replace him.

title: Seahawks Postgame Quotes vs. Titans That Matter From Mike Macdonald
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are heading home in the loss column once again after falling 19-16 to the Tennessee Titans in their second preseason game.
While the final score doesn't tell the full story, Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald expressed disappointment about not coming out on top.
"Look, we're trying to win games. So ultimately, the goal is—we fell short in that department, which I actually think it's going to be a really great opportunity for our team to learn from this on how we manage games and the things you need to be able to do in the second half to win football games, first half included," Macdonald said postgame.
The Seahawks scored on three drives in the first quarter, building a 16-3 lead after the first 15 minutes of the contest. It showed that the Seahawks are moving in the right direction in some areas.
"But the bright side is I really do feel like our team got better this week from the work that we got in practice, and I thought we did a lot of great things, especially earlier in this game, which is what we're looking for. I think we took a step. I think we're improving. I think the important thing for our team is that we have to shed an expectation about where we need to be right now," Macdonald said.
"I think the focus needs to be about how fast can we improve on a daily basis, and our guys have had that attitude. So through that lens, I think it was a successful week. But ultimately, we want to be able to win these games. But we definitely made an improvement from last week, so let's keep going."
Most of the Seahawks starters did not participate in the game, which likely explains Macdonald's feelings a little bit. The Seahawks played most of their second-stringers in the earlier part of the game, while the back half of the roster took over for the second half.
The defining moment from the game came in the early part of the first quarter when rookie second-round pick Bud Clark broke his ankle, ending his entire first season in the league. It was an unfortunate injury, but the Seahawks still have to find a way to work around it.
"We had two really tough injuries today. Bud has a broken ankle to my knowledge. Severity I'm not sure, but he's going to be out multiple months. We're going to try to figure out what's going on with Mason (Richman), but we also think that's a major injury, a long-term injury," Macdonald said.
"Two guys that we love, that play our style of ball, that are our type of guys. Teammates love them. Great teammates, great guys, great football players. They have great futures. It's a really—it's a heartbreaker, honestly. We had three heartbreakers this week, which is tough."
With Clark likely heading to injured reserve, it opens up some competition in the secondary for a spot on the 53-man roster. Macdonald spoke highly of some players who could take that opportunity.
"Yeah, we're going to have to re-evaluate where we're at. But we saw some good things out AJ (Finley) and D'Anthony (Bell), so we'll see. Max(en Hook) I think did some good stuff, but we'll definitely have to re-evaluate," Macdonald said.
The Seahawks will have the upcoming week to evaluate alternative options with their preseason finale on Friday against the Kansas City Chiefs and the roster cutdown deadline for Sunday.

title: Seahawks Biggest Winners, Losers and Role Changes From Preseason Week 2
full_text:
The start of preseason week two for the Seattle Seahawks wasn’t great. The Seahawks had intense practices coming off the previous preseason game loss to the Dallas Cowboys. Then the Seahawks started slow in their joint practice with the Tennessee Titans. They also lost wide receiver Jake Bobo for the year to a torn ACL in the process .
Seattle started the first half against the Titans on Sunday well before the third-string players gave away the lead. This game and week gave a lot for the Seahawks to think about as they head into the final week of preseason.
Each position group faced challenges after a lackluster performance against the Cowboys. One group that benefited from the challenge was the second group of younger linebackers. Chris Paul Jr., Chazz Surratt and Connor O’Toole have been on the team for a few years, but they haven’t received many opportunities to shine.
In the game against the Titans, they were among the most productive players. Paul accounted for eight total tackles, six solo tackles and a tackle for loss. Surratt had five total tackles, with four solo, one sack and one tackle for loss. Finally, O’Toole had four total tackles, 1.5 sacks, two tackles for loss and two quarterback hits. This should set up an exciting competition for one or two of them to make the 53-man roster.
Drew Lock showed why he deserved the second-string quarterback title with a solid performance Sunday night against the Titans. Lock completed 12-of-14 of his passes for 103 yards, a touchdown and a passer rating of 121.1.
He took command of the offense and consistently drove the ball down-the-field against the Titans’ first-team defense. He rarely made mistakes, with only one of his incompletions being from a dropped pass.
This past week was difficult for many players, including some who needed a standout performance. Just as Lock showed he deserved the main backup quarterback spot, second-year dual-threat quarterback Jalen Milroe showed he was rightfully the No. 3 quarterback spot. After a rough performance against the Cowboys, Milroe needed to show more in his competition against Lock .
Instead, Milroe was one of the main reasons why the Seahawks blew a 16-3 lead at halftime . He was incapable of extending drives, making the throws when needed and made critical mistakes. He finished the game completing 6-of-11 of his passes for 52 yards, two interceptions and got sacked twice.
This week saw many backup and third-stringers step up for their spot on the 53-man roster. Power back Emanuel Wilson remains out with an injury , allowing other running backs to make a case for the third-string spot. Second-year running back Jacardi Wright not only overlapped Velus Jones on the depth chart after Sunday, but he is now a legitimate threat to Wilson.
Wright rushed for 81 yards on eight carries, including a 69-yard touchdown run against the Titans’ first-team defense. The longer Wilson remains out, the more players like Wright become threats for a roster spot.
The Seahawks made a few changes against the Titans going into the game. One of them was the players who returned punts and kickoffs. Those players were veteran Cody White and rookie Emmanuel Henderson .
White had two decent kickoff returns, but made a terrible decision on a punt return that gave the Titans the ball deep in Seahawks’ territory. Henderson hesitated in one kickoff return, but was more consistent and didn’t turn the ball over.
With rookie Bud Clark out for multiple months with a broken ankle, the Seahawks stressed the importance of the next safety coming in. Veteran D’Anthony Bell stepped up and was all over the field . He played a good bit of safety and nickel throughout the game against the Titans.
He might have earned a spot on the roster because of Clark’s injury, but his experience and dynamic are significant for the Seahawks’ defense.

title: Seahawks Depth Chart Update After Bud Clark Injury
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks ended their rough week within the first half against the Tennessee Titans. Seattle had a rough set of practices, including the joint practice against the Titans. The Seahawks lost wide receiver Jake Bobo for the year due to a knee injury . Seattle started strong, but they experienced one more disastrous result on the field.
In the first quarter, the Seahawks saw rookie Bud Clark go down holding his ankle and wasn’t able to put any weight on it. Clark had to be carted off the field with all Seahawks players wishing him luck. This is likely the third major injury either a starter or a key role player this training camp and preseason. With Clark out for several months , the Seahawks will need a solid supporting cast.
Clark wasn’t going to be the starter for the Seahawks as the season kicks off against the New England Patriots on September 3. He was, however, set to be utilized in a dynamic role for the Dark Side Defense by playing all over the field at safety, slot cornerback, box linebacker and boundary cornerback. The Seahawks need a new depth chart at the safety position and nickelback.
The two easiest spots at the safety positions are Julian Love and Ty Okada , who is coming in as a full-time starter. Love will be one of the Seahawks’ biggest defensive leaders. Okada has been solid in the last few weeks in preseason and should be a great player after stepping up with 11 games last season.
A.J. Finley is another veteran who stepped up during training camp and preseason . He has been a reliable defender since the Seahawks’ fan fest shortly before their first preseason game against the Dallas Cowboys. Finley remains the backup behind Love.
At the other second-string safety spot was originally Clark’s protected spot behind Okada. His athleticism and dynamic playmaking made him a key fit with head coach Mike Macdonald’s multi-role defense. With Clark out, the Seahawks need another dynamic player.
Luckily, the Seahawks have moved players around in the defensive backs in multiple positions. One of the players is D’Anthony Bell, who has been active throughout the offseason . Not only has Bell played strong safety, but he has practiced at the box linebacker position. The Seahawks have flexed him out at nickel to play pass coverage. His experience with the team and how dynamic gives him an extra push to make the roster.
Bell was likely fifth in line filling at nickel . If Nick Emmanwori is still injured, the Seahawks would likely have cornerback Devon Witherspoon go back to where he spent his first two years of his career. With Clark out, that No. 3 nickel spot likely goes to Noah Igbinoghene, then Nehemiah Pritchett. It wouldn’t be a surprise to see Bell take some nickel reps during the season.
The other two veteran safeties, Rodney Thomas and Maxen Hook, have good NFL experience, but they have less experience than the other four players. Thomas is likely to make the 53-man roster based on his consistency through the training camp and preseason.
Finally, rookie cornerback Andre Fuller has experience playing nickel and safety . He could make a good emergency spot on the practice squad if he doesn’t make the initial 53-man roster.

title: Bud Clark Injury Update is Bad News for Seahawks
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are disappointed after No. 64 overall pick Bud Clark broke his ankle in the team's 19-16 loss against the Tennessee Titans in the second game of the preseason at Nissan Stadium.
Clark suffered the injury early in the first quarter, which put a damper on the rest of the game. The Seahawks were able to score 16 points in the first 15 minutes of the game, but they were held scoreless in the final three quarters. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald spoke after the game about Clark and offensive lineman Mason Richman, who also suffered a lower-leg injury.
"We had two really tough injuries today," Macdonald said via the team's website. "Bud has a broken ankle to my knowledge, the severity I'm not sure, but he's going to be out multiple months. Then we're going to try to figure out what's going on with Mason, but we also think that's a major injury, a long-term injury.
"Two guys that we love that play our style of ball that are our type of guys. Teammates love them, great teammates, great guys, great football players, they have great futures. It's a heartbreaker, honestly. We got three heartbreakers this weekend, which is tough."
Clark is in the mix to be one of the key contributors in the secondary at the safety position, but his injury is going to derail most, if not his entire, rookie season. That's a big loss for the Seahawks, who are counting on Clark to help replace Coby Bryant, who ironically enough also suffered an injury earlier in training camp in his first season with the Chicago Bears.
With Clark likely heading to the injured reserve, it will now require the depth behind the rookie to step up in his place.
"We're going to have to reevaluate where we're at, but we saw some good things today out of AJ (Finley) and D'Anthony (Bell), so we'll see," Macdonald said postgame. "Max (Maxen Hook) I think did some good stuff, but we'll definitely have to reevaluate."
The Seahawks could look to sign some veterans or possibly even trade for one on the open market, but it's clear that the Seahawks are going to have to pivot off of their original plans.

title: 4 Winners & 4 Losers in Seahawks Preseason Week 2 Loss vs. Titans
full_text:
After a loss to Dallas in Week 1, the Seattle Seahawks were on the road for the second week of the NFL preseason. The Seahawks went into Nashville to take on the Tennessee Titans in a prime-time game on Sunday night.
Once again, the majority of the starters were out, including rookie running back Jadarian Price. The first-round pick didn't play against the Cowboys, and fans were hopeful to see his debut on Sunday. We learned early in the day that wouldn't happen, as Seattle said Price would sit the entire preseason .
As for the game itself, Seattle was in control until the final quarter, which is when Tennessee scored a late touchdown to take a 19-16 lead, which wound up being the final. With this game behind us, let's see who stands out as both winners and loser from Week 2 of the preseason.
Undrafted out of Utah in 2025, Connor O'Toole appeared in eight games as a rookie and had five tackles. He's a long shot to make the team this year, but he made a strong case for himself against the Titans. O'Toole was active all night and broke through the line to record 1.5 sacks.
It was all Seattle in the first half, but the Titans were given life late in the second quarter. The Seahawks forced a punt, but Cody White was unable to track the ball as the returner and fumbled it away. Tennessee recovered the ball at the Seattle 11. The defense held, but White still gave the Titans three points for free.
Veteran linebacker Chazz Surratt is fighting for a roster spot after playing in 11 games for the Seahawks last year. On Sunday, he made an excellent play, chasing down Cam Ward and recording a strip-sack.
Great hustle by Chazz Surratt! SEAvsTEN on FOX Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/fCfwXy09Rm
Surratt finished with five tackles and one sack, doing much of his damage against the Titans' starters.
With Jake Bobo suffering an injury earlier this week, there's an open spot at wide receiver. Ricky White III has all the tools to take that job, but made a costly mistake late in this one. After surrendering the lead in the fourth quarter, White made a third-down reception for 30 yards, but the play didn't count. White was flagged for offensive pass interference, putting the Seahawks in a third-and-15 situation.
A second-round pick in 2025, Elijah Arroyo joined the Seahawks with plenty of promise but didn't reach his potential as a rookie. This year, he has looked like a vastly improved player during camp and had a great night against the Titans. Arroyo wasn't on the field long, but made an impact with 50 yards on two receptions, including a 36-yard touchdown.
Drew Lock ➡️ Elijah Arroyo for a Seahawks TD! SEAvsTEN on FOX Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/mpb74cucFq
Arroyo was the No. 2 tight end in 2025 with AJ Barner having a breakout season. Don't be surprised if the sophomore begins to eat into his targets as he continues to develop.
Jason Myers has been one of the league's most consistent kickers and went 41-of-48 in 2025. There shouldn't be any reason for long-term concern, but Myers had a rough night on Sunday. He missed an extra point and field goal in the first half. Even his first make, which was a 48-yarder during the second quarter, only narrowly snuck in.
With Price and George Holani out, Jacardia Wright was given a chance to shine, and that's exactly what he did. The second-year player put a lot of pressure on players ahead of him, most notably Emanuel Wilson, by rushing for 81 yards on eight attempts. The big play was a 69-yard touchdown in the first quarter that led to an explosion of excitement from the sidelines .
Jacardia Wright takes it straight to the end zone for a 69-yard TD 🗣️ SEAvsTEN on FOX Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/bVuJlpcBGS
You would have liked to see more on the remainder of his carries, but Wright did enough to insert himself into the conversation at running back.
Jalen Milroe has more than enough talent to compete for the QB2 spot with Drew Lock, but he still hasn't put it all together. Sunday was a perfect example of this as he had some great plays, including a 16-yard run. He also had two interceptions, including one to end a potential game-winning drive. In all, he was 6-of-11 for 52 yards and was sacked twice. Not an ideal outing for the sophomore.

title: Seahawks Rookie Bud Clark Suffers Injury vs. Titans
full_text:
The preseason is a good tool for teams that want to see some of their younger players get some snaps in a live game. The results don't matter, but the injury risk is still there, which is why the Seattle Seahawks went into their Week 2 meeting with their starters on the bench.
Early in their game against the Tennessee Titans , Seattle was reminded of the risk as one of their top rookies went down with an injury to his right leg. It didn't take long for the training staff to bring out an air cast for his leg, and Clark was then carted to the locker room .
For the Seahawks, it's the second player they lost to injury this week. During their joint practice with the Titans, they lost wide receiver Jake Bobo to an injury as well. Bobo also had to be carted off, and head coach Mike Macdonald said it was a significant injury .
A second-round pick out of TCU, Clark is currently fighting for his spot on the roster behind starters Ty Okada and Julian Love. When he was initially selected, there were whispers that he could push for a starting role, but Okada has proven to be the better option at this point. That said, Clark was in line for a key role as a rotational piece of their secondary puzzle.
Clark had three tackles in his preseason debut and still needed to hold off players such as A.J. Finley and Rodney Thomas. He was still seen as a more promising overall prospect, especially with the ball-hawking skills he displayed at TCU. NCAA rules allowed Clark to play in a sixth season in 2025, allowing him to play 61 games. He recorded 214 tackles, 21 pass defenses, and 15 interceptions.
Seattle was unable to retain former starting safety Coby Bryant, which opened the door for Okada. Their defensive scheme leans heavily on safeties, however, which is why Clark was expected to see plenty of snaps.
As for the Seahawks' first-round pick, Jadarian Price has yet to suit up. Seattle announced earlier in the day that they wouldn't play Price in the preseason , and this injury helps justify that decision.
We will keep you updated with any developments regarding Clark's injury.

title: Why the 49ers Must Not Play George Kittle in Week 1
full_text:
After undergoing surgery for his torn Achilles in mid-January, the 49ers have George Kittle back on the practice field . He's managed to accomplish the unthinkable.
If you were to tell me that Kittle would practice at any point in training camp after seeing him carted off in the playoffs against the Eagles, I would've called you crazy.
Tearing an Achilles is typically a 9-to-12-month recovery. Yet Kittle has beaten the odds and has proven that, at 33 years old, a significant injury cannot stop him.
Now that he's back practicing, Kittle has a legitimate shot at suiting up when the 49ers play Week 1 in Australia against the Rams. I'd say it's likely he does.
However, the 49ers must not play Kittle in Week 1. As amazing as it's been to see him work his way back, it would be rushed if he jumped right into a game so quickly
It's unwise to have him play. Week 1 in Australia is a little over two weeks away. Kittle barely got back to practice on Aug. 23. The 49ers will have roughly 10 practices in that span.
Is that enough time for Kittle to be ramped up and acclimated to play a game? I have my doubts. He's such an important player to the 49ers that it would be wise if they give him at least another week to work.
And since the 49ers are flying all the way to Australia a week early, he won't have the same routine that's worked for him to get to this point.
Obviously, that impacts everyone on the 49ers, but none of them are coming off a torn Achilles tendon. Kittle's in a sensitive situation, which requires delicate handling.
Everything needs to be careful with him, and sitting him for Week 1 exercises necessary caution . It's not just about making sure his surgically repaired Achilles is fine -- it's his opposite leg as well.
That leg has been overworked the whole time. He needs to ensure that he has full trust in both legs to reduce the chances of injuring the healthy leg.
If anything, that is the most important element for his return. It's that, and to make sure he feels conditioned and is in shape. Giving him at least another week to acclimate increases those chances.
The 49ers shouldn't risk Kittle in Week 1, but I think they will. They know it's a must-win game, given how far they're traveling. A loss would feel like two.
Kittle understands that too, which is why he's worked so hard to get back. But that's exactly why he shouldn't be so hasty. Maybe he'll be perfectly fine if he plays.
But is it worth the risk? I don't think it is. Being careful with Kittle is the right approach, which means the 49ers need to sit him for Week 1.

title: 49ers Coach Can't Stop Raving About Rookie Kaelon Black
full_text:
It's undeniable that 49ers rookie Kaelon Black looked solid in his preseason debut against the Chargers . He was one of the top players who raised their stock from that game .
Black ran hard and refused to go down easily. He looked natural in the 49ers' offense, which is tremendous for a rookie. Usually, it takes a long time for rookies to get accustomed.
But Black performed as if he had been on the 49ers forever. It didn't even look like he missed a couple of weeks of practice with an injury.
Missing all of that time should've derailed him. However, offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak knew it wasn't going to. And after Black's performance against Los Angeles, Kubiak can't stop raving about him.
“I loved how he ran. He really brought kind of a spark to our offense," Kubiak said. "He's a guy who you don't have to block it perfect every time. He's going to muscle his way through for five, six yards, but he's got good speed to burst and get some explosive runs. I thought he did a really good job. His first time in NFL action, the moment wasn't big for him.
"He didn't blink. He was ready to go. Love his development. Love where he's at, but he needs to keep getting better, too, and stacking days. I think we're going to have a good player on our hands down the road, but he's got to keep pushing himself every day.”
Black did himself a huge favor with his performance against the Chargers. Now, it is just one performance in the preseason, but for a guy who missed a chunk of training camp, it is very encouraging to see.
It makes you wonder how much better he can get with more practice reps under his belt. He's going to need it if he wants to convince the 49ers to steal some carries from Christian McCaffrey.
Getting McCaffrey off the field is something the 49ers never want to do, but if Black is proving valiant, it'll be impossible for them to not play him and give McCaffrey some necessary rest.
McCaffrey shouldn't be receiving the bulk of the carries anymore. If the 49ers want to preserve him for pivotal games and a playoff run, then they'll be mindful of his usage and incorporate Black.

title: 49ers Owner Jed York Found Guilty of Two Misdemeanors in Ohio
full_text:
What a bad look for the 49ers and the NFL.
This past weekend, Jed York spent a day in jail in East Palestine, Ohio after pleading no contest to two misdemeanors, according to court documents. The misdemeanors were disorderly conduct and possession of a criminal tool. Court records also show that York was initially going to be charged with engaging in prostitution, but that was dropped .
York was arrested at 9:35 a.m. on Sunday at Wheat Hill Mobile Home Community. What in the world was he doing at a mobile home community, and why was he there first thing in the morning?
In addition, his cell phone and $160 were seized from him. The cell phone was returned , while the $160 went to the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force. That doesn't sound good.
The 49ers have yet to release a statement about this. Considering York pleaded no contest and is guilty, it's fair to assume that he will face discipline from the NFL under the Personal Conduct Policy, but it's unclear what the discipline will be. The NFL did not punish New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft when he was charged with two counts of soliciting prostitution, but he didn't plead no contest. His charges were dropped.
Stay tuned. This story is still developping.

title: 49ers Practice Squad Projection Ahead of Roster Cuts
full_text:
With less than a week to go until roster cutdowns, the San Francisco 49ers will have their practice squad set in the next week as well. Based on where things stand with one preseason game to go, who is setting themselves up to make the practice squad?
Kurtis Rourke appears to have two options: making the roster or being placed on an injured list. Unless they find a better option, Martinez will be their PS candidate.
Sincere McCormick has been the best running back among all of their depth options. They do not appear to have another good option.
This likely comes down to four players for two spots. Will Pauling appears to be ahead of Wesley Grimes as the top UDFA on the roster. However, Khadarel Hodge against Trenton Irwin for the final spot might be the most underrated storyline of the third preseason game.
Hayden Rucci or Brayden Willis are locks if they do not make the 53-man roster. Right now it appears Willis has a slight edge. The question is whether Josiah Deguara or freshly signed Khalil Dinkins makes it as well .
If one of Enrique Cruz or Austen Pleasants does not make the 53-man roster , they are locks. However, the injury status of Vederian Lowe makes both of them more likely to stick. So, this spot should go to Brandon Parker, who has run with the second team in the preseason.
Whoever loses the backup center battle between Brett Toth and Drake Nugent should circle back to the practice squad. Long-standing practice squad candidate Nick Zakelj is in the mix at guard. Isaac Alarcon makes it as a 17th player due to an international exemption.
Whoever does not make the team between Sebastian Valdez, James Thompson, and Bryson Eason will be priority practice squad adds.
Ogbo Okoronkwo is a great PS option. He is a veteran coming off of an injury with familiarity of the coaching staff. It is him or Quinton Bell.
If Tatum Bethune does not make the roster, he is a priority addition. Otherwise, it would likely be rookie UDFA Larry Worth.
Jakob Robinson is a great PS option. As long as Darell Luter does not get calls from other teams, he should be a PS player.
Rookie UDFA Jalen Stroman seems like the smart choice over veteran Ashtyn Davis.

title: What 49ers LBs Warner and Greenlaw Have Instilled in Rookie Jaden Dugger
full_text:
San Francisco 49ers rookie Jaden Dugger has had the privilege of learning from two of the NFL’s most established linebackers in Fred Warner and Dre Greenlaw.
The two are the most experienced linebackers on the 49ers’ roster and formed one of the league’s most formidable pairings from 2019 to 2023.
Dugger revealed that he stayed in the Bay Area between the offseason program and the start of training camp to learn the ropes from Warner and Greenlaw, working every day to improve his game and adjust to the NFL standard.
"I just learned so much from them, just what they expect out of certain stuff, just certain techniques, just a lot of stuff," Dugger told reporters on Saturday .
"Just picking up stuff from those vets, and the two best linebackers, so it's been good for me.
"Really, the approach to the game, that's what's the most important—being relentless, running to the ball all the time.
"If you watch film, you're going to see those guys running to the ball all the time. That's like the Forty-Niner way.
"You're taught that in college, but they don't harp on it as much. But now, when you come here, that's the standard. In practice, even if you're 40 yards away, you go chase the ball.
"So, just watching those guys and watching the team in general, just the culture around here, just that's what it taught me."
It deserves respect that Dugger decided to stay in the area to learn and understand more before training camp.
Being a rookie means everything is brand new, but using the opportunity to learn from Warner and Greenlaw is the perfect way to gain familiarity with the scheme and the very high standards they set within the organization.
How much Dugger will be seen on the field during his rookie season remains to be seen. But it's realistic that his first-year contributions could be primarily on special teams and in a rotational role on defense.
That way he can continue developing without being asked to shoulder too much responsibility right away. After all, he's doing and learning various jobs that could be important later on in the season if injuries hit.
He played nine special-teams snaps against the Los Angeles Chargers in the second preseason game, while also making his presence felt defensively with two solo tackles and a pass breakup. So there's plenty of optimism.

title: 49ers RB Christian McCaffrey Puts To Bed All Hold-In Narratives
full_text:
Rumors about Christian McCaffrey holding out for a pay rise with the San Francisco 49ers have now been put to bed.
McCaffrey had been away from training camp for several days, and without any further context, his absence looked worrying on paper.
The reason given was simply “tightness,” with no elaboration on where or how serious it was. When head coach Kyle Shanahan was pressed for more information, he didn’t want to reveal much more, so naturally, speculation began to swirl.
A key theme throughout this offseason has always centred around the 49ers being careful with McCaffrey’s workload . It’s a point that has been emphasised time and time again.
The 49ers cannot afford an injury to McCaffrey or for him to miss significant game time. He played every single game last season and was hugely influential in San Francisco defying the odds to make the playoffs despite a heavily injured roster.
He remains the focal point of the offense, with much of the 49ers’ game plan built around him and his attributes, even though last season saw him lose some of the explosiveness that has defined his career.
Thankfully, at least for now, McCaffrey has put those concerns to rest, explaining that his absence was more about preparing for the Week 1 season opener in Australia than anything related to his contract.
“Yeah obviously when you don’t practice, the way the media works now it’s a firestorm," McCaffrey told reporters on Sunday .
"But this was part of the plan from the jump was to ramp up pretty big, get 9 or 10 practices in, kind of come back down and then ramp back up so we’re fresh for the duration.
"Our staff's done a great job of coming up with specific plans. Again, I feel great. I feel fresh, and it’s good to be back out there.”
A key point with McCaffrey is that he enters this season in much better physical shape than he did 12 months ago, when he was coming off a disastrous 2024 campaign that limited him to just four games.
San Francisco now need to keep their promise of carefully managing his workload, because freshness could define his season. There are plenty of people who believe McCaffrey has lost the explosiveness that once made him so dangerous, but his improved health compared to a year ago offers plenty of reason for optimism that we could see more glimpses of his 2022 and 2023 self.

title: The Case For and Against the 49ers Playing George Kittle Week 1
full_text:
Sunday, August 23, is a pivotal moment for San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle.
The 49ers announced they had activated Kittle from the Active/Physically Unable to Perform List.
He took part in certain individual drills but wasn't participating in team drills, which is the right move, as slowly easing him back in makes sense. But prior to the 49ers activating him, Kittle had been doing solo drills away from the roster during training camp, so think of this as the next step.
It’s absolutely admirable that Kittle is out there and looks to be in fine shape. But is he fully 100%? Or is he at 80% and just easing back into it?
If he feels anything other than 100%, making the 16-hour flight to face the Los Angeles Rams at the Melbourne Cricket Ground in Week 1 wouldn’t make any sense.
Kittle’s rehab to be in this position has been nothing short of miraculous, and he deserves every bit of credit. But the last thing the 49ers need is a reinjury or a setback in his recovery.
It’s Week 1. As Kittle rightfully called playing in Australia a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity , risking him in the season opener simply isn’t worth it if he’s not 100%. The recovery period between Week 1 and Week 2 provides the perfect buffer for Kittle to continue building himself back up and potentially be ready for San Francisco’s Week 2 game at Levi’s Stadium.
Every encouraging update makes it look more and more likely that Kittle will actually be 100% in time for the trip. The 49ers will be flying out on September 2, more than a week before the season opener.
That gives Kittle additional time to prove he can handle an increased workload in practice before the team has to make a decision on his availability.
If Kittle continues progressing without any setbacks and starts participating in team drills, then the conversation changes significantly. There would be far more reason for the 49ers to feel comfortable putting him on that flight.
Nobody should expect the 49ers to take an unnecessary gamble, but if Kittle is genuinely 100% and receives full medical clearance, there’s little reason to hold him back from an opportunity he clearly wants to be part of.
It's a tough choice to make. Let's see what happens in the next week.

title: The Good and Not So Good from Day 16 of 49ers Camp: Kittle and McCaffrey Return
full_text:
SANTA CLARA -- The 49ers just finished Day 16 of training camp. Here's who stood out.
Practiced for the first time since he tore his Achilles in January. Participated in individual drills with the other tight ends but did not participate in 1-on-1 or 11-on-11 team drills, which are dangerous. The 49ers are smart to go slow with Kittle, considering he's way ahead of schedule. I expect he will fly to Australia and play against the Rams in Week 1. I don't think he'll dominate as he has in the past, but I think he'll help, and I think the 49ers will win. Call me a homer.
He must be worried about Kittle taking all of his playing time, because in the past two practices, Tonges has gone crazy. Today, he caught a team-high six passes. He was Brock Purdy's go-to guy, particularly after Mike Evans went down for the third time in camp (more on him in a minute). After Evans left the field, the 49ers started using lots of tight ends. I've never seen them do this before. Hopefully, they'll do it during the season with Kittle, Tonges and Luke Farrell.
Practiced for the first time in two weeks and looked fresh and ready for Week 1. Unlike Kittle, McCaffrey participated in team drills with no restrictions. He seems poised to have a good year, particularly because the 49ers seem intent on resting him at times. They really like Kaelon Black.
Caught two passes from Purdy in the first three plays of 11-on-11s. Black isn't a hybrid slot receiver like McCaffrey, but he can catch passes, and the 49ers will throw to him. He's a three-down player. But the best thing he does is run the ball, particularly between the tackles. He has the speed to get to the perimeter, but he wants to run downhill. He hits holes between the tackles with zero hesitation, and can squirt through the tiniest of creases. In that sense, he reminds me of Frank Gore. At one point, he took a helmet-to-helmet hit from Fred Warner on a pass over the middle, stayed down for a second, shook his head, ran back to the huddle, lined up in the backfield, took the handoff and exploded around the left side for a 20-yard gain. He's so tough.
Returned to practice after missing yesterday with a shoulder injury. Wore a black non-contact jersey but still participated fully and even caught a 15-yard pass near the sideline from Purdy while being covered by Jack Jones.
Also returned to practice after missing yesterday with a shoulder injury. At one point, he even lined up in the slot as a nickelback, something I haven't seen him do in two years. Wherever he lines up, Purdy usually stays away from him.
Intercepted Purdy while covering Stribling in the slot. Stribling ran a dig route over the middle, Purdy released the pass before Stribling turned his head, and Stout broke on the pass before Stribling knew it was coming his way. Stout and Lenoir are by far the best players in the 49ers' secondary. The rest of the starters are shaky.
Intercepted Mac Jones on a pass over the middle that was intended for Jacob Cowing. Davis is nearly 30 years old, and he hasn't had much success playing safety in his career, but he just might be good enough to start for the 49ers, considering their starting free safety, Marques Sigle, almost never makes plays on the ball. And today, he blew his assignment in the middle of the field and gave up an uncontested 70-yard touchdown catch to Jordan Watkins. Give Davis a chance.
Broke up two passes -- a deep one intended for Will Pauling, and a short one intended for Malik Turner. It's just a matter of time before Prysock joins Lenoir and Stout as starters in the secondary. He has incredible athletic gifts, he doesn't give up much separation, and he makes plays on the ball. What more could you want?
Broke up and nearly intercepted a pass from Purdy over the middle that was intended for Evans. Greenlaw hasn't made a ton of plays in camp, and he frequently comes off the field in clear passing situations such as third down. But on this play, he nearly made a one-handed interception. Still, I wonder about his ability to break down and change directions after tearing his Achilles. Don't expect him to be a full-time player this year.
He's probably the second-best defensive tackle on the team after Osa Odighizuwa. Thompson Jr. is a terrific run defender who actually can rush the passer as well. Today, he lined up with the starters and beat Carver Willis to "sack" Purdy. Whoever scouted this guy deserves a promotion.
Left practice early yet again. A few days ago, he left the joint practice against the Chargers early due to a quad strain. This injury doesn't appear serious, and yet Evans can't make it through consecutive practices without reaggravating it. Today, he ran a deep corner route, which required him to sprint, he pulled up at the end of the play, took off his shoulder pads and watched the rest of practice from the sideline. He just doesn't seem like he's going to make it through the entire season. I wouldn't be surprised if he starts some games he doesn't finish. No wonder the 49ers are breaking out their three-tight-end formations. Practically all of their wide receivers are banged up.
Hasn't practiced in more than three weeks. Didn't even show up to watch practice from the sideline. Either he's extremely unhappy with his contract and is holding in for an extension, or his knee tendinitis is worse than the 49ers have let on. If he plays Week 1, it's fair to wonder how effective he'll be. He probably won't be in football shape, and new defensive coordinator Raheem Morris might not know how to use him. And without Bosa, the 49ers defense is in serious trouble. I don't think Morris has the chops to build a viable defense without his only effective edge rusher.
Missed practice with an undisclosed injury. Which means both of the 49ers' primary edge rushers are injured. Not to mention Mykel Williams, their first-round pick from last year, who seems months away from returning from a torn ACL. I don't see how the defense can be good without a legitimate edge rush.
Nearly knocked out Kaelon Black with a vicious helmet-to-helmet hit. Remember, Warner knocked out Renardo Green from the joint practice against the Chargers a few days ago, and knocked out Jordan James for three weeks after punching him when he wasn't wearing pads and breaking his ribs. Warner has been out of control all of camp. And he has been loud, too. You frequently can hear him taunting the offense. So today, Purdy completed a pass right over Warner's head, then immediately screamed an obscenity at Warner. I didn't know Purdy uses words like that. Afterward, Warner walked over to Purdy and they appeared to hash things out.
He's trying to install so many new things, and he doesn't currently have the personnel to pull off any of them. To be fair, his players do a good job aggressively breaking on intermediate passes over the middle, but they can't seem to stop anything else. Today, Morris kept using a defense with five defensive linemen, one linebacker and five defensive backs. And it couldn't stop anything -- not the run or the pass. On third down, he wants to be aggressive and blitz. This just leaves his subpar safeties one on one against superior players. And if the blitz doesn't get to the quarterback right away, which it usually doesn't, the defense gives up huge catches. I have a feeling this defense will struggle big time this season.

title: 5 Major Questions the 49ers Must Answer Before Cutdowns
full_text:
As the San Francisco 49ers enter the last week of practice before roster cutdowns , what are the biggest questions facing the team?
Stribling has been one of the most impactful rookies of the preseason . The only question now is how often he plays and in what role? The team has been resting Mike Evans, but it is notable that Deebo Samuel and Demarcus Robinson started at wide receiver in two wide-out sets in the second preseason. Those two were held out in the preseason opener with the starters.
Stribling had a hot preseason but might be a rotational player early in his career.
The left guard battle might end up with a winner by default. Connor Colby appears to have bowed out after moving over to right guard for the past few weeks. Robert Jones has been banged up and has not taken over the job. Austen Pleasants looked unfamiliar with left guard.
Meanwhile, rookie Carver Willis got work with the first team last week and started in front of Brock Purdy in the preseason game. Did he just win the job?
The backup center job could end up being resolved soon. Brett Toth was signed to take on the role, but he has not been healthy enough to take it. Third-year UDFA Drake Nugent has taken snaps once again and appears to be going from practice squad lock to backup center. Can he finalize winning the job?
The 49ers have investments in Osa Odighizuwa, Alfred Collins, Gracen Halton, and C.J. West. However, three of the best stories in training camp are Sebastian Valdez, James Thompson, and Bryson Eason.
All three have bottom-of-the-roster potential with practice squad lock ability. Can they keep all three around in some manner?
The 49ers signed Vederian Lowe to be their backup left tackle. He started the year on PUP, returned, and immediately got hurt . Austen Pleasants has held the job down with Lowe out. Does Lowe return, do they ride with Pleasants, or does rookie Enrique Cruz sneak into the mix?

title: Buccaneers Rookie Jalon Daniels is Creating a Big QB Problem
full_text:
Quarterback Jalon Daniels has taken Tampa Bay by storm.
The undrafted Tampa Bay Buccaneers rookie has been on full display against the New York Jets and Kansas City Chiefs.
Daniels has shown out in his limited action by completing 19 of 29 passes (65.5%) for 182 yards and a touchdown with no turnovers. He's also added another 26 yards on the ground with a trip to the end zone.
Daniels was already thought to have surpassed Connor Bazelak for third on the depth chart after his performance against the Jets, but he is now playing at such a high level that it's creating a bit of an issue in the quarterback room.
Daniels' stats aren't out of this world by any means, but it's what he has shown outside of those numbers that is drawing the attention of his teammates, coaches, front office and fans.
His efficiency, comfort level, poise in the pocket, tight-window throws and decision-making have been on full display early in his career. And while there are still things he needs to improve or learn, he is clearly looking like a guy who can make it in this league.
Daniels' play has reiterated head coach Todd Bowles' statements of there indeed being a QB battle on the Bucs' hands.
With Jake Browning being signed this offseason to provide a better schematic fit and veteran presence behind Baker Mayfield, it was thought that he would be handed those backup keys with no such competition.
That is no longer the case with the emergence of Daniels through camp and the preseason.
Browning did okay in his first preseason action as a Buccaneer. However, the thing with Browning is that there could be a limited upside to having him in the game.
Whereas with Daniels, the upside seems almost unlimited given what he has shown, the ability to use his legs and the ceiling of development that is still there considering how fresh he is into the NFL.
While Daniels' emergence has definitely created a problem when it comes to the state of the QB room, it's a good one to have if you're the Bucs.
It's been a while since they have had much excitement outside of the starter, so having a guy like Daniels could set them up for the future if he can continue to develop.
The Bucs have been synonymous with carrying two quarterbacks on their roster in recent years, but they may have to take a different approach this go-around and keep three to avoid losing Daniels to another team via waivers.

title: Buccaneers First-Round Pick Rueben Bain Jr. Is Living Up To The Hype
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers thought they hit big when they drafted Miami edge rusher Rueben Bain Jr. with the 15th-overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. Many teams passed up on him due to his small arm length, but the Bucs weren't worried about it and thought they got a steal with Bain.
It's the preseason, and Bain has only played a few snaps so far, but early returns are looking quite promising.
Bain has looked very strong so far in training camp against his own offense and in joint practices against the New York Jets. He hadn't gotten any preseason action in that Jets game, but he did get a little against the Kansas City Chiefs last Saturday, and boy, did he make the most of those snaps.
Pro Football Focus has graded every player's preseason so far, and Bain notably comes out on top among all rookies. He boasted an 88.8 overall grade, which is the highest for a defensive rookie and places him right above Giants linebacker Arvell Reese (88.2) and Bain's former Miami teammate and current Los Angeles Chargers edge rusher Akheem Mesidor (81.6)
Top graded defensive rookies this preseason, among first round picks Rueben Bain Jr           88.8 Arvell Reese                88.2 Akheem Mesidor       81.6 pic.twitter.com/5uB8UA4StN
It's important to contextualize this, though. Bain has played just one game so far in the preseason, and he only played six snaps for the two three-and-outs the starting defense forced. The sample size is small, which could put him over his peers.
That being said, he was still impressive. His hump move on Kansas City's left tackle has gone somewhat viral on social media, and he also stuck to his man in coverage when he was asked to during his short stint in the game as well.
oh look Rueben Bain Jr. casually moving a 325 pound man against his will pic.twitter.com/ux6TcRoEer
Bain will get some more chances to show off his prowess this week when the Bucs head to Jacksonville to hold joint practice with the Jaguars. The Bucs and Jaguars will hold two joint practices before they play each other in what will be each team's final preseason game on Friday night.

title: 3 Buccaneers Players Who Need a Big Week in Joint Practice vs. Jaguars
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are set to head to Jacksonville this week to face off against the Jaguars. It will be Tampa Bay's second joint practice of training camp after heading to New York to play the Jets, and it will also be the last part of training camp before the Bucs begin to prepare for Week 1.
Naturally, time is running out as cut day approaches. Many Buccaneers have secured their spots on the 53-man roster, but others among the rest of the 90-man roster are fighting for their spot and to stick in the NFL.
Plenty of UDFAs and career practice-squad players are going through that battle, but there are some veterans who could be in danger as well. Here are three Bucs players who need a big week to stick around on Tampa Bay's 53-man roster:
Braswell was Tampa Bay's second-round pick in 2024, but he certainly hasn't lived up to that status. The former Alabama edge rusher has gotten very scarce playing time the past two seasons, and with two (technically three) new additions to the edge rushing room, he's in decent danger to miss out on the roster.
The problem? Braswell didn't participate in training camp last Thursday and didn't play in Week 2 of the preseason against the Chiefs. Braswell can't play if he's really hurt, obviously, but any time he isn't on the field is time that edge rushers like David Walker can show their stuff, and that would certainly spell disaster for Braswell.
The Bucs are likely to keep four tight ends on the roster. Three of those tight ends (Cade Otton, Payne Durham, Ko Kieft) are already accounted for, but there will be a battle for TE4 — and it's a battle that Culp is certainly losing.
Culp is competing wiith 2026 sixth-round pick Bauer Sharp, and Sharp has impressed so far with his raw athleticism and willingness to do the dirty work. Culp showed flashes in 2024, but he hasn't been able to get on to the field very often. With the Buccaneers likely keeping Jalon Daniels on as a third QB on the 53-man roster, one position will likely get cramped. If it's tight end, Culp could be out if he doesn't really impress this week.
Tucker was set to be Tampa Bay's third back after the Bucs picked up his option as a restricted free agent this offseason, but something interesting happened during the team's second preseason game against the Chiefs.
Tucker was the fourth back to play, with running back Josh Williams getting the nod over him at RB3. That's at least something to note, and it might mean that Tucker's job isn't quite safe as we previously imagined in Tampa Bay. The team seems to like Williams and wants to see what he can do, so it would behoove Tucker to have a big week and then a strong preseason game against the Jaguars to secure his spot.

title: 12 Winners, 4 Losers From Bucs' Win Over Chiefs: Edge Rushers Show Out
full_text:
Things started slowly for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers as they trotted out their starters for the first time this preseason against the Kansas City Chiefs.
Fortunately, everything turned around after the slow start for Tampa Bay, as it would go on to defeat the Chiefs 16-15 in come-from-behind fashion.
While some nitpicking moments and some players could have done better, most of the team played well, and we have identified those winners and losers from the Bucs' victory.
First on the list of winners is backup undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels. Daniels strung together yet another solid performance against the Chiefs, completing 64% of his passes for 71 yards and a touchdown while also adding another 19 yards on the ground.
The rookie has shown poise, confidence, and energy through his first two NFL games and looks to be pushing Jake Browning for the backup job behind Baker Mayfield. If Daniels hadn't been in the game, it's unlikely the Bucs' offense would have seen much success on the night.
The Bucs' pass rush was on full display in this game after revamping the entire defensive line this offseason.
Anthony Nelson came away with 1.5 sacks, including a strip sack, with Mo Kamara also notching half a sack on three pressures.
Three of the Bucs' top edge rushers didn't get home but created pressures as well in limited time. Yaya Diaby looked strong, coming away with a pressure. David Walker also showed up late in the first half, getting three pressures in the final drive before halftime. But the highlight came from rookie Rueben Bain Jr., who showed his strength on his pressure with a nasty hump move.
Rueben Bain Jr. pic.twitter.com/DeGhkcMTs2
Punter Riley Dixon had a rough 2025 season, and things didn't look to have improved through the Bucs' first preseason game.
However, Dixon bounced back in a big way against the Chiefs. He averaged 47 yards on five punts, with two downed inside the 20-yard line, including one that was downed at the 10.
Linebacker Caden Fordham saw lots of action against the Chiefs and once again had a good showing when on the field.
The stats aren't going to knock you off your rocker, but Fordham was constantly around the ball, playing well in coverage as well as coming in second on the team in tackles with seven, six of which were solo and included a tackle for loss.
He is making a strong case to make the Bucs' practice squad or roster.
The tight ends weren't all that heavily involved in the game, but Ko Kieft was the bright spot from the unit.
Kieft came away with two catches for just four yards, but secured the game-winning score from Jalon Daniels.
Kieft isn't known for his catching ability, but he was able to snag the throw in a tight window for the score. He also continued to show why he is a special-teams ace, consistently being one of the first down the field and coming away with a tackle as well.
The secondary as a whole did fairly well on the night, but early in the game, rookie Keionte Scott's talents were on full display.
The box score won't reflect how well he played, but Scott was seen all over the field and made a couple of big-time tackles that show that he is ready for a large role on this team. He's a very physical player, and that was seen on Saturday night.
The Buccaneers' wide receiver unit is one of the deepest in the league, and there are a handful of players likely vying for a final roster spot.
Two of those guys, Kameron Johnson and Dean Patterson, both had great outings against the Chiefs.
Johnson was heavily involved on offense and special teams, catching four passes for 56 yards, taking a kickoff 28 yards and returning two punts for 24 yards total.
Patterson matched Johnson offensively, catching six passes for 56 yards, which was highlighted by a spectacular toe-tap grab on the sidelines.
Look at that toe tap catch by Dean Patterson IV 🔥 Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Bl2sBGi0Bm
Jake Browning didn't see any playing time in the Bucs' first preseason game, so we wanted to get a good look at him in his first action. Things didn't quite go well.
With his offensive line and running backs missing blocks, Browning took three sacks on the night, two of which saw him get absolutely lit up.
While the blocking wasn't up to par, Browning also looked to hold on to the ball too long at times. It wasn't the best outing from Browning as he looks to fend off Jalon Daniels from taking the QB2 spot. He finished the night 8/11 for 84 yards.
Sean Tucker led the team in rushing with 23 yards and a touchdown on five carries. However, Josh Williams got snaps before him in the game, which could be something to monitor moving forward.
Despite Tucker being efficient, the same things that have kept him from becoming a well-rounded back bit him again in this one as he missed a free blitzer that led to a huge sack on Jake Browning.
Ted Hurst has been making noise through training camp and almost had his first NFL touchdown last week against the Jets.
Things couldn't have gone any different for the young athletic rookie against the Chiefs.
Hurst was targeted just once in the matchup, but failed to come down with a reception. He wasn't involved in the offense for much of the game, which likely stemmed from a boneheaded mistake early in the game where he smacked fellow rookie Mansoor Delane in the back of the head for a 15-yard penalty.
Ted Hurst got a 15-yard penalty for slapping Mansoor Delane (via @TheRealKrock_ ) pic.twitter.com/MXvVNaZcLM
Last on the losers list but perhaps the biggest loser on the night is third-string right tackle Marshall Foerner.
Foerner got the start in place of Luke Goedeke, but he was absolutely abysmal during his time on the field.
Penalties and missed assignments were glaring, and much of the pressure on Jake Browning came from that side of the line.
Foerner would go on to be replaced by guard Elijah Klein at halftime, ending his night. With this type of showing, it would be hard to imagine that he will be on the team much longer.

title: Grading the Buccaneers' 16-15 Preseason Win Against The Chiefs
full_text:
The Buccaneers yet again got another preseason, win this time against the Kansas City Chiefs. Many players stepped up, especially on the defensive side of the ball. Let's go over each position group in the Bucs' win and talk about who played well and who played badly.
Jalon Daniels looked fantastic for the Bucs, with 9/14 passing for 71 yards and a touchdown. He had a 100.6 quarterback rating and also added 19 yards on the ground on seven rushing attempts. Browning, for what it's worth, was not bad either, and finished 8/11 passing for 84 yards and also had 14 rushing yards on two carries. Starter Baker Mayfield posted 2/4 passing for 10 yards.
It was rough sledding for the Bucs backs in this game. Sean Tucker was the best out of the bunch with five carries for 23 yards and a touchdown. Meanwhile, starter Bucky Irving finished with three carries for 14 yards. Josh Williams had two carries for nine yards and new running back Barika Kpeenu had four carries for 13 yards.
Kameron Johnson and Dean Patterson led the way for the Bucs receivers in this one. Johnson finished with four catches and 56 yards and Patterson had six total receptions for 56 yards. Garrett Greene had one catch for eight yards and David Sills V had one catch for negative one yard. Rookie receiver Ted Hurst III had one target, but no catches.
Shoutout to Bucs veteran tight end Ko Kieft, who had two catches for four yards and a touchdown as well. Rookie Bauer Sharp had two catches for 13 yards, while rookie Kenny Fletcher Jr. had one target but no catches.
The Bucs' offensive line was very thin at tackle in this matchup, as starter Tristan Wirfs and backups Ben Chukwuma and Justin Skule did not play in this game. The line struggled to protect the quarterback as Jake Browning took multiple heavy hits, and Jalon Daniels had to show his athleticism to the fullest to avoid pressure in the pocket. Luke Haggard especially struggled, giving up multiple pressures and having a penalty or two.
If I didn't include pass-rushing outside linebackers in this group, they would likely get a B- or a C+. Yasir Holmes led the way for this group with four tackles, while Anthony Nelson had four tackles, one and a half sacks and one quarterback hit. Elijah Roberts had four tackles, Jack Pyburn had three tackles and Mohamed Kamara had three tackles, a half sack and two quarterback hits. Al-Quadin Muhammad, Yaya Diaby and David Walker combined for four quarterback hits, with Walker having two of the four.
Caden Fordham continues to impress with seven total tackles tonight and one tackle for loss. John Bullock also had some very good moments in the game with four tackles, one tackle for loss and a forced fumble. Finally, Javin Wright had three tackles and one pass deflection.
Rashad Wisdom led the way for the Bucs today with nine total tackles. Rookie Ayden Garnes had five tackles and one pass deflection, while second-year player Roman Parodie had two tackles, one pass deflection, and one interception.
B.T. Potter was great on the night, making his lone 46-yard field goal and his lone extra point. Meanwhile, Riley Dixon had five punts for 235 yards, averaging 47 yards per punt, with two of his punts going inside the 20-yard line.

title: The Good, Bad, and Ugly From Buccaneers' 16-15 Win vs. the Chiefs
full_text:
Even though the Tampa Bay Buccaneers played a preseason game in New York a week ago, the excitement heading into this second preseason game vs. the Kansas City Chiefs was palpable for a couple of reasons.
First of all, it was a home game. Not only that, it’s the only home game for the Bucs during the preseason, so it was an opportunity for the fans in Tampa to see their team in live action before the regular season kicks off in a few weeks.
The second and most significant reason for the added anticipation heading into this game was the fact that Todd Bowles would be playing a number of starters on both sides of the ball in this contest.
So although it’s still just the preseason, this preseason game vs. the Chiefs provided at least a glimpse into the product fans can expect to see this year from the Buccaneers.
As we’ll be doing throughout each game the Buccaneers play this season, let’s take a look at the good, the bad and the ugly from the Bucs’ victory over the Kansas City Chiefs at Raymond James Stadium.
Although they only played a couple of series, the Buccaneers' starting edge duo of Yaya Diaby and Rueben Bain Jr. looked as advertised in this contest. Both Diaby and Bain found themselves dangerously close to sacking Justin Fields on numerous occasions, while at the same time, their pressures halted drives and forced the Chiefs to punt each series they played.
Bain showed off his incredible power on one play by launching the Chiefs' RT with one arm before forcing Fields to get rid of the ball quickly. The highlight clip quickly made its rounds on social media, generating even more excitement from NFL fans who were eager to watch Bain rush the passer as a pro.
Bain with a sick hump move. Sheesh! pic.twitter.com/err5hv3PH2
Once Diaby and Bain were done for the night, the momentum continued behind some stellar play from the team's depth rushers in Anthony Nelson, David Walker and Mo Kamara. Nelson, the veteran of the group, had 1.5 sacks, while both Kamara and Walker applied relentless pressure on KC's offensive linemen and quarterbacks when they were in the game.
The difference between UDFA rookie QB Jalon Daniels and experienced veteran Jake Browning could not be more staggering. Browning played the first half (and one series in the third quarter), yet the best throw during that portion of the game came when Daniels had to sub in for Browning for a single play after Browning was forced to exit the game briefly after getting obliterated on a sack.
When Daniels finally took over the reins permanently, he immediately marched the offense down the field with a combination of impressive throws and elusive scrambles before firing a beautiful TD strike on the run to Ko Kieft to put the Bucs on the board for the first time.
Jalon Daniels gives the Bucs their first points of the night on his first drive. Really nice throw on the run. Good stuff from the rookie QB. pic.twitter.com/tySaLJkut6
Was Daniels perfect? Certainly not. But it's impossible to deny the impact he has on the game compared to his main competitor. As soon as Daniels entered this game with the Bucs trailing, the momentum shifted in their favor. When it was all said and done, it was Daniels who secured the victory for his team, just like he did last week in New York.
This one won't apply to those who were in attendance at Raymond James Stadium this evening, but for those who weren't, they got a real treat with Jon Gruden calling the game for WFLA-TV alongside Ronde Barber. Gruden's knowledge, enthusiasm and passion for Buccaneers football came through in a way that engages viewers in a way few others could emulate.
Although Gruden was just filling in for Chris Meyers, those watching the television broadcast got a real treat with the coach who delivered the franchise its first-ever Lombardi Trophy on the call.
This was our first look at the third-year WR out of Barton College so far this preseason, and he made it very easy to understand why Jason Licht has kept him around. Johnson looked explosive in the return game, taking his one kickoff return for 28 yards and two punt returns for 24 yards. Johnson has the ability to be more than just a return man, though, and his four receptions for 56 yards were second on the team to Dean Patterson, who also looked excellent as a receiver.
Aside from some impressive Bucky Irving runs, fans didn't get much excitement from the Buccaneers' starting offense in the two series they played. As most OCs do in the preseason, Zac Robinson unveiled a pretty vanilla script to start this game, mixing runs and screens with little-to-no progress to be made by his starters.
Is this something to actually be concerned about? Absolutely not. The Bucs were without their star LT as well as all of their best wide receivers. The goal was simply to get their healthy starters a little taste of game action and then get them back to the sidelines at full health. Mission accomplished.
In the first half, promising rookie receiver Ted Hurst got an unnecessary roughness penalty, which ultimately squandered the Buccaneers' drive. In isolation, a common penalty is not alarming. Especially for a rookie. That said, the flag was thrown because Hurst lost his cool and smacked Chiefs' CB Mansoor Delane in the back of the helmet.
LMAOOOOO https://t.co/JPPypXnR6W pic.twitter.com/qVxyGtbUFd
For a rookie who is trying to earn a role in the NFL, mental errors like this simply can't happen, especially in a game where Hurst is being depended on as the team's top wideout.
Hurst does not have a reputation for making these types of decisions on the field, so hopefully it's more of an anomaly than it is a sign of things to come. Either way, Hurst needs to make better decisions in games in order to continue to earn the trust and respect of his coaches as he had prior to this incident.
After missing the Bucs' first preseason game because of a back issue, Jake Browning got to see his first live game action as a member of the Buccaneers in this one. Unfortunately, Browning got absolutely annihilated by Chiefs' defenders on numerous occasions while failing to put any points on the board.
Jake Browning just got OBLITERATED. My goodness. He has to get checked on the sideline. Jalon Daniels checks in. pic.twitter.com/UC80zMkz63
It was a rough night for Browning, who got roughed up both literally and figuratively. If Browning hopes to earn the backup quarterback job he was brought to Tampa to play, he's going to need to show a lot more in the team's final preseason game next week, especially with how Jalon Daniels has been playing.
Before he can worry about that, though, he'll likely need to take a little bit of time to let his body recover from this one.
Jake Browning going to bed tonight pic.twitter.com/01lgCXAIsf
The Bucs will finish off their preseason scheduled next Friday in Jacksonville when they take on Liam Coen and the Jaguars.
