title: Buccaneers Studs and Duds From First Half vs. Chiefs
full_text:
TAMPA, FL — The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have completed the first half of their second preseason game against the Kansas City Chiefs. Tampa Bay's starters played for two drives, but after that, their night was over and the backups headed onto the field.
It was a short showing for starters, but a few of them still impressed, as did some backups. Unfortunately, some other players didn't impress against the Chiefs in the first half, and their play stood out for the wrong reasons.
Here are some studs and duds from Tampa Bay's first half against the Chiefs during Saturday's preseason matchup:
Outside linebacker Yaya Diaby had a great two drives with the starters out and playing. Diaby had two key pressures across both series, and he caused incompletions and stalled the Chiefs on both occasions. He had the help of the rest of the line, but his ability to get to Chiefs QB Justin Fields would be a boon for the Bucs if it could continue during the regular season.
Fordham is trying to make the roster, and so far, he's doing a good job at making his case.
Fordham had four combined tackles, three of which were solo tackles. He also had one tackle for loss, disrupting a run play, which helped the Bucs get a stop on defense. He has some competition in the room with the likes of Nick Jackson and John Bullock, but so far, he's made a strong impression in Tampa Bay.
It was a great pass-rushing night, as you can tell. Walker didn't get any sacks in the first half, but he did have three pressures, the last of which came on a pretty lethal spin move.
This spin move by David Walker 🌀🤯 📺: #KCvsTB on WFLA 📻: @98rocktampabay 📲: In-market on the Bucs app pic.twitter.com/pZdISQ9xoj
Walker tore his ACL and couldn't play in 2025, but now that he's been able to get some reps in 2026, he's looked really strong in camp and in preseason. This is the second time he's shown how good his spin move is in the preseason, and the Bucs will hope he can do the same thing in the regular season, too.
Nelson had a strip sack on Fields that didn't result in a turnover, but it did result in the Chiefs losing yards and punting back to the Bucs. He also had another half-sack later in the second quarter to make the Chiefs kick outside the red zone.
The whole edge unit looked strong during the first half, but Nelson made a play just as he's apt to do during the regular season in key moments. He'll serve as EDGE4 as it stands, and plays like that will keep him around on the roster.
Hurst didn't get much action across the two quarters, but unfortunately, he did cause a 15-yard penalty. He slapped the helmet of a Chiefs defender, which brought the Bucs back on their drive and caused them to punt.
LMAOOOOO https://t.co/JPPypXnR6W pic.twitter.com/qVxyGtbUFd
Hurst is competing to get some serious snaps in 2026. He has the talent, but he'll have to be smarter if he wants to make a big impact in Tampa Bay.
Unfortunately, it can take just one bad play as a tackle to land here, and that's what happened to Foerner. Foerner failed to pick up edge rusher Felix Anudike-Uzomah, and quarterback Jake Browning got hit so hard that he had to leave the game temporarily. That's never a great look, and unfortunately, Foerner getting swiftly beaten on the line is the main reason it happened.
Marshall Foerner toasted and Jake Browning laid out because of it. pic.twitter.com/sY843TmdCp

title: Buccaneers Players You Should Watch in Preseason Game vs. Chiefs
full_text:
TAMPA, FL — The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are set to play their second preseason game Saturday night against the Kansas City Chiefs, and it's arguably the most pressing game of the year — starters are expected to play.
The Bucs will put out starters that aren't injured on Saturday, so there are a few we're excited to get a look at. But even beyond those starters, there are a few players who played in the first preseason game against the New York Jets that we — and head coach Todd Bowles — are looking to get some more tape on before the regular season.
With all that in mind, here are four players to keep an eye on Saturday when the Bucs play the Chiefs:
Bain is a rookie, so in theory, he should have gotten some playing time against the New York Jets during the team's first preseason game. Bowles felt confident in his work all training camp, though, and as a result, he sat him with the rest of the starters.
Now, though, Bain is set to make his debut on the edge and get his first NFL action. He's looked strong in training camp against the Bucs and in joint practice against the Jets, but we haven't really seen him take full reps without restriction so far this offseason.
Now, Bain will get the chance to dazzle and put on the moves Saturday night, so definitely keep an eye out.
Daniels looked strong during his preseason debut against the Jets, but he also played the second half of the game against lesser competition. It's unknown if quarterback Connor Bazelak will once again play over him on Saturday, but if Daniels plays against some better competition, he'll be one to watch.
Daniels played well without most of Tampa Bay's star or even backup receivers, so it would be interesting to see him with some real weapons at his disposal. He's a raw prospect, but if he plays well again, he could be an intriguing player for the Bucs to potentially stick on the 53-man roster.
UPDATE: Dennis was not dressed in pre-game warmups and won't play.
Bucs ILB SirVocea Dennis is also not dressed tonight. Means more snaps for rookie Josiah Trotter, as well as fellow rookie Caden Fordham, who has impressed in preseason and is battling for a 53/PS spot.
Fans are really excited about linebacker Josiah Trotter this offseason, and for good reason. But so far, Dennis is the starter during first-team drills, and he'll likely come out that way with the starters on defense too.
If he does, many will be watching to see if he has a strong performance after disappointing in a few respects last season when he had the starting job. If he doesn't and Trotter starts instead, that will say a lot about where Bowles is with the linebacker room, and that's worth watching as well anyway.
Either way, Dennis should get some reps. He needs a great offseason to convince the NFL sphere that he can start, and this will be his first chance.

title: Predicting Buccaneers Starters vs Chiefs for NFL Preseason Game 2
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are set to play their next preseason game against the Kansas City Chiefs, and it should be an interesting one — for the first time all preseason, starters will play, and it will probably be the only time we see them before Week 1.
Head coach Todd Bowles wants the starters to get some reps, and they certainly will on Saturday night. But who exactly among those starters will play? And for how long?
Here's what to expect on Saturday night, and which starters will likely play on either side of the ball:
• QB Baker Mayfield • RB Bucky Irving • RB Kenny Gainwell • LG Ben Bredeson • C Graham Barton • RG Cody Mauch • RT Luke Goedeke • WR Chris Godwin
The Buccaneers will roll out with an offense that will be similar to its starting lineup in Week 1, with quarterback Baker Mayfield the most notable member. He didn't play at all during preseason last year, but he'll get some playing time this year.
The entire offensive line should start sans left tackle Tristan Wirfs, who is still recovering from a hamstring injury. The running back room with Irving and Gainwell should go, but the wideouts room is a little beat up at the moment with both Emeka Egbuka (toe) and Jalen McMillan (knee) likely resting.
As a result, wideout Chris Godwin should be the only starter to play at wideout. Expect him to play alongside players like Ted Hurst and Tez Johnson, among others.
• EDGE Rueben Bain Jr. • DT Calijah Kancey • DT A'Shawn Robinson • EDGE Yaya Diaby • LB Alex Anzalone • LB SirVocea Dennis • S Tykee Smith • S Antoine Winfield Jr. • CB Zyon McCollum • CB Jacob Parrish • CB Benjamin Morrison
Most of Tampa Bay's starting defense should play on Saturday.
The one notable player who will not is defensive tackle Vita Vea. Vea recently netted himself a $30 million extension with the Bucs, but he hasn't been practicing all training camp and probably won't see any meaningful playing action until Week 1.
Dennis has been starting at linebacker for the Bucs during first team drills, so he should get the start in this preseason game over draft pick Josiah Trotter.
The cornerbacks are the hardest ones to predict, as both McCollum and Morrison are a bit banged up. That being said, both have practiced in team drills this week, and there's a good chance they both get a small amount of work for a series or two given that.

title: Should the Buccaneers Pursue Steelers CB Joey Porter Jr.?
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are almost set to head into their 2026 season, with a preseason game coming up on Saturday night against the Kansas City Chiefs and one more week of joint practices with the Jacksonville Jaguars the following week.
There are a few concerns with the team before it heads to Week 1, though. One of the biggest concerns is with the secondary, which is currently a bit banged up — Benjamin Morrison is working back from a hamstring injury and Zyon McCollum is dealing with an unknown injury that has kept him sidelined for a few practices now.
With that in mind, some have wondered if the Buccaneers would try to grab a veteran cornerback on the market to help bolster the room ahead of the regular season. And per NFL insider Jordan Schultz, the opportunity may be there for Tampa Bay to make a splash and land a starting corner.
Schultz reported on Thursday that some parties believe the Pittsburgh Steelers may be open to moving corner Joey Porter Jr., who is currently in the final year of his rookie contract.
#Steelers CB Joey Porter Jr. is a name multiple teams around the NFL have wondered about as a potential trade target, per sources. JPJ is in the final year of his rookie contract, and with where the CB market is, teams have wondered if Pittsburgh could ultimately be open to a… pic.twitter.com/0t1CX9laOQ
Porter has played in 47 games for the Steelers over three seasons, and he's netted three interceptions, 120 solo tackles and 31 passes defended in that time. He posted a PFF coverage grade of 74.1 last season, the highest of his career to date.
With all of that in mind, should the Bucs go after Porter to help shore up a questionable secondary heading into the 2026 season?
No. As it always goes with trades, it's important to think about both how much it would cost to get Porter and where he'd fit into the team.
So what would it cost to get Porter? He hasn't had any yearly accolades so far in his career and he's currently on the PUP list, but he's a young corner who had a good coverage season last year. It would probably take a high draft pick, such as a second or a first, and maybe even multiple — and that's not a price that general manager Jason Licht has ever been willing to pay.
On top of that, Porter will likely request an extension to anyone he'd be traded to, and that could be upwards of $30 million per year. That's a lot to commit to a player, and especially in a time when the Buccaneers are retooling some things and have a lot of free agents to account for next offseason.
Finally, Porter would be difficult to fit into the roster. He'd likely start outside, and that would displace both Jacob Parrish, who is playing good football and is much cheaper, and Benjamin Morrison, who the Bucs drafted with a second-round pick last year. Paying money like that to cast aside two high draft picks is an unlikely move from Tampa Bay.
Trading for Porter would probably be more pain than it's worth, and on top of that, the Steelers would have to be interested in moving him in the first place. Realistically? They probably aren't.

title: Carnell Tate's Zero Preseason Catches: One Major Reason Why Titans Fans Shouldn't Panic
full_text:
Carnell Tate is almost as central to the Tennessee Titans' ongoing rebuild as Cam Ward. The latter certainly takes more pressure under center as the face of the franchise, but Tate was taken just one year (and only three picks) later. The Titans are staking a lot on their rookie wide receiver.
If you were to judge that pick through two preseason games, that would look like a mistake. On just five targets, Tate has brought in zero (none, zip, nada) catches. In fact, per PFF, Tate has the lowest completion percentage of anyone with a minimum of five targets this preseason: 0%, for those keeping track at home.
However, there are many reasons we don't judge rookies based on their short-snap preseason performances, and there's one major reason why Titans fans shouldn't yet worry about Tate's lack of production.
Lowest comp pct when targeted this preseason (min. 5 targets) Carnell Tate         0% Charlie Jones     28.6% Jacob Cowing    28.6% Phillip Dorsett    30% 6 players tied      33.3% pic.twitter.com/6vmllMIBSv
Tennessee simply isn't scheming to get Tate open right now. Say what you will about his route-running or targets, but Robert Saleh himself isn't concerned with Tate because of the play-calling not being engineered to him.
If Saleh isn't concerned, that's a reliable tell that Titans fans shouldn't be, either.
Saleh confirmed this after last night's win over the Seattle Seahawks, adding an extra layer of comfort on the subject of Tate specifically: "When it's time to scheme, we'll get guys the rock."
That may seem like a smokescreen to the more pessimistic contingent in Nashville, but it makes enough sense from Tennessee's perspective. Tate will have all year to make an impact as a starter, and he's already shown plenty of chemistry in their system with Ward in camp.
The preseason so far has been more about the Titans' position battles than anything else, especially on offense. It's less about whether or not Tate will be WR1 material out of the gate, and more focused on guys like Bryce Oliver and Xavier Restrepo fighting for a spot at the bottom of that rotation.
Regarding Tate's trajectory, fans should have their eyes firmly trained on Sep. 13. When the Titans host Saleh's former team in Nashville that Sunday, the expectation for Tate to show out will eventually be in order.
That will be because, we can assume, the staff will be drawing up plays to get him open. You can trust that Tennessee didn't draft the arguable top receiver in the class to bury him downfield, even if he spends much of the season second to Wan'Dale Robinson.
Tate's time to prove himself in this offense will come sooner rather than later. Just because that time isn't right now doesn't mean that we need to doubt the rookie's long-term potential.

title: Titans Sign Rookie LB Reid Carrico: More Potential Than You Might Think
full_text:
Just three days after signing Milo Eifler, the Tennessee Titans have placed the veteran lineback on injured reserve. Immediately replacing Eifler is LB Reid Carrico, who signs with the Titans as an undrafted rookie waived by the Cleveland Browns earlier this month.
Carrico could certainly be joining Tennessee at a more opportune time. After all, he's hopping into rotation just six days before roster cuts are due for the regular season. If he wants to make any kind of lasting impact in Nashville, he'll have to do it fast.
Yet, this is a prospect that Titans fans should be careful not to count out too hastily. Carrico's brief stint with the Browns in camp showed flashes of his defensive ability, and under Robert Saleh, maybe the rookie will be in a better scenario to truly prove what he's made of.
That's not to say that Carrico will trot out with the starters in this coming Saturday's preseason bout with the Chicago Bears, but the tools are here for a player that could contribute in time. It wasn't even a full month ago that Carrico came down with a pick in one of Cleveland's practices.
#Browns LB Reid Carrico picked the ball in the end zone during today's training camp practice. pic.twitter.com/95TJNwL0wj
Cleveland ultimately waived the first-year defender, sure, but this is also a matter of time and place. Whether or not Carrico is meant to play a somewhat serious role in Tennessee is irrelevant to the fact that he potentially could.
Looking back at his metrics in college shines a little more light on the Titans' newest addition.
In his final year with the West Virginia Mountaineers, Carrico logged a career-high 4.5 sacks and 69 total tackles. A former four-star recruit who began his career with the Ohio State Buckeyes back in 2021, it took Carrico transferring away from that prestigious program to get a real shot at playing time.
It didn't take long after that for the spry, 6'2" linebacker to make an impact in the Big 12 conference. Given a few more productive years in the NCAA, we may have been looking at a different draft profile for Carrico entirely. Still, his development tract remains alive in the NFL.
The Titans are the newest team to lay the groundwork for him to keep building on that. Carrico isn't at all a likely candidate to make the 53-man roster, but he's the ideal sort of player to keep around on the practice squad.
If the rookie gets his chance against the Bears this week, few players would be more hungry than the guy trying to make sure he doesn't get waived twice in the same month. Keep an eye on this one, Titans fans.

title: Everything Robert Saleh Said After the Titans' Preseason Win vs. Seahawks
full_text:
Another preseason game has come and gone for the Tennessee Titans, and with it are the varied reactions of a fanbase hungry for an improved season. Really, anything more than three wins will do for now - Tennessee already has two in the preseason, which is a good sign?
Expectations for the regular season aside, Robert Saleh addressed the media this morning to temper any worries that may have been spawned by Tennessee's intermittent struggles in their victory. With roster cuts looming large, too, discussion is lively around Titans football this week.
Here's everything of note that Coach Saleh said in the wake of week two.
Saleh admitted that the Titans can expect "peaks and valleys" all season, as he's taking over one of the worst situations in the league. To boot, it's only Saleh's second stint as a head coach. The preseason thus far is going as expected, according to him.
Still, Saleh guaranteed that his team will be better every week. That's a bold sentiment, but that's why he was hired over someone like Matt Nagy. Titans fans are tired of softball quotes and philosophies, and today is the latest example of Saleh raging against that.
Through two preseason games so far, Carnell Tate has zero catches on five targets. The opportunities are scarce already in his limited minutes, although Tennessee's top-pick has yet to make good on even a single one.
Saleh, however, isn't worried about Tate's skills not showing in the preseason.
Saleh said on Monday that Tate is doing a "good job" day-to-day, adding that he's proven his ability in practice regardless of how the games themselves have panned out. Saleh also noted after the game last night that "When it's time to scheme, we'll get guys the rock."
You have to believe that applies to Tate in a major way.
Aug. 30 is when NFL teams are required to make their final cuts prior to the regular season. With just one more preseason game remaining on the schedule, the window is smaller than ever for Titans players to make their case for a permanent spot.
To raise the stakes even higher, according to Saleh, there are multiple jobs still wide open.
For guys like Xavier Restrepo and Julius Chesnut who are bordering on the edges of their respective units, the matchup with the Chicago Bears on Aug. 29 is monumental. Taking place just one day before cuts, too, we could see a lot of these positions make or break in-game.
There are certainly preseason trends to keep an eye on, but Saleh made it clear that much remains up in the air.
Lastly, Saleh provided a mild update on Tennessee's ongoing position battle at right guard. Rookie Fernando Carmona has been ticking upward for the starting gig, and last night looked like another step toward securing that.
Saleh called Carmona's showing "decent," saying also that he likes the way the RG is progressing right now. Veteran Cordell Volson may have an outside shot at the gig, but Saleh continually finding ways to pat Carmona on the back suggests that his odds are falling by the game.

title: 2 Titans Players Who Helped Their Roster Case vs. Seahawks, and 2 Who Hurt it
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans improved to 2-0 in the preseason with a win over the Seattle Seahawks last night. While a win wasn't as exciting as it should be for the second week in a row, this contest still yielded more positives than Tennessee's first victory over the San Francisco 49ers.
However, with roster cuts due at the end of the month, the margins to impress have thinned. Against Seattle, a sizable chunk of this Titans team was fighting for their place in the regular season rotation.
By our count, two players greatly helped their chances, alongside two who unfortunately didn't.
Defensive end Truman Jones has been a bubble candidate for the Titans' defense up to now. Posting 11 tackles and 1.5 sacks in nine games last season, the third-year rusher needed a splash this preseason to keep his name firmly in the hat. Last night, he got it.
Jones matched last season's sack total in just one contest, logging another 1.5 as he terrorized the Seahawks offense. Jones split a fourth-quarter sack with Mohamoud Diabate that had Tennessee's sideline in hysterics. The two forced a Seattle turnover on the play that essentially ended the game.
Finishing with three tackles in total and one of the wildest highlights of the night, there is no argument that Jones helped his case for a roster spot come September.
It's like crying wolf at this point, but it's true every time. With Mitch Trubisky holding down the QB2 spot, Will Levis appears firmly on the outside of contention in the Titans' locker room. His showing last night didn't do him any favors, either.
Levis went just 4/9 passing, scoring 15 yards and enduring a sack in the process. He managed to rush for an equal metric on four attempts, but without throwing a score and coming in as the least effective QB, even behind Hendon Hooker, Levis simply didn't have the game he needed to.
He'll have one more shot at preseason redemption against the Chicago Bears next Saturday, Aug. 29, but it's almost safe to say already that time has run out for Levis in Nashville.
Much like everyone else on this list, Julius Chestnut is toward the bottom of a position battle attempting to break through the floor. Most notably, Kalel Mullings has come up at his primary opposer in the Titans' backfield.
Mullings reportedly missed game two with a hip pointer, and for the second straight week, Chesnut led the running back room. Chesnut collected eight carries on his way to 48 yards, breaking off for a 15-yard rush that also went down as the longest of the night for Tennessee.
Chestnut even impressed through the air, hauling in three catches for 24 yards in total. That was also the most on the team. With a performance like that, it's hard to imagine that Chestnut didn't do himself a massive favor against Seattle.
Finally, remaining on offense, wide receiver Bryce Oliver came up short while direct position competitor Xavier Restrepo had a solid turnout. Oliver may have been the slight favorite coming into this contest, but his quiet zero catches on two targets can't be taken as good news.
Restrepo, on the other hand, snagged two of his three targets for 10 yards. That's not a breakout showing by any means, but when the aforementioned Chestnut is leading the team with three receptions, each one goes a little further.
Oliver did manage a catch last week vs. San Francisco, but even then, Restrepo finished with one more. That sixth WR spot may be gradually beginning to favor the latter.

title: 4 Titans Players with the Most at Stake Entering Final Week of Training Camp
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans wrapped up their second preseason game on Sunday, defeating the Seattle Seahawks by a score of 19-16 at Nissan Stadium.
Tennessee is now 2-0 in the preseason, but the wins were pretty ugly and saw both units struggle mightily against backups. The Titans will finish training camp in Nashville with a joint practice and preseason game against the Chicago Bears this week.
Though the last week of preseason means the regular season is one step closer, a few Titans have a lot at stake over the next few days as the franchise looks to cut the roster down to 53 players.
Restrepo hauled in two more catches in Tennessee's win over Seattle, and though the Miami product isn't posting eye-popping numbers, it's clear that he's progressing in his development .
As of now, Restrepo likely doesn't have a roster spot. If the Titans keep six receivers, Bryce Oliver will surely receive that spot because of his special teams ability. However, Restrepo has one final opportunity this week to bolster his roster case or even make Tennessee consider retaining seven receivers.
Barton has been outplayed by rookie Anthony Hill Jr. and James Williams Sr. in camp, and his starting spot should be on the line this week.
Though Barton is experienced and was a serviceable player for the Titans last year, Hill and Williams provide much more upside as the starter next to Cedric Gray in the middle of Tennessee's defense. Barton must stand out versus the Bears, or his starting gig could get snatched sooner than expected.
Carmona has risen from a rookie fighting for a role to the favorite to be the Titans' starting right guard. The Arkansas product has gotten better and better as camp has gone on , and has been fantastic in the preseason, allowing just one pressure so far.
However, Carmona hasn't locked up the starting job just yet. The 24-year-old needs to turn in a solid week of work against Chicago and prove that he is capable of being a key piece of offensive coordinator Brian Daboll's group as a rookie.
While Carmona has risen, Volson has fallen. The former Cincinnati Bengal entered camp as the favorite to be the starting right guard, but he's now in danger of getting cut.
Volson was awful in the preseason opener against the San Francisco 49ers, and though the veteran was better on Sunday, he still didn't play well enough to ensure a roster spot. Volson posted an 85.1 Pro Football Focus run-blocking grade versus the Seahawks, but was subpar in pass protection with a 45.0 grade.
If Volson doesn't assert his presence this week, it could be the end of the road for him in Nashville. The 28-year-old might have the most at stake out of any Titan in the next couple of days.

title: 3 Standouts and 2 Disappointments from Titans Preseason Win vs. Seahawks
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans improved to 2-0 in the preseason tonight with their comeback win over the Seattle Seahawks, 19-16. A great crowd in Nashville came out for what was ultimately a slow-rolling contest resulting in a home victory. The Titans trailed 16-3 after the first quarter.
With roster cuts due just one week from today, on Aug. 30, multiple Titans players came into this contest with their NFL status on the line. Tennessee had plenty to take a closer look at on either side of the ball by the time the final whistle blew.
We've got the three biggest standouts, as well as the two greatest disappointments, from game two.
Chestnut is likely in contention with Kalel Mullings for the Titans' final spot in the running back room. For the second week in a row, he made a convincing case in tonight's contest to carry his role into the regular season.
Leading Tennessee's backfield with 48 yards on seven carries, the fifth-year back proved his willingness to do the dirty work as a fringe veteran that has long embraced being a depth piece in Nashville. The lone Titans touchdown of the night went to recent signee D'Ernest Johnson, but Chestnut's consistency this offseason bodes extremely well for his chances of making the cut next week.
Levis entered this game fighting for his NFL career. His 3/8 passing, three-sack performance in Tennessee's preseason opener against the San Francisco 49ers set a negative tone for his roster outlook, and Levis did little tonight to make up any ground there.
Save for a diving run that kept the Titans' aforementioned touchdown drive alive, Levis went just 4/9 for 15 yards passing and, again, took a sack. He overthrew open receivers when he had them and continued to rely on the ground game to a predictable degree, notching 15 yards on four rushes.
It simply wasn't enough to inspire any confidence in Levis, which is made worse by just how near cut day now is. It also didn't help that fourth-string passer Hendon Hooker came in and completed one ball to match Levis' total yardage.
Anthony Hill Jr. is the only Titans rookie to catch a pass this preseason. Carnell Tate's struggles can be mostly ignored due to the starting offense's low snap count, at least for the time.
Hill, on the other hand, accounted for the Titans' first of two interceptions vs. Seattle on a sneaky play underneath. He also finished with a team-high seven tackles in an effort from the linebacker that defined an otherwise lackluster night from Robert Saleh's defense.
Between Hill (second round) making impact plays and Fernando Carmona (fifth round) pulling away for the starting right guard position, it's been Tennessee's rookies beyond the first round that have truly surprised ahead of the regular season.
What's left to say about Cor'Dale Flott in the preseason at this point? We're stuck between worrying about him for the regular season and considering excusing his consistent shortcomings due to the limited looks we've had at the cornerback so far.
Whichever way you decide to tackle it, Flott looked outmatched once again tonight. Prior to sitting with the starters in the first half, Flott's only notable play was an illegal contact penalty that canceled out an interception from safety Kevin Winston Jr.
Titans fans will hold out until September to make any lasting judgements, but it's been bad break after bad break this month thus far.
Look at Joey Slye go. Between his showings against the 49ers and Seahawks this preseason, Slye is a perfect 8-8. To think that Tennessee was trying out kickers earlier this offseason as potential replacements is hard to imagine in light of Slye's recent play.
Slye, who played for five different teams prior to his stop in Nashville, may have found a sturdy home with the baby blue and red. Slye hitting this stride couldn't come at a better time, as the Titans' young offense experiences growing pains that are bound to continue throughout the year.
He's a reliable offensive piece and, once again this week, a massive standout for Tennessee.

title: Titans' Defensive Failures vs. Seahawks Should Worry Fans With Regular Season Looming
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans hosted the Seattle Seahawks for a preseason game on Sunday at Nissan Stadium, and the first two drives couldn't have gone worse for Robert Saleh's defense.
Seattle mostly played their backups against Tennessee's starting defense, but that didn't stop the Seahawks from carving up the Titans. On the opening drive, Seattle moved the ball effortlessly and notched the first score of the game on a Drew Lock touchdown pass to Elijah Arroyo from 36 yards out. On the touchdown, Titans safety Kevin Winston Jr. looked lost and didn't fulfill his assignment on the play and allowed Arroyo to break free for the score.
On the ensuing series, Tennessee's defense was even worse, as it surrendered an explosive 69-yard touchdown run to Seahawks running back Jacardia Wright. After that, Saleh pulled most of the starters to get a look at depth players.
The Titans' No. 1 defense was incredibly uninspiring Sunday night, and it may be time to hit the panic button on the unit.
Though it's just the preseason, the Titans' first-team defense has struggled in both preseason contests. Given the resources general manager Mike Borgonzi invested in the group , including signing cornerbacks Alontae Taylor and Cor'Dale Flott, and defensive tackle John Franklin-Myers, it's deflating to see them post awful performances against backups.
If the Titans want to make any kind of noise in the AFC this season, the defense must be one of the top groups in the league. They've looked the exact opposite through two preseason contests , and they haven't provided much optimism that improvement is on the way.
We'll see whether Saleh and defensive coordinator Gus Bradley's group can respond to the adversity in the final week of training camp. But there's no denying that these ugly showings in the preseason should be worrying.
The Titans will finish the preseason at home against the Chicago Bears, and will also stay in Nashville for Week 1 versus the New York Jets. The defense needs to step it up from here on out because the regular season is rapidly approaching.

title: Studs and Duds From Titans' First Half in Preseason Game vs. Seahawks
full_text:
We're halfway through the Tennessee Titans' second preseason game, this time hosting the Seattle Seahawks at home. It's been more than a week since the team's narrow road win over the San Francisco 49ers last week, which has given Titans fans ample time to chew on the results.
Down 16-9 at the break tonight, this is a game that Tennessee is lucky to be in right now. It's not been all bad for the Titans, but the reigning Super Bowl champions have come out swinging in Nashville with their secondary unit.
Here are the most notable studs and duds from Tennessee's first two quarters of football.
The worst disappointment of the night so far has been the Titans starting defense. Against the Seahawks' backup offense, led by Drew Lock, Robert Saleh's unit allowed two touchdowns in two possesions.
One came on a particularly painful 69-yard touchdown run by Jacardia Wright. The clip went viral on X right when it happened, and predictably not in a good way.
The #Titans ’ starting defense has allowed 2 TDs on 2 possessions to the #Seahawks ’ backup offense, including this 69-yard TD run by Jacardia Wright, who went untouched. Not ideal for Robert Saleh’s group. pic.twitter.com/WUfCGXlIX2
A Cor'Dale Flott illegal contact penalty washing away the Titans' lone interception from Kevin Winston Jr. in the first quarter was the cherry on top of a sad defensive half. Following a solid joint practice from the defense on Friday, this was the last thing Titans fans were expecting to see.
Ward attempted the same number of passes tonight as he did against the San Francisco 49ers last week. Facing Seattle, the Titans' franchise quarterback completed three more passes and 12 more yards (69).
His operation was just generally cleaner, too. Not ending up with a score holds Ward back from a fully positive stint in the first half, but if Gunnar Helm had stayed inbounds on an early circus throw, that likely would've changed.
Score or no score, it was a cleaner showing from Ward in every facet. That qualifies him as a stud.
After nabbing zero catches on his three targets in Tennessee's preseason opener, tonight was immediately circled as a comeback opportunity for Tate. Unfortunately, even as Ward showed improvement, Tate failed to come down with a reception once again.
The notable miss came on a long ball to the sideline, where Ward's pass sailed just out of reach for Tate. In the limited minutes that Tennessee's starters got tonight (being pulled early in the second quarter), it isn't easy for anyone to make a significant splash.
But with Wan'Dale Robinson, Elic Ayomanor, and Daniel Bellinger all notching catches (not even mentioning the backs), Tate's continued lack of production earns him dud status tonight.
Slye has to be a stud, as he's the only Titan with any points at all through the first half. Ward, not to the full fault of own, didn't throw a score. Tennessee failed to find points on the ground and Mitch Trubisky also came up empty in his brief showing in the second quarter.
Kicking 3/3 with one cashing in from 55 yards, Slye piled onto his perfect preseason in the first half. He's yet to miss in live play so far, and he's the only reason the Titans remain within striking distance heading into the final two quarters of play.

title: 3 Things Titans Need to Prove in Preseason Battle With Seahawks
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans take their talents to the national state tonight. In a preseason duel with the Seattle Seahawks airing live on FOX. Details on how you can watch the game go down here.
Comparing Friday's joint practice with the Seahawks to the one that the Titans had last week with the San Francisco 49ers is night and day. Tennessee looked like a more comfortable team all around, and in their second-to-last game of the preseason, they'll work to capitalize on that momentum.
Here are three things the Titans still need to prove in their bout with the defending Super Bowl champs tonight.
We know that Cam Ward is capable of driving a momentous offense. However, entering just his second year, and doing so in an entirely new system, resets the clock for the sophomore a little. We saw him struggle to produce after the Titans' opening drive score last week vs. the Niners.
This week, it should be about getting in a rhythm for Ward. Even if that means staying out for longer than three drives, the Titans quarterback needs to show a little more consistency as the operator of Brian Daboll's offense.
We saw it already in his showing at joint practice this week. A Ward breakthrough before the regular season would mean a comfortable extra mile of comfort for Titans fans. Under the primetime T.V. spotlight for the first time, no less - the heat is turned all the way up.
This charge falls more on Tennessee's secondary than any other aspect of Robert Saleh's defense, but there are enough moving parts within than unit to charge them with this task on the whole.
The Seattle Seahawks have one of the best playmakers in the league, in Jaxon Smith-Njigba, as well as a weathered, championship-winning signal caller under center. This is an upper echelon offense that the Titans need to find a way to contain.
That doesn't mean outright shutting the Seahawks down - almost nobody managed to do that consistently last season. Throw in another pick-six from Alontae Taylor like the one he had on Friday, though, and Tennessee would be able to walk away from this one with confidence.
It's about keeping the Titans in the game. Pressure Darnold, break up big-play passes, and allow the offense to make good on those stops. This is a collaborative win to pull for tonight.
Fernando Carmona is the name to keep an eye on here. Tennessee's starting offensive line hasn't solidified this offseason due mainly to the right guard spot. Dan Moore Jr., Peter Skoronski, Austin Schlottmann, and JC Latham are as sure as sugar.
Cordell Volson was listed as the starter at RG on the Titans' unofficial depth chart, but since, Carmona has been tabbed as the player with the "inside track" to the job. He needs to drive that home tonight.
His progress is made even more impressive by Carmona being a fifth-round rookie. If he can show another sound job as a starter tonight, alongside more encouraging play from JC Latham, you'd likely be able to call this group where they lie.
The Titans having their starting offensive line set in stone before the final preseason, not to mention with a rookie in contention, would form the perfect response to the questions that plagued that unit all offseason.

title: Where to Watch and What to Expect: Titans Host Seahawks in Preseason Game 2
full_text:
With a total of 10 preseason games taking place yesterday, the NFL had perhaps their biggest Saturday of the entire year. Oppositely, tomorrow is set to be the league's quietest Sunday, and the Tennessee Titans are firmly at the center of the spectacle. The Seattle Seahawks are coming to town for the Titans' second preseason matchup.
In the wake of a narrow win - with many problems that have already been ground to dust - over the San Francisco 49ers last week, Tennessee comes into this contest with markedly higher stakes. Roster cuts are due just one week from today. It's now or never for a handful of guys on both sides.
That's one of the many reasons to tune into tonight's contest. As for how to tune in:
Titans vs. Seahawks on Sunday, Aug. 23, will air live on FOX 7 p.m. CT. You can also watch on the Nashville affiliate WZTV FOX-17, as well as on FOX One and NFL+.
After last week's western duel went well into the night, the hour-earlier kickoff against Seattle bodes well for Titans fans trying to stay up for this one. Now, let's get into what you'll be staying up to watch for.
After a generally poor opening vs. the Niners, Tennessee's secondary bounced back in their joint practice with Seattle on Friday, While Cor'Dale Flott has still yet to show out, fellow signee Alontae Taylor led a recovery for the unit that helped build some momentum ahead of tonight.
Taylor secured a pick-six off Sam Darnold in an outing that spurred Tennessee's defense to hold their own against a team that won the Super Bowl just earlier this year.
Flott will have to be more impactful down the stretch, but Taylor's leap checked a box for the pass defense that could mean a better showing in Sunday's game. Certainly something to keep tabs on.
On a more individual note, Will Levis continues to battle for his roster spot. After Mitch Trubisky returned from a brief injury scare earlier this week, Levis' momentary chance at QB2 faded away almost as quickly as it appeared. He looks to be firmly back on the outside, looking in.
Levis, while unable to score a touchdown in Friday's joint practice, reportedly threw a 5/7 clip and avoided turning the ball over, unlike Trubisky and Ward. After throwing just 3/8 and being sacked three times by San Francisco last Thursday, Titans fans can expect his urgency to be through the roof against Seattle.
At this point, Levis may be auditioning for other teams more than anything else. It really is now or never entering his technical fourth year in Nashville either way.
Given Carnell Tate's rock-solid camp up to now, it's surprising to see his current lull. Tate caught zero balls on three targets vs. the 49ers before missing practice the following Wednesday with stiffness. Tate had previously exited early in Monday's runs following a collision with safety Kevin Winston Jr.
He eased back into the action on Friday, coming down with one highlight catch that defined his day, but Tate has still yet to secure a reception in live play. Of the notion that Tate is on a cold streak, however, Cam Ward is not a fan.
"He [Tate] doesn't have a cold streak," Ward said after the Seahawks joint practice. "He plays one of the hardest positions in the sport... The thing about Carnell, he always comes back with the next-play mentality."
Tennessee's Ward-Tate combo remains at the forefront of their rebuilt operation, and Titans fans will have to look out for the pair to finally make good on their growth on the national stage.

title: Athan Kaliakmanis Builds Momentum in Commanders' Quarterback Battle
full_text:
Despite the changes the Washington Commanders' front office has made since embracing the Jayden Daniels era , its slew of quarterback understudies has remained largely stagnant over the past two years of roster-building.
Save for Josh Johnson's continued league-wide journey back through Washington last fall, Daniels has always remained supported by the same helping hands in veteran spot starter Marcus Mariota and Sam Hartman , another draft-eligible quarterback from the summer of 2024.
Except unlike Mariota, who's repeatedly stepped in to take charge of the Commanders whenever Daniels has had to tend to his injuries, Hartman's still yet to check into an NFL game. He's functioned more as Daniels' caddy as the perennial third-stringer, a position that the previously undrafted Hartman has enjoyed without much competition through two full-season stints.
Except now, there's a new deep-cut gunslinger crowding the quarterback room, and unlike the regular benchwarmer in Hartman, Athan Kaliakmanis actually looks poised to challenge the positional hierarchy. And for anyone who wasn't yet aware of his ambitions to rise up D.C.'s totem pole, his most recent preseason exhibition served as yet another advertisement of what he's capable of offering.
He's picked a wise time to rise to the August occasion, now having strung together back-to-back positive performances against the competition and in front of the cameras. And what's more, Kaliakmanis has helped answer a lingering question taking up space in the mind of the concerned fan.
Viewers left the squad's second preseason outing with a sharp sense of disappointment this weekend. Losing 17-13 to the Detroit Lions was already frustrating enough on its own, but their patchwork offensive line held up Washington's offense sufficiently, which in turn limited Daniels from getting anything going over his only series of the day.
All-22 of Jayden Daniels & the starting offense vs the Lions pic.twitter.com/sf5rZLssSP
The need is clearly there for a game-ready backup should Daniels miss extensive time, especially coming off a season in which their franchise star logged more absences than in-game appearances. And for everything that Hartman means as a positive locker room personality, he's already falling behind Kaliakmanis in the depth chart standings.
Hartman wasn't missing simple reads like he was in the Commanders' preseason debut against the Miami Dolphins, but he can't match Kaliakmanis' raw willingness to mix creativity with arm power. Kaliakmanis threw for 162 yards on 11-of-14 passing and completely avoided any sacks after taking two against Miami the week before.
What a perfect throw and catch by Athan Kaliakmanis to Nick Nash #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/xGpBa0qr32
For the second week in a row, though, Hartman appeared before Kaliakmanis in the Commanders' opening drives. Despite the 27-year-old's capable-enough conversion numbers in Detroit, the hand-drafted prospect in Kaliakmanis should soon combine his intrigue with steadily growing results to scale the longtime alternate. The risky quarterback is still several levels away from challenging former Offensive Rookie of the Year Daniels for his job, but his talent is growing increasingly clear against measurable competition.
Even if the change doesn't happen overnight, the young asset is quickly endearing himself to those searching for inning-eating Daniels replacements, rapidly raising the stakes on a less-than-obvious roster battle.

title: 3 Things We Learned From Commanders’ Added Day 15 Training Camp Practice
full_text:
The Washington Commanders unexpectedly added a Day 15 practice to the training camp schedule that was originally scheduled as a walk-through. The practice gives them three consecutive days of work before Wednesday's joint practice session with the Ravens. Monday's session ran about an hour and featured limited 11-on-11 work, so the main value came from Dan Quinn talking about the coming week before the practice session. That said, let's take a look at three things we learned from Day 15.
Dan Quinn started his press conference Monday by saying the addition of an extra practice session was not a "knee-jerk" reaction to Saturday . He was not pleased with parts of Saturday's game . "I didn't love all that I saw from an identity standpoint, but it wasn't like a knee-jerk reaction to that," Quinn said. The bigger reason is that Washington was having players move around to different positions, making extra reps especially valuable this close to final cuts. Robert Henry Jr. and Kaytron Allen handled most of the running back opportunities with Jacory Croskey-Merritt and Rachaad White unavailable for full work, and both produced positive runs. For fringe players, these last few practices are no longer just about development; they're about changing the staff's mind before the roster is reduced to 53.
Commanders WRs at work during practice earlier today: pic.twitter.com/cl6RZd4mGj
Quinn called Wednesday’s joint practice with Baltimore a “big deal” and said the focus will move more toward the starters and players expected to sit out the preseason finale. The practice session fits what Quinn wants by giving Jayden Daniels , who has had limited preseason work, a controlled joint practice environment against a quality Ravens team that can give him competitive reps without Washington needing to expose him deep into Friday’s finale, if at all. "As far as Jayden goes, we haven't gotten there with the game, but having the joint is a big deal for us," said Quinn. "And so, that's where we want to get a lot of reps for him and for many others." Essentially, Wednesday will be the closest thing the starters may get to a dress rehearsal that actually matters.
More than anything, Washington is still evaluating several positions while key players remain unavailable or limited. Center is the perfect example and a glaring weakness now as well . Quinn said Nick Allegretti is still not ready , while Matt Gulbin will move back exclusively to center this week after getting some work at guard. Hearing Quinn say Washington still has work to do moving forward feels like someone telling me water is wet. "We do, but we still have work to do there... between the three of them, we're still in the process of evaluating what's the best way for us to go." The center position has remained unsettled and unfilled all summer after spending the offseason program hearing about how confident they were that Allegretti would win the competition. Rachaad White returned to practice, but only in a limited capacity; Croskey-Merritt worked on the side, and that again created extra opportunities for Henry and Allen. Tim Settle returned to practice while Quinn said several were targeting next week, rather than Wednesday's Baltimore practice. With roster cuts approaching and only a few evaluation opportunities remaining, Baltimore and the preseason finale will do more to settle Washington’s remaining questions than Monday’s light practice ever could.

title: 6 Commanders Who Have Played Their Way Onto the 53-Man Roster
full_text:
While training camp roster projections are largely built on expectations, two preseason games give the Washington Commanders crucial game evidence to help them as final cuts approach. A small group of individuals entered the summer fighting for jobs and have done enough through practices, a joint session, and preseason games to reach the point where a roster spot should be more than a dream at this point. Below are six players whose performances have strengthened their positions enough that leaving them off the initial roster would now be difficult to justify.
No player on the team has increased their roster standing more dramatically than Athan Kaliakmanis . In a span of just a few months, he's gone from a seventh-round rookie competing for a chance to be in the developmental quarterback battle to owning it. Backup quarterback Marcus Mariota's MCL injury opened the door for an extended competition between Sam Hartman and Kaliakmanis. Against Detroit, Kaliakmanis was 11 of 14 for 162 yards and no turnovers; his passer rating was 114.9. His passes produced the longest offensive plays of the game for Washington with a 55-yard pass to Nick Nash, a 30-yarder to Jaden Bradley, and a 21-yarder to Antonio Williams. Quinn acknowledged both Hartman and Kaliakmanis, saying the competition was ongoing; he also praised the downfield shots and accuracy against man coverage, clearly giving Kaliakmanis' performance more weight as they head to Baltimore. While Hartman has one final opportunity to change the conversation, Kaliakmanis has played well enough to earn a spot on the 53-man roster.
#Commanders QB Athan Kaliakmanis (The Greek Rifle) All-22 vs the Lions • 11 for 14 passing (79%) • 162 pass yds • 114.9 RTG • 92.4 PFF grade #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/j0tXnFAMNT
Joshua Josephs has progressed significantly since arriving as a fifth-round developmental pick. The former Tennessee Vol has forced his way into Washington's plans throughout camp, and once pads came out, he started separating himself from others. Josephs' particular case has been building at each stage over several weeks. Quinn noticed early on what type of player he had. "I feel his length as a pass rusher. How does that come to life? Long arm. Gain separation on offensive tackle," Quinn said earlier in camp. "He’s got a nice natural bend to him." Josephs recovered a fumble for his first NFL touchdown against the Lions Saturday after cornerback Amik Robertson strip-sacked Detroit QB Josh Dobbs. Josephs has long since passed the "will he make the roster" questions; now the more interesting question involves how many rotational snaps Washington can find for him.
Commanders rookie Joshua Josephs earned this touchdown. Won quickly and his pressure forced Dobbs to escape left - into Amik Robertson. Then hauled his ass off and ripped the ball out of the lineman's hand for a touchdown. Impact play. #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/TPZR9t10CB
Kaytron Allen was drafted into a room that only had one running back returning, Jacory Croskey-Merritt; eventually, Jeremy McNichols re-signed. Allen has responded confidently every single time, going back to rookie OTAs when the buzz started that he was going to make some roster noise this year. In the Miami preseason opener, Allen had 23 carries for 85 yards (no loss of yards on any carry) and a touchdown after injuries kept Jerome Ford and others off the field. Allen then was given another ten carries against Detroit, a sign the staff is comfortable with him. After Allen and fellow rookie Robert Henry Jr. stepped up when Ford went out, Quinn had this to say , "There was really no flinch from these guys playing on teams, returning, and so that was a good sign."
Maurice Hurst II presents a different story altogether. Hurst was signed after Johnny Newton suffered his pectoral injury, adding another interior pass-rush option at a time when Washington suddenly needed depth there . In his first opportunity with the team in preseason, Hurst produced five combined tackles, two sacks for 17 yards, two tackles for loss, and two quarterback hits against Detroit. The value hidden in this one is that the Commanders do not need Hurst to become a starter or replace Newton , as the team plans on doing that by committee, and Hurst’s ability to create interior pressure gives him a specific role that is now much easier to justify on the 53.
Every sack from yesterday’s game vs. Detroit. The defense finished with 5 sacks on the day, highlighted by DT Maurice Hurst II (2.0 sacks) and a strip-sack TD from CB Amik Robertson. Is Daronte Jones cooking? 🧑‍🍳 #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/KWmFss2YV1
This is probably the easiest name to include in this list since he's officially already won the kicking battle . But Drew Stevens had to earn his way onto the 53-man roster after getting signed as an undrafted free agent. Stevens earned the spot by staying consistent against an erratic incumbent in Jake Moody . Stevens then turned around after winning the job and hit field goals from 27 and 32 yards, along with his extra point, accounting for seven of Washington’s 13 points against the Lions.
Tyler Owens best represents how much Washington’s final roster can be shaped by contributions that extend beyond traditional defensive statistics. His combination of athleticism, versatility, and special teams skills makes him an invaluable commodity. Will Harris offers substantially more NFL experience , but Owens currently gives Washington more ways to use the final safety spot and appears to be a perfect match for new defensive coordinator Daronte Jones' system . Harris still has time to change that decision, but Owens has done enough this summer to deserve the roster spot. While the Baltimore joint practice session and preseason game could certainly change several decisions, these six have already done more than earn their spot in contention through two preseason games. Washington entered camp with questions about all six players, and with final cuts approaching, each has supplied enough evidence that the harder question may now be what would have to happen for the Commanders to leave them off.
Tyler Owens blows it up 💥 Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/mroSBCRtHK

title: Dan Quinn Admits Washington Still Has to ‘Figure Out’ Center — Commanders Daily
full_text:
The Washington Commanders have spent their entire training camp trying to establish a starting center, only for head coach Dan Quinn to finally acknowledge after Saturday's preseason game that they still don't have an answer . Julian Good-Jones started against Detroit with Nick Allegretti still unavailable , and nearly gave up a sack on his first snap. Rookie Matt Gulbin also received snaps in the two rotating series with its available options. Quinn's wording was different than before on this subject, as he has spent weeks calling it a competition , but now it's something they need to "figure out." Quinn praised several aspects of the line before getting to the central conversation that won't go away. "Yeah, there's a lot of groups that went in and out. And so, the first crew of Conerly and Cosmi, I thought I liked how they're playing together, their communication," said Quinn. "And Sam's really having a good camp. He's maybe playing the best that I've seen him play in the couple, three years. His technique, he's on it. I like what I'm seeing on the outside at left tackle. So, we got work to do to figure out where we want to get to at center."
Every #Commanders C Julian Good-Jones snap in Preseason Week 2 He was not the only offensive lineman who disappointed in this game, but nonetheless, sending him out to face Jordan Davis and Jalen Carter in Week 1 is offensive suicide #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/MyLxoHJOw1
Good-Jones has by far received the largest opportunity created by Allegretti's injury, but the last two games in preseason have done very little to establish anything from him. While Good-Jones' Pro Football Focus grades slightly improved from a blocking standpoint Saturday against the Lions over where he was against Miami, he committed two penalties, which made his overall grade drop drastically. His PFF numbers from the preseason are listed below. Quinn went on to say that there was "a lot to be desired" from the running game overall against Detroit, another shot at the offensive line. While he can't be blamed for every problem, he touches the ball on every play and sits in the center of both the protection communication and an interior run game that has struggled to establish anything consistent.
This is a problem the team has had since they cut veteran center Tyler Biadasz this past offseason. Heading into camp, they were extremely confident in Nick Allegretti's ability to transition to a position he has played periodically throughout his career, despite making only two NFL starts there in seven seasons. Allegretti has, of course, been dealing with a calf issue, and renewed tightness after his return kept him out of the Detroit game. That leaves the team choosing between a veteran still learning the position and recovering from injury, a clearly in-over-his-head Good-Jones, and sixth-round draft pick Matt Gulbin. The calendar is becoming the team's biggest opponent with just one preseason game remaining before roster cuts and Week 1 preparations begin. Wednesday's joint practice is likely the most valuable remaining evaluation because it will allow Washington to test its center options one more time against an unfamiliar defensive front. Whoever wins the competition still has to work with Jayden Daniels to establish the snap, protection calls, and communication consistency the team will need not only in Philadelphia, but for the entire season. This is no longer a situation where Washington is waiting for somebody to separate from the rest of the pack — Washington is currently running out of opportunities for any separation to happen organically. From this position, the overall plan is starting to look like it will need GM Adam Peters' help in finding a capable player among the roster cuts coming in the next week.

title: Around the NFC East: Preseason Week 2 Fallouts, Key Injuries, and Roster Battles Across the Division
full_text:
With preseason moving into Week 3 across the NFL, there is no shortage of notable developments throughout the NFC East as the league heads toward the final weekend of preseason games. From emerging players and heated practices to injuries and position battles, each team gave its fans something new to monitor.
Police responded to Lamb’s home in Fairview, Texas, the afternoon of July 31 for a report of a home burglary. When officers arrived, they met with “individuals representing Mr. Lamb” who showed them a broken window on the side of the home where the burglars most likely entered, Fairview police said in a statement Sunday. Evidence pointed to a single person’s entering and exiting through that window, taking “several high-end personal items,” officials said. More than $300,000 worth of property was stolen, including four luxury bags, the Fort Worth Star-Telegram reported, citing the police report. To continue reading this article, CLICK HERE...
this game, this star, this team will make us brothers 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/rEcvDTzSkd
Cowboys rookie offensive lineman Shiyazh Pete is the first member of the Navajo Nation, the largest Native American reservation in the United States, to sign with an NFL team. In Saturday's 34-14 win over the Cardinals, Pete saw just how much his accomplishment meant to his people. Thousands of members of the Navajo Nation, including President Buu Nguyen, made the short trip south to Glendale to show their support for Pete in his first NFL preseason appearance. When Pete entered the game in the fourth quarter, the members were the first to notice and began cheering. Pete played just six total plays on one drive that resulted in a Phil Mafah touchdown, but that was more than enough for everyone who made the trip to see him, as he received a standing ovation upon his return to the Cowboys bench. To continue reading this article, CLICK HERE...
Joe Milton had the offense humming in the first half when Dallas built a 24-6 lead by the break, while Sam Howell did not have the same success in the second half. Jaydon Blue returned to the field after not being seen much at practice leading up to this game, missing the joint practice against the Saints too, and led the team in carries. These 15 carries for Blue compared to eight for Israel Abanikanda and five for Malik Davis don’t nearly tell the full RB competition story though, as Davis again looked good in his limited opportunities, and even Phil Mafah took his one carry of the night for a 15-yard touchdown. Jonathan Mingo scored a touchdown on a 53-yard bomb from Milton. Mingo is an experienced player looking to separate himself from the fan-favorite, Camden Brown. It wasn’t long after this though that Brown had a 69-yard catch and run that was a yard away from being another preseason touchdown for the UDFA, keeping the WR depth chart fight entertaining. On defense, Jaishawn Barham asserted himself in his rookie debut, playing as the “green dot” of Christian Parker’s defense and flying around to make the types of plays that made him one of the stars of the Oxnard portion of camp. Shavon Revel Jr. had an interception that gave the offense a short field to score the first touchdown of the night, and take a lead they never relinquished. To continue reading this article, CLICK HERE...
Winner: Jaishawn Barham - LB The rookie linebacker from Michigan missed Week 1 of the preseason due to a groin injury, but he surely made up for it in Week 2. Barham played just 22 defensive snaps, but he made five tackles, three stops, and recorded a pressure. It's also worth noting that he made another play on a screen pass, but he was unable to finish the tackle. Still, he made a big enough impact on the play for his teammates to clean up the missed tackle. It remains to be seen what Barham’s role will be during the 2026 season, but he’s checked every single box so far in camp and now in the preseason. There is a level of physicality to his game that none of the other linebackers possess and that could earn him a spot on the starting defense sooner rather than later. To continue reading this article, CLICK HERE...
Joe Milton looked comfortable and outright dominant at times. He also made routine throws, used his legs to extend plays and continued to be automatic on QB sneaks. He ripped several deep throws up the sideline and scored on an easy QB draw. Milton missed a few throws, but still. Sam Howell didn't fare as well, turning it over in the end zone. He did look mobile and efficient otherwise. Jaishawn Barham came downhill like a missile and swerved around an offensive lineman for an easy TFL on the first drive, and then again later in the first quarter. He also had a pressure and a nice tackle in coverage during the early going. Barham missed one tackle but was otherwise stupendous. Saturday was Jaydon Blue 's best showing, as he ran for a handful of solid gains. What should impress fans most, though, is the fact that he was finally running through contact and kept his legs churning to pick up a few extra yards. He tallied 75 yards on 15 carries. Dud: RB Tyrone Tracy, Jr. For the second straight week, Tracy made a killer mistake. Last week, he missed a block that nearly got Jaxson Dart beheaded. This week, Tracy fumbled on the Miami 11 in the first half, killing a Giants' scoring drive. Tracy rushed for 26 yards on six carries and added 22 more on three receptions, but none of that detracts from the mistake. He's in no danger of being cut, but he has to shape up if he is going to be a key contributor this season. Stud: CB Deonte Banks Banks looked sharp again in coverage and appears to be an entirely different player than the one we've seen the past three years. Banks had two total tackles and two passes defensed. He is pushing hard to regain his starter status. Whether he gets back to that remains to be seen, but Banks has been crushing it this summer. "Appreciate the effort by the guys. I thought we did a lot of things really well. I like the way we handled having the lead in terms of continuing to play in such a way as to extend the lead. That's really important to learn how to do that as a team. We did that. I do believe we're a better team than we were Wednesday when we came down here. That was the goal. And now we move forward." - Harbaugh "I think our offensive line just did a good job of setting the tone by establishing the run game. Now sometimes, you get to show the young-school cats that I can still be an athlete and get out the pocket." - QB Jameis Winston on his 11-yard touchdown run to open the scoring To continue reading this article, CLICK HERE...
Arvell Reese, LB The box score suggests that Arvell Reese didn’t make much of an impact. The 6-foot-4, 243-pound linebacker played only 10 snaps and made one tackle. Still, he’s impressed all offseason and looks tailor-made for a Defensive Rookie of the Year campaign. He didn’t raise or lower his stock, and I’d be surprised if they had him play in Friday’s final preseason game against the Jets, given that his starting role isn’t going anywhere. Verdict: Stock neutral Bobby Jamison-Travis, DL Finally, we have some movement. After posting a dismal 47.5 Pro Football Focus grade against Minnesota, the 6-foot-3, 328-pound space-eater bounced back in a big way, earning a 75.6 overall grade. He held up better against the run and even recorded his first live-action sack. BJT is firmly on the bubble, and another strong performance on Friday could get him into the conversation for a 53-man roster spot. Stock going up. title: Quan Martin Is Starting to Answer Commanders’ Biggest Safety Question
full_text:
The Washington Commanders entered training camp needing real answers from Quan Martin's play. The team yearns for Martin to turn his athletic ability and experience into something bigger than they've seen so far. Back at the end of June, I wrote an article about Quan Martin's uncertain future in the burgundy and gold titled " Running Out of Time to Answer Commanders’ Biggest Safety Question ." Since that time, Martin has looked the part, getting two interceptions in as many preseason contests, with the latest coming off Lions quarterback Josh Dobbs after ending 2025 without a pick. Martin is productive overall; his 2025 season included 99 tackles, a forced fumble, and three passes defensed, but his lack of interceptions and inconsistent tackling have raised concerns. Quinn sounded extremely confident in Martin's skills after the Lions game: "He’s always somebody that has good ball skills, and he’s got the speed to get to the locations for that. So, I’m not surprised," Quinn said. "He’s usually at his best when he’s got, as a high safety, to come and make some plays." Quinn ended the conversation by saying, "He’s off to a great start," which shows he's still paying close attention to Martin's progress.
Quan loves INTs in this building 😎 📺 #WASvsDET @wusa9 pic.twitter.com/9Y08h1Wagt
When the team added Nick Cross to the room, the bar was raised for Martin to come in and give more than he had before. The types of things Martin has been doing this preseason are exactly what the previous article spoke about: ranging from the back end, ball production, and making plays capable of changing possessions. None of this frees Martin from his tackling issues from a year ago, as we haven't seen enough evidence to confirm or deny an improvement in that situation. The team's next checkpoint is Baltimore and this week's joint practice session, followed by one more preseason opportunity before the results start counting. At the end of the day, Martin entered camp this year running out of time to show whether he was a reliable answer at safety, and after two preseason games, he is finally beginning to make that answer easier to see.
COMMANDERS DARONTE JONES DEFENSE 📈 Three Commanders intercepted Dolphins passes on Thursday night - Quan Martin, Ale Kaho and Malik Spencer. It gave us a glimpse of what this defense might look like under Daronte Jones this season. @DCNewsNow pic.twitter.com/wP6XTkkTmh

title: Updated Commanders 53-Man Roster Projection After Two Preseason Games
full_text:
The Washington Commanders roster picture has changed quite a bit since our last projection, which came after nine days of camp . Since that time, Drew Stevens won the kicking competition; Laremy Tunsil and Johnny Newton are both out with significant injuries; Marcus Mariota and Jeremy McNichols have been sidelined; and several new players are in the mix. The first two preseason games have allowed Athan Kaliakmanis , Kaytron Allen, Joshua Josephs, and Maurice Hurst II chances to strengthen their cases while others have lost ground. So with one preseason game remaining and several injury/reserve decisions still capable of changing the final roster math, here is Commanders Roster Projection 3.0.
Jayden Daniels, Marcus Mariota, Athan Kaliakmanis The quarterback position has been one of the biggest changes to the projection, which is now slotted at three quarterbacks. Marcus Mariota's MCL injury has put increased importance on the QB3 competition, and Athan Kaliakmanis has stepped into that spot . In what should be the final piece of evidence, Kaliakmanis completed 11 of 14 passes for 162 yards against the Lions while committing no turnovers and completing the three longest Commanders plays of the day. While Hartman hasn't played horribly, Kaliakmanis has clearly outplayed him and appears to be the right quarterback to have behind Daniels and Mariota moving forward.
#Commanders QB Athan Kaliakmanis (The Greek Rifle) All-22 vs the Lions • 11 for 14 passing (79%) • 162 pass yds • 114.9 RTG • 92.4 PFF grade #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/j0tXnFAMNT
Jacory Croskey-Merritt, Rachaad White, Kaytron Allen, Jeremy McNichols There are no changes at this position, but Robert Henry Jr. made it a bit more difficult to project after the Miami game , then slipped back against the Lions with minus three yards and a kickoff return fumble. Of course, Jeremy McNichols' injury didn't help much either. Kaytron Allen has only strengthened his case for his roster spot after putting up 85 yards and a touchdown against Miami, and then another 10 carries against Detroit.
Give Kaytron Allen an inch and he'll take a mile pic.twitter.com/36UJUETk8H
Terry McLaurin, Stefon Diggs, Antonio Williams , Luke McCaffrey, Treylon Burks, Jaylin Lane, Dyami Brown While the seven receivers have not changed, undrafted rookie Jaden Bradley is a guy who has spent part of camp catching the attention of anyone looking. He also snagged two receptions against Detroit for 42 yards, including a nice, one-handed 30-yard catch while he was being held, along with a tackle on special teams. Bradley is making those at the bottom of the list give everything they've got until the final preseason game.
Chig Okonkwo, John Bates, Ben Sinnott, Colson Yankoff John Bates' injury made this position interesting for a couple of weeks . During camp, a decent battle at the back end of the room emerged with Lawrence Cager and Colson Yankoff showing out. Yankoff has spent the entire camp process showcasing his improvements on the football field; his versatility and special-teams pathway continue to give him the edge for the final spot
Sam Cosmi, Chris Paul, Daniel Brunskill, Nick Allegretti, Matt Gulbin, Brandon Coleman, Josh Conerly Jr., Andrew Wylie, Trent Scott Laremy Tunsil's injury really blew up this room. Brandon Coleman was close to beating out Chris Paul at left guard; now he has shifted back to left tackle . Nick Allegretti has yet to practice meaningfully with Jayden Daniels as the number one center this year, and Washington has zero reliable options otherwise. Rookie Matt Gulbin has looked serviceable, but he is a rookie with plenty to learn and room for growth. If the team was heading that direction, they should have been pushing that evaluation over the last few weeks with Allegretti out with a calf issue; instead, Julian Good-Jones has been the plug-in. Good-Jones is not the answer from what I've seen, and Quinn acknowledging that Washington still has work to do at center certainly doesn't suggest otherwise. You could make an argument for or against keeping Trent Scott over Nicholas Petit-Frere. But based on Scott’s familiarity with Washington and the fact that Petit-Frere is still trying to establish himself after not playing in 2025, Scott appears to be the safer pick, although I wasn't that impressed with Scott this camp or in the preseason. This group will likely see some shuffling as teams start to cut players and better options become available.
Odafe Oweh, K’Lavon Chaisson, Joshua Josephs *** Reserve/Suspended - Dorance Armstrong for Week 1 *** First and foremost, Dorance Armstrong is suspended for Week 1 , which means he will not count in Week 1's total. Charles Omenihu's ability to play all along the defensive front will help pick up any slack if they only carry three. Not to mention, rookie Joshua Josephs' continued upward push has him in prime position to make a splash this season.
This is a very simple breakdown defensively. It is man coverage. The edge needs to play the QB here and keep contain. Styles is doing his job and fitting inside of the WR. This isn't difficult stuff. pic.twitter.com/CAdcPth28D
Daron Payne, Javon Kinlaw, Tim Settle, Charles Omenihu, Maurice Hurst II With Johnny Newton facing a significant absence , the team had to find someone who could replace his pass-rushing ability. Maurice Hurst II had two sacks, two tackles for loss, two quarterback hits, and five combined tackles in his first game since being signed against the Lions. The team is not looking for starter reps out of Hurst, just rotational options currently.
Sonny Styles , Frankie Luvu, Leo Chenal, Jordan Magee, Kain Medrano The real battle left here is between Jordan Magee, Kain Medrano, and Ale Kaho, although Krys Barnes is probably the most capable of making any type of roster push to change this projection this late.
Can you tell the Commanders' new DC is a Flores guy? Diabolical to break out a 6-man pressure with match coverage in the preseason like this lmao. Perfect example of "pressure is the coverage" pic.twitter.com/hyi9g04N9O
Trey Amos, Rasul Douglas, Mike Sainristil, Amik Robertson, Fabian Moreau My only slight question about this group is about Trey Amos' lack of offseason work within the new defensive program. He has put in virtually no time during the new system's installation, but will likely be slung back into the top of the depth chart once cleared, which is concerning. Amik Robertson is a natural fit for Daronte Jones' system, and he showed that with his strip-sack against his old team , Detroit. Moreau's veteran presence rounds out the room well.
Nick Cross, Quan Martin, Jeremy Reaves, Tyler Owens, Malik Spencer The major change here is keeping Tyler Owens over Will Harris. Owens brings more to the conversation beyond defensive snaps, particularly through his athleticism, special-teams value, and ability to contribute in multiple roles. Harris offers veteran experience, but Owens' upside fits the defense's need for versatility.
Brought the boom 💥 pic.twitter.com/cjAkhQWb1R
Drew Stevens, Tress Way, Tyler Ott Officially, the Washington Commanders released kicker Jake Moody and named Drew Stevens the kicker for the 2026 season. He kicked field goals from 27 and 32 yards, as well as the extra point after the lone Commanders touchdown against Detroit on Saturday. Tress Way is back for another year, and Tyler Ott keeps his place without any competition, rightfully so.
Van Jefferson, Hartman, Henry, Bradley, Good-Jones, Byron Cowart, Barnes, and Petit-Frere are players who are right on the outside looking in. Bradley and Henry realistically need another strong game to shift the roster math. Last-minute injuries, of course, could change the entire direction of this group.
